## Deep-Reasoning

This Agent1 Explore step repaired the global direction after Step 17 and turned the correction into an operational crux program. The central mathematical correction is that Hitchin--Thorpe is not an external obstruction to the positive four-dimensional pinched branch; sufficiently tight normalized pinching already implies strict Hitchin--Thorpe in both signs. The Step 2 sign-blind Chern--Weil lemma gives, for \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-\sigma g\|_{op}\le\varepsilon<1/(1+\sqrt3)\), \(2\chi\pm3\tau>0\), since \(|s|\ge4(1-\varepsilon)\), \(|E|^2\le4\varepsilon^2\), and \(2\chi\pm3\tau=(4\pi^2)^{-1}\int(2|W^\pm|^2+s^2/24-|E|^2/2)d\mu\). Therefore \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\), \(\#_4\mathbb{CP}^2\), and all Hitchin--Thorpe violators or equality cases cannot carry arbitrarily tight normalized pinching and must not be used as positive-branch enemies. This changes Bridge 3 from a general Einstein-existence obstruction problem into a pinching-rigidity problem: does tight positive pinching force topology into the known/expected positive-Einstein region, or at least a finite list whose Einstein existence can be separately settled? Positive pinching also gives positive scalar curvature, so the usual Seiberg--Witten/monopole nonexistence mechanisms used in LeBrun-type examples are not directly available on a positive-pinched counterexample; refuting \(P_4^+\) would require a new nonexistence mechanism beyond the current toolkit. The real positive-branch stress family is strict-Hitchin--Thorpe, positive-Ricci, large-topology material such as \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), not Hitchin--Thorpe violators.

The second correction is strategic: the toric invariant work is not merely a laboratory for the \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) crux. A general-to-invariant bridge is needed to prove that arbitrary positive-pinched collapse is toric, but a construction or obstruction on the actual crux topology may assume the toric structure. The sourced toric paper records the Orlik--Raymond polygon/slopes description of closed simply connected toric four-manifolds, and also states the connected-sum and Sha--Yang positive-Ricci context for diagonal torus actions on connected sums of \(S^2\times S^2\). Thus A02 should directly attack smooth \(T^2\)-invariant metrics on the \((2k+2)\)-rod models of \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\): either construct \(\delta_k\to0\) positive-pinched collapsing metrics, breaking the simply connected volume-gap route, or prove that rod/holonomy/horizontal Ricci matching prevents the Step-15 high-negative-edge formal collapse, yielding a genuine \(\chi\)-uniform invariant gap. The Step-17 separated SdS/Nariai rigidity theorem does not decide this multi-rod toric problem, because it concerns a cohomogeneity-one two-bolt family with the same collapsing circle at both ends; the polygonal crux has changing primitive rod labels and only requires the full pinched inequalities, not exact Einstein equality.

This step also clarified the exact computational object. In a diagonal polar probe \(g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2\), with \(w=pq\) and \(v=\log(p/q)\), the vertical eigenvalues are \(r_p=-\Delta\log p-|\nabla\log p|^2-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle\) and \(r_q=-\Delta\log q-|\nabla\log q|^2-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle\), so \(r_p+r_q=-\Delta w/w\) and \(r_p-r_q=-w^{-1}\operatorname{div}(w\nabla v)\). The horizontal block is \(\operatorname{Ric}^H=K_Bg_B-[\nabla^2\log w+\frac12(d\log w\otimes d\log w+dv\otimes dv)]\). The normalized positive pinching residual is the supremum of the deviations of \(r_p,r_q\) and the two horizontal endomorphism eigenvalues from 1. The high-negative-edge seed from Step 15 remains the leading formal enemy: \(K_B|_{rod}=-A\), \(Q''+(1+2A)Q=0\), \(\Phi=2/(1+2A)\), and \(A\sim m^2\) gives formal total flux \(m\Phi\sim1/m\). The prior flat Faber--Krahn barrier is not available without a base-curvature lower bound, so the next discrimination must use the full Ricci inequalities and smooth toric closure, not a pure spectral-area estimate.

The step created a topology sanity infrastructure for the periodic characteristic labels \((1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),\ldots\) on even \(m=2k+2\)-gons. An initial checker produced scaled rational forms, exposing a normalization bug; a corrected integral checker uses the quasitoric cohomology presentation, solves self-intersections from the two linear characteristic relations, restricts to a free divisor basis, and verifies for \(m=4,6,8,10,12\) that the intersection form has rank \(m-2\), determinant \(\pm1\), even parity, and signature zero. A second script explicitly split the periodic-label forms for \(m=4,6,8,10,12,14\) into sums of hyperbolic planes with unimodular congruence matrices, giving concrete evidence that these labels are the intended \(\#_{(m-2)/2}(S^2\times S^2)\) models, subject to the caveat that a full Orlik--Raymond diffeomorphism proof/source should be supplied if a later theorem relies on it. I also wrote a finite-difference residual-evaluator scaffold for diagonal conformal-base metrics and calibrated it analytically and numerically on \(S^2\times S^2\). The analytic product residual is zero and the volume is \(16\pi^2\); finite differences converge but remain boundary-sensitive (e.g. \(N=257\) still gives about 0.052 residual due to near-boundary discretization), so this scaffold is a starting point, not a certified solver.

A01/A03's negative-branch cutoff-flow program was assimilated but not accepted as complete. Their latest messages identify the remaining load-bearing gap as degenerate epsilon-regularity: from coupled small \(L^2\) energy under the \(\chi^2\)-weighted operator to weighted pointwise \(\|\chi^2\operatorname{Rm}\|\le C/t\) on transition regions. This is important and may later support the negative branch, but it is independent of the immediate A02 toric crux probe. The orbifold/ALE Lichnerowicz route from TTCS remains valuable for noncollapsed approximate-to-exact bridges, but its first real prerequisite is a weighted annular normal form for \(C^0\)-pinched metrics, which Step 11 showed cannot come from pointwise Ricci-only regularity; it should not prematurely replace the direct toric \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) test. Higher dimensions remain open: product with an Einstein sphere propagates positive pinched input metrics from dimension 4 to \(n\ge6\), but does not propagate Einstein nonexistence without a separate theorem, and says nothing about \(n=5\) or genuinely non-product high-dimensional pinched manifolds.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Execute step tested the Step-18 toric positive-branch crux at the finite rod/corner level rather than over-reading a noisy global PDE residual. The exact Yau-26 target remains unresolved: the work concerns only the four-dimensional positive branch, only the toric periodic-label models consistent with #_k(S^2 x S^2), and only necessary local/finite matching conditions for a possible collapsed pinched family. The strategically important update is that the Step-15 high-negative-edge seed survives the first serious corner attack. For the periodic labels (1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),... every adjacent pair is a standard basis up to sign, so the diagonal fiber ansatz with p vanishing on the ±e1 rods and q on the ±e2 rods is locally compatible with the source smoothness conditions at fixed points. Reading the toric source lines 92--138 showed that in the diagonal fixed-corner special case the parity conditions allow mu^2 even, p^2 in r^2+r^4 R_even, q^2 in t^2 mu(r,0)^2+t^4 R_even, and zero fiber cross-term. Thus a diagonal residual floor in this periodic family cannot be dismissed automatically as a local corner-smoothness artifact, although arbitrary non-coordinate labels would still require the full matrix-fiber h_IJ formulation.

The symbolic Ricci computations then addressed the strategist's proposed finite matching system. In a fixed-point chart with g=dr^2+mu(r,t)^2dt^2+p(r,t)^2dtheta^2+q(r,t)^2dphi^2 and lowest jets mu=1+u r^2, p=r+a r^3, q=t(1+u r^2)+b t^3, the base edge curvature at the p=0 rod is K_B=-2u, so A=-K_B=2u. Both an independent warped-product Ricci calculation and a direct Christoffel/Ricci computation gave the same constant Ricci-endomorphism conditions along all rays t=z r: -6a-4u-1=0 and -6b-4u-1=0. Hence a=b=-(4u+1)/6=-(2A+1)/6, exactly the Step-15 one-dimensional rod coefficient for Q''+(1+2A)Q=0. A second, faster formal series calculation through the r^2 ray coefficient used the smooth ansatz mu=1+u r^2+m40 r^4+m22 r^2t^2, p=r+a r^3+p50 r^5+p32 r^3t^2, q=t(1+u r^2+m40 r^4)+b t^3+q23 r^2t^3+q05 t^5. After the constant solution, the r^2 conditions form a rank-5 linear system in six higher coefficients and remain solvable with u, hence A, free. Choosing q05=(1+2A)^2/120 matches the fifth-order Taylor coefficient of the rod profile and gives m40=-A(2A+1)/24, m22=0, p50=(22A^2+10A+1)/120, p32=0, q23=-A(2A+1)/12. Therefore neither the local smoothness parity nor the constant/first nontrivial exact Ricci corner equations impose any cap on the large negative edge-curvature parameter A.

I encoded the finite rod/corner configuration for even m=2k+2 with common A_m=m^2. Each rod has Q_i(s)=sin(sqrt(1+2m^2)s)/sqrt(1+2m^2), length L_m=pi/sqrt(1+2m^2), unit endpoint slopes, and flux Phi_i=2/(1+2m^2), so total flux 2m/(1+2m^2) is asymptotic to 1/m while the total rod perimeter tends to pi/sqrt(2). Every corner is unimodular and diagonal-standard-basis up to sign, and the local corner formal conditions through r^2 are compatible with the same A_m. This gives a finite formal collapsed rod/corner certificate, not a global metric. Its scientific value is negative for a simple BUILD proof: a chi-uniform toric volume gap cannot be proved merely from periodic-label determinant conditions, 1D rod ODEs, unit rod closure, right-angle smoothness, or low-order local corner Ricci algebra. The separated same-circle cone-slope obstruction mu(A)<1 remains real, and I retained it in the finite-matching data, but it does not decide the alternating polygon problem because the finite configuration assumes the edge bubble is absorbed at adjacent fixed points where a different circle collapses rather than closing the same circle at a second bolt.

The remaining wall is now clearly global/analytic: constructing a disk base with these collars and a determinant w satisfying -Delta_B w/w=2+O(delta), enforcing the horizontal Ricci operator inequality and especially its traceless part, controlling collar-interior transitions, deciding whether twist or non-diagonal fiber terms are forced, and understanding Chern-Weil or edge-cone/boundary-bubble accounting. I deliberately did not run a new global finite-difference optimization because the Step-18 product calibration still has approximately 0.052 boundary residual at N=257; such a numerical residual would be diagnostic only. Peer messages #285 and #286 were also assimilated: A01/A03 have further weakened the negative-branch cutoff-flow claims, leaving a degenerate weighted curvature-potential regularity theorem and unweighted Q(t) control as real open problems, so no branch of Yau-26 is solved. ## Deep-Reasoning

This step resolved three mathematical questions about the toric BUILD/BREAK fork on the #_k(S²×S²) crux family, changing the direction of the next investigation from the strategist's proposed 'clean 2D eigenvalue test' to a genuine global coupled-system analysis.

The first and most consequential finding, through a grounded TTCS verifier call with the full Steps 12-19 synthesis, is that the fork is NOT reducible to a scalar Dirichlet eigenvalue question. The volume gap is equivalent to a Dirichlet-to-Neumann flux problem for the full coupled reduced system: eigenvalue equation -Δ_B w = 2w, v-equation div(w∇v) = 0, traceless horizontal equation, Gauss-Bonnet constraint, and unit rod closure, all simultaneously on the m-gon. The eigenfunction scale is fixed geometrically (not by L² normalization) through unit-slope rod closure, but this normalizes the collapsing fiber derivative, NOT the surviving fiber value. So the rod flux = ∫q ds on a p-rod is a global system output, not a locally determined quantity. Three specific corrections: (a) Area(Ω) ≥ c > 0 does NOT imply ∫w ≥ c' > 0, so the Faber-Krahn area bound does not directly control volume; (b) boundary-localized negative curvature does NOT raise λ₁ because domain monotonicity lets an interior subdomain with moderate curvature control the eigenvalue; (c) the Step 14 Euclidean Faber-Krahn constant has a gap because it applies to flat domains, not arbitrary curved polygons.

The second finding is that the traceless horizontal equation u_{zz} + (1/2)(u_z² + v_z²) = 0, when evaluated in flat rod-collar coordinates, gives a residual of exactly (1+2A)/4 — not a new obstruction, but exactly the base curvature effect (K_B = -A at the rod). The Step 19 corner matching in Fermi coordinates of the curved base already checked the full Ricci tensor including this traceless part, and found it compatible with A free. An initial computation with an incorrect coefficient was caught and corrected. The corrected residual is confirmed numerically to machine precision at multiple parameter values.

The third and most substantive finding is the m=4 rectangular calibration. For the rectangle (flat base, separated solution), the eigenvalue constraint π²/L_x² + π²/L_y² = 2 combined with AM-GM on L_x²L_y² ≥ π⁴ gives flux ≥ 8. The seed with A=16 gives flux = 8/33 ≈ 0.242 — a 33× gap. This proves that the global system is far more constraining than local rod/corner matching. The mechanism is the coupling between the eigenvalue equation and the v-equation through the base geometry: the full system forces the base to be nearly flat for m=4 (the square S²×S² being the unique minimizer), making the rods long and the flux large.

From this calibration I developed a stream-function approach. The v-equation div(w∇v) = 0 gives a stream function ψ with dψ = *(w dv), constant on rods with jumps = rod fluxes, total oscillation = total flux. Its energy is ∫|∇ψ|² = 2∫w² + 4∫K_B w². This connects the total flux to a conformal modulus problem: if the conformal modulus of the alternating-rod polygon is bounded below uniformly in m, a rigorous BUILD theorem follows. For the square, the energy/flux² ratio = 0.077, and the AM-GM argument is equivalent to a modulus lower bound in the separated case.

The open mathematical question is now sharply formulated: does the conformal modulus of the m-gon with alternating Dirichlet boundary conditions (ψ-values) remain bounded below as m → ∞? This is a 2D conformal geometry question that does not require solving the full 4D Einstein system. A positive answer gives the χ-uniform volume gap (BUILD). A negative answer (collapsing modulus) means the seed survives and the harder global construction is earned.

A01/A03's negative-branch work has progressed to Whitney-ball decomposition and volume-independent β = A²||Rm||₂ ≈ Cr²√K₀, reducing the negative-branch closure to two non-degenerate PDE theorems (localized curvature ε-regularity and localized weighted Bernstein). This is independent of the toric positive-branch work.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Execute step deliberately corrected the trajectory rather than continuing into small-m toric numerics. The active Yau-26 target remains the original all-dimensional, sign-unrestricted statement, and nothing in this step proves or refutes it. The step resolved two lower-level route questions that materially affect where effort should go next.

First, the toric positive-branch line no longer supports a quick chi-uniform volume-gap strategy via perimeter, modulus, or small hexagon computations. I extracted the exact one-dimensional rod identity from the edge equation Q''+(1-2K_edge)Q=0 with unit endpoint slopes: int_rod(1-2K_edge)Q ds=2, hence Phi_i=int Q ds=2+2 int K_edge Q ds. In the constant edge-curvature model K_edge=-A, Phi_i=2/(1+2A)=2L_i^2/pi^2 and Vol_4=2pi^2 sum Phi_i=4 sum L_i^2. This identity was numerically checked against the exact toric anchors S^4, CP^2, and S^2 x S^2 with roundoff-level errors: S^4 gives 24pi^2, CP^2 gives 18pi^2, and S^2 x S^2 gives 16pi^2. The consequence is sharp for route selection: Cauchy-Schwarz only gives Vol_4 >= 4 L_tot^2/m, so any global O(1) control of total perimeter, coarse scale, or a comparable modulus can at best yield C/m. Such a v_0(chi)->0 lower bound cannot feed the finite-cover amplifier from Proposition A, because that amplifier requires topology-uniform noncollapse. Thus the Step-20 modulus/perimeter program is not by itself a route to the needed theorem unless it proves a stronger rod-scale or Q-weighted curvature control that forces a flux bounded below independently of m.

Second, I audited the strategist's alpha-family and confirmed that it passes the scalar/global/local necessary tests currently on record. With A_m=m^alpha, 1<alpha<=2, L_m=pi/sqrt(1+2m^alpha), Phi_i=2/(1+2m^alpha), the total flux is ~m^{1-alpha} and the normalized four-volume tends to zero. The signed Gauss-Bonnet burden can be carried by constant -A_m collars with width/length ratio tending to 1/pi; the script records width/L about 0.312 for m=200 at alpha=1.5 and alpha=1.9. Bishop's positive-Ricci upper-volume scale is far from saturated. The regular right-angled constant-curvature polygon mismatch is real but narrow: a regular right-angled m-gon in curvature -A has side length asymptotic to 1.762747/sqrt(A), while the rod ODE asks for pi/sqrt(2A)=2.221441/sqrt(A), ratio 1.2602155895; solving equality gives A_match -> about 0.849, so large-A regular constant-curvature polygons are impossible. But this only rules out a too-symmetric model, not the strip-like collar geometry where curvature is boundary-localized and the interior nearly flat. Therefore the current toric evidence says: scalar rod identities, Gauss-Bonnet bookkeeping, local corner compatibility, and perimeter/modulus controls do not give a chi-uniform volume gap; any remaining BUILD obstruction must live in the full horizontal/traceless collar-to-interior transition, holonomy/twist/matrix-fiber effects, or a stronger edge-cone/Chern-Weil mechanism not yet formulated. A true BREAK still needs an actual smooth global metric with ||Ric-g||_op -> 0, and because Einstein existence on #_k(S^2 x S^2) remains open, even such a toric collapse would not refute Yau-26.

Third, I shifted A02 toward the negative-branch smoothing route and tested the most obvious possible falsification: whether the Step-11 opposite-warp Calderon-Zygmund spike immediately breaks A01/A03's weighted parabolic target |a Rm| <= C beta/t for a=chi^2. I built a constant-diffusivity heat scaling model u_t=a_0 Delta u with Gaussian spikes. For k active dimensions, u(0,t)=B(sigma^2/(sigma^2+2a_0t))^{k/2} and ||u_0||_2=B pi^{k/4} sigma^{k/2}; the relevant ratio is R(t)=t a_0 u(0,t)/||u_0||_2. The result is that for full four-active-dimensional spikes sup_t R=1/(8pi)≈0.0397887, independent of sigma and chi_0, while for the two-active-dimensional fiber-invariant CZ-type spike sup_t R=O(sigma)->0. The elliptic initial ratio can still be arbitrarily large, which is why Step 11 killed elliptic pointwise regularity, but the positive-time t^{-1} parabolic estimate is not contradicted by this mechanism. Thus A01/A03's zero-order weighted smoothing theorem remains plausible at scaling level, though completely unproved as a geometric PDE theorem.

I also reran peer verification scripts. A03's q->3q/2 recurrence product script confirmed convergence of polynomial/cutoff products and endpoints gamma/t for curvature and delta(r^2/t)^(1/3) for defect. A03's weighted-moment hierarchy script confirmed the exact H_q and J_m weights and the cubic-potential factorization. A01's finite-exponent smoothing script confirmed the arithmetic of the finite-exponent route: in dimension four parabolic Sobolev gives spacetime L^3, L^3 is supercritical over n/2=2, Whitney time scaling is independent of chi_0, and only fixed q=2,3 critical absorption is needed before local boundedness. These are useful checks but not a proof: the load-bearing missing object is still the localized weak moment inequality with nested time cutoffs, finite-neighbor leakage, evolving measure, Hessian-a integration by parts, and normalized cutoff-flow terms all controlled without hidden global assumptions.

The scientific judgment after this step is that the current toric route should be paused as a candidate for fast chi-uniform noncollapse, while the negative-branch cutoff-flow route has become the more consequential branch to audit. A02's previous strength has been breaking false regularity and compactness lemmas; this step found that the naive CZ transplant does not break the new weighted parabolic formulation. The next useful work should therefore be a direct local tensor-energy audit of that formulation, not another numerical toric polygon experiment.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Execute/Preceptor step audited the current four-dimensional negative cutoff-flow route before investing in a heavy term-by-term derivation. The active Yau-26 target remains the full all-dimensional statement, and no proof, refutation, or Lean formalization was obtained. The key correction is that Step 21's weighted-CZ heat audit should not be treated as positive evidence for the weighted parabolic estimate. In dimension four, both the critical L^2 curvature energy and the schematic bound |a Rm| <= C beta/t are scale invariant, so an O(1) Gaussian ratio is expected; moreover the Step-11 opposite-fiber CZ spike is determinant-preserving and hence noncollapsed, while the serious failure modes for energy-to-curvature estimates occur under collapse.

I therefore tested the collapsed model directly. On S^1_ell x B^3 with fiber-independent test functions, ||u||_4 = ell^(1/4)||f||_4 and ||grad u||_2 = ell^(1/2)||grad f||_2, forcing any downstairs four-dimensional Sobolev constant to grow at least like ell^(-1/4). A hyperbolic/cusp-type model normalized by Ric=-g has E=0, |Rm|^2=8/3, and int|Rm|^2 -> 0 as the collapsed volume tends to zero, but A_ell^2||Rm||_2 remains O(1). The script `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step22_collapse_sobolev_and_scope_audit.py` and data `workspace/data/step22_collapse_sobolev_and_scope_audit.json` record this numerically for ell from 1 to 1e-8. This decisively rejects any route that uses raw downstairs small L^2 curvature energy plus a dimension-only Sobolev/Poincare/isoperimetric constant in collapsed regions. It does not refute the corrected A01/A03 route, because their latest formulation retains a relative Sobolev constant A and the critical product gamma=A^2||F||_2; the collapsed model exactly explains why that product is the right invariant.

Source checking sharpened where noncollapsing enters. Min-Oo's paper explicitly obtains the Sobolev constant from lower Ricci and diameter control, not from collapse-neutral local data; Wang/Yang's local Ricci flow theorem assumes a Sobolev inequality and a small critical product A_0^2|Rm|_{n/2}, so it cannot be cited as a dimension-only collapsed estimate. The remaining A01/A03 theorem must therefore be written in one of two honest forms: either a downstairs relative-Sobolev finite-neighbor theorem that carries A_alpha and gamma_alpha=A_alpha^2||F||_2 until the four-dimensional cancellation is used, or an accessible-cover theorem on genuine buffered normal covers where chi, eta, a=chi^2, and the normalized cutoff flow pull back equivariantly and smallness is transported as a local mean. Exponential-pullback chart selection is useful only after positive-time bounded curvature has been produced; it does not supply the Sobolev input for the smoothing theorem.

I also performed the downstream scope check requested by the strategist. A pure Chern-Weil/Hitchin-Thorpe endpoint would buy nothing, because tight four-dimensional Ricci pinching already implies strict Hitchin-Thorpe for small delta by the sign-blind Chern-Weil accounting from Steps 4 and 18. Min-Oo cannot be the endpoint either: large-diameter closed hyperbolic manifolds are exact Ric=-g examples with delta=0 and unbounded diameter-curvature scale, while already Einstein. The real A01/A03 endpoint is stronger but narrow: the critical Ishida-LeBrun/Seiberg-Witten 7/24 calibration plus exponential chart/projector-Derdzinski contradiction could at most give a fixed-topology gap, or perhaps a standard-subclass uniform gap, for critical Ishida-LeBrun four-manifolds. It would not prove unrestricted P_4^-, P_4^+, any dimension n>=5, or the full Yau-26 proposition. In varying topology the terminal defect control must be volume-normalized, Q/Vol -> 0, and used on a plateau set of fixed positive volume fraction; absolute Q -> 0 is only a fixed-topology statement.

Finally, I preserved the toric work as reusable mathematics rather than a vanished route verdict. The exact diagonal rod identity is int_rod(1-2K_edge)Q ds = 2 and Phi_i = 2 + 2 int K_edge Q_i ds; for constant K_edge=-A this gives Phi_i=2/(1+2A)=2L_i^2/pi^2 and Vol_4=4 sum L_i^2 in the A02 normalization, anchor-checked on S^4, CP^2, and S^2 x S^2. I also recorded the twisted determinant/flux identity from the vertical trace formula: for exact Ric=g, (-Delta_B + |F|_h^2/2)w=2w, hence Phi_boundary + (1/2) int |F|_h^2 w = 2 int w and Vol_4 = 2pi^2 Phi_boundary + pi^2 int |F|_h^2 w. This sign is important: twist increases volume for fixed boundary flux but can reduce boundary flux at fixed volume. The formal alpha-family remains a useful collapsed adversary for future Sobolev/Moser and determinant-volume claims, but not a global metric or counterexample.

The broad resolution state is therefore sharper but still open. The negative smoothing route has valid algebraic and four-dimensional scale assets, but its material gaps are the weak nested time-space estimate with finite-neighbor leakage/evolving measures, current-time gamma control, explicit relative-Sobolev or cover hypotheses, volume-normalized chart selection in varying topology, and adaptation from -2a Ric to -2a(Ric+g). More importantly, even full success there remains four-dimensional and special-family. A knowledge request for high-dimensional no-Einstein reservoirs or obstructions returned only already-relevant Ozuch/Morteza-Viaclovsky desingularization sources and did not reveal a broad n>=5 no-Einstein source. Given the all-dimensional target, the next research move should reopen the n>=5 problem and all-dimensional mechanisms rather than letting the session remain indefinitely in a narrow four-dimensional laboratory.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Explore step re-centered the session on the exact all-dimensional Yau-26 target after Step 22 showed that the active four-dimensional cutoff-flow program, even if successful, would only give a special critical Ishida--LeBrun negative gap. The controlling logic remains: for each fixed dimension, the interval formulation is equivalent to \(P_n^+\vee P_n^-\), so a proof needs one sign branch in every dimension, while a refutation needs one fixed dimension in which both normalized signs fail on no-Einstein underlying manifolds. That makes the high-dimensional landscape decisive: unlike dimension four, where Seiberg--Witten/Hitchin--Thorpe-type obstructions give many no-Einstein manifolds but tight pinching tends to collide with those obstructions, in dimensions \(n\ge5\) the basic reservoir of closed smooth manifolds known to admit no Einstein metric of any sign appears absent from the sources inspected. A refutation in high dimension therefore cannot simply import a known no-Einstein topology; it would first have to solve or sharply advance the open problem of producing such a topology, and then independently realize arbitrary tight two-sided Ricci pinching on it. This asymmetry makes the high-dimensional counterexample route much weaker than a proof/structural-reduction route.

The strongest conceptual update is that \(n\ge5\) should be treated as an entanglement with the general Einstein-existence problem, not as a parallel replay of the four-dimensional obstruction search. The Yau 1982 preview itself says no method was known for producing Einstein metrics on general compact manifolds except in the Kähler case, and the Wang survey on symmetry and bundle constructions states that in dimensions \(\ge5\) it is still unknown whether every closed manifold admits an Einstein metric and that there are no known general obstructions to existence; the same source stresses that homogeneous nonexistence results are only nonexistence of invariant Einstein metrics and may not say anything about the underlying smooth manifold. LeBrun 2025 strengthens this warning from the opposite direction: high-dimensional manifolds can carry Einstein metrics of both signs, beginning with product constructions in dimensions divisible by four, and sign is not a diffeomorphism invariant in general. Hence for Yau-26, the conclusion may be vacuous in high dimension if every closed manifold admits some Einstein metric; if not, the missing theorem is not just existence/nonexistence but whether any no-Einstein manifold can lie arbitrarily close, in the normalized Ricci operator norm, to \(\sigma g\). This reframes \(n\ge5\) as a rigorous boundary statement: \(P_n^\sigma\) is automatic if all closed \(n\)-manifolds admit Einstein metrics, while failure requires a simultaneous no-Einstein obstruction and tight Ricci-pinching construction.

The classic Anderson/Ye source obligation was advanced but not closed. Focused retrieval through `knowledge_request` twice failed to ingest Anderson 1989 or Ye 1993 as primary Knowledge objects, instead returning mostly already-known desingularization/stability sources. I therefore wrote reproducible metadata/access probes. `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step23_classic_source_access_probe.py` produced `workspace/data/step23_classic_source_access_probe.json`, and `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step23_classic_open_api_probe.py` produced `workspace/data/step23_classic_open_api_probe.json`. These establish stable bibliographic metadata: Anderson, “Ricci curvature bounds and Einstein metrics on compact manifolds,” JAMS 2 (1989), 455--490, DOI `10.1090/s0894-0347-1989-0999661-1`; Ye, “Ricci flow, Einstein metrics and space forms,” Trans. AMS 338 (1993), 871--896, DOI `10.1090/s0002-9947-1993-1108615-3`, JSTOR `2154433`. OpenAlex reports bronze OA AMS PDF URLs for both, but direct AMS/JSTOR access in this runtime returned Cloudflare/client-challenge HTML rather than readable theorem text. Crossref/OpenAlex reconstruct an abstract-like summary for Ye: Ricci-pinched stable metrics can be deformed to Einstein metrics by Ricci flow, suitably negatively pinched manifolds to hyperbolic space forms, and \(L^2\)-pinched manifolds to space forms. For Anderson, OpenAlex gives an OCR-like abstract fragment about Lipschitz convergence/compactness under Ricci curvature bounds, but not Corollary B(4) or exact hypotheses. Therefore the route map may use these papers only as identified source obligations and abstract-level signposts, not as verified theorems. In particular, it remains plausible, but not yet source-proved in this session, that Anderson’s result isolates volume/noncollapse as the missing positive-branch hypothesis.

The four-dimensional smoothing side branch was also kept honest in response to peer messages #299--#302. I read A01’s repaired `step22_current_energy_formulation.md`, `step22_weak_nested_moment_estimate.md`, `plans/route_assessment_step22.md`, and A03’s `step21_consolidated_status.md`. The corrected variables are now \(S_\alpha=A_\alpha^4H_{2,\alpha}\), \(\Gamma=\sup_\alpha S_\alpha^{1/2}\), with support energy propagated by a bounded-degree graph inequality \(S_\alpha'\le Cr^{-2}\sum_{\beta\sim\alpha}(A_\alpha/A_\beta)^4S_\beta\), not by a false Whitney-volume-normal energy bound. This is self-consistent only if neighboring relative Sobolev constants are genuinely comparable under the chosen finite-neighbor/buffer construction; then graph semigroup estimates give \(\Gamma(t)\le e^{C\theta}\Gamma(0)\) on \(t\le\theta r^2\). If collapse levels can jump so that adjacent \((A_\alpha/A_\beta)^4\) is unbounded, the graph absorption mechanism fails. Thus A02 can later verify this precisely, but it remains side work: even a full proof of U1--U6 would address only the critical four-dimensional negative laboratory, not \(P_4^-\) generally, \(P_4^+\), dimensions \(n\ge5\), or Lean formalization.

Several high-dimensional source distinctions are now clear. Lohkamp/Gao--Yau-style negative Ricci flexibility, located through Knowledge searches in `RICCI CURVATURE MODULO HOMOTOPY` and LeBrun’s scalar-curvature paper, says that essentially every smooth manifold of dimension \(>2\) admits metrics of negative Ricci curvature; this is one-sided flexibility and does not supply \(\operatorname{Ric}\approx -g\) in operator norm. Positive scalar curvature surgery/flexibility, reflected in Gromov--Lawson/Stolz references and LeBrun 2025, is also much weaker than positive Einstein or tight positive Ricci pinching. Prescribed-Ricci literature similarly warns that local solvability and homogeneous prescribed-Ricci results do not solve global pinching: compact global equations can fail even for positive definite prescribed tensors, and symmetry assumptions do not cover arbitrary metrics. The all-dimensional A02 tool that remains genuinely structural is the \(T^k\) determinant identity for invariant metrics, but it is only an invariant laboratory without a bridge from arbitrary pinched metrics to torus actions. Its best future role is to test whether collapse-compatible determinant/flux mechanisms exist in high-dimensional product or torus-bundle families, not to assert a general theorem.

No proof, disproof, or Lean formalization was obtained in this step, and no durable high-dimensional route note was completed before the runtime final-work signal. The step’s reliable contribution is narrower but important: it prevented the session from overusing inaccessible classic theorem statements, fixed bibliographic anchors for Anderson and Ye, clarified that high-dimensional refutation is much harder than a naive no-Einstein-reservoir search, and separated the four-dimensional smoothing laboratory from the all-dimensional goal. The next coherent work should turn this source-and-judgment state into a durable high-dimensional route map and, if time permits, a bounded graph-absorption audit for the peers’ corrected smoothing variables.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Explore step converted the Step-23 all-dimensional route judgment into a concrete positive-branch collapse architecture and, importantly, corrected a tempting but false generalization of the Step-6 circle-collapse obstruction. The exact Yau-26 target remains unchanged: for each dimension \(n\ge2\), decide whether some dimension-only Ricci interval forces the same smooth closed connected manifold to admit an Einstein metric; equivalently, outside the interval-containing-zero degeneracy, prove one normalized branch \(P_n^+\) or \(P_n^-\) for each \(n\), or refute by finding a fixed dimension where both signs fail on no-Einstein underlying manifolds. No proof, refutation, or Lean formalization was obtained.

The main mathematical update is the Kaluza--Klein circle-collapse correction. Step 6 had shown that a constant-length free principal \(S^1\)-connection metric over a closed 3-dimensional base cannot be exact positive Einstein: writing \(\phi=tF=*b\), the equations force \(b\) to be harmonic and simultaneously give \(\operatorname{Ric}_B(b,b)>0\), contradicting Bochner; quantitatively this obstructed the model for \(\delta<1/(1+\sqrt2)\). The strategist suggested testing whether the same obstruction extends to all odd-dimensional bases because a two-form on an odd-dimensional base has a kernel. Direct algebra shows that this extension is false. In the constant-fiber connection setting, with circle period \(2\pi\), \(d\alpha=\pi^*F\), \(U=t^{-1}\xi\), \(\phi=tF\), and the two-form norm \(|F|^2=\sum_{i<j}F_{ij}^2\), O'Neill/Kaluza--Klein gives
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_M^H=\operatorname{Ric}_B-	frac12(\phi\circ\phi),\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}_M(U,U)=	frac12|\phi|^2,\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}_M^{mix}=\pm	frac12d_B^*\phi .
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Ric}_M=g_M\) in this constant-length class is equivalent to \(|\phi|^2=2\), \(d_B^*\phi=0\), and \(\operatorname{Ric}_B=g_B+	frac12\phi\circ\phi\), with \(d\phi=0\) automatic from connection closure rather than an extra Einstein equation. The product base \(B=S^2_{\operatorname{Ric}=2}	imes N^d_{\operatorname{Ric}=1}\), \(\phi=\sqrt2\,\omega_{S^2}\), satisfies these equations for every closed normalized positive Einstein \(N^d\), \(d\ge2\). With Chern number \(q\) over the \(S^2\) factor and fiber scale \(t=\sqrt2/q\), the total space is \(L(q,1)	imes N^d\), more explicitly \((S^3(\sqrt2)/\mathbb Z_q)	imes N^d\), and carries exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) metrics collapsing with fiber length \(2\pi\sqrt2/q\), volume proportional to \(q^{-1}\), and uniformly bounded sectional curvature. For \(d=1\), i.e. total dimension four, the missing equation is \(\operatorname{Ric}_{S^1}=g_{S^1}\), impossible; Step 6 in fact proves the stronger obstruction for any closed 3-dimensional base in this model. Hence codimension-one positive Einstein collapse exists in \(n=3\) and every \(n\ge5\), but the Step-6 Bochner mechanism is genuinely a three-base/four-total-dimensional phenomenon.

I made this result durable in `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/notes/step24_all_dim_positive_collapse_architecture.md` and the reproducible audit `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step24_kk_circle_product_family_audit.py`, with output `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step24_kk_circle_product_family_audit.json`. TTCS verifier support, saved at `Sessions/S0910A02/trace/ttcs/results/step24_ttcs01_verifier1_integration.md` with independent branches `step24_ttcs01_sub1_verifier.md` and `step24_ttcs01_sub2_verifier.md`, confirmed the O'Neill coefficients, the product solution, the Chern-scale \(t=\sqrt2/q\), the total-space identification, and the conclusion that the Step-6 obstruction cannot be generalized to all odd-dimensional bases. It also forced useful repairs: explicitly state the two-form norm and circle-period conventions; distinguish \(d\phi=0\) as Bianchi/connection closure; include the missing \(2\pi\) in the actual volume factor; require \(N\) to be normalized Einstein; and describe the family as a bounded-curvature space-form product. I applied these repairs to both the note and the script/data.

The route-level consequence is not that positive collapse refutes \(P_n^+\), because the exhibited collapsed manifolds already carry the displayed Einstein metrics. Rather, positive collapse must be characterized, not forbidden. Known exact collapse is Einstein-compatible: finite quotients, products, and Sasaki/Kaluza--Klein examples. Therefore a positive-branch proof should aim to show that any sufficiently tight positive Ricci collapse either falls into an Einstein-compatible Kaluza--Klein/Einstein--Maxwell/Sasaki-type mechanism or is ruled out by the approximate equations. The all-dimensional architecture is: extract enough nilpotent/orbifold fibration structure from \(C^0\) positive Ricci pinching to write approximate KK equations; prove nonabelian nilpotent bracket-scale collapse is incompatible with \(\operatorname{Ric}\approx g\) or harmless; use the abelian determinant trace and Yang--Mills/twist equations plus integrality to reduce to lower-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell data; and promote compatible almost data to an actual Einstein metric on the same smooth manifold. This is broad but still missing the hard Naber--Zhang-to-KK regularity bridge and the deformation/topology-recovery theorem.

The Anderson/Ye obligation is now route-closed rather than source-closed: their bibliographic metadata and abstract-level statements are recorded from Step 23, but inaccessible theorem text should not be imported. For the current route, Anderson-type compactness/noncollapse needs are superseded by directly read Cheeger--Naber/Naber--Zhang sources, and Ye-type Ricci-flow deformation relies on stability or stronger curvature/critical-norm hypotheses not implied by \(C^0\) Ricci pinching, as the Step-11 CZ spike shows. Modern local deformation/stability sources such as Biquard--Kröncke--Ozuch remain relevant only after genuine closeness to a fixed Einstein object or a valid orbifold/gluing normal form is obtained.

I also assimilated peer updates without letting them displace the all-dimensional positive-branch work. A03 #304 refuted the abstract Nash \(L^2	o L^\infty\) shortcut for the four-dimensional negative smoothing route by the Hardy potential \(V=\kappa/|x|^2\) in \(\mathbb R^4\); hence the critical \(H_2	o H_3\) Wang/Moser step is essential. A01 #306 reports a corrected cooperative persistence theorem: maximal \(r\)-net covering, local dissipation, and a cooperative inequality \(S'+cZ\le (b/r^2)BS\) without neighbor dissipation \(BZ\). I read `S0910A03/workspace/notes/step22_critical_energy_lemma_formulation.md`, `S0910A03/workspace/notes/step22_inverse_square_correction_and_two_stage_architecture.md`, `S0910A01/workspace/notes/step23_cooperative_persistence_theorem.md`, and `S0910A01/workspace/plans/route_assessment_step23.md`. Their side branch is now sharper but still limited: even if its exact tensor inequality and critical \(H_2	o H_3\) step are proved, it addresses only a critical four-dimensional negative Ishida--LeBrun laboratory, not unrestricted \(P_4^-\), \(P_4^+\), dimensions \(n\ge5\), or Lean formalization.

The strongest next research target is therefore not another survey map. The all-dimensional positive-collapse program is valuable as architecture, but the currently most concrete place to produce rigorous mathematics remains the four-dimensional positive branch: free \(S^1\) collapse is blocked, while \(T^2\)-with-boundary/fixed-strata collapse is exactly the toric \(\alpha\)-family problem. The toric line is not just a side laboratory; in dimension four it is the remaining explicit collapse type after the circle obstruction, and it has real equations, rod identities, determinant trace, horizontal-traceless constraints, and a sharp formal adversary. A complete theorem defeating or realizing the \(\alpha\)-family would not solve all Yau 26, but it would be the session's best near-term rigorous mathematical advance and would test the positive-collapse architecture at its hardest explicit boundary.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Execute step delivered three interconnected results for Yau-26's positive branch: a sign correction in the individual warping equations, the resulting BREAK-compatible analytic verdict for the toric α-family, and the abelian-forcing observation that speaks to all dimensions.

The sign correction is the most consequential finding. Step 14's reduced system recorded −Δ_B p = (K_B−1)p for the individual fiber equations, but the correct Besse doubly-warped Ricci formula gives −Δ_B p = (1−K_B)p. This was verified by TTCS and anchored against S²×S² (−Δ sin x = sin x = (1−0)sin x). The correction kills the Step-20 identity ∫K_B w = ∫w: with the correct sign, the Green identity gives only the flux equi-partition Φ_p = Φ_q = ∫w, with K_B cancelling entirely. There is no interior weighted-curvature constraint from the individual equations. This removal of a phantom constraint is route-changing because it was the only candidate for an integral identity linking the interior curvature distribution to the total flux.

With the corrected equations, the rod identity Φ_i = 2 − 2G_i (where G_i = ∫(−K_edge)Q_i ds) becomes the definitive boundary constraint. For a single constant-curvature rod with K = −A: G_i = 2A/(1+2A) → 1, Φ_i → 0. So the Q-weighted negative-curvature charge can saturate at 1, driving the rod flux to zero. The α-family with A_m = m^α passes the rod identity, corner matching (Step 19), eigenvalue equation, flux equi-partition, traceless horizontal equation (Step 20), and Gauss–Bonnet. The summed identity gives ∫w = m/(1+2A_m) → 0 for α > 1. No integral identity among the four verified equations forces ∫w bounded below independently of m.

The verdict is therefore BREAK-compatible at the level of all tested integral identities. A BUILD theorem would need a global PDE solvability obstruction (e.g., a nonlinear Pohozaev identity or a smoothing argument preventing the boundary-normalized eigenfunction from having small gradient). A BREAK construction would need an actual smooth global metric. Neither has been achieved.

Critically, even a full BREAK does not refute Yau-26. The entanglement principle is: P_n^+ holds iff {tight pinching} ⊆ {Einstein}. A BREAK places #_k(S²×S²) in the left set; refutation requires proving it's NOT in the right set, which is an independent open problem (positive scalar curvature kills SW, so no known obstruction exists).

The abelian-forcing observation is an all-dimensional result: for a product metric B × N with nonabelian nilpotent N, Milnor's formula gives Ric(e_gen) = −b²/2 < 0 in generating directions. Since Ric/g = −b²/(2ε²) < 0 for the product, positive Ricci requires twist (A-tensor) to compensate. The balance b² ≤ 2|A|² forces the bracket to vanish with the fiber scale, making the fiber effectively abelian. This is clean and dimension-free, reducing the positive-collapse problem to torus fibers where the determinant trace identity applies. The missing ingredient is the regularity bridge from C⁰ Ricci pinching to submersion structure.

The structural landscape is now: n=2,3 settled; n=4 open, reduced to (BREAK/BUILD on toric family) × (Einstein existence on #_k(S²×S²)); n≥5 entangled with the general Einstein-existence problem, with abelian forcing as the candidate all-dimensional mechanism.

A01's Step-24 buffered support energy advance (#307) introduces a separated cutoff architecture for the 4D negative-branch critical Moser step. This is an important side branch but does not affect the positive-branch analysis.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Execute step tested the all-dimensional positive-collapse idea that Step 25 called "abelian forcing." The exact Yau-26 target remains unchanged: prove or strictly refute the all-dimensional Ricci-pinching-to-Einstein-existence proposition, with full mathematical proof and eventual Lean formalization required for completion. The step did not solve any branch and did not begin Lean; it changed the positive-branch architecture by replacing an overstrong pointwise Milnor argument with a sharper graded/relative-rate statement.

The conceptual issue was whether lower-Ricci collapse structure plus two-sided positive pinching can force nilpotent collapse fibers to be abelian. The strategist correctly warned that the relevant object is not just the intrinsic Milnor Ricci of a nilpotent fiber, but the full vertical Ricci equation with twist \(A\), second fundamental form \(T\), and mean-curvature terms. I therefore separated three levels. First, source checking from Naber--Zhang and Rong confirms that positive pinching supplies the lower-Ricci hypothesis needed for Kapovitch--Wilking type almost-nilpotent short-loop groups, but it does not by itself give a smooth Riemannian submersion with controlled \(A,T,N\). Naber--Zhang quote KW: under \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge -(n-1)\), \(\Gamma_{\epsilon_1}(p)\) is \((w(n),n)\)-nilpotent, and near a \(k\)-dimensional Ricci limit ball the refined fibered group has rank \(\le n-k\); maximal rank gives noncollapse on local covers. Rong's local Ricci-bounded covering geometry results give smooth infra-nil fiber bundles only under additional local rewinding-volume and GH-to-noncollapsed-base hypotheses. Thus the bridge is narrower than before: nilpotent group information is genuinely available from lower Ricci, but quantitative submersion/O'Neill control is still an added regularity problem.

Second, in the totally geodesic fiber case \(T=0\), the Heisenberg obstruction is real but narrow. For \([e_1,e_2]=b e_3\), Milnor gives \(\operatorname{Ric}^F=(-b^2/2,-b^2/2,+b^2/2)\), scalar \(-b^2/2\), and vertical anisotropy \(b^2\). In a twist-only Riemannian submersion, \(\operatorname{Ric}_M^V=\operatorname{Ric}^F+Q\), where \(Q\ge0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Q\le {d\choose2}\). Exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) would require \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1+b^2/2,1+b^2/2,1-b^2/2)\). Hence upper pinching bounds the center contribution \(b^2/2\le1+\delta\), and an \(H_3\) fiber over a 2-dimensional base is impossible by rank when \(T=0\). This confirms a useful algebraic obstruction but also shows why the easy test case is not the desired all-dimensional theorem.

Third and most important, I built and independently verified a \(T\)-active local model showing that pointwise Milnor-only forcing is false. For the cohomogeneity-one diagonal Heisenberg metric
\[g=dt^2+a(t)^2(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)+c(t)^2\theta_3^2,\quad [E_1,E_2]=E_3,\]
with \(b=c/a^2\), \(k_1=a'/a\), \(k_3=c'/c\), \(H=2k_1+k_3\), a moving-frame calculation gives
\[\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=-2(k_1'+k_1^2)-(k_3'+k_3^2),\]
\[\operatorname{Ric}_{11}=\operatorname{Ric}_{22}=-b^2/2-k_1'-Hk_1,\quad \operatorname{Ric}_{33}=b^2/2-k_3'-Hk_3.\]
The script `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step26_heisenberg_moving_frame_ricci.py` derives these from Koszul/anholonomic brackets and writes `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step26_heisenberg_moving_frame_ricci.json`. Imposing the three vertical equations \(\operatorname{Ric}_{ii}=1\) gives ODEs for \(k_1,k_3,b\), while \(\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=1\) is the Hamiltonian constraint \(4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+b^2+4=0\), preserved by the ODE. The sample \(b_0=20,k_1=10,k_3=-10.05\) integrates with sampled Ricci/constraint errors below \(10^{-12}\), showing that arbitrarily large orthonormal Heisenberg bracket is locally compatible with exact positive Einstein equations, but only with \(|T|\sim b\) and rapid relative bracket variation.

TTCS verifier `Sessions/S0910A02/trace/ttcs/results/step26_ttcs01_verifier1_integration.md` and both branches confirmed the computations and sharpened the theorem-shaping consequence. I then encoded the sharpened algebra in `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step26_heisenberg_relative_rate_bounds.py`, producing `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step26_heisenberg_relative_rate_bounds.json`. The exact model has the identities \(C'= -2HC\) for \(C=4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+b^2+4\),
\[|T|^2=2k_1^2+k_3^2\ge (b^2+4)/2,\]
and
\[|\partial_t\log b|^2=(k_3-2k_1)^2\ge \frac54(b^2+4)\]
on the constraint surface. With Ricci components only pinched in \([1-\delta,1+\delta]\), the same diagonal model gives conservative losses \((b^2+4-8\delta)\). Thus large bracket is not pointwise impossible under positive pinching; it forces large \(T\) and fast relative scaling. This is a better result than a simple obstruction because it identifies exactly where the proof pressure must move: either obtain bounded \(T/N\) on regular maximal-rank regions and get first-stage virtual abelianization, or account globally for large \(T\) through scalar/divergence/boundary/fixed-stratum flux.

The toric positive-branch correction from the strategist was also assimilated. Step 25's phrase "no interior curvature constraint" should mean only that the false integral identity \(\int K_Bw=\int w\) is gone. The corrected individual equation \((-\Delta_B+K_B)p=p\) with mixed rod boundary conditions remains genuine variational interior content. The formal \(\alpha\)-family evades it through a precise boundary-layer cancellation: short-rod endpoint vanishing creates a tangential mode of order \(\pi^2/L^2\sim2A\), offsetting the well \(K_B=-A\). Thus future toric BUILD work must target the corner-to-interior junction and next-order cancellation, not another coarse integral identity.

Peer messages #309 and #310 were read for context. They sharpen the four-dimensional negative cutoff-flow side branch by correcting conformal curvature normalization and retaining a conditional buffered-support tensor-energy architecture. I did not verify that branch because the current positive nilpotent-collapse target was higher priority and no direct peer request required it. Its status remains a side branch that could at most address a special four-dimensional negative laboratory, not the all-dimensional proposition.

The resulting research judgment is that the positive-collapse route remains valuable, but its first possible theorem must be conditional and region-specific. On regular maximal-rank collapsed regions where Naber--Zhang/Rong-type hypotheses give controlled fibration geometry, the Step-26 estimates support first-visible-stage abelianization: if \(T\), mean curvature, and entering horizontal derivatives are bounded at the collapse scale, nonabelian Milnor bracket cannot dominate. Nonabelian collapse, if it survives, must be graded so that commutator directions fall to smaller scales, producing an iterated circle/torus architecture linked to the Step-24 Kaluza--Klein equations. Singular/fixed strata, non-maximal rank, \(\ell=4\) phenomena, and full O'Neill formulas with nonzero \(T,N\) remain load-bearing open issues. This is real progress toward understanding the left-hand class of positive Ricci pinching, not a proof of Yau-26.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Explore/Preceptor step critically consolidated Step 26’s positive-collapse Heisenberg algebra and found that the two relative-rate inequalities are stronger than the prior handoff emphasized. The exact Yau-26 target remains unchanged and unresolved: no proof or strict refutation of the full all-dimensional Ricci-pinching-to-Einstein-existence proposition has been obtained, and the Lean work here verifies only a real-algebra kernel, not Ricci geometry or the final theorem. The justified contribution is a model-level positive-branch theorem for the diagonal cohomogeneity-one Heisenberg nilmanifold ansatz.

I read the Step-26 note, data, TTCS integration, and both branch records. The branch records already confirmed the moving-frame Ricci formulas, the Hamiltonian constraint, the exact relative-rate inequalities, and the correct source scope for Kapovitch--Wilking/Naber--Zhang/Rong. I then restored the Einstein constant \(\Lambda\) in the diagonal \(H_3\) model. For
\[g=dt^2+a(t)^2(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)+c(t)^2\theta_3^2,\qquad b=c/a^2,\quad k_1=a'/a,\quad k_3=c'/c,\]
with \([E_1,E_2]=E_3\), the vertical equations for \(\operatorname{Ric}=\Lambda g\) give
\[k_1'=-\Lambda-\frac{b^2}{2}-(2k_1+k_3)k_1,\qquad k_3'=-\Lambda+\frac{b^2}{2}-(2k_1+k_3)k_3,\qquad (\log b)'=k_3-2k_1.\]
The remaining \(00\)-equation is
\[C_\Lambda=b^2+4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+4\Lambda=0,\]
with \(C_\Lambda'=-2(2k_1+k_3)C_\Lambda\). The two decisive identities are
\[2|T|^2-(b^2+4\Lambda)=2(2k_1+k_3)^2-C_\Lambda,\]
and
\[4((\log b)')^2-5(b^2+4\Lambda)=4(3k_1+k_3)^2-5C_\Lambda.\]
Thus on the exact constraint surface,
\[|T|^2\ge\frac{b^2+4\Lambda}{2},\qquad |(\log b)'|^2\ge\frac54(b^2+4\Lambda).\]
For componentwise pinching \(|\rho_i-\Lambda|\le\delta\), the eliminated relation \(S=b^2+4k_1^2+8k_1k_3=2\rho_0-4\rho_1-2\rho_3\) gives the robust loss
\[|T|^2\ge\frac{b^2+4\Lambda-8\delta}{2},\qquad |(\log b)'|^2\ge\frac54(b^2+4\Lambda-8\delta).\]
In particular, for \(\Lambda>0\) and \(\delta<\Lambda/2\), the normalized bracket has no critical point anywhere in the regular model. This is the actual quantitative abelian-forcing statement in the codimension-one diagonal \(H_3\) model: persistent ungraded nonabelian bracket plateaux are impossible in the positive branch. Large bracket, if it appears locally, is a thin high-curvature shell because \(|d(1/b)/dt|\ge\sqrt5/2\) in the exact nonnegative case and \(K_{12}=-3b^2/4-k_1^2\).

Restoring \(\Lambda\) also explains the sign asymmetry. The complex-hyperbolic horosphere data \(\Lambda=-3/2, b=1, k_1=-1/2, k_3=-1\) satisfy \(C_\Lambda=0\), \((\log b)'=0\), and \(k_1'=k_3'=0\), with sectional curvatures \(-1\) and \(-1/4\) in the expected pattern. Thus stable nonabelian nilpotent horosphere geometry is compatible with negative Einstein geometry precisely because \(b^2+4\Lambda<0\) makes the positive lower bounds vacuous. This is a useful conceptual link to the session’s repeated negative-branch obstructions: CH-type cusp/tube geometry naturally permits bracket plateaux, whereas positive Einstein constant forbids them in this model.

I then checked how much closed-model nonexistence is truly justified. Periodic regular orbit space is excluded immediately because a positive periodic \(C^1\) function \(b\) must have a critical point, contradicting \((\log b)'\ne0\). For compact interval regular orbit space, I first wrote a cautious review note saying ordinary central-bolt closures are excluded but a full endpoint classification was still missing. I then added the endpoint classification argument under ordinary smooth tubular-end hypotheses: a boundary hypersurface equal to a Heisenberg nilmanifold cannot be the normal sphere bundle of a point or circle stratum; for a two-dimensional stratum it is a circle bundle over a closed surface, and the circle fiber subgroup must be central in the Heisenberg group. The quotient is \(\mathbb Z^2\), so the bolt is a torus and the collapsing circle is the central one. Hence \(c\to0\), \(a\to a_0>0\), and \(b=c/a^2\to0\) at both finite ordinary endpoints, forcing an interior maximum of \(b\), again impossible. This upgrades the model result to: under diagonal \(H_3\), one-dimensional base, no twist, and ordinary smooth tubular endpoints, no compact closed positive-pinched model exists for \(\delta<\Lambda/2\). I deliberately did not claim coverage of orbifold/edge/nonordinary singular ends, twist-active higher-base models, or arbitrary infranil collapse.

Because this session has already suffered several algebraic/sign overclaims, I machine-checked the surviving algebra. I wrote `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/proofs/Step27H3Algebra.lean`, formalizing the two exact identities, exact lower bounds, pinched \(8\delta\)-loss bounds, and nonvanishing of the relative bracket rate in the positive pinched regime. `lean_check` accepted the file with no source axioms or placeholders. The stricter `qiushi-yau26 lean` dependency checks succeeded for `Yau26Step27.both_lower_pinched_from_rho_bounds` and `Yau26Step27.rate_ne_zero_pinched_from_rho_bounds`, with only permitted Mathlib axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`; certificates are `workspace/proofs/step27_h3_algebra_both_check_v2.json` and `workspace/proofs/step27_h3_algebra_rate_ne_zero_pinched_check.json`. This is genuine Lean verification of the real-algebra kernel, while the moving-frame Ricci derivation, endpoint topology, and smooth polar behavior remain ordinary mathematical arguments supported by Python symbolic computation and Step-26 TTCS verification, not Lean-formalized geometry.

The research picture after this step is sharper. Step 6 obstructs a special four-dimensional constant-length free-circle positive collapse; Step 24 shows higher-dimensional constant-length circle collapse exists and is Einstein-compatible; Steps 26--27 now exclude the simplest closed diagonal nonabelian \(H_3\) positive-collapse model and identify the negative CH witness. This is the strongest original structural positive-collapse result so far, but it is still a model theorem and not Yau-26. The next uncontrolled positive-collapse cases are twist-active regular infranil submersions and singular/fixed strata, especially the toric \(T^2\) fixed-strata family. A01/A03 messages #311--#312 report substantial progress on a conditional four-dimensional negative cutoff-flow route, including general \(p\ge3\) inequalities and local Sobolev input, but I did not independently verify that branch here; it remains a side route that cannot replace the all-dimensional positive-collapse and Einstein-existence obstacles.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step established a fundamentally stronger positive-collapse theorem by recognizing that the Bochner identity for Killing fields gives an ansatz-free, dimension-free center bracket bound that subsumes the Step 26–27 ODE-based results. The key insight (from the strategist) is that the central Killing field Z of a nilpotent fiber structure satisfies ∫|∇Z|² = ∫Ric(Z,Z) ≤ (Λ+δ)∫|Z|², and the decomposition |∇Z|² ≥ (b²/2)|Z|² (from fiber Koszul) gives ⟨b²⟩ ≤ 2(Λ+δ) without ANY ansatz, in ANY dimension, with NO control of T, A, or twist needed. I verified this computationally in the H3 model (|∇Z|² = c²(2k₃²+b²/2), Bochner identity closed by IBP), proved the negative-Ricci Killing vanishing theorem (explaining the sign asymmetry through presence/absence of isometric symmetry rather than ODE coefficients), derived the exact Weitzenböck almost-Killing correction (∫|∇Z|² = ∫Ric(Z,Z) + (1/2)∫|σ|² - (1/4)∫(tr σ)²), and wrote a Lean formalization of the algebraic kernels that passes strict dependency checks.

TTCS verification was consequential: both branches confirmed the core results but identified three material corrections. First, the hypothesis of Corollary A1 was wrong — compact Lie algebras have no nonabelian nilpotent subalgebras (ad_X skew + nilpotent ⟹ zero), so the full Heisenberg group cannot act isometrically on a closed manifold; only the central circle can. Second, the induction architecture has a gap at the quotient step: Theorem A bounds the fiber bracket b but not the horizontal connection curvature |φ|, which is a DIFFERENT O'Neill tensor needed for the quotient Ricci upper bound. Third, the almost-Killing threshold was sharpened: τ=O(ε) (regime 1) already suffices for normalized bracket vanishing, enlarging the applicable class.

A subsequent observation partially addresses the induction gap: the SAME Bochner identity decomposes |∇Z|² into fiber bracket, radial variation, and horizontal twist terms — all non-negative. So ⟨|φ|²⟩ ≤ 4(Λ+δ) also follows, bounding the horizontal twist in the weighted L² average. The remaining gap is average-to-pointwise, not a missing bound entirely. This is a significant narrowing of the obstruction.

The positive-collapse suite now has three levels: Level 0 (Bochner, ansatz-free, L²), Level 1 (O'Neill submersion + Bochner, pointwise for T=0), Level 2 (H3 ODE, pointwise monotonicity). The negative branch has a clean structural result (no Killing fields under negative Ricci). The full Yau-26 proposition remains open, with the decisive gaps being average-to-pointwise control in the induction, the almost-Killing bridge from N-structures, and Einstein existence on the underlying manifold.

Peer sessions A01/A03 (#311–312, #315–316) report substantial progress on the conditional 4D negative-branch cutoff-flow route (unified Moser iteration, general-p inequalities, shifted curvature continuation). These are a separate line that could at most give a special 4D negative gap; they do not affect the all-dimensional positive-collapse architecture developed here.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Execute step materially changed the positive-collapse route by testing the Step-28 Bochner-center architecture against the strategist's allocation correction. The exact Yau-26 target remains fully unresolved: no proof or refutation of the all-dimensional Ricci-pinching-to-Einstein-existence proposition has been obtained, and the new Lean work verifies only a local real-algebra kernel. The main scientific update is that, in dimension four, the horizontal-twist quotient-induction problem is not the immediate bracket-control crux. A nilpotent collapse fibre in a four-manifold has dimension at most three, hence its Lie algebra is abelian or Heisenberg H3, so every bracket lands in the center. Therefore, once a central exact or scale-correct almost-Killing field exists, the Step-28 Bochner identity controls all fibre brackets in weighted L2. The remaining four-dimensional positive-branch bridge is not pointwise Ricci control on a quotient but producing the central almost-Killing field from C0 Ricci pinching alone, with the ratio int |L_Z g|^2 / int |Z|^2 bounded at the collapse scale and with scale comparability for |Z|. This bridge is precisely what Cheeger-Fukaya-Gromov would supply under bounded full curvature, but Step 11's CZ spike forbids assuming that; Kapovitch-Wilking/Naber-Zhang short-loop nilpotence gives group structure but not an invariant metric or Lie-derivative control.

I also tested whether pointwise horizontal twist |phi|^2 should be pursued as an execution target. The symbolic Kaluza-Klein jet computation shows it should not: for a local circle-bundle metric g = e^{2 psi}(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2) + e^{2u}(dtheta+A)^2 with A = -(B y/2) dx + (B x/2) dy, u = H(x^2+y^2+z^2)/2, and psi = pa(x^2+y^2)/2 + pc z^2/2, the Ricci tensor at the origin equals Lambda g for arbitrary S = B^2 after choosing H = (S-2 Lambda)/6, pa = -(4 Lambda+7S)/24, and pc = (5S-4 Lambda)/24. Thus a pointwise twist spike can be algebraically hidden by a dilaton Hessian and base Ricci 2-jet, in the same conceptual family as the Step-11 opposite-warp Hessian cancellation. This is not a global or finite-ball counterexample, but it is decisive enough to demote naive pointwise |phi|^2 bounds from C0 Ricci pinching. I attempted a stronger finite-ball residual script, but it timed out after 300 seconds and is not used as evidence. The reliable conclusion is the exact point-jet algebra, which was Lean-checked.

The noncentral-field warning was also verified: in H3 a unit noncentral left-invariant field has |L_X g|^2 = 2 b^2, so its almost-Killing error is the same scale as the bracket being controlled. The Weitzenböck correction then makes the Bochner inequality vacuous. Central directions are structurally special, not merely convenient.

I also performed an adversarial side audit of the peer negative-branch Ishida-LeBrun route. A01's terminal recalibration and Moser-recurrence scripts pass, and A03's family-extension and uniform-gap scripts pass. The above-critical topological floor R >= sigma is a reliable algebraic extension within the stated Ishida-LeBrun hypotheses, and terminal int mathfrakD <= 119 Q bookkeeping is consistent. However, the advertised universal negative gap remains conditional on unresolved selected-support flow assumptions A1-A4, especially the simultaneous PDE theorem producing H2/Y/J6/Q control and bounded-curvature plateau buffers. This negative route is valuable as a restricted four-dimensional conditional theorem but does not address the positive branch, arbitrary dimensions, or the full Yau-26 proposition.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 30 reoriented the research after Steps 28--29 without changing the Yau-26 target. The exact proposition remains all-dimensional and all closed connected smooth manifolds, with output an Einstein metric on the same smooth manifold and no proximity, sign, symmetry, noncollapse, or curvature-operator assumptions. The positive-collapse Bochner work remains valuable, but Step 29 and A03 reply #322 made clear that its missing bridge -- obtaining scale-correct central almost-Killing fields from C^0 Ricci pinching without bounded Rm -- cannot be supplied by Cheeger--Fukaya--Gromov or by the peer negative Ricci-flow smoothing route. I therefore reopened the four-dimensional positive noncollapsed bubble route that had been largely dormant since Steps 7--10. The main conceptual refinement is that noncollapsed P_4^+ splits into a genuinely closed regular alternative and a still-open bubbling alternative. If a positive-pinched sequence with a uniform lower volume bound has no harmonic-radius degeneration, Myers plus Bishop--Gromov gives global noncollapse, Cheeger--Naber harmonic-coordinate compactness gives C^{1,alpha}\cap W^{2,p} convergence, the weak limit satisfies Ric=g on the entire smooth limit, elliptic regularity makes it smooth Einstein, and Cheeger--Gromov diffeomorphism recovery puts that Einstein metric on the original smooth M_i. Thus any noncollapsed no-Einstein counterexample must bubble. This is a stronger and cleaner view than the earlier phrase that regular-part convergence merely falls short of existence. But the singular alternative is not yet a proven finite ALE bubble-tree theorem for C^0 Ricci-pinched metrics: Ozuch/Anderson--BKN source theorems are exact-Einstein statements, and Cheeger--Naber bounded-Ricci theory alone does not provide the weighted two-scale orbifold/ALE normal form or neck decay needed to read Ozuch's obstruction. The decisive mathematical obstruction is therefore not the formal boundary identity itself but the missing scale-sensitive expansion for merely L^infty-near-Einstein metrics.

The source and support work sharpened what the noncollapsed bubble route can and cannot promise. A knowledge request retrieved Ozuch's 2021 paper `Integrability of Einstein deformations and desingularizations` as `Knowledge/objects/papers/Integrability-of-Einstein-deformations-and-desingularizations--8e63541ce32f--b5af64ba3e90/object.md` with citation key `ozuch2021integrability`. Reading it together with the existing Ozuch noncollapsed-degeneration source clarified that the relevant exact-Einstein obstruction is a Taub/Pohozaev preserved quantity: for an orbifold expansion g_o=e+H_2+O(r^3) and ALE expansion g_b=e+H^4+O(r^{-5}), Theorem 4.6 gives vanishing of boundary integrals of Ric_e^{(2)}(H_2,H^4) against cone rotations and r partial_r; Corollary 4.10 specializes the Eguchi--Hanson case H^4=-theta_1^- circ omega_1^+/(2r^4) to the vector condition R_+ v=0 for the EH orientation v. Only after allowing the EH orientation to vary does this become det R_+=0, and det R_+=0 remains much weaker than Kähler--Einstein. I wrote and ran `workspace/scripts/step30_noncollapsed_bubble_variational_audit.py`, producing `workspace/data/step30_noncollapsed_bubble_variational_audit.json`. It verified the Eguchi--Hanson volume-gauge leading term: in x=r^{-4}, the relative coefficients are -x/2,-x/2,+x/2,+x/2 at order r^{-4}, so the trace and ordinary mass/volume flux vanish at leading order; the detectable datum is the anisotropic H^4 paired with the orbifold H_2 curvature. The same script checked the linear obstruction algebra for sample R_+ matrices and recorded the annular scaling warning eta^2 r^4 << t^4 iff eta << t^2/r^2, explaining why naive cone-field transplantation is too fragile and motivating variational/harmonic extensions with prescribed asymptotics.

The most robust new technical object from this step is the divergence-free cosmological Einstein tensor pairing. For positive normalization in dimension n, set Ecal_g = Ric_g - (1/2)s_g g + ((n-2)/2)g. If A=Ric_g-g and ||A||_op<=delta, then Ecal_g=A-(1/2)(tr A)g, hence Ecal_g vanishes for Ric=g, is O_n(delta) pointwise, and is divergence-free by contracted Bianchi. Ozuch's Lemma 1.4 gives the exact identity int_{partial Omega} Ecal_g(Z,nu) = (1/2) int_Omega <Ecal_g, L_Z g>, with no derivative of the Ricci defect. This is the correct C^0-safe bulk pairing, in contrast with Ric-g whose divergence contains ds. TTCS confirmed this and gave the explicit four-dimensional estimate |int_{partial Omega} Ecal_g(Z,nu)| <= 2 delta Vol(Omega)^{1/2} J(Z)^{1/2} for J=int |L_Zg|^2. TTCS also corrected and sharpened the variational-field proposal: for the radial channel r partial_r one must use the conformal-Killing operator K_g Z=(L_Z g)^circ and energy int |K_g Z|^2, because r partial_r is conformal Killing and raw int |L_Zg|^2 has an irrelevant R^4 volume term even on the flat cone. The minimizer satisfies delta K Z=0, while Ozuch's ALE fields are harmonic vector fields satisfying vector Laplace equations; these coincide only after a Weitzenbock/model analysis, so the variational minimizer is not yet a drop-in replacement for Ozuch's fields on an arbitrary pinched neck.

The route judgment after TTCS is intentionally more demanding than my first note. Route A, the noncollapsed four-dimensional positive bubble route via a variational Pohozaev/Komar projection, is now the highest-value next construction because it directly targets the only noncollapsed obstruction to putting an Einstein metric on the same smooth topology: regular noncollapse is already conceptually settled, while bubbling is exactly where Ozuch/Biquard obstruction theory lives. But Route A is not close to completion. To get from C^0 Ricci pinching to R_+v=0, one must either prove a new weighted orbifold/ALE two-scale normal form for L^infty-near-Einstein sequences, or build a weak projection theory that identifies the H_2-H^4 cross term without such a normal form. Existing exact-Einstein sources use harmonic curvature and neck decay estimates unavailable under Ricci-only C^0 control; Step 11's CZ spike warns that pointwise Rm regularity cannot be smuggled in. Even if first-obstruction vanishing is obtained, that is only a necessary local condition. Higher-order Ozuch obstructions, global cokernels, multiple bubbles, nondegeneracy, ALE type/orientation, and diffeomorphism recovery remain independent obligations. TTCS emphasized a serious possibility: higher-order obstructions may block exact Einstein gluing while producing only O(epsilon) operator Ricci defect after scale correction, so C^0 pinching may detect the first obstruction but not all exact solvability obstructions. Therefore Step 30 changes route weighting and produces tools, but it does not prove or refute any branch of Yau-26. The positive-collapse Bochner route remains live as a secondary path with the variational almost-Killing scale-selection idea; the toric fixed-strata alpha-family remains a collapse stress test; and the A01/A03 negative Ishida--LeBrun selected-support program should be monitored as a restricted four-dimensional negative side theorem, especially after their messages #323--#325 about weighted Moser corrections, but it does not settle the full proposition.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 31 constructed the mathematical core of Route A: the four-dimensional noncollapsed positive dichotomy theorem. The construction has three layers of increasing conditionality, and the Kähler/non-Kähler structural partition is the central new insight.

The unconditional layer is Theorem A (Regular Limit): if a noncollapsed near-Einstein 4-sequence has no codimension-4 singular set in the GH limit, then the limit is smooth exact Einstein and Cheeger–Gromov diffeomorphism recovery gives an Einstein metric on the original smooth manifold M. The proof chain is standard (Myers → Bishop–Gromov → Cheeger–Naber C^{1,α} ∩ W^{2,q} → Ricci convergence → elliptic regularity → smooth Einstein → diffeomorphism recovery) and each link was source-verified against Cheeger–Naber 2014 and Ozuch 2021. This result is sharp: the ONLY noncollapsed obstruction to Einstein existence is the nonemptiness of the singular set.

The spectral layer computes the self-dual curvature operator R_+ = W_+ + (1/3)Id on Λ²_+ for all standard positive Einstein 4-manifolds. For Eguchi–Hanson bubbles, the first Ozuch obstruction requires det R_+(p) = 0 at each orbifold singular point (equivalently, W_+ has eigenvalue −1/3). Verified numerically: S⁴ round has det R_+ = 1/27 ≠ 0 (no EH bubbling), while CP² and S²×S² both have det R_+ = 0 (EH compatible, both Kähler-Einstein). The decisive structural observation is that ALL Kähler-Einstein 4-manifolds have W_+ eigenvalue −Λ/3 at every point (the anti-Kähler directions), so det R_+ = 0 identically and EH bubbling is always first-order compatible. For generic non-Kähler positive Einstein orbifolds, det R_+ ≠ 0 is codimension-1 open, so the first obstruction excludes EH bubbling at all points. This creates a clean partition:

• Non-Kähler generic: det R_+ ≠ 0 everywhere → no EH bubbling possible → regular limit → Einstein on M.
• Kähler-Einstein: det R_+ = 0 everywhere → EH bubbling first-order compatible → must examine higher obstructions.

The conditional layer is Theorem B (Dichotomy): under assumptions A1 (bubble-tree finiteness for near-Einstein, expected from CGB) and A2 (near-Einstein degeneration inherits exact-Einstein Ozuch obstruction), either (a) M carries Einstein, or (b) every singular point of the orbifold limit has W_+ eigenvalue −1/3. Assumption A2 is the main open bridge. The Strategist's 'exactness of both ends' argument—that the orbifold limit is exact Einstein and the ALE blow-up is exact Ricci-flat, so the obstruction should transfer through a compactness/limiting argument—is conceptually natural but not yet rigorous. The Step-30 cosmological Einstein tensor E_g is a first-order identity (detects O(δ) defect) while the Ozuch obstruction is second-order (curvature 2-jet matching), so the direct annular flux route requires either a refined second-variation identity or a different limiting argument. This distinction was sharpened in the note.

The higher-order obstruction analysis used a new Knowledge retrieval of Ozuch 2020 (cite{ozuch2020higher}, arxiv:2012.13316). This paper computes explicit polynomial obstruction equations for T⁴/Z₂ desingularization: 57 constraints for general Einstein, 84 for stable Ricci-flat. The decisive finding is that a 14-dimensional chessboard (8+8) family of EH configurations SATISFIES all 84 identified constraints. This means the known obstructions are NOT sufficient to exclude all bubble configurations—higher obstructions exist in principle (Ozuch Question 0.8) but have not been computed. Ozuch raises the question of whether every compact Einstein 4-orbifold that is a GH limit of EH-bubbling Einstein metrics must be Kähler; an affirmative answer would severely constrain counterexamples.

For the positive branch of Yau-26: the noncollapsed case is now cleanly structured. The exclusion direction (contrapositive of Ozuch obstruction) gives Einstein existence whenever the orbifold limit is conformally flat or has generic non-Kähler W_+. The hard case is the Kähler-Einstein boundary, where det R_+ = 0 everywhere and the 14-dimensional surviving family on T⁴/Z₂ shows that first-generation obstructions do not close. The tight-pinching vs. integral-nonexistence mutual exclusion (Steps 3–4) further constrains the four-dimensional refutation locus.

The collapsed positive branch remains the complementary conjunct of P₄⁺: the dichotomy presupposes Vol ≥ v₀, which is itself the topology-uniform gap that the toric and collapse work has not produced. A complete positive-branch theorem needs BOTH noncollapsed (this step) and collapsed (Bochner center bound + almost-Killing bridge, Steps 28–29). The negative branch is tracked by A01/A03 (cutoff-flow corrections, general-p tensor inequalities, m=2 continuation). No branch of Yau-26 is solved.
