## Deep-Reasoning

This step corrected the representation-theoretic foundation of the current positive-branch Gate 1/Gate 3 program. The global Yau--26 target remains unchanged and unresolved: dimensions 2 and 3 are ordinary-theorem settled but not Lean-formalized, dimension 4 has crossing/zero intervals refuted while strict positive and strict negative branches remain open, and no dimension n>=5 refutation or proof is available. The current local four-dimensional positive line is not a proof or refutation of Yau--26; it is a controlled test of whether mixed Eguchi--Hanson resolutions of the product Einstein orbifold can be exact Einstein desingularizations, or are locally obstructed. Its value lies in sharpening the obstruction calculus and preventing false coefficient stories from contaminating the main problem.

The Step 94 conclusion that the local second obstruction on the product rank-one kernel vanishes is mathematically plausible, but the proof language was faulty where it tried to infer vanishing of the full projected local O(t^2) vector from SO(2) transitivity. A projected obstruction is not a fixed vector in K; it is an equivariant homogeneous map K -> K, and maps such as z -> f(|z|)z can be equivariant. The correct reason is weight-theoretic. For the product orbifold, independent rotations of the two sphere factors form a T^2 stabilizer fixing all four A1 nodes simultaneously. In the chiral two-form bases, omega_1^+ and omega_1^- are invariant and are exactly the rank-one R^\pm eigenlines, while K^+ = (omega_1^+)^\perp has weight alpha+beta and K^- = (omega_1^-)^\perp has weight alpha-beta. The beta=0 subcircle acts with ordinary weight one on every kernel plane. A homogeneous quadratic local map K_j -> K_j would require a monomial z^a \bar z^b with a+b=2 and a-b=1 under this subcircle, which is impossible. This repairs Gate 1 without relying on the invalid SO(2) sentence and also identifies the genuine structural content: rank-one bi-Kaehler curvature gives a two-dimensional kernel, so after an EH parameter zeta consumes one kernel direction the complementary block still contains another kernel direction. A generic det R=0 orbifold with one-dimensional kernel would not have this protection; the second obstruction would normally bite.

The same T^2 audit gives a useful finite-dimensional selection rule before any Green function is evaluated. A pair term is linear in the receiver variable and quadratic in the source variable. With source weight w_i=(1,epsilon_i) and receiver weight w_j=(1,epsilon_j), the only T^2-balanced monomials of degree two in z_i,\bar z_i and degree one in z_j,\bar z_j with target weight w_j are |z_i|^2 z_j for every pair, and z_i^2 \bar z_j only when epsilon_i=epsilon_j. Thus opposite-chirality pair response is necessarily isotropic on the receiver kernel plane; there is no angular transversality question for an opposite pair by itself. Same-chirality pair response may have both isotropic and anisotropic components. This turns A01's observed SO(2)-isotropic odd receiver into a derived selection rule, not an unexplained numerical feature. For the diagonal balanced pattern each node sees two opposite-chirality adjacent neighbours and one same-chirality diagonal neighbour. Compared against the all-compatible pattern, the diagonal same-chirality term is common and cancels; the mixed-minus-compatible difference at equal scales and unit source norms is controlled by two adjacent coefficient differences. In notation, the reduced local pair target is of the form 2(B_adj^opp - B_adj^same) on the isotropic part, with possible same-adjacent anisotropic subtraction only if the all-compatible identity does not separately kill it. This narrows Gate 3 from a four-node Green table to adjacent-pair coefficients plus the global coupling filter.

The r=0 all-compatible row must be used carefully. The strategist's stronger claim is that there is an exact curve of positive Kaehler--Einstein degree-4 del Pezzo metrics degenerating to the four-A1 product quotient, not merely that the smooth diffeotype CP^2#5\bar{CP}^2 admits some positive Einstein metric. I source-checked this during the step. Odaka--Spotti--Sun's JDG paper, newly retrieved/read as `Knowledge/objects/papers/COMPACT-MODULI-SPACES-OF-DEL-PEZZO-SURFACES--3cb2439eac00--b970fe5e4bdb/object.md`, gives the degree-four GH/GIT compactification, Theorem 4.1 GIT stability for intersections of two quadrics, Theorem 4.2 identification with KE moduli, and explicitly states that the unique degree-four surface with four A1 singularities is isomorphic to (P^1 x P^1)/(Z/2), admitting the quotient KE metric. This strongly supports the existence of smooth KE degree-four surfaces approaching that boundary point in moduli, but I did not have time to extract exact local deformation coordinates, smoothing scales, or an Ozuch-chart statement proving F_j(S0;t) vanishes order-by-order in the same finite-dimensional variables being used in our real Riemannian gluing expansion. Spotti's nodal KE deformation paper was also read and supplies an analytic smoothing theorem for nodal KE del Pezzo orbifolds with finite automorphism group, but the product four-A1 quotient has positive-dimensional automorphism, so it is not a direct substitute for the OSS moduli-continuity statement. Consequently, the r=0 row should be treated as a powerful calibration and likely exact baseline, but the next step must write the precise source-grounded version before using it to assert pairwise or order-by-order coefficient cancellation.

The global deformation coupling is now also better organized. T^2 symmetry filters it: only T^2-invariant orbifold deformation/kernel modes can be excited by a T^2-symmetric configuration, and the source-quadratic invariant is |z_i|^2. However, T^2 alone does not eliminate the four scalar Ozuch zero modes u_A g_A, u_A g_B, u_B g_A, u_B g_B, because axial pole harmonics are invariant under rotations about the pole axes. Existing A-symmetry, factor-tracelessness, and Bianchi-corrected local calculations from A01/A02 support leading scalar decoupling in the diagonal symmetric problem, but a full Ozuch-gauge Delta-nu calculation is still required. If the T^2-invariant part of Delta nu vanishes, the O(t^3) global coupling disappears in the symmetric sector and adjacent pair coefficients become the sole decider. If it survives, Gate 3 must include it at the same order as the pair response.

The high-dimensional Gromov half of Step 94 also needs a wording repair before any Lean formalization. The usable statement is: there is a dimensional constant C(n) with ||M|| <= C(n) Vol(M,g) whenever Ric_g >= -(n-1)g; if Ric_g >= 0, then for epsilon^2 g the Ricci lower bound remains compatible with the comparison while volume scales like epsilon^n, forcing ||M||=0. Step 94's displayed argument using a proportionality-principle-style expression was garbled. The conclusion that positive simplicial volume obstructs nonnegative Einstein metrics is correct, but the proof should be patched before becoming a formal arithmetic target.

The executable evidence produced in this step is `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step95_t2_selection_rules.py` and `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step95_t2_selection_rules.json`. The first run exposed a script bug from converting symbolic expressions to strings too early; I repaired it and reran successfully. The output records the exact T^2 chiral blocks, the beta=0 weight-one action on both K^+ and K^-, absence of quadratic local K->K monomials, pair monomial selection for same and opposite chiralities, diagonal balanced neighbour counts, and a cautious global-coupling filter. This is a representation audit, not a coefficient computation and not a gluing theorem. No branch of the original Yau--26 proposition has been proved, refuted, or Lean-formalized in this step.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step completed three overdue repairs and one structural advance for the positive-branch desingularization program. The repairs had been deferred for three consecutive steps.

**Gate 1 proof**: The SO(2)-transitivity argument was fundamentally wrong. Pi_K(mu) is an equivariant map K→K, not a vector, and maps zeta↦f(|zeta|)zeta are equivariant. The correct proof uses the T² = SO(2)_A × SO(2)_B stabilizer, which fixes all four A₁ nodes simultaneously. On chiral two-forms, the beta=0 subcircle acts with weight |theta|=1 on every kernel plane. A homogeneous quadratic equivariant map K→K requires a monomial z^a·zbar^b with a+b=2, a-b=1, giving a=3/2 (not integer). The structural content is deeper: rank-one bi-Kähler curvature gives a two-dimensional kernel, so after zeta consumes one direction, the complementary 2×2 block retains the other with det=0. A one-dimensional-kernel det(R)=0 orbifold would NOT have this protection.

**Selection rules**: Step 95 used uniform weights w_i=(1,eps_i) for all four nodes. This was wrong because the two poles of a circle action on S² carry opposite weights. The correct weight is theta_j = s_A^j alpha + eps_j s_B^j beta with node-dependent pole signs. The anisotropy condition is sigma_i = sigma_j where sigma_j = eps_j s_A^j s_B^j, NOT chirality matching. The computational verification confirms: all-compatible has sigma=(+,-,-,+) with 2 aniso pairs (both diagonal, zero adjacent); diagonal balanced has sigma=(+,+,+,+) with ALL 6 pairs aniso (4 adjacent + 2 diagonal); adjacent balanced has sigma=(+,-,+,-) with 2 aniso pairs (both adjacent). The diagonal balanced has strictly MORE anisotropic freedom than the KE row, which tilts the leading-order expectation toward solvability rather than obstruction — the opposite of the tacit assumption that mixed patterns are harder.

**Determinantal framework**: The r=0 all-compatible KE equation gives DEGENERACY of the response map, not vanishing of coefficients. OSS places the four-A1 product quotient at the boundary of compactified KE moduli; smooth KE metrics with t_i→0 exist, and at any limiting direction the response must have a kernel. The response map is xi_j ↦ P·xi_j + Q·conj(xi_j) where P=sum c_i|xi_i|² (isotropic, all pairs) and Q=sum_{sigma-matched} q_i·xi_i² (anisotropic). The kernel condition is |P|²=|Q|², i.e., |P|=|Q|. At equal scales t cancels (both P and Q are degree 2 in source norms), so the equation is SCALE-FREE. This is the representation-theoretic reason the Step 92 critical-scale story could never have worked, independent of the curvature error. Linear subtraction F(mixed)-F(r0)=0 is invalid because these are determinantal conditions, not vector identities.

**Cross-verification with A01 Step 96-97**: A01's AB-sector data gives c_adj^(AB)=-0.03144 (adjacent, P-only), c_diag^(AB)=+0.01773 (diagonal, P-only), and Q^(AB)=0 (no anisotropy in the AB sector). The AB partial sum P^(AB)=2(-0.03144)+0.01773=-0.04515 with Q^(AB)=0 confirms that the Q-channel lives entirely in the tensor sectors (AA/BB). This is consistent with the T² selection rule: angular anisotropy requires tensor coupling between matched kernel-plane weights.

**Gate 3 computational target**: The decision reduces to three numbers: c_adj (known from A01, ≈-0.0354 full or -0.0314 AB-sector), q_diag (from diagonal tensor-sector response), and q_adj (from sigma-matched adjacent tensor-sector response). The r=0 calibration |2c_adj+c_diag|=|q_diag| constrains one combination. The mixed decision is |q_diag| vs |2q_adj+q_diag|. A01's tensor-sector computation (their item 1) is where this data will come from. The global coupling feeds P but not Q (under product-preserving IED hypothesis), so Q is purely pair-determined.

The Gromov proof was also corrected to use the standard ||M||≤C(n)Vol under Ric≥-(n-1)g with epsilon² scaling.

Nothing in this step proves or refutes any branch of Yau-26. The contribution is a correct mathematical framework that turns an ill-defined 'compute the coefficient' program into a precise two-number decision. The qualitative surprise that mixed patterns have more anisotropic freedom than the KE row is a genuine structural insight that inverts the earlier heuristic expectation of obstruction.

The main structural advance is the variational reframing. The reduced obstruction equation in an Einstein gluing problem should come from a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction of the normalized total scalar curvature / Einstein-Hilbert functional: solve the complement equation, obtain a finite-dimensional function of the kernel parameters, and set its gradient to zero. This is not merely a philosophical point. It imposes algebraic constraints on the P/Q response map developed in Steps 95--96. The quartic leading potential has the form, schematically,
\[f_4=\sum_{i<j} c_{ij}|\xi_i|^2|\xi_j|^2+\operatorname{Re}(q_{ij}\xi_i^2\overline{\xi_j}^2)+\cdots,\]
so the reduced equation is a gradient, \(\partial f_4/\partial\overline{\xi_j}=P_j\xi_j+Q_j\overline{\xi_j}\), up to convention factors. This immediately gives cheap but essential diagnostics: the isotropic coefficients must be real and symmetric in a common variational normalization, anisotropic pair coefficients must satisfy reciprocity \(q_{ji}=\overline{q_{ij}}\) after frame transport, and Euler homogeneity implies that a nonzero critical point of the quartic leading functional must lie on the zero level \(f_4=0\). These are stronger and more global constraints than a single receiver-node determinant.

This Agent4 step was a critical review of the positive Gate-3 framework after Step97 reframed the product-orbifold problem as a variational finite-dimensional obstruction rather than a frozen coefficient comparison. The active Yau--26 target remains far from resolved: the full proposition asks for a dimension-by-dimension existence theorem or a strict counterexample manifold carrying Ricci-pinched metrics but no Einstein metric, with Lean formalization at completion. The four-dimensional product-orbifold line is valuable because it probes the strict positive branch and exposes how Ricci pinching, Einstein gluing, topology, and Kähler versus non-Kähler smoothings interact; it is not itself a global no-Einstein theorem and must not be allowed to replace the user's universal target.

I first tested the Strategist's stronger compatible-locus calibration against actual sources and prior artifacts. Reading the Step96 correction note, the patched Step94 three-gate note, Step97's gradient audit data, and OSS lines 300--328 confirmed that the current A02 notes still contained now-dangerous formulations: the equal-phase comparison \(|q_{\rm diag}|\) versus \(|2q_{\rm adj}+q_{\rm diag}|\) was still presented too much like the Gate-3 criterion, and Step94/Step96 outcome logic even contained a linear-algebra error by treating \(|Q|>|P|\) as producing a kernel of \(z\mapsto Pz+Q\bar z\). The correct linear algebra is \(\ker(Pz+Q\bar z)\ne0\) iff \(|P|=|Q|\); both strict inequalities give an invertible real-linear map, with orientation change when the determinant is negative. This matters because a sign or magnitude bias is not a solvability theorem.

The source request and source reading clarified the local geometric calibration. OSS establishes that degree-4 del Pezzo moduli have a Zariski-open smooth locus, polystable intersections of two quadrics have only smooth/two-node/four-node possibilities, and the unique four-\(A_1\) surface is \((\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1)/\mathbb Z_2\) with the quotient KE metric. Biquard--Rollin supplies the missing period geometry: near canonical singularities the smoothing parameters lie in \(\mathfrak h_{\mathbb C}/W\), the real cohomology of fibers is identified with \(\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}\), the local deformation-with-Kähler-class is encoded by \(\zeta=(\zeta_r,\zeta_c)\), and \(\zeta_r\) represents the restriction of the Kähler class. Their Lemma 6 states that when the real/Kähler component lies in \(\ker\theta\), the root class is Lagrangian, while when the complex component lies in \(\ker\theta\), the root is represented by a holomorphic cycle. This supports the essential interpretation: Kähler smoothings of an \(A_1\) node use periods in the plane orthogonal to the local Kähler form, i.e. in the product-orbifold kernel plane \(K=\omega^\perp=\ker R^\pm\), whereas the holomorphic resolution direction is the Kähler exceptional-curve direction. Biquard--Rollin also explicitly distinguishes smoothings from resolutions and notes that in the positive KE case desingularizations/resolutions containing holomorphic \((-2)\)-spheres generally cannot carry KE metrics unless \(c_1=0\), while smoothings can.

I then made a grounded TTCS verifier call with the A02 Gate-3 notes/data, A01's Step97 AB physical-cone note, and the OSS, Biquard--Rollin, and Ozuch sources. It verifies, at every available tensor rung `(tau,Lmax)=(0.08,80),(0.04,120),(0.02,180),(0.01,260)`, that the physical same-chirality maps `B++` and `B--` vanish in AA/BB tensor sectors, with cross-parity zero and `B+-=B-+`; the AB sector ladder and pair comparison also have same-chirality maps zero. I then wrote `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step99_selected_spectral_recompute.py` and reran selected A01 spectral computations from the scripts rather than trusting the stored JSON alone. This makes A01's same-chirality vanishing a real cross-verified raw inter-node fact, not merely a note-level assertion.

The audit also corrects the meaning of the earlier coefficients. The old values `c_adj=-0.03144` and `c_diag=+0.01773` were parity components, not physical same-chirality pair coefficients. In the physical cross-chirality table at receiver NN, the AB sector is pure trace/isotropic: adjacent sources NS and SN have trace coefficient `+0.12576998928`, equivalently isotropic eigen coefficient `+0.06288499464`; the diagonal source SS has trace coefficient `-0.070907042884`, equivalently eigen coefficient `-0.035453521442`. The AA/BB tensor sectors are traceless: adjacent NS gives a Q-type coefficient `0.0080049973185`, adjacent SN gives a P-type coefficient of the same magnitude, and the stored diagonal tensor cross coefficient is zero. Thus the leading obstruction is not the old `|q_diag|` versus `|2q_adj+q_diag|` comparison. ## Deep-Reasoning

This step achieved a structural breakthrough in the positive-branch local obstruction program for Yau Problem 26. The active goal remains the full proposition: for each n≥2, determine whether dimension-only Ricci pinching constants force Einstein existence on closed manifolds. The four-dimensional positive branch is the leading laboratory because it has concrete topology (product-mirror rows), computable spectral data (A01/A02 inter-node coefficients), and calibration controls (OSS/Tian-Yau KE existence on the compatible pattern).

The Step 99 handoff left two open questions: (1) whether the adjacent-balanced row's single-node scale-ratio window survives when all four nodes' equations are imposed simultaneously, and (2) what the uncomputed diagonal tensor cross-chirality coefficient q_diag is. Both are now resolved.

The four-node exchange-closure theorem is a clean finite-dimensional result. In the adjacent-balanced pattern ε=(+,+,-,-), nodes 1 and 2 (positive chirality) have swapped adjacent/diagonal roles to the opposite class: node 1 sees node 3 as adjacent and node 4 as diagonal, while node 2 sees node 3 as diagonal and node 4 as adjacent. This means the single-node feasibility window for node 1 at scale ratio r=u₄/u₃ is the reciprocal of node 2's window. The intersection S₁∩S₂ is nonempty if and only if r=1 lies in S₁, reducing the entire four-node system to a single algebraic condition: |c_adj+c_diag| ≤ q_adj+q_diag. With the audited values |0.06288-0.03545|=0.02743 versus 0.00800+q_diag, this requires q_diag ≥ 0.01943.

The structural diagonal tensor vanishing is the more surprising result. By loading A01's validated step98/step96 spectral framework and calling compute_full_chirality with source pair 'SS' (which the framework already supports but A01 never ran), I found that both AA and BB tensor sectors give identically zero cross-chirality response for the diagonal pair, at all four convergence-ladder rungs. The mechanism is exact pairwise cancellation between cos(2φ) and sin(2φ) tensor modes at antipodal S² poles: sign_c=(-1)^ℓ and sign_s=-(-1)^ℓ are always opposite, while SO(2) rotational symmetry of the kernel plane K=ω⊥ ensures equal contribution magnitudes. This cancellation occurs at every spectral level (ℓ_t, ℓ_s) and in every mode family (electric, magnetic). I verified the sign structure explicitly: at ℓ_t=2,3,4,5, the c2 mode ratio at the S node is (-1)^ℓ_t while the s2 ratio is -(-1)^ℓ_t. Adjacent pairs survive because one factor's tensor poles are the same (ratio +1 for both c2 and s2), so reinforcement rather than cancellation.

The consequence is complete: since q_diag=0 < 0.01943, the adjacent-balanced row is obstructed at leading inter-node order, joining the diagonal-balanced (margin 0.05488) and one/three-reversed rows (also margin 0.05488). ALL five mixed chirality patterns on the positive mirror are obstructed. The coefficient table now explains the known KE/non-KE dichotomy: same-chirality vanishing makes f₄≡0 on the compatible locus (consistent with KE by Tian-Yau), while nonvanishing cross-chirality couplings on mixed rows produce the obstruction (consistent with non-Kähler/non-symplectic structure).

The weakest link is the adjacent-balanced margin at 0.01943. This is about 3.5× the tensor adjacent coefficient (0.008), so it is a comfortable margin at leading order. But the ratio of this margin to the leading AB coefficient (~0.063) is about 31%, which means the relative remainder estimate o(t³) must ultimately control terms at the 31% level relative to the leading cubic.

Several important gaps remain before this becomes a theorem:

1. The self-interaction terms (node j's bubble affecting its own equation) and complement Schur terms must be shown pattern-independent or negligible. The Biquard-Rollin/OSS calibration suggests they cancel in the mixed-minus-compatible comparison, but this requires a full Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction with fixed volume and Bianchi/Ebin slice.

2. Frame/projector motion as the bubble scale varies may contribute O(t³) terms that are not captured by the fixed-frame spectral computation.

3. Global Einstein deformations (the ν_l variables in Ozuch's framework) couple through the chirality change at O(t²), producing O(t³) contributions to the node equations. These must be shown pattern-independent or bounded.

4. The relative remainder must be o(t³), including possible t³log(t) terms from the logarithmic annulus structure. The current crude estimate is O(t^{5/2}) which dominates t³ as t→0—this is the most serious remaining gap.

5. Even a completed local theorem only obstructs the specific product-orbifold degeneration channel, not global Einstein nonexistence on #₃(S²×S²) or 3CP²#3CP̄².

For the negative mirror (Σ₂×Σ₂)/Z₂ with 36 nodes and R^±=diag(-1,0,0), the same spectral framework should apply with sign-flipped curvature. The compatible rows are KE by Aubin-Yau. The structural diagonal vanishing should hold by the same mechanism (it depends on the kernel-plane SO(2) symmetry, not on the sign of Λ). But the much larger number of nodes (36) means the combinatorics of chirality patterns is richer, and the four-node exchange closure needs to be generalized.

For the full Yau-26 problem: the positive mirror local obstruction, even if promoted to a theorem, would need to be combined with (a) a global no-Einstein argument on the mixed rows and (b) a negative-branch obstruction or tight negative pinching on an all-sign no-Einstein manifold. Both remain substantial open problems. The diffuse N#N connector and the Lean curvature formalization are the other two major open fronts.

The structural diagonal vanishing is worth recording as an independent mathematical observation: it says that the Ozuch inter-node tensor-sector coupling has a strict bipartite structure aligned with the product factorization. Diagonal node pairs, which differ on both S² factors, produce no tensor (traceless) coupling—only scalar (trace/isotropic) coupling through the AB sector. This simplifies the finite-dimensional obstruction system and may have implications beyond the specific Yau-26 application.

### Decisions and Recorded Reasons

- The target remains the original all-dimensional Yau–26 quantifier statement: for every \(n\ge2\), find dimension-only constants \(c_n<C_n\) such that every closed connected smooth \(n\)-manifold carrying a metric with
  \[
  c_ng\le \operatorname{Ric}_g\le C_ng
  \]
  also carries some Einstein metric, or strictly refute this. The Einstein output need not be close to the input, preserve auxiliary structures, or have prescribed sign. A proof needs one valid interval in every dimension; a refutation in one dimension must defeat every possible interval, not merely one normalized sign branch [Steps 1, 58, 72–74, 83–85].

- The opening survey considered Min–Oo negative stability, prescribed-Ricci flexibility, positive compactness and collapse, orbifold/ALE resolutions, gauge-theoretic obstructions, toric and nilpotent models, and explicit constructions. Four-dimensional degeneration initially received priority because it offered concrete topology, gauge theory, curvature identities, and bubbling models, while negative and higher-dimensional routes were retained rather than ruled out [Steps 1–9].

- Min–Oo’s negative almost-Einstein theorem was retained only as a restricted boundary result because it assumes \(d(g)^2\max|K_g|<\Lambda^2\), not merely two-sided Ricci pinching. A negative near-pinched sequence can escape through diameter growth, collapse, or full-curvature concentration [Steps 1, 22].

- The first Calabi/ALE gluing shortcut to a counterexample was rejected. Weighted or \(L^p\)-small residuals can coexist with an order-one nonscalar Ricci endomorphism on a scaled ALE core. This produced the obstruction-amplitude principle: a first obstruction \(t\lambda o\), raised by \(g_t^{-1}\sim t^{-1}\), stays order \(|\lambda|\), whereas a \(k\)-th obstruction \(O(t^k)\) contributes \(O(t^{k-1})\) and is subcritical for \(k\ge2\) [Steps 1, 32, 48–50, 74].

- A Step-2 LeBrun conclusion was withdrawn after the user identified a factor-four scalar-curvature error. The corrected thresholds are \(k\ge2A/3\) and \(k\ge A/3\), with the individual square \(A-k\) distinguished from the convex-hull estimate \((a^+)^2\ge A\). The surviving restricted estimate is
  \[
  \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\ge\sqrt{\frac{p-1/3}{2}},\qquad p=k/A,
  \]
  which yields a fixed gap for \(p>1/3\) but degenerates at the endpoint [Steps 2–4, 53–54].

- Four-dimensional Chern–Gauss–Bonnet and signature identities were retained as a common ledger, including the pointwise-optimal \(\beta(\delta)\) estimate, but demoted as standalone contradiction mechanisms because scale-invariant curvature energy can concentrate on shrinking rods, bolts, bubbles, and necks [Steps 4, 14–18, 34–37].

- The claim that tight positive Ricci pinching excludes collapse was withdrawn after Berger anisotropy, lens-space, product, and Kaluza–Klein examples. The proposed unrestricted smooth compactness theorem was also withdrawn because Cheeger–Naber regularity permits codimension-four singular sets. The replacement problem is to classify noncollapsed and collapsed degeneration mechanisms compatible with Einstein existence [Steps 3–10, 24].

- The opposite-warping spike on \(S^2\times S^2\), with \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) but unbounded full curvature, ruled out a general \(C^0\)-Ricci-to-pointwise-curvature estimate. It is not a counterexample because the topology already carries an Einstein metric. It redirected work toward weak harmonic-radius, determinant, pairing, tower-subtraction, and flux methods [Steps 10–12, 33–35].

- Toric and nilpotent collapse programs were retained as adversarial tests rather than assumed routes. Euclidean Faber–Krahn, orbit-curvature sign, signed Gauss–Bonnet, corner spectral rigidity, and “Milnor curvature forces abelianization” shortcuts were discarded. Exact toric edge germs showed local Einstein compatibility is abundant and global closure is the issue. The nilpotent argument was reduced to a Bochner center estimate; producing scale-correct almost-Killing or nilpotent fields from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching remains the missing keystone [Steps 12–30, 34–41].

- The Biquard–Ozuch first obstruction was fixed in vectorial, orientation-sensitive form:
  \[
  R_\pm(p)\zeta^\pm=0,\qquad R_\pm=W^\pm+\frac{\Lambda}{3}I.
  \]
  Determinants are only shorthand for the existence of a nonzero kernel vector. ADE representation refinements were retained, while an earlier “second exceptional locus” description for \(E\)-types was withdrawn after isotropy calculations showed the relevant nontrivial blocks have \(W=0\) [Steps 7–8, 30–33, 42–47].

- The operator-norm scaling correction initially made killing the first obstruction essential for near-pinching while reserving higher obstructions for exact Einstein desingularization [Steps 48–50]. The general cone-mode calculation later showed that small \(C^0\) Ricci-endomorphism defect cannot force the higher obstruction tower to vanish: only the quadratic mode is unweighted log-critical, while higher modes are structurally subcritical. The Step-70 proof skeleton that required pinching to force the entire tower was therefore withdrawn as unattainable from the stated hypothesis, not merely analytically incomplete [Steps 70, 73–74].

- The product-quotient construction was first treated as a conditional-hardness reduction and then upgraded at fixed-family level. The logarithmic \(A_1\) construction permits pointwise chirality and marking choices, so every fixed smooth mixed row carries metrics with
  \[
  \delta(g_a)=O(|\log a|^{-1})\to0.

  An all-sign no-Einstein theorem on one positive mixed row would refute the normalized positive branch \(P_4^+\), but not the original proposition because a strictly negative interval might still work [Steps 49–51, 68–69, 74, 78, 83–84].

The \(m=1\) collar closed by integration by parts, but a forced-Moser endpoint remained. Later exact reflected and then reflection-free complete free-\(T^2\) orthogonally transitive connector classes were excluded, while general forced, twisted, or non-OT connectors remained open [Steps 51–54, 62–63, 86–95].

Mixed rows were proved non-Kähler and nonsymplectic in both orientations using an embedded non-torsion \(+2\)-sphere and adjunction. All sign-pattern fillings are simply connected, making simplicial-volume and fundamental-group obstructions vacuous on these rows [Steps 55–57].

Since \(\chi\) is fixed while \(\tau\) varies and Hitchin–Thorpe margins improve inward, invariants depending only on \(\chi,\tau,\|M\|\), or degree cannot distinguish the mixed rows.   \[

  3\mathbb{CP}^2\#3\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2},\qquad
  r=3:\ 4\mathbb{CP}^2\#2\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2},
  \]
  with \(r=4\) orientation-reversing \(r=0\). Only homeomorphism types were established. The working spin-lift/seam convention identifies the diagonal balanced row with \(\#_3(S^2\times S^2)\) and the adjacent balanced row with the non-spin type, but an independent Kirby or boundary-spin audit remains required [Steps 64, 75–76].

- Every proposed Einstein computation was required to use the \(r=0\) del Pezzo row as control. A solver failing there is uninterpretable; convergence on a mixed row could support a rigorous symmetric boundary-value problem, while nonconvergence proves no nonexistence. Raw EH insertion, elementary radial and conformal ansätze, a scalar Kähler-potential shortcut, and finite-difference radial least squares were rejected as certificates because they miss bolt regularity, gauge, nonradial ambient modes, or direct pointwise Ricci-endomorphism control [Steps 64–67].

- The product-orbifold jet showed that \(U(2)\)-radial reduction is incomplete: the isotropy is \(T^2\), and five angular components occur in the \(\omega_i^+\circ\omega_j^-\) decomposition, only one radial. Correct correction equations require nonradial \(l=2\)-type tensor modes [Step 67].

- LeBrun–Ozuch and Ozuch source reading corrected the nearby-existence picture. The all-compatible \(r=0\) configuration has actual nearby Kähler–Einstein desingularizations. Mixed patterns are non-admissible for that conformally Kähler classification, not excluded by it. Exact mixed existence reduces locally to finite-dimensional obstruction and transversality questions after slicing the full gauged kernel [Step 67].

- The product Green computation was narrowed repeatedly to avoid false simplifications. The relevant object is the receiving second jet of a Bianchi-gauge \(P\)-harmonic solution with \(r^{-4}\) tensor-quadrupole asymptotics, after singular subtraction, kernel projection, and normalization:
  \[
  P=\tfrac12\nabla^*\nabla-\mathring R,\qquad
  P(g_1-g_2)=-\Lambda(g_1-g_2).
  \]
  The quotient TT kernel is zero, but the full gauged operator has four non-TT scalar zero modes. Static factor Green functions cannot be multiplied because product spectral denominators are additive. Heat-kernel formulas need separate treatment of negative, zero, and positive sectors [Steps 68–69, 75–76].

- The biaxial Einstein family \(q_\Lambda\), differentiated at \(\Lambda=0\) and gauge-corrected, supplies a smooth tensor \(\widetilde h\) satisfying
  \[
  D\operatorname{Ric}_{\mathrm{EH}}\widetilde h=g_{\mathrm{EH}}.
  \]
  Logarithmic interpolation between quadratic tensors with equal Ricci linearization gives the fixed-\(A_1\) near-pinched construction. It is not an exact Einstein desingularization theorem [Steps 68–69].

- The annular flux identity settled the clean local pairing:
  \[
  \int_A\langle D\operatorname{Ric}u,o\rangle
  =-\frac{n+2}{2}I_K,
  \]
  with coefficient \(-3\) in dimension four. The sharp recorded constants are \(1/8\) in the unconstrained model and \(1/6\) under constant scalar curvature. Transfer to genuine bubbling sequences still requires tower subtraction and endpoint matching [Steps 69–70].

- The cone-mode extension was classified in transverse dimension \(d\ge4\):
  \[
  H_2(b,R)=\log(R/b),\qquad
  H_\ell(b,R)=\frac{b^{2-\ell}-R^{2-\ell}}{\ell-2}\quad(\ell>2).
  \]
  Thus \(\ell=2\) is uniquely unweighted log-critical for Yau–26; higher modes give power-scale unweighted bounds, although weighted logarithmic estimates survive. This replaced the requested all-\(\ell\) higher-obstruction necessity theorem [Steps 73–74].

- Tight positive pinching was recorded to imply positive Ricci and scalar curvature, finite \(\pi_1\), \(b_1=0\), Myers diameter bounds, and Bishop volume upper bounds in every dimension. In dimension four, sufficiently tight pinching also gives strict Hitchin–Thorpe. Existing inspected four-dimensional no-Einstein mechanisms were predominantly monopole-driven and incompatible with the positive-pinching class. This was an allocation judgment, not evidence that Yau–26 is true [Steps 22–24, 58, 72–73].

- Product propagation was corrected from a reduction to a family-specific stress test. Multiplying a four-dimensional near-pinched metric by an Einstein sphere with the same constant preserves the factorwise maximum defect, propagating hard families to dimensions \(n\ge6\). It does not prove \(P_4^+\Rightarrow P_n^+\), because \(P_n^+\) quantifies over all manifolds and the resulting Einstein metric need not split. Dimension five is not reached by a one-dimensional Einstein factor [Step 74].

- The high-dimensional noncollapsed frontier remains codimension-four singular strata rather than isolated points. The tentative object is a bundle-valued normal obstruction along the stratum, schematically \(R_{\mathrm{normal},\pm}(y)\zeta(y)\), modified by normal-connection curvature, tangential derivatives, and mixed components. No general stratified ALE-bundle theorem exists in the record; bubble trees require nested scale subtraction and cannot be hidden behind the no-tree LeBrun–Ozuch framework [Steps 53, 71, 73–74].

- Four-node symmetry reduced chirality patterns to three classes: \(r=1\) with \(r=3\) as complement, adjacent balanced \(r=2\), and diagonal balanced \(r=2\). Both balanced patterns are self-conjugate after composing an appropriate \(D_8\) element with the orientation-reversing isometry \(c\); the diagonal pattern has larger stabilizer [Steps 75–76].

- The initial \(T^2\)-selection rule was retained only as a representation reduction. Pole second jets impose low total angular characters and quotient parity, but infinitely many spherical degrees remain. Closed forms, projected heat kernels, Abel/Ewald summation, or certified tail bounds are needed for full sums [Steps 75–76].

- Chirality splitting gave a useful local check: an EH source of chirality \(\epsilon\) perturbs the opposite Weyl block. Same-chirality kernel-block coupling was initially expected to vanish in selected channels, and in-kernel EH tensors are factor-traceless so tracked scalar \(\nu_\ell\) projections vanish after the relevant symmetry and slice analysis. These remained diagnostic cancellations until later spectral work directly verified the physical same-chirality leading inter-node maps [Steps 77, 97–99].

- Pattern-dependent inter-node effects enter at \(t_jt_i^2\), hence order \(t^3\) for comparable scales, below the existing \(O(t_{\max}^{5/2})\) necessary-equation resolution. First-obstruction vanishing is also nontransversal. Available finite-dimensional equations therefore could not initially distinguish mixed patterns or support a contraction theorem. Any decisive cubic coefficient still requires an adapted expansion or a relative remainder \(o(t^3)\) [Steps 76–78, 93–99].

- A01’s \(A+J+L\), \(K\)-symmetry, and AB-sector work was retained as local input rather than a global theorem. \(K\)-symmetry eliminates cross-parity sectors, makes odd sources orthogonal to the negative shape mode and scalar zero modes, and reduces selected interactions. An unconditional positivity claim was corrected because \(q=g_A-g_B\) is a TT negative mode and point-source self-pairings are singular. An apparent AA/BB coincident-point divergence was later traced to an electric/magnetic normalization error; corrected sector sums are finite [Steps 78, 80, 84–94].

- The empirical pattern \(\min(b_+,b_-)\le1\) among familiar simply connected positive Einstein four-manifolds was not promoted to a theorem. It is explained in inspected examples by symmetric, Hermitian, del Pezzo, or conformally Kähler classifications. Mixed rows with \(\chi=8\) are simply connected, PSC, strict-Hitchin–Thorpe, SW-void in the available sense, and non-Kähler/nonsymplectic in both orientations, but no known classification excludes arbitrary positive Einstein metrics on them [Steps 57, 64, 78–80].

- Classical magnitude estimates were closed as obstruction routes. Gursky’s positive-Yamabe inequality, Gursky–LeBrun’s positive-Einstein estimate, Chern–Weil budgets, harmonic-form alignment, generic CLR estimates, and Gram/transgression variants all leave slack or reproduce known inequalities. The user directed that further variants of the positive harmonic-form wall not consume more steps because they address only the \(\lambda>0\) leg of a larger all-sign problem [Steps 78–83].

- The Ricci-flat leg was corrected after the claim “every compact simply connected Ricci-flat four-manifold is K3” was withdrawn. The \(\chi=8\) rows exclude torus, flat, reducible, locally symmetric, and known \(SU(2)\)/hyperkähler mechanisms, but Berger’s list still permits hypothetical irreducible generic \(SO(4)\) holonomy. Thus a Ricci-flat metric would be unprecedented, not excluded [Step 82].

- The Einstein Chern–Weil sign was repaired:
  \[
  \int |W|^2=8\pi^2\chi-\frac23\lambda^2V,\qquad
  \int |W^\pm|^2=2\pi^2(2\chi\pm3\tau)-\frac13\lambda^2V.
  \]
  The formulas depend on \(\lambda^2\); negative Einstein metrics do not reverse the scalar contribution. Harmonic-form alignment is sign-locked to \(\lambda>0\) [Steps 81–82].

- Fixed-row refutation therefore requires three independent sign legs: exclusion of \(\lambda>0\), closure of the generic-\(SO(4)\) Ricci-flat loophole, and exclusion of \(\lambda<0\). Deciding \(\#_3(S^2\times S^2)\) and \(3\mathbb{CP}^2\#3\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\) is a genuine frontier, not a missing short computation [Steps 82–84].

- The logarithmic construction became the highest-priority audit because the mixed-row reductions depended on it and earlier ansätze hid order-one raised-index defects. A rational ten-dimensional Weyl basis checked all five \(W^+\) and five \(W^-\) quadratic sectors: trace-free, divergence-free, harmonic, radial-gauge, and \(D\operatorname{Ric}_eK=0\), with the radial monomial identity. TTCS required common radial normal gauge, \(O_2\) tail/Taylor control, and arbitrary-cutoff accounting, which were adopted [Step 83].

- The resulting theorem-grade fixed-\(A_1\) construction states that, for a fixed Einstein four-orbifold with finitely many \(A_1\) points, fixed equivariant charts, EH markings and chiralities, and the stated gauge and \(O_2\) hypotheses, the marked resolution carries metrics
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_a}-\sigma g_a\|_{\mathrm{op}}
  \le C|\log a|^{-1}.
  \]
  The core raised-index residual, logarithmic annulus, ambient patch, and finite multi-node constants are all controlled. The result is sign-neutral and covers active non-\(U(2)\) sectors, but produces only near-pinched metrics [Step 83].

- Exact interval logic separated the sign branches. On \(S^1\times S^3\), a flat-circle/round-sphere product scales into every interval \([0,C]\), Lohkamp metrics scale into every \([c,0]\), and arbitrary metrics handle crossing-zero intervals. The manifold has no Einstein metric because \(\chi=0\) would force a four-dimensional Einstein metric to be flat, while \(\pi_1=\mathbb Z\) is not virtually \(\mathbb Z^4\). Thus in dimension four the original proposition is equivalent to the validity of some strict positive branch or some strict negative branch [Step 84].

- Strict one-sign intervals normalize by constant metric scaling. The correct factor is \(h=\frac{c+C}{2}g\) for \(c,C>0\) and \(h=-\frac{c+C}{2}g\) for \(c,C<0\); the earlier reciprocal formula was wrong. Ricci as a \((0,2)\)-tensor is invariant under constant scaling [Step 88].

- In every \(n\ge3\), Lohkamp gives \(\operatorname{Ric}<0\) on every closed manifold, so a boundary interval \([c,0]\) contains every smooth type after scaling. Any refutation therefore needs at least one closed manifold carrying no Einstein metric of any sign. This is only a necessary prerequisite; no certified all-sign reservoir for \(n\ge5\) has been found [Steps 85–87].

- The functional
  \[
  F(g)=\int\left(|W|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}\right)
      =8\pi^2\chi+\frac12\int|E|^2
  \]
  was briefly adopted as a sign-neutral attainment instrument and then closed as an obstruction route. The logarithmic modification itself gives
  \[
  \int|E|^2=O\!\left(\frac{a}{|\log a|^2}\right),
  \]
  producing a degenerating minimizing sequence with \(\inf F=8\pi^2\chi\). Ordinary \(L^p\), direct-method, or weak Palais–Smale arguments do not see the sharp unweighted \(C^0\) scale [Steps 84–85].

- The exact energy ledger explains repeated magnitude-estimate failures. The positive mirror has orbifold contribution \(16\pi^2\) plus four EH contributions \(12\pi^2\), totaling \(64\pi^2=8\pi^2\chi\). The negative mirror totals \(448\pi^2=8\pi^2\cdot56\). The degenerations saturate the closed-manifold lower bound [Step 84].

- Gauge-theoretic disjointness was sharpened and scoped. Tight positive pinching gives PSC and kills the monopole/Bauer–Furuta data used by current no-Einstein theorems at the class level. In the negative \(A_1\) family, compatible fillings lie in an ample-canonical negative Kähler–Einstein regime, while reversed fillings contain non-torsion \(+2\)-spheres. Relative Bauer–Furuta adjunction shows that the standard nonzero BF certificates used in Ishida–LeBrun/Kotschick-type results cannot coexist with those spheres, subject to the closed-to-relative interface hypotheses. This is not a claim that all conceivable gauge invariants vanish [Steps 55–57, 86–88].

- A non-gauge all-sign no-Einstein reservoir was recovered from Sambusetti and Besson–Courtois–Gallot. For a closed real-hyperbolic four-manifold \(N\),
  \[
  M_N=N\#N,\qquad \chi(M_N)=2\chi(N)-2,\quad \tau(M_N)=0,
  \]
  admits a degree-two map to \(N\), has positive simplicial volume and strict Hitchin–Thorpe, yet Sambusetti’s inequality would require \(2\chi(N)-2\ge2\chi(N)\). Hence \(M_N\) carries no Einstein metric of any sign [Step 87].

- BBCG volume rigidity is stable under lower Ricci control, but only produces a fixed-\(N\) or additive obstruction. Correct scaling from
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}+3g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta
  \]
  uses \(\widehat g=(1+\delta/3)g\), so
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_g(M_N)\ge
  \frac{2\operatorname{Vol}(N)}{(1+\delta/3)^2}.
  \]
  Combining this with Chern–Gauss–Bonnet yields asymptotically
  \[
  \delta\ge\frac{3}{4\chi(N)}+O(\chi(N)^{-2}).
  \]
  BBCG’s rigidity constant depends on the target diameter and Corollary 1.7 is fixed-\(X\); the source does not provide a dimension-only multiplicative gap over all hyperbolic \(N\) [Steps 87–92].

- The warped-product connector was ruled out sharply. At a waist of
  \[
  g=dr^2+f(r)^2g_F,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_F=2kg_F,
  \]
  with \(k\ge0\), the minimum possible negative-Einstein defect is \(3/2\), with a stronger cost for round \(S^3\). A negatively curved fibre permits a defect-free \(\cosh r\) waist because it is locally hyperbolic. Thus round-sphere and torus warped turnarounds cannot approach the negative branch [Step 88].

- The general minimal-hypersurface Gauss equation was judged insufficient by itself to exclude non-warped \(S^3\) or \(T^3\) waists. A general near-negative “no connected-sum waist” theorem would address Sambusetti sums and LeBrun blowups but remains open [Steps 88–90].

- Hyperbolic Einstein four-orbifolds with isolated \(A_1\) points were located in the Davis-manifold symmetry literature, but the proposed Davis group computation was superseded. Positive \(b_1\) does not imply positive simplicial volume or provide a nonzero-degree hyperbolic map, and stabilizer relations can destroy entropy data after resolution [Steps 88–89].

- The Chern–Weil neutrality principle replaced that case-by-case search. For a Ricci-flat ALE bubble,
  \[
  |12\pi^2\Delta\tau|
  \le \int|W|^2=8\pi^2\Delta\chi,\qquad
  |\Delta\tau|\le\frac23\Delta\chi.
  \]
  Thus ALE resolution cannot decrease \(\chi-\frac32|\tau|\); half-flat bubbles are neutral and mixed chiralities increase the surplus. This explains why Hitchin–Thorpe, Gursky-type estimates, entropy budgets, and \(F\)-energy retain slack under ALE insertion [Step 90].

- BCG plus ALE neutrality gives entropy-inaccessibility for hyperbolic-orbifold \(A_1\) resolutions. Any degree-\(d\) map from the resolution \(M\) to a closed hyperbolic \(Y\) satisfies
  \[
  |d|\,\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\le\operatorname{Vol}(O),\qquad
  \chi(M)-\frac32|\tau(M)|\ge\chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(O)\ge |d|\chi(Y).
  \]
  Thus the orbifold-plus-Ricci-flat-ALE construction class cannot violate Sambusetti’s inequality [Steps 90–92].

- This was summarized as “triple disjointness” for the currently used certificate families:
  1. positive pinching is class-level disjoint from monopole/BF certificates by PSC and Weitzenböck;
  2. compatible negative \(A_1\) fillings are Kähler–Einstein, while reversed fillings are disjoint from standard BF certificates by \(+2\)-sphere adjunction;
  3. orbifold-plus-ALE constructions cannot access Sambusetti/entropy violations because ALE bubbles preserve the Chern–Weil surplus and BCG bounds degree-map volume.
  
  It is not a theorem that all no-Einstein invariants are blind [Steps 86–92].

- A topological explanation was added to ALE neutrality. A smooth four-dimensional Ricci-flat ALE bubble with trivial group at infinity and \(\mathbb R^4\) topology is flat by the Bando–Kasue–Nakajima/Nakajima positive-mass input. Nontrivial topology-changing bubbles therefore use \(S^3/\Gamma\) seams with \(|\Gamma|>1\), not the simply connected \(S^3\) seam of an ordinary connected sum. The orbifold-resolution machine cannot perform the connected-sum operation that lowers \(\chi\) by two and is detected by Sambusetti [Steps 91–92].

- The scalar-excess ledger changed the negative connector problem from local to diffuse. Writing \(s=-12+u\) under \(\|\operatorname{Ric}+3g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\) gives \(|u|\le4\delta\) and
  \[
  8\pi^2\chi
  =\int|W|^2+6\operatorname{Vol}-\int u+\frac1{24}\int u^2-\frac12\int|E|^2.
  \]
  For fixed hyperbolic \(N\), a sequence on \(N\#N\) with \(\delta\to0\) must carry a leading \(16\pi^2\) scalar-curvature excess, forcing the set where \(s>-12\) to have volume of order at least \(1/\delta\), subject to the recorded lower-order terms. For varying \(N\), the estimate loses \(O(\delta\chi(N))\), so no uniform obstruction follows. A refuting sequence only needs \(\delta_i\to0\), not the critical \(1/\chi(N_i)\) rate [Step 91].

- The negative branch was consequently reframed. Warped and free-\(T^2\) orthogonally transitive barriers are genuine subclass results, including the reflection-free complete two-outward-end theorem and its \(\delta<0.246249763690668\) threshold, but they do not cover the \(S^3\)-neck \(N\#N\) reservoir. The honest frontier is a diffuse, non-warped, non-OT topology change spread over volume \(\gtrsim1/\delta\), or a nonlocal theorem excluding such spreading [Steps 91–99].

- The positive local coefficient program underwent a load-bearing curvature correction. A Step-92 note incorrectly called the product orbifold conformally flat and used
  \(R^\pm=(\Lambda/3)I\), creating an artificial critical scale \(t_*\). The correct product curvature is
  \[
  R^+=R^-=\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda,0,0),\qquad
  W^\pm=\operatorname{diag}(2\Lambda/3,-\Lambda/3,-\Lambda/3).
  \]
  The first obstruction therefore vanishes on the two-plane
  \[
  K^\pm=\ker R^\pm=\operatorname{span}\{e_2,e_3\},
  \]
  while the Kähler/image direction \(e_1\) is excluded. There is no positive background eigenvalue to cancel and no critical scale; admissible EH directions lie in \(K^\pm\) at arbitrarily small scale [Steps 44–50, 67–69, 92–93].

- The corrected local problem is a kernel-plane angular response, not a scalar scale equation. For \(\zeta_j=t_j\xi_j\) with \(\xi_j\in K_j\), the leading pattern-sensitive term is cubic, schematically
  \[
  \Pi_{K_j}F_j
  =t_j\sum_{i\ne j}t_i^2B_{ji}(\xi_i,\xi_j)+\cdots.
  \]
  Same-order local, self, frame/projector, complement, global-kernel, and nonlinear terms must remain until proved absent. Ozuch Proposition 2.10 is a global boundary pairing, not directly the receiver \(2\times2\) block [Step 93].

- Gate 1 was initially justified incorrectly by saying no nonzero \(SO(2)\)-equivariant vector exists in \(K\). The obstruction is an equivariant map \(K\to K\), so that argument was invalid. The repaired proof uses the full stabilizer \(T^2=SO(2)_A\times SO(2)_B\), which fixes all four nodes. The \(\beta=0\) subcircle acts with weight one on every kernel plane, and no homogeneous quadratic monomial has degree two and weight one. Therefore the projected local quadratic obstruction vanishes by weight parity. Structurally, rank-one bi-Kähler curvature has a two-dimensional kernel; after \(\zeta\) uses one kernel direction, the complementary \(2\times2\) curvature block retains the other and has zero determinant. A generic one-dimensional-kernel orbifold would not enjoy this cancellation [Steps 94–96].

- Node-dependent pole signs corrected the first pair-selection rule. At node \(j\),
  \[
  \theta_j=s_A^j\alpha+\epsilon_j s_B^j\beta,\qquad
  \sigma_j=\epsilon_js_A^js_B^j.
  \]
  The real-linear pair response has the form
  \[
  \xi_j\longmapsto P_j\xi_j+Q_j\overline{\xi_j},
  \]
  with anisotropic channels allowed when \(\theta_i=\pm\theta_j\), equivalently \(\sigma_i=\sigma_j\), not simply when chiralities match. The all-compatible pattern has anisotropic diagonal pairs, the diagonal balanced pattern permits all pair anisotropies, and the adjacent balanced pattern has two anisotropic adjacent pairs [Steps 95–96].

- The kernel condition for \(z\mapsto Pz+Q\bar z\) was repaired:
  \[
  \ker\ne0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |P|^2=|Q|^2.
  \]
  Both strict inequalities give an invertible real-linear map; \(|Q|>|P|\) does not itself produce a solution. The common bubble scale cancels from the leading homogeneous equation. This finite-dimensional fact was formalized in the checked Lean artifact `workspace/proofs/Step99RealLinearPQ.lean`; it formalizes no geometry [Steps 96–99].

- The leading obstruction was reframed variationally. In a valid fixed-volume Bianchi/Ebin slice with complement solved, the finite-dimensional Einstein equation should be the gradient of a reduced normalized Einstein–Hilbert functional. The leading real quartic has schematic form
  \[
  f_4(\xi)=\sum_{i<j}
  \left(c_{ij}|\xi_i|^2|\xi_j|^2
  +\operatorname{Re}(q_{ij}\xi_i^2\overline{\xi_j}^{\,2})\right)
  +\text{self/global terms},
  \]
  and
  \[
  \frac{\partial f_4}{\partial\overline{\xi_j}}
  =P_j\xi_j+Q_j\overline{\xi_j}.
  \]
  This imposes real symmetric isotropic coefficients, reciprocity \(q_{ji}=\overline{q_{ij}}\) after frame transport, and Euler’s zero-level condition at a nonzero homogeneous critical point. It also shows that phase and relative scale variables cannot be frozen without justification [Steps 97–98].

- The compatible smoothing geometry was source-grounded. Biquard–Rollin identifies the real/Kähler and complex/smoothing periods of an \(A_1\) deformation; compatible Kähler smoothing periods lie in the plane \(K=\omega^\perp=\ker R^\pm\), while the excluded \(e_1=\omega\) direction is the holomorphic resolution/Kähler exceptional-curve direction. This matches the first obstruction: it admits the smoothing configuration that yields KE del Pezzo surfaces and excludes the holomorphic resolution direction whose weak del Pezzo has no positive KE metric [Step 98].

- OSS places the unique four-\(A_1\) surface \((\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1)/\mathbb Z_2\) at the boundary of compactified degree-four KE moduli, and smooth degree-four del Pezzo surfaces form the KE open locus. The user sharpened the calibration: in versal smoothing coordinates \(\mathbb C^4\), the all-nonzero compatible locus is open and corresponds to kernel-plane smoothing parameters, so a correctly normalized full leading quartic must vanish on that compatible open set and hence have zero compatible coefficients. The record retains a coordinate/slice caveat for converting this geometric statement into a specific partial spectral table, but later raw computation independently verified the physical same-chirality leading inter-node vanishing [Steps 95–99].

- A01’s corrected spectral calculations were independently audited rather than accepted from note-level summaries. The audit reran selected scripts and matched stored data exactly. Across all checked tensor rungs, the physical same-chirality maps \(B^{++}\) and \(B^{--}\) vanish in AA/BB sectors, cross-parity blocks vanish, and \(B^{+-}=B^{-+}\). The AB ladder also gives zero physical same-chirality maps. This is a genuine cross-verification between the compatible KE geometry and the raw inter-node calculation [Step 99].

- Earlier values \(-0.03144\) and \(+0.01773\) were corrected in interpretation: they are parity components, not physical same-chirality coefficients. At receiver NN, the physical cross-chirality AB sector is pure trace/isotropic, with adjacent trace coefficient
  \[
  0.12576998928
  \quad\text{and isotropic eigenvalue}\quad
  0.06288499464,
  \]
  and diagonal trace coefficient
  \[
  -0.070907042884
  \quad\text{and eigenvalue}\quad
  -0.035453521442.
  \]
  AA/BB cross-chirality tensor sectors are traceless, with adjacent coefficient magnitude
  \[
  0.0080049973185,
  \]
  and no stored diagonal tensor response in the audited table [Step 99].

- The balanced rows consequently split at the raw leading inter-node level. For the diagonal balanced pattern \(\epsilon=(+,-,-,+)\), every receiver has two opposite-chirality adjacent sources and a same-chirality diagonal source. The diagonal source vanishes at this order, and
  \[
  B_j=
  0.06288499464\,(u_1+u_2)I+T,\qquad
  \|T\|\le0.0080049973185\,(u_1+u_2).
  \]
  The positive margin
  \[
  0.0548799973215
  \]
  makes this raw leading matrix uniformly positive definite for arbitrary positive source scale-squares and phases [Step 99].

- The adjacent balanced pattern \(\epsilon=(+,+,-,-)\) is not covered by that uniform trace argument. Each receiver sees one opposite-chirality adjacent source and one opposite-chirality diagonal source, giving
  \[
  P=0.06288499464\,u_{\mathrm{adj}}
    -0.035453521442\,u_{\mathrm{diag}},
  \qquad
  |Q|\le0.0080049973185\,u_{\mathrm{adj}}.
  \]
  The equality \(|P|=|Q|\) is possible at positive ratios
  \[
  u_{\mathrm{diag}}/u_{\mathrm{adj}}
  \approx1.54794206864,\quad 1.99951906257,
  \]
  with \(P=0\) near \(1.77373056560\). Thus the diagonal balanced row has a strong local obstruction candidate, while the adjacent balanced row retains a possible scale/phase existence window [Step 99].

- The Step-99 margin is not yet a local obstruction theorem. A theorem still requires a calibrated slice-compatible Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction, proof that self-interaction, frame/projector motion, complement Schur terms, and global Einstein-deformation variables cannot cancel or alter the positive trace, and a relative expansion with remainder \(o(t^3)\), including possible \(t^3\log t\) terms. Ozuch’s higher-order framework supplies a template but has not yet been adapted fully to the product orbifold [Steps 93–99].

- Even a completed local diagonal-balanced obstruction would exclude only Einstein branches converging to this product-orbifold degeneration with the selected markings and chirality pattern. It would not prove that \(\#_3(S^2\times S^2)\) has no distant Einstein metric and therefore would not by itself refute \(P_4^+\) or Yau–26. Conversely, a transversal adjacent-balanced solution could produce the first known positive Einstein metric with \(\min(b_+,b_-)\ge2\), an important theorem and evidence for \(P_4^+\), but still not a universal branch proof [Steps 78, 94, 97–99].

- The high-dimensional discussion was corrected from a claimed structural theorem to a limitation of current methods. Positive simplicial volume obstructs nonnegative Einstein metrics in every dimension: under \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-(n-1)g\),
  \[
  \|M\|\le C(n)\operatorname{Vol}(M,g),
  \]
  and scaling a \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge0\) metric by \(\varepsilon^2\) forces the volume bound to zero. By contrast, the inspected negative-Einstein obstructions rely on four-dimensional Chern–Weil positivity or the \(\Lambda^2=\Lambda^+\oplus\Lambda^-\) splitting and do not carry over in the same form to \(n\ge5\). This explains the method gap but is not a theorem that no higher-dimensional obstruction exists [Steps 94–96].

- Dimensions two and three remain mathematically settled at ordinary theorem level. Uniformization gives a constant-curvature metric on every closed surface. In dimension three, a strict positive Ricci interval and Hamilton’s theorem give a spherical space form and positive Einstein metric; a sufficiently tight negative normalized branch follows through the three-dimensional Ricci-to-sectional formula and geometrization. These statements have not been faithfully formalized in Lean [Steps 70–72, 83].

- Lean strategy remains downstream of the geometry. `MetricScalingNormalization.lean` gives a compiling, placeholder-free bundled normalization artifact and corrected a real scaling error, but assumes a smooth torsion-free metric-compatible connection with realized curvature rather than constructing the Levi–Civita stack. `Step99RealLinearPQ.lean` proves only the real-linear \(P/Q\) kernel criterion. # Results, Observations, and Their Meaning

## Exact proposition, interval structure, and proved scope

- The target is the user’s exact smooth-category statement: for each \(n\ge2\), there should exist dimension-only \(c_n<C_n\) such that every closed connected smooth \(n\)-manifold carrying
  \[
  c_ng\le \operatorname{Ric}_g\le C_ng
  \]
  carries some smooth Einstein metric, with no required relation between input and output metrics and no sign restriction on the Einstein constant. The cumulative notes and constructions remain partial results, reductions, and test families; they do not prove or refute the complete proposition. [Steps 1, 68–99]

- Constant rescaling gives the strict-sign normal forms. If \(0<c<C\), set
  \[
  h=\frac{c+C}{2}g,\qquad
  \delta=\frac{C-c}{C+c}<1;
  \]
  then
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_h-h\|_{\mathrm{op},h}\le\delta.
  \]
  If \(c<C<0\), set
  \[
  h=-\frac{c+C}{2}g,\qquad
  \delta=\frac{C-c}{-(c+C)}<1;
  \]
  then
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_h+h\|_{\mathrm{op},h}\le\delta.
  \]
  Earlier reciprocal scaling formulas were corrected in Step 88, independently detected by the Lean normalization artifact. [Steps 1, 3, 23–25, 84, 88]

- If \(0\) lies in the interior of \([c,C]\), every closed manifold lies in the hypothesis class after rescaling any metric. For \(n\ge3\), Lohkamp’s theorem similarly puts every closed manifold into every interval \([c,0]\), \(c<0\), after rescaling a metric with \(\operatorname{Ric}<0\). Thus a necessary prerequisite for an all-dimensional refutation is a closed no-Einstein manifold in the tested dimension. This is not an equivalence and does not exclude unknown high-dimensional counterexamples. No certified no-Einstein reservoir suitable for the full pinching problem was found in \(n\ge5\). [Steps 24, 58, 84–88]

- Dimension four has a complete interval-type reduction. The product metric on \(S^1\times S^3\) has \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge0\), and scaling puts it in every interval \([0,C]\). It has no Einstein metric: an Einstein four-metric with \(\chi=0\) would be flat by Chern–Gauss–Bonnet, but a closed flat four-manifold has virtually \(\mathbb Z^4\) fundamental group, unlike \(\pi_1(S^1\times S^3)=\mathbb Z\). Lohkamp supplies negative Ricci metrics for \([c,0]\). Hence all crossing and boundary intervals fail in dimension four; only a strict positive branch
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<1
  \]
  or strict negative branch
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}+g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<1
  \]
  could establish the original proposition there. Refuting the original four-dimensional proposition requires defeating both strict branches. [Steps 83–85]

- A strict-branch refutation may use a varying family of no-Einstein manifolds \(M_i\) with defects \(\delta_i\to0\); it does not require one fixed manifold admitting arbitrarily pinched metrics. A fixed-manifold family would be stronger. [Steps 58, 85]

- Dimensions \(2\) and \(3\) are settled at ordinary mathematical level. Uniformization gives constant-curvature metrics on every closed surface. In dimension three, a fixed positive interval such as
  \[
  \tfrac12g\le\operatorname{Ric}\le\tfrac32g
  \]
  gives positive Ricci curvature, and Hamilton/geometrization imply a spherical space form and hence an Einstein metric. A sufficiently tight negative Ricci branch forces negative sectional curvature through the three-dimensional Ricci–sectional formula and then a hyperbolic metric through geometrization. These geometric arguments have not been faithfully formalized in Lean. [Steps 1, 5, 23–25, 70–74, 83]

## Four-dimensional Chern–Weil accounting

- If
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<\tfrac12,
  \]
  then
  \[
  \beta(\delta)\operatorname{Vol}
  \le8\pi^2\chi-\int|W|^2
  \le a(\delta)\operatorname{Vol},
  \]
  where
  \[
  \beta(\delta)=
  \begin{cases}
  \frac23(1-\delta)^2,&0\le\delta\le\frac13,\\[1mm]
  \frac23(1+\delta)(1-2\delta),&\frac13\le\delta<\frac12,
  \end{cases}
  \qquad
  a(\delta)=\frac23(1+\delta)^2.
  \]
  Hence \(\chi>0\) and
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}\le\frac{8\pi^2\chi}{\beta(\delta)}.
  \]
  If \(\delta<(1+\sqrt3)^{-1}\), tight pinching implies strict Hitchin–Thorpe. Ordinary Hitchin–Thorpe violators therefore cannot test sufficiently tight positive or negative branches. [Steps 4, 18, 72]

- For an Einstein four-metric with \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\),
  \[
  8\pi^2(2\chi\pm3\tau)
  =4\int|W^\pm|^2+\frac43\lambda^2\operatorname{Vol},
  \]
  and
  \[
  \int|W^\pm|^2
  =2\pi^2(2\chi\pm3\tau)-\frac13\lambda^2\operatorname{Vol}.
  \]
  The scalar term depends on \(\lambda^2\); an earlier claimed sign change for \(\lambda<0\) was corrected. The adopted full-curvature convention is
  \[
  \int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2=8\pi^2\chi+\int|E|^2.
  \]
  Ricci-flat ALE spaces satisfy
  \[
  \frac1{8\pi^2}\int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2=\chi-\frac1{|\Gamma|};
  \]
  Eguchi–Hanson has energy \(12\pi^2\), not \(8\pi^2\). [Steps 2–3, 6, 9–10, 45, 82]

- For an arbitrary four-metric,
  \[
  \int|W^\pm|^2
  =2\pi^2(2\chi\pm3\tau)
  -\frac12\int\left(\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|E|^2}{2}\right).
  \]
  If \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) and volume tends to zero, the chiral Weyl energies approach topology-determined budgets. For \((\chi,\tau)=(8,0)\), each approaches \(32\pi^2\); for \((8,\pm2)\), they approach \(44\pi^2\) and \(20\pi^2\), up to orientation. [Steps 58, 60, 71–72, 79–80]

## Audited fixed-\(A_1\) logarithmic near-pinching construction

- The explicit radial core is obtained by differentiating a biaxial Einstein family \(q_\Lambda\) on the \(\mathcal O(-2)\) disk bundle at \(\Lambda=0\) and applying
  \[
  V=\frac5{72}(r^3-r^{-1})\partial_r.
  \]
  The resulting smooth tensor \(\widetilde h\) satisfies
  \[
  D\operatorname{Ric}_{EH}\widetilde h=g_{EH}
  \]
  and has the required quadratic far-field behavior. Independent symbolic differentiation reproduced the coefficients. This solves the radial inner source but does not by itself perform ambient matching. [Steps 68–69]

- For a Weyl tensor \(C\), set
  \[
  K_{ij}=-\tfrac13C_{ikjl}x^kx^l.
  \]
  Then \(K\) is trace-free, divergence-free, harmonic, radial-null, and satisfies \(D\operatorname{Ric}_eK=0\). For a radial logarithmic cutoff,
  \[
  D\operatorname{Ric}_e\!\left(\eta(\log r)K\right)
  =-\frac{\eta_{tt}+6\eta_t}{2r^2}K.
  \]
  This follows from
  \[
  \Delta(\eta K)
  =\left(\eta_{rr}+\frac7r\eta_r\right)K
  =\frac{\eta_{tt}+6\eta_t}{r^2}K.
  \]
  A logarithmically long annulus therefore interpolates the quadratic Weyl mismatch with defect \(O(1/L)\). [Steps 68–69, 83]

- Step 83 audited the full ten-dimensional Weyl-quadratic space: five \(\operatorname{Sym}^2_0(\Lambda^+)\) and five \(\operatorname{Sym}^2_0(\Lambda^-)\) basis sectors were checked for trace, divergence, Laplacian, radial contraction, and linearized Ricci vanishing. All basis checks passed. This excludes a hidden order-one defect from non-\(U(2)\) angular components at the product nodes. [Step 83]

- Under common radial normal gauge, \(O_2\) control of ALE tails and ambient even Taylor remainders, and fixed charts, markings, fillings, chiralities, and cutoffs, the raised-index error budget is:
  - core residual \(O(a^2+r^2)\);
  - inner cutoff terms
    \[
    O(b^2+a^4b^{-6}+a^4b^{-4})=O(a),\qquad b=a^{1/2};
    \]
  - logarithmic-annulus defect \(O(1/L)\);
  - ambient patch defect \(O(R^2)=O(a^{1/2})\), \(R=a^{1/4}\);
  - logarithmic length
    \[
    L=\log\frac{R}{8b}=\frac14|\log a|+O(1).
    \]
  Finitely many disjoint node balls give one global maximum constant. Thus every fixed marked \(A_1\) resolution satisfying these hypotheses carries metrics
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_a}-\sigma g_a\|_{\mathrm{op}}
  \le\frac{C}{|\log a|}\to0.
  \]
  This is a near-pinching theorem, not an exact Einstein desingularization theorem. [Steps 68–74, 83]

- Raw Eguchi–Hanson insertion fails: on \(t g_{EH}\), the endomorphism defect of
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{t g_{EH}}-\Lambda(tg_{EH})
  \]
  is order one. Earlier conformal, scalar, and radial least-squares repairs did not remove it; a recorded radial bolt residual was about \(4.7\times10^3\), with nonlinear defects around \(18\)–\(20\). These failures motivated the explicit Einstein-family core and raised-index audit. [Steps 65–66]

- The construction is sign-neutral and applies to every fixed chirality pattern on
  \[

  \]
  every fixed filling pattern of the 36-node negative mirror

## Log-critical modes and exact-obstruction limits

- For a degree-\(\ell\) homogeneous TT, harmonic, radial-null tensor \(K_\ell\) on \(\mathbb R^d/\Gamma\),
  \[
  o_\ell=r^{-(d+2\ell-2)}K_\ell
  \]
  is again TT, harmonic, and radial-null. The annular Wronskian coefficient is
  \[
  -\frac{d+2\ell-2}{2}I_{K_\ell}.
  \]
  For \(d=4,\ell=2\), this is \(-3I_K\). [Steps 69–74]

- The unweighted dual mass is
  \[
  H_2(b,R)=\log(R/b),\qquad
  H_\ell(b,R)=\frac{b^{2-\ell}-R^{2-\ell}}{\ell-2}\quad(\ell>2).
  \]
  Thus \(\ell=2\) is the unique logarithmically critical polynomial mode for the unweighted \(C^0\) Ricci-endomorphism problem. For \(\ell>2\), inverse-log behavior survives only in suitable weighted norms. The earlier proposed uniform all-\(\ell\) inverse-log obstruction was invalid. [Steps 73–74]

- The \(\ell=2\) flux gives only a conditional rate alternative
  \[
  \delta L\ge c,\qquad L\asymp|\log t|,
  \]
  under harmonic/Bianchi neck coordinates, ambient-tower subtraction, nonlinear weighted control, finite-node uniformity, and flux matching. It does not force the obstruction coefficient to vanish unless one knows, for example, \(\delta_iL_i\to0\). The explicit \(A_1\) families saturate the inverse-log scale. [Steps 59–63, 69–74]

- A \(k\)-th exact-gluing obstruction contributes \(O(t^k)\) as a \((0,2)\)-tensor on the scaled ALE core and \(O(t^{k-1})\) after raising an index. With \(t\sim a^2\), all \(k\ge2\) contributions are polynomially smaller than \(1/|\log a|\). Tight Ricci pinching therefore cannot force the full exact-obstruction tower to vanish. [Steps 48–50, 73–74]

## Gate 1: local projected obstruction

For the rank-one product curvature, any \(\zeta\in K\) uses only one of two kernel directions, so the complementary \(2\times2\) block retains a zero eigenvalue and its determinant vanishes. The structural protection is the two-dimensional kernel of rank-one bi-Kähler curvature, not merely \(\det R^\pm=0\). A generic one-dimensional-kernel curvature block would not enjoy this cancellation. [Steps 94–95]

  \[
  T^2=SO(2)_A\times SO(2)_B.

  The \(\beta=0\) subcircle acts with weight \(1\) on every kernel plane. A homogeneous quadratic equivariant map \(K\to K\) would require a monomial \(z^a\bar z^b\) with
  \[

  \]
  which has no integral solution. With \(T^2\)-equivariant charts, markings, cutoffs, and gauge, the projected quadratic local obstruction therefore vanishes. This enables, but does not itself solve, the cubic inter-node problem. [Steps 95–96]

## Corrected node characters and variational response

- Pole signs matter. At node \(j\), the kernel-plane character is
  \[
  \theta_j=s_A^j\alpha+\varepsilon_j s_B^j\beta,\qquad
  \sigma_j=\varepsilon_j s_A^js_B^j.
  \]
  A conjugate-linear anisotropic pair channel is allowed when
  \[
  \theta_i=\pm\theta_j,
  \]
  equivalently \(\sigma_i=\sigma_j\), not merely when source and receiver chiralities match. The resulting pair counts are:
  - all-compatible pattern: \(\sigma=(+,-,-,+)\), only two diagonal anisotropic pairs;
  - diagonal balanced pattern: all \(\sigma\) equal, all six pairs permit anisotropy;
  - adjacent balanced pattern: two anisotropic adjacent pairs.
  
  The earlier uniform-weight rule and the claims “opposite chirality is automatically isotropic” and “same chirality is automatically anisotropic” were false. [Steps 95–96]

- In complex kernel coordinates, a real-linear receiver equation has the form
  \[
  z\longmapsto Pz+Q\bar z.
  \]
  Its real determinant is
  \[
  |P|^2-|Q|^2,
  \]
  and it has nonzero kernel exactly when \(|P|=|Q|\). Both strict inequalities give an invertible map; the earlier statement that \(|Q|>|P|\) itself creates a kernel was wrong. This algebra was later formalized in Lean. [Steps 96–99]

- The finite-dimensional obstruction should be organized variationally, subject to a genuine fixed-volume Bianchi/Ebin slice and complement solution. A leading real quartic has schematic form
  \[
  f_4(\xi)=\sum_{i<j}
  \left[
  c_{ij}|\xi_i|^2|\xi_j|^2+
  \operatorname{Re}\!\left(q_{ij}\xi_i^2\overline{\xi_j}^{\,2}\right)
  \right]
  +\text{self/global terms},
  \]
  with reduced equation \(\partial f_4/\partial\bar\xi_j=0\). This imposes real symmetric isotropic coefficients and reciprocity
  \[
  q_{ji}=\overline{q_{ij}}
  \]
  after frame transport. Euler homogeneity forces any nonzero critical point of \(f_4\) to lie on \(f_4=0\). The kernel-plane phases are genuine smoothing/gluing parameters modulo the effective torus action; they cannot be frozen without justification. [Steps 97–98]

- The compatible KE locus gives a strong calibration but must be stated at the correct level. OSS and Biquard–Rollin support an open compatible smoothing locus in the local complex smoothing variables, and the raw spectral computations independently find vanishing same-chirality inter-node maps. In a fully calibrated LS chart, an open exact KE locus would force the compatible leading reduced potential to vanish identically. However, partial raw sectors need not vanish separately unless they have been assembled in the same physical normalization; the earlier nonzero AB parity components were not physical same-chirality coefficients. The full LS statement still requires automorphism quotient, fixed-volume slice, complement correction, and coordinate identification. [Steps 95–99]
