  \]
  symbolic jet calculations give
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^{V}
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}+\frac12|F|_h^2.
  \]
  Exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\) therefore implies
  \[
  \left(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|_h^2\right)w=2\lambda w.
  \]
  If the action degenerates at the orbit-space boundary, \(w\) is a positive Dirichlet ground state. Under \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\),
  \[
  \lambda_1^{\rm Dir}\le2(1+\delta).
  \]
  [Steps 12–13]

- The mixed Ricci equation gives
  \[
  d(wh_{IJ}*_BF^J)=0.
  \]
  Exact orthogonal transitivity is source-supported for the relevant simply connected Einstein \(T^2\)-setting, but no approximate orthogonal-transitivity theorem is known for merely pinched metrics. [Steps 12–13]

- In the twist-free diagonal \(T^k\) case,
  \[
  g=g_B+\sum_{I=1}^kp_I^2d\theta_I^2,\qquad w=\prod_Ip_I,
  \]
  one has
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^{V}
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w},
  \]
  and under normalized positive pinching,
  \[
  k(1-\delta)\le\lambda_1^{\rm Dir}\le k(1+\delta).
  \]
  This is an all-dimensional invariant identity, not an arbitrary-manifold theorem. [Steps 13, 17]

## Corrected diagonal toric system

- For
  \[
  g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2,\qquad
  w=pq,\qquad v=\log(p/q),
  \]
  the vertical equations are
  \[
  r_p+r_q=-\frac{\Delta w}{w},\qquad
  r_p-r_q=-\frac1w\operatorname{div}(w\nabla v),
  \]
  and
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}^{H}
  =K_Bg_B-\left[
  \nabla^2\log w+
  \frac12\bigl(d\log w\otimes d\log w+dv\otimes dv\bigr)
  \right].
  \]
  [Steps 14, 18]

- The corrected exact positive-Einstein warping equations are
  \[
  -\Delta_Bp=(1-K_B)p,\qquad
  -\Delta_Bq=(1-K_B)q.
  \]
  The earlier sign \(-\Delta p=(K_B-1)p\) was false. This correction also retracted the claimed identity \(\int K_Bw=\int w\). The correct Green calculation yields flux equipartition
  \[
  \Phi_p=\Phi_q=\int_\Omega w.
  \]
  Each warping function separately satisfies a mixed-boundary ground-state problem with eigenvalue \(1\). [Steps 25–26]

- The corrected orbit curvature relation is
  \[
  K_B
  =\frac14\bigl(|\nabla v|^2-|\nabla\log w|^2\bigr)
  =-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle.
  \]
  The earlier \(K_B\ge3\) assertion was false. Checks on \(S^2\times S^2\) and normalized \(S^4\) agree with the corrected formula. [Step 14]

- Near a rod, the edge equation and fixed-surface curvature are
  \[
  Q''+\bigl(1-2K_B|_{\rm edge}\bigr)Q=0,
  \qquad K_\Sigma=1-2K_B|_{\rm edge}.
  \]
  Unit endpoint slopes give
  \[
  \int_{\rm rod}(1-2K_{\rm edge})Q\,ds=2.
  \]
  For constant \(K_{\rm edge}=-A\),
  \[
  Q(s)=\frac{\sin(\sqrt{1+2A}\,s)}{\sqrt{1+2A}},\qquad
  L=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{1+2A}},\qquad
  \Phi=\frac{2}{1+2A},
  \]
  and, in the session’s torus-period normalization,
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_4=2\pi^2\sum_i\Phi_i
  =4\sum_iL_i^2.
  \]
  These reproduce \(24\pi^2\) for normalized \(S^4\), \(18\pi^2\) for normalized \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), and \(16\pi^2\) for \(S^2\times S^2\). [Steps 13–14, 20–21]

- Local corner expansions remain formally solvable with arbitrarily large \(A\). At a fixed point,
  \[
  a=b=-\frac{2A+1}{6},
  \]
  and a verified next order has
  \[
  q_{05}=\frac{(1+2A)^2}{120},\quad
  m_{40}=-\frac{A(2A+1)}{24},\quad
  p_{50}=\frac{22A^2+10A+1}{120},
  \]
  with the recorded mixed coefficients. Thus local parity, smoothness, and low-order Einstein equations impose no cap on \(A\); global filling and closure are the unresolved constraints. [Step 19]

- Periodic alternating labels
  \[
  (1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),\ldots
  \]
  yield even unimodular intersection forms consistent, in all tested cases, with sums of hyperbolic planes and therefore with \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\). A full Orlik–Raymond diffeomorphism proof is still required if this topology identification becomes theorem-critical. [Steps 18–19]

- The formal collapse adversary sets \(A_m=m^\alpha\), \(1<\alpha\le2\). Then
  \[
  L_m\sim\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2\,m^{\alpha/2}},
  \qquad
  \Phi_i\sim m^{-\alpha},
  \qquad
  \sum_i\Phi_i\sim m^{1-\alpha}\to0.
  \]
  It passes the tested rod ODEs, corner series, flux equations, signed Gauss–Bonnet scaling, and mixed spectral cancellation. It is not a global metric; variable-curvature filling, determinant closure, horizontal traceless equations, corner-to-interior matching, and stability under \(O(\delta)\) field-equation error remain unresolved. [Steps 19–21, 25–26]

## Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Kottler and local collapsed models

- The exact separated germ
  \[
  g=dr^2+p(r)^2d\theta^2+a(r)^2g_{S^2(\kappa)},
  \qquad \kappa=1+2A,
  \]
  satisfies
  \[
  a'=Ap,\qquad
  2aa''+(a')^2=\kappa-a^2,
  \]
  with first integral
  \[
  a(a')^2=\kappa(a-1)-\frac{a^3-1}{3}.
  \]
  Its second bolt occurs at
  \[
  a_+=\frac{-1+\sqrt{9+24A}}2,
  \]
  with surface-gravity ratio
  \[
  \mu=\frac{2a_++1}{a_+(a_++2)}.
  \]
  [Step 15]

- This is Euclidean Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Birmingham–Kottler,
  \[
  f(\rho)=1-\frac{2M}{\rho}-\frac{\rho^2}{3},
  \qquad
  M=\frac{A+\frac13}{(2A+1)^{3/2}}.
  \]
  Both bolts are smooth only when \(\mu=1\), hence \(A=0\); the matching is nondegenerate,
  \[
  \left.\frac{d\mu}{dA}\right|_{A=0}=-\frac43.
  \]
  This is a theorem for the separated cohomogeneity-one ansatz, not a universal theorem about two same-circle rods. Page later provided a direct counter-calibration to that overgeneralization. [Steps 15–17, 39]

- At large \(A\), scaling by \(\sqrt{2A}\) sends the local model to Euclidean Schwarzschild with mass \(\widehat M\to1/2\). Adjacent rods remain at finite rescaled distance because
  \[
  \sqrt{2A}\,L\to\pi.
  \]
  Thus the formal collapsed limit is better viewed as an infinite or periodic toric Ricci-flat rod chain with Schwarzschild-type bolts and corner transitions, not isolated ALE bubbles. [Steps 34–35]

- Atiyah–LeBrun edge-cone terms and smooth bulk energy are distinct. A rod conical defect is a period/surface-gravity defect along a codimension-two rod, not a corner defect. Any smoothing-energy argument must track scale and boundary transgression; bulk energy saturation alone cannot rule out period defects. [Steps 16, 35–37]

## Rod-period correction and noncompact Weyl probes

- Step 36’s inference that alternating Delzant labels imply “NUTs, not struts” was retracted. Adjacent rods do meet at codimension-four fixed points, but a conical singularity lies along a rod when the collapsing circle closes with the wrong global period. Labels \(v\) and \(-v\) generate the same unoriented circle subgroup, so nonadjacent rods impose repeated closure conditions for one global circle period. Emparan–Reall’s generalized Weyl source explicitly states that different rods for the same coordinate can demand incompatible periods. [Steps 36–37]

- A corrected finite noncompact Weyl-line probe partitions every axis interval between the two unbounded ends as a source for exactly one coordinate and enforces \(U_1+U_2=\log r\). For equal alternating rods, the same-label exponential period range is exactly
  \[
  \prod_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{2k+1}{2k}
  \]
  for \(n\) rods in one label class: \(3/2,15/8,35/16,315/128\) for \(n=2,3,4,5\). Interior differences are rational; the central pair ratio for even \(n\) is \((n+1)/n\). Symmetric truncations show the central mismatch tends to \(1+O(1/n)\), so the drift is predominantly an end/closure effect rather than a fixed local defect. [Steps 37–38]

- In this finite asymptotically Euclidean model, if all periods matched, positive mass rigidity would force the Ricci-flat space to be flat and hence bolt-free. This structurally explains the finite-chain mismatch, but it does not apply to a compact polygon or an infinite periodic chain. A single isolated rod has transfer matrix \(-I\); the mismatch is encoded by the inter-rod Weyl potential. [Step 38]

- These noncompact ratios cannot be imported as compact toric obstructions. The compact \(S^2\times S^2\) rectangle closes despite a noncompact four-rod ratio \(3/2\), and compact toric Einstein metrics such as Page and Chen–LeBrun–Weber contain repeated circle classes. The noncompact chain has asymptotic ends absent from the compact problem. [Steps 38–39]

## Known compact calibration and diagonal-sector scope

- From an explicit \(U(2)\)-invariant Page formula, the orbit-base metric has
  \[
  \int K_B\,dA\simeq7.6\times10^{-17},
  \]
  while \(K_B\) is nonconstant, ranging approximately over
  \[
  [-0.1051,\,0.0716].
  \]
  Two nonadjacent rods collapsing the same circle have equal slopes
  \(1.281701557864\) and \(1.281701557888\), relative difference \(1.9\times10^{-11}\); the common nonunit value reflects the chosen global lattice normalization. This is a successful unit test for the surface-gravity calculation and disproves “same-circle multiplicity plus nonzero \(K_B\) forces mismatch.” [Step 39]

- Page, CLW, and toric Kähler–Einstein del Pezzo metrics do not calibrate the diagonal twist-free equations because their fans have at least three unoriented circle classes. They remain calibrations for the general polar/non-diagonal theory. [Steps 39–41]

- Liu’s source was checked directly. Theorem 3.1 gives geometric polarity for a closed simply connected Einstein four-manifold with isometric \(T^2\)-action, and Proposition 5 states that a diagonal action forces a diagonal metric without assuming nonnegative sectional curvature. For
  \[
  h=\operatorname{diag}(p^2,q^2),
  \qquad h(v,v)=a^2p^2+b^2q^2,
  \]
  codimension-two collapse is possible only for \(v=\pm e_1\) or \(\pm e_2\); otherwise both factors vanish and one has a corner. Thus the alternating even-polygon actions are exactly the diagonal-action sector under Liu’s exact-Einstein hypotheses. [Steps 40–41]

- Liu’s machinery also shows that for fixed orbit metric \(g_\Sigma\), the invariant fiber metric is at most uniquely determined through the orbit-volume eigenfunction and a linear equation. Existence additionally requires nonlinear determinant closure
  \[
  \det(g^\Omega)=\phi^2,
  \]
  horizontal Einstein compatibility, positivity, edge derivative data, and corner smoothness. “Overdetermined” is therefore a valid compatibility description, but not a proved Fredholm count or rigidity theorem. [Steps 40–41]

- Step 40’s claimed product linearization was corrected. Directly linearizing the orbit-volume equation at the product square with \(g_\Sigma=e^{2\varepsilon s}g_0\) gives
  \[
  -(\Delta_0+2)\psi=4s\sin x\sin y,
  \]
  not the previously recorded equation involving \(\Delta s\). The claimed kernel/rescaling interpretation also ignored fixed-\(\Lambda\) rod derivative data. Product isolation in the full diagonal sector remains unproved. [Step 41]

- For regular constant-curvature right-angled polygons, a corrected finite-element computation uses Euclidean Dirichlet energy and Poincaré mass weight \(4/(1-r^2)^2\). For \(m=6\),
  \[
  \mu_6\approx6.973,\qquad
  A_{\rm eig}\approx0.2868,\qquad
  A_{\rm side}\approx0.2710,
  \]
  with \(\lambda_1\) at \(A_{\rm side}\approx1.88945\) and rod/side mismatch at \(A_{\rm eig}\approx1.84\%\). This numerically excludes only the regular constant-curvature submodel and corrects the earlier misleading \(68.7\%\) large-\(A\) emphasis. Variable-curvature orbit metrics remain open. [Steps 40–41]

## Positive noncollapsed Route A: balanced annuli and mode projection

- Ozuch’s exact-Einstein Taub/Pohozaev identity pairs the orbifold expansion
  \[
  g_o=e+H_2+O(r^3)
  \]
  with the ALE expansion
  \[
  g_b=e+H^4+O(r^{-5}).
  \]
  For Eguchi–Hanson,
  \[
  H^4=-\theta_1^-\circ\omega_1^+/(2r^4),
  \]
  and the first obstruction is a vector condition involving the relevant chiral curvature block. [Steps 30–31]

- The bilinear Wronskian scales as \(t^4\):
  \[
  r^3\bigl(H_2\partial(t^4H^4)-t^4H^4\partial H_2\bigr).
  \]
  The balanced radius is \(r=t^{2/3}\), where both pieces have size \(t^{4/3}\). A \(C^0\) Ricci residual contributes \(O(\delta r^6)=O(\delta t^4)\) on that shell. Global neck transport would instead accumulate uncontrolled error, so the target is a single balanced-annulus comparison. [Steps 32–33]

- On the flat \(A_1=\mathbb R^4/\{\pm1\}\) cone, the sanity indicial roots are
  \[
  \alpha=l,\qquad \alpha=-l-2.
  \]
  Antipodal parity keeps even \(l\). The \(l=0\) mass/volume channel is gauge/removable for the first obstruction; \(l=2\) is the first even nongauge pair \((2,-4)\), corresponding to \(H_2/H^4\). Wronskians pair only within the same angular harmonic, so a larger \(l=0\) mode is invisible to the \(l=2\) obstruction. This remains a model calculation rather than a complete Lichnerowicz–Bianchi representation theorem. [Steps 33–34]

- The previously proposed condition
  \[
  \delta\log(1/t)\to0
  \]
  was retracted. It arose from transporting the growing coefficient through the whole neck. In the bubble frame, on a fixed annulus \(\rho\in[1,R]\), the relative error is
  \[
  O(\delta\log R)+O(1/R),
  \]
  so the correct order is fixed \(R\), then \(\delta_i\to0\), then \(R\to\infty\). [Steps 34–36]

- A pointwise second-order limit
  \[
  k=\lim\frac{\widehat g_i-g_{\rm EH}}{t_i^2}
  \]
  is not justified by \(C^0\) Ricci pinching: harmonic-coordinate regularity is only \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,p}\), and the CZ spike demonstrates the endpoint obstruction. Step 42 proposed a derivative-free replacement: project metric values onto the \(l=2\) tensor harmonic, obtaining a radial coefficient that schematically satisfies
  \[
  f''+\frac3\rho f'-\frac8{\rho^2}f=O(\delta),
  \]
  with homogeneous modes \(\rho^2,\rho^{-4}\) and constant Wronskian
  \[
  \rho^3(f_1f_2'-f_2f_1')=-6
  \]
  after normalization. On a fixed dyadic annulus, this could recover second-order mode information from first-order metric convergence. [Step 42]

- This is a promising proof framework, not yet a theorem. Missing interfaces include construction of a suitable Bianchi/volume/tangent-cone gauge under the available annular regularity, projection onto all three EH obstruction tensors, control of nonlinear and angular-mode coupling, treatment of the harmonic-radius bad set and cutoffs, and identification of the ALE \(r^{-4}\) coefficient and orbifold \(r^2\) coefficient. The recorded \(\Lambda\)-source contribution \(\Lambda t^2c_{-4}/24\) is a model calculation and should not be used as a completed matching formula. [Steps 42–45]

## Chiral first obstruction and topology

- For positive Einstein normalization, define
  \[
  R_\pm=W_\pm+\frac{\Lambda}{3}I.
  \]
  Ozuch’s obstruction depends on the orientation of the EH bubble. For a specific gluing parameter \(\zeta^\pm\), the coefficients have the form
  \[
  \lambda_k(\zeta^\pm)
  =c\langle R_\pm(p)\zeta^\pm,\zeta^\pm_{(k)}\rangle.
  \]
  The actual necessary condition is therefore
  \[
  R_\pm(p)\zeta^\pm=0.
  \]
  The weaker statement \(\det R_\pm(p)=0\) only says that some kernel direction exists after allowing the EH parameter to vary. [Steps 43, 45]

- For a positive Kähler–Einstein four-orbifold in the complex orientation,
  \[
  W_+=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2\Lambda}{3},
  -\frac{\Lambda}{3},-\frac{\Lambda}{3}\right),
  \qquad
  R_+=\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda,0,0).
  \]
  Thus the Kähler-compatible chiral block has a two-dimensional kernel, but a particular EH direction must still lie in that kernel. The opposite block \(R_-\) is not constrained by Kähler geometry and generically obstructs reversed bubbles. Step 42’s description of \(\det R_+=0\) as a universal ceiling was therefore inverted: chirality can recover a generic admissibility/\(b_+=1\) mechanism for Kähler limits. [Steps 42–45]

- In a pure \(A_1\)/EH resolution model, an orientation-compatible EH contributes a negative compactly supported class, while a reversed EH contributes a positive one. If a Kähler orbifold has \(b_+=1\), reaching a target with larger \(b_+\) forces positive compactly supported rank and hence opposite-chirality obstruction conditions. For general ALE spaces or bubble trees, the correct invariant is total positive compactly supported intersection rank, not a count of individual EH bubbles. [Step 43]

- This bookkeeping assumes the orbifold limit is Kähler or conformally Kähler. Cheeger–Naber gives only a positive Einstein orbifold. No theorem in the record says every positive Einstein four-orbifold is conformally Kähler. Derdziński-type results require a global or dense-set spectral condition; finitely many kernel conditions at bubble points do not suffice. [Steps 33, 43–45]

- Concrete model checks:
  - Round \(S^4\) has \(R_+=\frac{\Lambda}{3}I\), so EH bubbling is first-order obstructed.
  - Fubini–Study \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) is self-dual in its complex orientation, with \(R_-=\frac{\Lambda}{3}I\), so reversed EH bubbling is obstructed everywhere.
  - Equal-radius \(S^2\times S^2\) is Kähler for both orientations and has
    \[
    R_+=R_-=\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda,0,0).
    \]
    Both signs therefore admit possible kernel directions at first order, although not every gluing direction passes. [Steps 31, 43–45]

## Bi-Kähler quotient test and its corrected meaning

- The diagonal half-turn quotient
  \[
  (S^2\times S^2)/\mathbb Z_2
  \]
  has four fixed points where the action is \(-I_4\), hence four \(A_1\) orbifold singularities. The product Einstein metric descends, and at every singularity both chiral blocks are degenerate as above. This provides a genuine singular local model on which first-order determinant degeneracy is available for both bubble orientations. [Steps 44–45]

- The product computation does **not** prove that every EH parameter is unobstructed; the vector must lie in the two-dimensional kernel. Nor does it construct a near-Einstein sequence or exact desingularization. It demonstrates a concrete exceptional locus where first-order chirality alone cannot rule out all orientations. [Step 45]

- The corrected Euler/energy decomposition is
  \[
  \chi_{\rm orb}\bigl((S^2\times S^2)/\mathbb Z_2\bigr)=2,
  \]
  so the orbifold contribution is \(16\pi^2\), while each \(A_1\)/EH bubble contributes \(12\pi^2\). Hence
  \[
  16\pi^2+4(12\pi^2)=64\pi^2.
  \]
  This equals \(8\pi^2\chi\) for the proposed \(\chi=8\) resolution, but it is an Euler/Chern–Gauss–Bonnet consistency identity, not evidence that no further analytic obstruction exists. [Steps 44–45]

- If \(r\) of the four EH pieces are orientation-reversed, rational intersection bookkeeping gives
  \[
  b_+=1+r,\qquad b_-=5-r.
  \]
  Signature zero forces \(r=2\), hence \(b_+=b_-=3\). The quotient’s underlying topological space is simply connected by the fixed-point version of Armstrong’s theorem. However, Step 44’s assertion that the resolution is spin/even and therefore has form \(3H\) was not proved: local spin liftability and spinness of each EH piece do not automatically match the boundary spin structures on \(\mathbb{RP}^3\). Without a separate parity proof, the strict conclusion is only the rational rank/signature data. Even if evenness were proved, Freedman would give a homeomorphism classification, not diffeomorphism to the standard \(\#_3(S^2\times S^2)\). [Steps 44–45]

- More generally, the corrected first-order picture is a dichotomy:
  1. generic non-Kähler limits may be obstructed on both chiral sides;
  2. Kähler limits automatically have one pinned degenerate block while reversed bubbles test the generically nondegenerate opposite block;
  3. an exceptional locus—extreme examples being bi-Kähler quotients of equal-radius \(S^2\times S^2\)—has both blocks degenerate at relevant points.
  
  Parallel Kähler forms for both orientations imply a parallel rank-two splitting, and a positive Einstein metric then locally splits into equal-curvature surfaces; this classifies the extreme bi-Kähler case locally as a quotient of \(S^2(r)\times S^2(r)\). Intermediate pointwise degeneracy without global bi-Kähler structure remains unclassified. [Step 45]

- The session’s \(\Lambda=0\) higher-obstruction evidence cautions against assuming that escalating to higher-order matching will close the exceptional locus: Ozuch’s \(T^4/\mathbb Z_2\) calculations produce 57 general and 84 stable Ricci-flat constraints, yet a 14-dimensional chessboard family satisfies all 84. This does not prove failure at \(\Lambda>0\), but no positive-\(\Lambda\) source in the record establishes closure. [Steps 31–33, 44–45]

## LeBrun–Ozuch classification and topology filter

- LeBrun–Ozuch 2026 Theorem B assumes an exact sequence of compact positive Einstein four-manifolds, a Hermitian/conformally Kähler Einstein orbifold limit with a genuine singularity, and admissibility/expected topology of the ALE bubbles. Under those hypotheses, Theorem 4.1 forces Del Pezzo topology with \(\pi_1=0\), \(b_+=1\), \(b_-\le8\). [Step 33]

- The chirality analysis gives a possible mechanism for generic admissibility rather than making it automatic: at a Kähler limit, opposite-orientation bubbles must satisfy nontrivial \(R_-\)-kernel conditions. But the theorem cannot be invoked merely from finitely many determinant conditions, and bi-Kähler exceptional models show why opposite orientations cannot be excluded universally at first order. [Steps 43–45]

- Conditional on the actual LeBrun–Ozuch hypotheses, \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), \(k\ge2\), is excluded from the classified branch because its even form \(kH\) has \(b_+=k\), whereas the only even/spin Del Pezzo member is \(S^2\times S^2\). This remains a conditional topological filter, not a theorem for arbitrary pinched degeneration. [Step 33]

- Constant rescaling leaves the Ricci \((0,2)\)-tensor unchanged but rescales its endomorphism relative to the metric; bubble rescaling suppresses the Ricci endomorphism quadratically. These facts control branch normalization and Ricci-flat blow-up limits. [Steps 1, 3, 9]

Approximate-to-exact arguments must use weak projections, harmonic-coordinate finite-\(p\) control, PDE structure, symmetry identities, or scale-adapted covers rather than universal pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-regularity. - In dimension four, tight pinching gives strong global topology and energy budgets. Under noncollapse and no bubbling it gives Einstein existence on the same smooth topology; under bubbling it reduces the problem to annular obstruction transfer. Over unbounded-\(\chi\) families, defect-to-zero sequences must collapse. [Steps 8–9, 18, 30–45]

- Exact Einstein collapse means that noncollapse cannot be a theorem conclusion. The main unresolved positive-collapse question is whether every tightly pinched collapsed topology is Einstein-compatible. The formal toric family is a concrete stress model but not a metric, while known lens/KK collapses are compatible. [Steps 6–7, 19–29, 34–45]

  from exact Ozuch theory to merely \(C^0\)-pinched sequences remains unproved. [Steps 42–45]

Its energy total is topological consistency, its smooth topology is unresolved because parity and diffeomorphism type were not proved, and it shows only that first-order local chirality has an exceptional locus—not that all noncollapsed degeneration is possible or unobstructed. ### Decisions and Recorded Reasons

- The target remains unchanged: prove or strictly refute Yau Problem 26 for every \(n\ge2\), for all closed connected smooth manifolds and arbitrary smooth metrics satisfying a dimension-only two-sided Ricci interval, with no extra noncollapse, sectional-curvature, topology, Kähler, symmetry, proximity, or sign assumptions. The quantifiers were normalized into positive and negative branches: in a fixed dimension, proving either normalized branch suffices for that sign, while refutation requires arbitrarily tight same-sign pinching on manifolds carrying no Einstein metric of any sign [Step 1].

- The first exploratory stage considered Min-Oo negative stability, positive compactness/collapse, prescribed-Ricci flexibility, orbifold/ALE resolution, topological and gauge-theoretic obstruction, and explicit model computations. A negative no-Einstein sequence with defect tending to zero must therefore escape through diameter growth, full-curvature concentration, collapse, or related degeneration; exact large-diameter hyperbolic manifolds later reinforced that this cannot be the endpoint of a general negative proof [Steps 1, 22].

- The first Calabi/ALE-resolution shortcut to a counterexample was rejected. Weighted or \(L^p\) smallness of a gluing remainder can coexist with an order-one nonscalar Ricci endomorphism on the ALE core, and separate singularities cannot cancel this in pointwise supremum norm. Surviving versions require local obstruction vanishing, relative obstruction decay, or a fundamentally different construction [Step 1].

- A major Step-2 LeBrun conclusion was retracted after the user identified a factor-four scalar-curvature error. For \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\) in four dimensions, \(s=4\lambda\); the corrected thresholds are \(k\ge2A/3\) from the scalar estimate and \(k\ge A/3\) from the refined mixed scalar–Weyl estimate. The distinction between an individual basic-class square \(A-k\) and the convex-hull/self-dual projection lower bound \((a^+)^2\ge A\) was also repaired [Steps 2–3].

- The valid LeBrun residue was retained as a stable-integral obstruction principle: if an all-metric curvature inequality has a strict gap from its Einstein equality value, a near-Einstein metric can pay the gap only through \(O(\delta^2)\operatorname{Vol}\) trace-free Ricci energy. In the recorded refined family,
  \[
  \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\ge

  Fixed \(p>1/3\) gives a uniform negative pinching gap; the apparent \(1/\sqrt A\) weakening came only from moving \(p\) toward the zero-margin boundary [Step 3].

Even success would address only a normalized negative branch in dimension four, and refuting the original four-dimensional proposition would also require failure of the positive branch. Known positive-Einstein obstruction mechanisms tended either to exclude the pinched input itself or to be automatically avoided under sufficiently tight positive pinching [Steps 3–4, 18].

- It was recorded that an admissible four-dimensional interval cannot straddle zero on a known no-Einstein manifold: rescaling any metric drives its Ricci endomorphism toward zero, so every fixed interval with \(c_4<0<C_4\) eventually contains it. Any possible interval must therefore be same-sign; this does not settle either normalized branch [Step 3].

- Four-dimensional Chern–Gauss–Bonnet was chosen as the shared accounting system:
  \[

  Under \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\), the pointwise-optimal coefficient

Berger collapse with a fixed connection becomes anisotropic, but round lens-space quotients and their products are exactly Einstein and collapse. Collapsed hyperbolic cusp/tube and \(S^1_\ell\times B^3\) models instead showed that raw downstairs \(L^2\) energy plus a dimension-only Sobolev constant cannot imply pointwise curvature control; the Sobolev constant degenerates like \(\ell^{-1/4}\) [Steps 21–22].

Its unresolved load-bearing pieces include nested weak tensor-energy inequalities, critical \(H_2\to H_3\) steps, finite-neighbor leakage, current-time critical-product control, and volume-normalized chart selection [Steps 22–24].

- A pure Chern–Weil/Hitchin–Thorpe endpoint for that negative route was rejected because tight pinching already yields strict Hitchin–Thorpe. The actual proposed endpoint—critical Ishida–LeBrun/Seiberg–Witten calibration plus chart/projector arguments—could at most prove a fixed-topology or special-family four-dimensional negative gap. It would not establish unrestricted \(P_4^-\), the positive branch, dimensions \(n\ge5\), or the full proposition [Step 22].

- After this scope audit, the work returned to Explore for \(n\ge5\). No source inspected supplied a closed \(n\ge5\) manifold known to admit no Einstein metric of any sign. Homogeneous nonexistence concerns invariant metrics only and does not imply no Einstein metric on the smooth manifold. High-dimensional refutation would require both a major no-Einstein existence result and an independent tight-pinching construction [Steps 22–23].

- The high-dimensional landscape was organized by the containment principle:
  \[
  P_n^+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \{\text{closed \(n\)-manifolds admitting sufficiently tight positive pinching}\}
  \subset
  \{\text{closed \(n\)-manifolds admitting an Einstein metric}\},
  \]
  with the analogous negative formulation. If every closed \(n\)-manifold admits some Einstein metric, the Yau–26 conclusion is automatic there; if a no-Einstein manifold exists, refutation still requires placing it in a tightly pinched class. The left-hand pinching class is poorly characterized in \(n\ge5\) [Steps 23–25].

- Anderson 1989 and Ye 1993 were recorded as bibliographic anchors only. Runtime access did not provide theorem text, so exact hypotheses were not imported. Their route obligation was later partly reopened for the noncollapsed bubble route because Anderson-type harmonic-radius/\(\varepsilon\)-regularity, unlike flow smoothing, may be directly relevant there; current local sources still do not supply the original Anderson text [Steps 23–24, 35].

- Lohkamp/Gao–Yau negative-Ricci flexibility and positive-scalar-curvature surgery were judged insufficient for Yau–26: they provide one-sided curvature or scalar information, not normalized two-sided almost-Einstein pinching. Prescribed-Ricci and homogeneous constructions likewise do not bridge to arbitrary closed metrics [Step 23].

- The proposed extension of the Step-6 Bochner obstruction to every odd-dimensional base was tested and disproved. In a constant-length principal-circle metric, exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) is equivalent, under the stated norm convention, to
  \[
  |\phi|^2=2,\qquad d_B^*\phi=0,\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_B=g_B+\tfrac12\phi\circ\phi,
  \]
  with \(d\phi=0\) automatic from connection curvature. Taking
  \[
  B=S^2_{\operatorname{Ric}=2}\times N^d_{\operatorname{Ric}=1},
  \qquad \phi=\sqrt2\,\omega_{S^2},
  \]
  and Chern number \(q\) gives exact Einstein collapse on
  \[
  (S^3(\sqrt2)/\mathbb Z_q)\times N^d
  \]
  in every total dimension \(n=d+3\ge5\). The four-dimensional obstruction is special because the remaining one-dimensional base factor cannot satisfy \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) [Step 24].

- This exact family strengthened the decision that positive collapse must be characterized rather than excluded. All explicit collapse families computed so far are Einstein-compatible. The proposed all-dimensional architecture is to extract nilpotent/orbifold fibration structure from pinching, identify abelian or graded Kaluza–Klein equations, and promote compatible approximate data to an Einstein metric on the same topology. The missing bridge is from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching to controlled submersion geometry and then to topology-preserving deformation [Step 24].

- Step 25 corrected another sign error. The earlier individual warping equation
  \[
  -\Delta_Bp=(K_B-1)p
  \]
  was wrong; the correct equation is
  \[
  -\Delta_Bp=(1-K_B)p,
  \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
  (-\Delta_B+K_B)p=p,
  \]
  with the symmetric equation for \(q\). This removes the false identity \(\int K_Bw=\int w\); Green’s identity gives only flux equipartition \(\Phi_p=\Phi_q=\int w\) [Step 25].

- “No interior curvature constraint” was subsequently narrowed. The mixed-boundary eigenvalue statements
  \[
  (-\Delta_B+K_B)p=p,\qquad
  (-\Delta_B+K_B)q=p
  \]
  were corrected in substance to the symmetric \(p,q\) equations and remain genuine variational interior constraints. The formal \(\alpha\)-family avoids them through exact collar cancellation: endpoint vanishing along a short rod creates tangential eigenvalue \(\pi^2/L^2\sim2A\), offsetting the potential well \(K_B=-A\) and forcing a hyperbolic transverse profile. Remaining toric freedom is concentrated at the corner-to-interior junction and higher-order matching, not in another coarse integral identity [Steps 25–26].

- With the corrected equations, the toric verdict became only “BREAK-compatible at the level of all tested local and integral constraints.” For constant edge curvature,
  \[
  G_i=\int(-K_B)Q_i\,ds=\frac{2A}{1+2A}
  \]
  tends to \(1\), while \(\Phi_i=2-2G_i\to0\). For \(A_m=m^\alpha\), \(\int w=m/(1+2A_m)\to0\) when \(\alpha>1\). No verified integral identity forces a uniform lower bound, but no smooth global pinched metric has been constructed. A BUILD theorem would require genuinely global PDE solvability or a junction obstruction [Step 25].

- The initial all-dimensional “abelian forcing” claim was deliberately weakened after carrying the full vertical geometry. Milnor’s Heisenberg Ricci pattern alone does not force brackets to vanish, because twist \(A\), second fundamental form \(T\), and mean curvature can compensate it. A rank argument excludes \(H_3\) over a two-dimensional base only in the totally geodesic \(T=0\) case; it is not the desired general theorem [Steps 25–26].

- The lower-Ricci source scope was fixed precisely. Kapovitch–Wilking/Naber–Zhang give almost-nilpotent short-loop groups and rank bounds under lower Ricci curvature; smooth infra-nil fibrations require additional maximal-rank, rewinding-volume, and regular-base hypotheses, and do not automatically control the original metric’s \(A,T,N\). Arbitrary \(C^0\)-Ricci pinching has not been converted into a controlled O’Neill system [Step 26].

- A \(T\)-active diagonal cohomogeneity-one Heisenberg model disproved pointwise Milnor-only forcing. For
  \[
  g=dt^2+a(t)^2(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)+c(t)^2\theta_3^2,
  \qquad [E_1,E_2]=E_3,
  \]
  with
  \[
  b=\frac c{a^2},\quad k_1=\frac{a'}a,\quad k_3=\frac{c'}c,\quad H=2k_1+k_3,
  \]
  the Ricci components are
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{00}=-2(k_1'+k_1^2)-(k_3'+k_3^2),
  \]
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{11}=\operatorname{Ric}_{22}
  =-\frac{b^2}{2}-k_1'-Hk_1,\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_{33}
  =\frac{b^2}{2}-k_3'-Hk_3.
  \]
  Local exact positive-Einstein solutions can have arbitrarily large \(b\), provided \(|T|\sim b\) and the relative bracket scale changes rapidly [Step 26].

- The model was sharpened into a quantitative positive-sign theorem. Restoring the Einstein constant \(\Lambda\), the vertical equations give the preserved constraint
  \[
  C_\Lambda=b^2+4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+4\Lambda=0,\qquad C_\Lambda'=-2HC_\Lambda.
  \]
  The exact algebraic identities are
  \[
  2|T|^2-(b^2+4\Lambda)
  =2(2k_1+k_3)^2-C_\Lambda,
  \]
  \[
  4((\log b)')^2-5(b^2+4\Lambda)
  =4(3k_1+k_3)^2-5C_\Lambda.
  \]
  Hence on the exact constraint surface,
  \[
  |T|^2\ge\frac{b^2+4\Lambda}{2},\qquad
  |(\log b)'|^2\ge\frac54(b^2+4\Lambda).
  \]
  Under componentwise \(|\rho_i-\Lambda|\le\delta\), both bounds survive with \(b^2+4\Lambda\) replaced by \(b^2+4\Lambda-8\delta\) [Steps 26–27].

- For \(\Lambda>0\) and \(\delta<\Lambda/2\), the normalized Heisenberg bracket \(b\) has no critical point in the regular diagonal model. Large \(b\) can only occur in a thin high-curvature shell; it cannot persist on a plateau. This was accepted as quantitative model-level abelian forcing, not as a theorem for arbitrary nilpotent collapse [Step 27].

- Restoring \(\Lambda\) revealed the positive/negative sign asymmetry. The complex-hyperbolic horosphere data
  \[
  \Lambda=-\frac32,\qquad
  b=1,\qquad k_1=-\frac12,\qquad k_3=-1
  \]
  satisfy the constraint with \((\log b)'=0\), validating the moving-frame derivation against a known Einstein metric and giving a stable nonabelian bracket plateau in negative Einstein geometry. This connects the model to cusp and Margulis-tube behavior that obstructs simple negative-branch compactness and smoothing arguments [Steps 27–28].

- The closed-model consequence was stated with explicit endpoint assumptions. A periodic regular-orbit model is impossible because a positive periodic \(b\) must have a critical point. For a compact interval with ordinary smooth tubular endpoints, the boundary Heisenberg nilmanifold must arise as the central-circle boundary of a disk bundle over \(T^2\); hence \(c\to0\), \(a\to a_0>0\), and \(b=c/a^2\to0\) at both ends, forcing an interior maximum. Therefore no compact closed positive-pinched model of this diagonal \(H_3\), one-dimensional-base, no-twist type exists when \(\delta<\Lambda/2\). Orbifold, edge, nonordinary singular endpoints, twist-active higher-base systems, and general infranil collapse are outside the theorem [Step 27].

- The algebraic kernel of the Step-27 model theorem was formalized in `workspace/proofs/Step27H3Algebra.lean`. Lean verified the exact identities, pinched \(8\delta\)-loss bounds, and nonvanishing of the bracket rate, with strict dependency checks and no placeholders. The moving-frame Ricci derivation, endpoint topology, and smooth polar behavior remain ordinary mathematics rather than Lean-formalized differential geometry [Step 27].

- Step 28 replaced the ansatz-dependent H3 argument with a general Bochner center bound. A central circle field \(Z\) on a compact nilmanifold fibre is Killing, and
  \[
  \int|\nabla Z|^2=\int\operatorname{Ric}(Z,Z)
  \]
  gives, using the fibre Koszul formula for \(H_3\),
  \[
  \langle b^2\rangle_{|Z|^2}\le 2(\Lambda+\delta).
  \]
  The result is ansatz-free, dimension-free at the level of central directions, and does not require \(A,T\), twist, or a cohomogeneity-one structure. It subsumes the Step-27 model bound in weighted \(L^2\), but it requires an exact or scale-correct almost-Killing central field [Step 28].

- TTCS verification of Step 28 imposed three corrections that were accepted. First, compact Lie algebras have no nonabelian nilpotent subalgebras, so the full Heisenberg group cannot act isometrically on a closed manifold; only the central circle can. Second, the quotient-induction architecture has a gap because the Bochner center bound controls the fibre bracket but not pointwise horizontal connection curvature \(|\phi|\). Third, the almost-Killing threshold is better than first stated: \(\tau=O(\varepsilon)\) suffices for normalized bracket vanishing. A later observation in Step 28 showed the same Bochner identity also gives a weighted \(L^2\) average bound \(\langle|\phi|^2\rangle\le4(\Lambda+\delta)\), narrowing the gap to average-to-pointwise rather than absence of any twist bound [Step 28].

- Step 28 also derived the exact Weitzenböck almost-Killing correction
  \[
  \int|\nabla Z|^2
  =\int\operatorname{Ric}(Z,Z)+\frac12\int|\sigma|^2-\frac14\int(\operatorname{tr}\sigma)^2,
  \]
  where \(\sigma={\cal L}_Zg\). This made the Bochner bridge depend quadratically on the Lie-derivative error. The algebraic kernels were formalized in `workspace/proofs/Step28BochnerKilling.lean`, including the negative-Ricci Killing vanishing sign and the center bracket bound. This remains a partial formalization, not differential geometry or Yau–26 [Step 28].

- Step 29 sharpened the allocation in dimension four. A nilpotent collapse fibre in a four-manifold has dimension at most three, hence is abelian or \(H_3\), so every fibre bracket lands in the center. Therefore, once a central exact or scale-correct almost-Killing field exists, the Step-28 Bochner identity controls all fibre brackets in weighted \(L^2\). Quotient induction and pointwise horizontal-twist control are not the immediate four-dimensional bracket-control crux [Step 29].

- Step 29 tested and demoted pointwise \(|\phi|^2\) as an execution target. A local Kaluza–Klein Ricci-jet calculation for
  \[
  g=e^{2\psi}(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)+e^{2u}(d\theta+A)^2
  \]
  with \(A=-(B y/2)dx+(B x/2)dy\) showed \(\operatorname{Ric}(0)=\Lambda g(0)\) for arbitrary \(S=B^2\) after choosing
  \[
  H=(S-2\Lambda)/6,\quad
  p_a=-(4\Lambda+7S)/24,\quad
  p_c=(5S-4\Lambda)/24.
  \]
  Thus a pointwise twist spike can be hidden by a dilaton Hessian and base Ricci 2-jet, analogous to the Step-11 opposite-warping cancellation. The reliable conclusion is the exact point-jet algebra, not a finite-ball counterexample [Step 29].

- Step 29 also verified that noncentral \(H_3\) fields cannot replace the central direction: for a unit noncentral left-invariant field, \(|{\cal L}_Xg|^2=2b^2\), so the almost-Killing error is the same scale as the bracket being controlled and the Weitzenböck inequality becomes vacuous. Central directions are structurally special [Step 29].

- The real four-dimensional positive-collapse bridge was restated: produce central almost-Killing fields with scale-comparable length and
  \[
  \int|{\cal L}_Zg|^2/\int|Z|^2=O(1)
  \]
  at the collapse scale from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching alone, without bounded full curvature. Cheeger–Fukaya–Gromov would supply this under bounded \(|\mathrm{Rm}|\), but Step-11 forbids assuming that; Kapovitch–Wilking/Naber–Zhang short-loop nilpotence gives group structure, not invariant metrics or Lie-derivative control [Step 29].

- A variational almost-Killing proposal was introduced and left speculative: define \(Z\) by minimizing \(\int|{\cal L}_Zg|^2\), or for radial bubble channels the conformal-Killing energy \(\int|({\cal L}_Zg)^\circ|^2\), and connect this to almost-splitting Hessian estimates and scale selection. TTCS emphasized that variational minimizers are not automatically Ozuch’s harmonic ALE vector fields; for collapse the almost-line hypothesis is close to normalized bracket smallness itself [Step 30].

- Step 30 reopened the dormant four-dimensional positive noncollapsed bubble route because the positive-collapse Bochner bridge had a single unsupported input. The conceptual refinement was that if a positive-pinched noncollapsed sequence has no codimension-four singular set, then Myers, Bishop–Gromov, Cheeger–Naber \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,p}\) convergence, weak Ricci convergence, elliptic regularity, and Cheeger–Gromov diffeomorphism recovery give a smooth Einstein metric on the original \(M_i\). Thus the noncollapsed regular alternative already delivers the Yau–26 conclusion in dimension four; the only noncollapsed obstruction is bubbling [Step 30].

- Ozuch 2021 was retrieved and used as the main source for exact-Einstein obstruction theory. The relevant exact-Einstein obstruction is a Taub/Pohozaev preserved quantity: for an orbifold expansion \(g_o=e+H_2+O(r^3)\) and ALE expansion \(g_b=e+H^4+O(r^{-5})\), Ozuch Theorem 4.6 gives vanishing boundary integrals involving \(\operatorname{Ric}_e^{(2)}(H_2,H^4)\); Corollary 4.10 specializes the Eguchi–Hanson case to \(R_+v=0\) for the EH orientation \(v\). Allowing EH orientation gives \(\det R_+=0\), but this remains first-obstruction vanishing only [Steps 30–31].

- Step 30 introduced the divergence-free cosmological Einstein tensor pairing as a \(C^0\)-Ricci-safe identity:
  \[
  \mathcal E_g=\operatorname{Ric}_g-\frac12 s_g g+\frac{n-2}{2}g.
  \]
  In positive normalization, if \(A=\operatorname{Ric}_g-g\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\), then \(\mathcal E_g=A-\frac12(\operatorname{tr}A)g\), is \(O_n(\delta)\) pointwise, and is divergence-free. Ozuch’s identity gives
  \[
  \int_{\partial\Omega}\mathcal E_g(Z,\nu)
  =\frac12\int_\Omega\langle\mathcal E_g,{\cal L}_Zg\rangle,
  \]
  with no derivative of the Ricci defect. TTCS confirmed this but warned it is linear and cannot by itself detect Ozuch’s bilinear \(H_2\)-\(H^4\) Taub/Wronskian obstruction [Steps 30, 32–33].

- Step 31 formulated the noncollapsed positive dichotomy under explicit open assumptions: A1 bubble-tree finiteness for near-Einstein metrics, expected from CGB/energy quantization; A2 transfer of exact-Einstein Ozuch first obstruction to merely \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched degenerations. Then either the noncollapsed sequence has a regular limit and \(M\) carries an Einstein metric, or every Eguchi–Hanson singular point satisfies \(W_+\) eigenvalue \(-1/3\), equivalently \(\det R_+=0\) after allowing orientation [Step 31].

- The spectral layer of Step 31 computed \(R_+=W_++\frac13I\) for standard positive Einstein 4-manifolds. Round \(S^4\) has \(\det R_+=1/27\neq0\), so EH bubbling is first-order excluded. \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) and \(S^2\times S^2\) have \(\det R_+=0\), and all Kähler–Einstein 4-manifolds have \(W_+\) eigenvalue \(-\Lambda/3\) in anti-Kähler directions. The retained interpretation is a Kähler/non-Kähler structural partition for first obstruction, not a theorem that \(\det R_+=0\) implies Kähler geometry [Steps 31, 33].

- Ozuch 2020 higher-order obstruction reading showed that for \(T^4/\mathbb Z_2\) Ricci-flat desingularization, 84 polynomial constraints exist for stable Ricci-flat configurations, but a 14-dimensional chessboard \((8+8)\) family satisfies all 84 known equations. Theorem 0.15 excludes a \(1\) positive + \(15\) negative EH bubble configuration, but the balanced configuration is not excluded. This means known higher obstructions do not close even in \(\Lambda=0\); it should not be imported as evidence of a positive-\(\Lambda\) counterexample without sign-specific checking [Steps 31–32].

- The proposed Page-metric annular-flux experiment was rejected. Page is a single rigid Einstein metric on \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2\), produced by blowing up a smooth point and carrying a \((-1)\)-sphere; an EH resolution of an \(A_1=\mathbb C^2/\{\pm1\}\) point inserts a \((-2)\)-sphere. Page has no degenerating scale \(t\to0\), so any flux calculation would be a zero consistency check, not evidence for or against A2. Its real relevance, together with Chen–LeBrun–Weber, is that no Kähler–Einstein metric does not imply no Riemannian Einstein metric [Step 32].

- The obstruction-amplitude principle from Steps 1 and 7 was restored as the correct interpretation of A2. In a Morteza–Viaclovsky/Calabi normal form,
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{g_t}-\Lambda g_t-t\lambda\chi_t o
  =O_{g_{\rm cal}}(t^2\rho^2),\qquad g_t\sim t\,g_{\rm cal}.
  \]
  Raising an index with \(g_t^{-1}\) converts the non-scalar obstruction term \(t\lambda o\) into an order-\(|\lambda|\) Ricci-endomorphism defect, while the remainder becomes small. Thus nonzero first obstruction is incompatible with \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-\Lambda g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) in the actual Yau–26 norm. The missing theorem is ansatz-independence: arbitrary pinched degenerations must admit a neck expansion or projection where this unsuppressed obstruction coefficient appears [Steps 1, 7, 32].

- The correct Route-A comparison was restricted to a single balanced annulus, not a full-neck flux and not an exact-family experiment. The orbifold mode has \(H_2\sim r^2\), the inserted ALE mode has \(t^4H^4\sim t^4r^{-4}\), and their Taub/Wronskian boundary signal is \(O(t^4)\) because the exponents \(2\) and \(-4\) sum to \(-2\). The balance radius is \(r=t^{2/3}\); on a dyadic shell there, a \(C^0\) Ricci residual contributes \(O(\delta r^6)=O(\delta t^4)\), so the error-to-signal ratio is \(O(\delta)\), independent of any coupling between \(\delta\) and \(t\). At \(r\sim1\), the error would be \(O(\delta)\) against a \(t^4\) signal, so any full-neck summation would need a false rate condition [Steps 32–33].

- Step 33 source-checked the classification bypass and sharply limited it. LeBrun–Ozuch 2026 Theorem B assumes an exact sequence of smooth compact oriented positive Einstein 4-manifolds, a Hermitian/conformally Kähler positive Einstein orbifold limit with a genuine singularity, and admissibility meaning all ALE bubbles are anti-self-dual in the induced orientation. It does not derive Hermitian or Kähler structure from \(\det R_+=0\). Under those hypotheses, Theorem 4.1 forces the smooth topology into the del Pezzo list with \(b_+=1\): \(S^2\times S^2\) or \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2\), \(0\le\ell\le8\). Thus, conditionally, the spin stress family \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), \(k\ge2\), cannot occur in that classified noncollapsed branch because its even form \(kH\) has \(b_+=k\ge2\). This does not apply to arbitrary \(\det R_+=0\) limits or collapse [Step 33].

- The flat-cone indicial work was reframed as a finite mode-diagonal calculation. On the \(A_1\) cone \(\mathbb R^4/\{\pm1\}\), in Bianchi gauge the tangent cone is flat and the linearized operator is componentwise Laplacian for the relevant sanity model. Homogeneous roots occur in pairs \(\ell\) and \(-\ell-2\), with only even \(\ell\) surviving antipodal parity. The \(\ell=0\) pair is pure gauge/removable on the growing side and mass/volume on the decaying side; \(\ell=2\) is exactly the \(H_2/H^4\) pair. The Wronskian pairs only within the same angular mode. This supports Route A but the full Lichnerowicz/Bianchi inventory remains a mathematical object to prove, not a completed theorem [Steps 33–34].

- Step 34 showed the \(\ell=0\) mass/volume mode can be larger at \(r=t^{2/3}\) but is invisible to the \(\ell=2\) Wronskian by angular orthogonality. The \((2,-4)\) pair carries the \(t^4\) Ozuch first obstruction \(R_+v=0\); higher-mode or cross-mode pairings are zero or subleading. Thus A2 need not say the metric is “cone plus only two modes plus small”; it only needs flux-visible \(\ell=2\) control [Step 34].

- Step 34 initially discovered a logarithmic resonance in the model equation
  \[
  f''+\frac3r f'-\frac8{r^2}f=S.
  \]
  A constant source \(S=\delta\) resonates with the \(r^2\) homogeneous solution and gives \(\delta r^2\log r/6\), yielding apparent relative contamination \(O(\delta\log(1/t))\) if one reads the growing coefficient through the long neck. The Bianchi identity was not found to remove this per-mode resonance [Step 34].

- Step 35 repaired the resonance conclusion. The log is an artifact of transporting the growing \(H_2\) coefficient inward; the correct comparison reads the orbifold quadratic coefficient at the orbifold end and reads the decaying EH coefficient outward in the rescaled bubble frame. With \(\hat g=t^{-2}g\), the Ricci defect and ambient curvature 2-jet signal both scale as \(t^2\) on fixed EH annuli. Over \(\rho\in[1,R]\), the relative nonconservation is \(O(\delta\log R)+O(1/R)\); the correct iterated limit is fixed \(R\), \(\delta_i\to0\), then \(R\to\infty\). Therefore no hypothesis \(\delta\log(1/t)\to0\) should be included in the candidate theorem [Steps 34–36].

- The real noncollapsed Route-A missing proposition was restated: after rescaling around an EH bubble, produce a second-order bubble-frame blow-up
  \[
  k=\lim(\hat g_i-g_{\rm EH})/t_i^2
  \]
  with quadratic growth, satisfying the appropriate \(D\operatorname{Ric}_{\rm EH}(k)=\Lambda g_{\rm EH}+O(\delta_i)\) equation, and match its quadratic asymptotic coefficient to the orbifold \(R_+\) 2-jet. Cheeger–Naber \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) convergence and harmonic-radius control may make this meaningful, but they do not by themselves transmit a second jet for non-Einstein prelimit metrics [Steps 35–36].

- The harmonic-radius/\(\varepsilon\)-regularity input was made explicit and separated from pointwise curvature control. The wanted lemma is roughly: bounded Ricci, noncollapse, and small buffered annular \(L^2\) curvature energy imply harmonic-radius control at the annulus scale. Cheeger–Naber 2015 supplies bounded-Ricci, noncollapsed four-dimensional harmonic-radius weak-type estimates and a cone-annulus theorem from almost volume-cone behavior; Ozuch/Gao exact-Einstein theory supplies small-\(L^2\) curvature \(\varepsilon\)-regularity in the Einstein setting. For merely \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched metrics, the small-\(L^2\)-only version is not source-established. Step-11 CZ does not refute the harmonic-radius version because it refutes pointwise curvature bounds while potentially preserving small \(C^{1,\alpha}\) harmonic-coordinate size [Steps 33–35].

- Step 34/35 opened a second, collapsed positive front. The toric \(\alpha\)-family bolt regions each carry an exact formal \(8\pi^2\) curvature-energy quantum; rescaling a single high-\(A\) bolt by \(\sqrt{2A}\) sends the SdS parameter to Euclidean Schwarzschild mass \(\widehat M\to1/2\). However, Step 35 corrected the isolated-bubble interpretation: rod lengths and rod spacings are both \(O(A^{-1/2})\), so after rescaling neighboring rods and nuts remain at finite distance. The collapsed limit is an infinite or periodic toric Ricci-flat rod-chain problem, not a single isolated Schwarzschild bubble [Steps 34–35].

- Euclidean Schwarzschild was recorded as ALF, not ALE, and not anti-self-dual. Therefore LeBrun–Ozuch admissible ASD ALE obstruction theory does not transfer to the collapsed toric front. The appropriate literature/language is generalized Weyl static vacuum metrics, rod regularity, Israel–Khan struts, periodic black-hole arrays, and Atiyah–LeBrun edge-cone Chern–Weil formulas [Steps 34–35].

- Step 36 corrected a load-bearing energy-accounting error in the collapsed front. The smooth \(g_i\) have bulk \(\int|W|^2\), while an edge-cone strut in an Atiyah–LeBrun limit contributes separate defect terms such as
  \[
  (2\chi\pm3\tau)(M)\ge(1-\beta)\bigl(2\chi(\Sigma)\pm(1+\beta)[\Sigma]^2\bigr)
  \]
  in the cited form, not ordinary bulk Weyl energy. Therefore “\(8\pi^2\chi\) is saturated, so there is no room for struts” does not follow directly. A strut smoothed at transverse scale \(\varepsilon\) would cost roughly \((1-\beta)^2|\Sigma|/\varepsilon^2\), and whether that overflows the smooth budget depends on the collapse-scale comparison [Step 36].

- Step 36 then found that the alternating-label toric adversary is not a strut configuration. The Delzant condition forces adjacent rod normals to form a \(\mathbb Z^2\)-basis, and in the adopted alternating labels adjacent rods collapse different \(S^1\) factors. Transitions occur through NUT points—codimension-four \(T^2\)-fixed points where both circles degenerate—not codimension-two struts where one circle remains regular. NUT smoothing costs \(O(1)\) per NUT by dimensional scaling \(\varepsilon^{-4}\varepsilon^4\), not the divergent strut cost. Thus the divergent strut-energy obstruction does not apply to the \(\alpha\)-family [Step 36].

- The rod-count/topology convention for compact toric four-manifolds was recorded as edges = corners = \(\chi = 2+b_2\) in the polygonal models under discussion. Step 36 warns not to assume a no-slack argument without settling which regions carry the \(8\pi^2\) quanta and how NUT/collar energies enter; the current conclusion is that the collapsed \(\alpha\)-family survives all energy-based arguments tested so far [Steps 35–36].

- The collapsed positive branch was recast as a concrete Weyl/gravitational-instanton decision problem: determine whether a smooth periodic alternating toric Ricci-flat four-manifold exists with Schwarzschild-type \(S^2\) bolts and smooth NUT transitions. If such a solution exists, it would provide a geometric mechanism for smooth toric collapse with \(\operatorname{Ric}\to g\); if impossible, the proof may yield a new topology-uniform collapse obstruction. This is distinct from Israel–Khan same-axis strut configurations and from self-dual multi-Taub-NUT geometry [Steps 35–36].

- The negative cutoff-flow/Ishida–LeBrun peer line remains unresolved. Step 33 briefly recorded A03’s correction that a Moser absorption parameter could diverge under local collapse, suggesting at best per-manifold gaps, but Step 36 notes A03 retracted that particular #330 correction and the branch should be treated as unresolved rather than established per-manifold or dimension-uniform. A01/A03 later reported repaired estimates, unregularized \(J_6\) persistence, and cutoff-jet continuation, but A02 did not independently verify those scripts in Steps 35–36. The route still does not currently supply a dimension-only Yau–26 gap [Steps 33–36].

- The current four-dimensional positive branch is split into two precise components. The noncollapsed component has a conditional theorem and two main analytic bridges: harmonic-radius/neck-energy control for merely \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched metrics, and second-order bubble-frame convergence/2-jet matching to transfer Ozuch’s first obstruction. The collapsed component has either the Bochner central almost-Killing bridge or the toric Weyl rod-chain decision problem. Neither component is solved, and neither covers dimensions \(n\ge5\), the negative branch, or the final Lean proof [Steps 28–36].

### Research Line

- The research began by fixing the logical burden of Yau–26 and testing whether known almost-Einstein stability or topological obstruction theorems already settled a sign branch. Min-Oo identified how a negative sequence could escape restricted stability; ALE gluing exposed the difference between weighted residual control and pointwise Ricci-operator control. The opening question changed from “is an existing theorem enough?” to “which degeneration permits a tightly Ricci-isotropic metric to evade Einstein existence?” [Step 1].

- Four-dimensional gauge theory was the first sustained attempt to answer that question. The Step-2 arithmetic error and user correction forced a reconstruction of the LeBrun inequalities. The broad obstruction claim failed, but the work produced a reusable stability principle: a strict metric-independent integral gap excludes sufficiently small trace-free Ricci error. Because the surviving near-equality regime concerned only the negative sign, A02 moved away from treating it as the central all-dimensional route [Steps 2–4].

- Chern–Gauss–Bonnet then became the accounting framework across positive collapse and negative bubbling. Tight pinching yields Euler/Weyl budgets and strict Hitchin–Thorpe, but not a topology-uniform collapse obstruction. Later bubble, rod, and edge analyses clarified that fixed \(L^2\) quanta can sit on shrinking features, so the identity records cost rather than forbidding degeneration [Steps 4, 8, 14–18, 34–36].

- The positive branch gained comparative priority because Myers and Bishop provide dimension-only diameter and volume ceilings, whereas the negative branch permits diameter escape. Initial hopes for noncollapsed smooth convergence were repaired using Cheeger–Naber: regular Einstein convergence occurs away from codimension-four singularities, but singular removal and same-topology Einstein existence remain open. In four dimensions, an infinite tightly pinched topological family must collapse, making collapse and bubbling the decisive positive regimes [Steps 5, 9–10, 30–31].

- Collapse models changed the program’s taste. Berger anisotropy showed that fixed-connection shrinking is not universal; lens spaces and later Kaluza–Klein products showed exact Einstein collapse. Four-dimensional topology removed globally free-circle collapse but left fixed strata and curvature concentration. The goal became collapse characterization—showing a collapse is Einstein-compatible or identifying a structural obstruction—rather than proving noncollapse [Steps 5–7, 10, 24].

- The ALE first-obstruction and compactness lines were combined in the proposed weak projection bridge. The intended mechanism was to pair the \(C^0\) Ricci defect with smooth approximate cokernel data instead of differentiating it. This remained dormant while collapse was explored, then returned in Steps 30–36 as the balanced-annulus Taub/Wronskian route for noncollapsed EH bubbling [Steps 7–9, 30–36].

- Step 10’s regularity audit made average-to-pointwise control the next decisive test. Step 11 settled that test negatively via the opposite-warping CZ spike. This invalidated generic Ricci-only pointwise curvature regularity and any collapse strategy relying on direct curvature supremum bounds, while preserving weaker harmonic, finite-\(p\), BMO, smoothing, and pairing methods [Steps 10–11].

- The same opposite-warping construction revealed the determinant variable \(w\) as a natural collapse observable: it leaves \(w\) fixed while changing the fibre ratio. The work shifted from generic regularity to toric orbit-space determinants, rod closure, and the simultaneous shrinking of both fibre directions [Steps 11–12, 14].

- The toric determinant equation initially suggested clean spectral and area routes. Exact source results supplied orthogonal transitivity, while round \(S^4\) and product examples fixed conventions. Successive checks removed optimistic shortcuts: \(K_B\) has no sign, Euclidean Faber–Krahn is not generally available, signed Gauss–Bonnet permits boundary-localized negative curvature, and the \(L^2\) energy budget permits many boundary bubbles [Steps 12–17].

- Local edge analysis sharpened the adversary rather than ending the route. Exact germs allow arbitrary negative edge curvature; identifying them as Schwarzschild–de Sitter located the exact obstruction in cone-angle mismatch at the other bolt. Exact two-bolt closure is rigid, but the user correctly blocked an unsupported extension to \(C^0\)-pinched metrics [Steps 15–18].

- Step 18 restored direct toric BUILD/BREAK analysis as a load-bearing stress test on \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), while limiting its relation to Yau–26. Step 19 showed that the periodic-label corners and low-order Ricci jets admit arbitrarily large negative edge curvature. This moved the possible obstruction from local smoothness to global filling and junction behavior [Steps 18–19].

- Step 20 tested coupled-system and modulus interpretations. The rectangular \(m=4\) calibration showed strong global rigidity at small topology, but Step 21 explained why perimeter or modulus controls cannot yield the \(\chi\)-uniform volume gap required by the cover amplifier. The \(A_m=m^\alpha\) formal family then passed scalar, local, and bookkeeping tests, prompting a pause in small-\(m\) numerics [Steps 20–21].

- The session briefly shifted toward the A01/A03 negative cutoff-flow route. The user redirected the audit to collapsed Sobolev input, where thin-circle and hyperbolic models showed why raw energy estimates fail downstairs. Relative Sobolev factors, buffered covers, and critical products survived, but the route was narrowed to a special four-dimensional Ishida–LeBrun laboratory and could not represent the full proposition. Later peer corrections and retractions kept the route unresolved rather than dimension-uniform [Steps 21–24, 29, 33–36].

- This scope correction triggered a high-dimensional Explore phase. Source review found no broad no-Einstein reservoir in \(n\ge5\), so high-dimensional refutation was judged at least as difficult as the general Einstein-existence problem plus a tight-pinching construction. The research reframed \(P_n^\pm\) as containment of a pinching-admissible topology class inside the Einstein-admissible class [Steps 22–23].

- The proposed all-dimensional extension of the four-dimensional circle-collapse obstruction was directly falsified. Exact Kaluza–Klein products \((S^3/\mathbb Z_q)\times N\) provide bounded-curvature positive Einstein collapse in every dimension \(n\ge5\). This clarified the positive architecture: known collapse is often already Einstein-compatible, so the proof target is classification or promotion rather than exclusion [Step 24].

- Returning to the toric \(\alpha\)-family produced another important correction. The individual warping equation had the wrong sign, and removing the false \(\int K_Bw=\int w\) identity eliminated the only apparent global weighted-curvature constraint. The corrected mixed-boundary Schrödinger equations remain genuine and force a precise collar cancellation, but all currently verified integral identities are compatible with collapse. The toric state remains unresolved between a global PDE obstruction and an actual smooth construction [Steps 25–26].

- In parallel, the all-dimensional collapse architecture turned to nonabelian nilpotent fibres. The first Milnor-based idea was too strong because \(A,T,N\) can compensate intrinsic negative fibre Ricci. The Heisenberg moving-frame model made this failure productive: large bracket is locally compatible with positive Einstein equations only through large second fundamental form and rapid relative scaling [Step 26].

- Step 27 extracted a stronger model consequence. Positive Einstein constant makes the normalized bracket strictly monotone, excludes a sustained nonabelian plateau, and confines large bracket to a thin curvature shell. Negative Einstein constant permits a plateau, with complex hyperbolic horospheres as an exact witness. Under ordinary endpoint assumptions, monotonicity closes into a compact-model nonexistence theorem. This is the strongest structural result of that model line, but deliberately confined to the diagonal cohomogeneity-one \(H_3\) ansatz [Steps 26–27].

- Step 28 converted the ansatz result into an ansatz-free Bochner center bound. The user’s central insight was that the nilpotent center supplies a genuine Killing field on the compact fibre, and Bochner directly bounds the centre bracket in \(L^2\). TTCS corrections narrowed the statement to central circle actions, separated fibre bracket from horizontal twist, and sharpened the almost-Killing threshold. This shifted the positive-collapse question from ODE modeling to the source of central almost-Killing fields from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching [Step 28].

- Step 29 cleaned the allocation. In four dimensions every nilpotent collapse fibre has central brackets, so the quotient-induction and pointwise twist problem first matter for higher-step fibres in dimensions at least five, not for the four-dimensional crux. A local twist-spike jet showed that pointwise \(|\phi|^2\) bounds are probably false, and noncentral almost-Killing fields are vacuous. The remaining collapse bridge became precise: manufacture central almost-Killing fields with controlled Lie-derivative error and scale-comparable length without full-curvature control [Step 29].

- Step 30 reweighted the program because that collapse bridge could not be supplied by Cheeger–Fukaya–Gromov or peer smoothing machinery as currently understood. The four-dimensional noncollapsed bubble route was restored: regular noncollapsed limits already yield an Einstein metric on \(M\), so the only noncollapsed failure is bubbling. This route has direct contact with known Ozuch/Biquard obstruction theory and with the only plausible noncollapsed counterexample mechanism [Step 30].

- Step 31 built the first noncollapsed dichotomy: regular limit gives Einstein existence; EH bubbling requires \(R_+v=0\) at each singular point, conditional on bubble-tree finiteness and obstruction transfer for near-Einstein sequences. The spectral computation gave a useful partition: round \(S^4\) is first-order protected, Kähler–Einstein examples are first-order compatible, and generic non-Kähler positive Einstein orbifolds are expected to avoid the codimension-one condition. This was immediately limited: first-obstruction vanishing is not gluing sufficiency and not a Kähler criterion [Step 31].

- Step 32 prevented a misleading Page-metric experiment and restored the obstruction-amplitude mechanism from the beginning of the session. Page and CLW instead became reminders that failure of Kähler–Einstein existence is not failure of Riemannian Einstein existence. The analytic issue A2 was redefined as ansatz-independence: arbitrary pinched degenerations must expose the same scale-critical operator-norm first-obstruction coefficient as the explicit MV/Calabi expansion [Step 32].

- Steps 32–34 refined the flux route into a single-annulus, mode-diagonal Taub/Wronskian problem. The balance radius \(r=t^{2/3}\), angular mode diagonality on \(\mathbb R^4/\{\pm1\}\), and invisibility of the \(\ell=0\) mass mode made the route more finite than a global weighted neck theory. The next mathematical object became the actual Lichnerowicz/Bianchi indicial inventory and Wronskian pairing for the \(A_1\) cone, together with a harmonic-radius/annular-energy lemma [Steps 32–34].

- Step 35 repaired the apparent logarithmic rate obstruction by moving to the rescaled bubble frame and using an iterated fixed-\(R\) limit. The noncollapsed route therefore no longer carries \(\delta\log(1/t)\to0\). Its real load-bearing theorem is second-order EH bubble-frame convergence and matching of the quadratic asymptotic to the orbifold curvature 2-jet. This is sharper and harder than a model flux computation because \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) convergence does not transmit second jets for non-Einstein prelimit metrics [Step 35].

- The classification bypass was source-grounded and demoted to a conditional filter. LeBrun–Ozuch’s Hermitian/admissible theorem can place exact Einstein limits into del Pezzo topologies, excluding the spin stress family \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), \(k\ge2\), only if independent hypotheses supply Hermitian/conformally Kähler structure and ASD ALE bubbles. Since \(\det R_+=0\) alone supplies neither, this line cannot replace A2 but remains useful when those hypotheses are available [Step 33].

- Steps 34–36 reopened the collapsed toric front with a new interpretation. The formal \(\alpha\)-family’s bolt energy matches \(8\pi^2\) per rod, and local rescaling sees Schwarzschild-type ALF behavior; but neighboring rods remain at finite separation, so the real limit is a periodic/infinite toric Ricci-flat rod chain. The literature to inspect is generalized Weyl static vacuum and edge-cone accounting, not ALE obstruction theory [Steps 34–35].

- Step 36 corrected the “no slack for struts” argument. Edge-cone struts contribute characteristic-number defect terms separate from smooth bulk Weyl energy, and smoothing costs depend on transverse scale. More importantly, the alternating Delzant rod model has adjacent rods collapsing different circles and therefore has NUT transitions, not codimension-two struts. NUT smoothing has \(O(1)\) energy cost, so the toric \(\alpha\)-family remains alive after all currently tested energy arguments. The collapsed branch is now a concrete PDE/geometric existence question: whether a smooth periodic alternating toric Ricci-flat rod-chain with Schwarzschild-type \(S^2\) bolts and NUT transitions exists [Step 36].

- The current high-level picture is: dimensions \(2\) and \(3\) are regarded as positive-side settled; dimension four is the explicit crux, split into noncollapsed ALE bubbling and collapsed toric/nilpotent regimes; dimensions \(n\ge5\) remain entangled with the general Einstein-existence problem and exact KK collapse; the negative branch remains a restricted and unresolved side line. No branch of Yau–26 is proved or disproved, and final Lean formalization is still far beyond the partial algebraic kernels [Steps 23–36].

- Important inactive lines remain available. The weak ALE projection bridge has been refined into the balanced-annulus Wronskian/second-order bubble-frame problem. The LeBrun zero-margin negative problem and A01/A03 relative-Sobolev cutoff-flow architecture remain possible four-dimensional side routes but currently do not supply dimension-only constants. The toric \(\alpha\)-family remains the main fixed-strata/collapsed adversary, now reframed as a Weyl rod-chain/NUT problem rather than a simple edge-cone strut obstruction. The Bochner center bound remains the main general nilpotent-collapse mechanism, conditional on producing central almost-Killing fields from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching [Steps 8–36].

- The current handoff direction is not to claim general positive abelian forcing or noncollapsed closure. The next review should assess the Step 34–36 corrections: whether the NUT-vs-strut distinction is correct and robust, whether the iterated-limit removal of the logarithmic rate is sound, whether the noncollapsed conditional theorem is logically stated, and which open bridge—A1/A2 noncollapsed second-order matching, the collapsed Weyl rod-chain problem, or the Bochner almost-Killing bridge—is most promising for the next steps. Any route must preserve that the complete Yau–26 proposition spans all \(n\ge2\), both signs, arbitrary closed smooth manifolds, and final Lean formalization [Step 36].

## 负分支开局：Min–Oo 尺度逃逸与 orbifold 解消的 \(C^0\) 障碍 [Steps 1–3, 22–24, 32]

早期研究先核对 Min–Oo 论文 OCR 与原记号，纠正了把附加条件理解为局部 \(r^{-2}\) 曲率控制的倾向。Min–Oo 在 \(n>3\)、负标量归一化、小 Ricci 各向异性并满足归一化尺度控制时得到 Einstein 存在；其尺度不变量条件是

\]

=O_{g_{\rm cal}}(t^2\rho^2),\qquad g_t\sim t\,g_{\rm cal},

则普通余项升指标后在核心区为 \(O(t)\)、过渡区至多 \(O(t^{1/2})\)，但第一障碍项 \(t\lambda o\) 变成阶一非标量端omorphism；TTCS 还确认 Calabi 核上障碍张量特征值差使优化标量 Einstein 常数后仍留下正的非标量谱间隙 [Steps 1–2]。
