M_k=\#_k(S^2\times S^2)
\]
[Steps 8,18]。CGB 预算显示若 \(M_k\) 上存在 \(\delta_k\to0\) 的正 pinched 度量，Weyl 能量至少线性增长而总体积有统一上界；若还能证明拓扑无关体积下界，则 Cheeger–Naber 有限型会给矛盾。因此正四维的核心逐渐变成理解非塌缩 bubble 与塌缩/fixed-strata collapse，而不是传统拓扑障碍 [Steps 8–10,18]。

## 紧致性计划纠偏与 CZ spike 否定点态正则性 [Steps 4–11, 30, 33–35]

Step 5 曾尝试由双侧 Ricci 界、直径界、总体积非塌缩和 \(\delta_i\to0\) 自动推出统一 harmonic radius、光滑 Einstein 极限和固定微分拓扑。TTCS 指出该命题在 \(n\ge4\) 错误：即使精确 Einstein 序列也会有 Weyl 集中、orbifold 极限与 ALE 泡 [Step 5]。修正后，可靠版本必须额外假设 \(|\mathrm{Rm}|\le K\)；erratum 文件为 `workspace/notes/step5_erratum_theorem2_correction.md` 与 `workspace/plans/step5_corrected_positive_branch_plan.md` [Step 5]。

随后研究转向 Cheeger–Naber/Naber–Zhang、Ozuch、Ge–Jiang/Li 的弱结构。非塌缩有界 Ricci 给 codimension-4 奇异集、四维 \(L^2\) 曲率与 harmonic-radius 分布控制；塌缩时需最大纤维化幂零秩、local rewinding、覆盖非塌缩等额外条件才能获得 harmonic/conjugate radius 或拓扑控制 [Steps 6,9–10]。Step 9 得到条件性四维非塌缩有限型结果：若
\[
\|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<1/2,\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(M)\ge v>0,
\]
则 Myers+Bishop–Gromov 给单位球非塌缩，Cheeger–Naber Theorem 1.12 推出有限微分同胚型 [Step 9]。这只给有限型，不给 Einstein 存在。

Step 11 直接检验并否定“\(C^0\) Ricci pinching + 小 \(L^2\) 曲率可推出点态曲率上界”的正则性猜想。在 \(S^2(1)\times S^2(1)\) 上取相反 warping
\[
g=dx^2+dy^2+e^{2(F_1+u)}d\theta^2+e^{2(F_2-u)}d\phi^2,
\]
使 \(\operatorname{Hess}u\) 在 Ricci 基块中抵消，Ricci 主要感知 \(\Delta u\)，而混合 Riemann 分量保留完整 Hessian [Step 11]。选择
\[
w_\sigma(X,Y)=-\frac12XY\log(X^2+Y^2+\sigma^2)
\]
及振幅 \(a_j=\Lambda^{-2/3}\)、\(\sigma_j=e^{-\Lambda}\)，得到
\[
\|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_j}-g_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(\Lambda^{-2/3})\to0,\qquad
|\operatorname{Rm}_{g_j}|(0)\gtrsim\Lambda^{1/3}\to\infty,
\]
同时局部 Hessian/\(\mathrm{Rm}\) 的 \(L^2\) 贡献可趋零 [Step 11]。记录为 `workspace/notes/step11_cz_spike_and_proposition_A.md`、`workspace/scripts/step11_cz_spike_analytical.py` 及 JSON [Step 11]。这迫使后续 compactness、smoothing 或 projection 方案使用 harmonic radius、有限 \(L^p\)/BMO、弱配对、相对 Sobolev、cover 非塌缩或能量量子，而不能暗中恢复点态 \(|\mathrm{Rm}|\) 控制 [Steps 11,21–24]。

Step 33–35 又细化了 CZ spike 对新路线的含义：它否定点态曲率 epsilon-regularity，但不必否定 harmonic-radius 小能量引理；其高 Hessian 集中在指数小尺度，\(C^{1,\alpha}\) seminorm 可趋零，所以有界 Ricci、非塌缩、小 annular \(L^2\) 能量推出 harmonic-radius 控制的命题仍是可能的负载引理 [Steps 33,35]。Cheeger–Naber 2015 提供 bounded-Ricci、非塌缩、volume-cone annuli 的 harmonic-coordinate/C^1 控制；Ozuch exact-Einstein neck Lemma 2.2 使用 Gao/Anderson 型 epsilon regularity。但对仅 \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched 度量，“小 \(L^2\) 能量 + 非塌缩 \(\Rightarrow\) harmonic radius”尚未 source-established [Step 35]。

## Torus 约化、rod/corner 模型与 \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) toric crux [Steps 12–21, 25–26]

CZ ansatz 自然导向一般 torus 约化
\[
g=g_B+h_{IJ}(d\phi^I+A^I)(d\phi^J+A^J),\qquad w=\sqrt{\det h}.
\]
Step 12 用符号 jet 计算得到竖直 trace 方程
\[
\operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^V
=-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}+\frac12|F|_h^2,
\]
Einstein 情形下
\[
\left(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|_h^2\right)w=2\lambda w,
\]
以及 twist 守恒式
\[
d(wh_{IJ}*_BF^J)=0
\]
[Step 12]。在轨道空间有退化边界时，\(w>0\) 于内部、\(w=0\) 于边界，给出带非负 twist 势的 Dirichlet ground-state 图景；正 \(C^0\) pinching 可用 \(w\) 做 Rayleigh/Barta 测试而不需要 \(\nabla E\) [Steps 12–13]。

该框架用 \(S^4(\sqrt3)\) 与 \(S^2\times S^2\) 校准；后续无 twist 对角形式
\[
g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2,\qquad w=pq,\quad v=\log(p/q)
\]
把系统拆为竖直 trace、竖直差、水平 trace/traceless 目标 [Steps 12–14]。Step 14 曾混淆 \(\operatorname{Hess}\log(pq)\) 与 \(\operatorname{Hess}p/p+\operatorname{Hess}q/q\)，错误推出 \(K_B\ge3\)；随即修正为
\[
K_B=\frac14(|\nabla v|^2-|\nabla\log w|^2)
=-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle
\]
并修正边缘方程为
\[
Q''+(1-2K_B|_{\rm edge})Q=0
\]
[Step 14]。Step 17 又撤回在任意曲面轨道空间上使用欧氏 Faber–Krahn 的错误，因为 \(g_B\) 可有任意负高斯曲率；只有附加 \(K_B\le0\) 等条件时才可用 Bol–Bandle 型工具 [Steps 14,17,21]。

Step 18 建立周期 characteristic labels
\[
(1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),\ldots
\]
作用于偶数 \(m=2k+2\) 边形。初始有理归一化 checker 有误，随后改用整数 quasitoric 上同调表示；脚本验证相邻 determinant、秩 \(m-2\)、行列式 \(\pm1\)、偶形式、signature \(0\)，并给出整 unimodular congruence 将交叉形式分解为 \(kH\)，强力支持底层为 \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) [Step 18]。主要文件为 `workspace/scripts/step18_toric_topology_checker_integral.py`、`workspace/scripts/step18_hyperbolic_split_periodic_labels.py` 及 JSON [Step 18]。用户随后要求不得把粗全局 PDE residual 数值趋势当作 BUILD/BREAK；数值只用于定位 defect，决定性对象应是 rod/corner 与解析匹配 [Steps 18–19]。

Step 19 直接检查周期标签模型的局部光滑性和角点 Einstein 方程，击破若干简单 BUILD 障碍。相邻标签为标准基向量符号变体时，对角 ansatz 局部兼容；固定点坐标
\[
g=dr^2+\mu(r,t)^2dt^2+p(r,t)^2d\theta^2+q(r,t)^2d\phi^2
\]
的最低 jets 给
\[
-6a-4u-1=0,\qquad -6b-4u-1=0,
\]
即
\[
a=b=-\frac{2A+1}{6}
\]
正好匹配 rod 方程的 Taylor 系数 [Step 19]。更高阶形式级数到第一非平凡 \(r^2\) 阶仍可在任意 \(A\) 求解，排除了仅靠 unimodularity、right-angle smoothness 或低阶角点 Ricci 代数封顶大负边缘曲率的路线 [Step 19]。

Step 21 构造形式 adversary
\[
A_m=m^\alpha,\qquad 1<\alpha\le2,
\]
每条 rod 常负曲率时
\[
Q_i(s)=\frac{\sin(\sqrt{1+2A_m}\,s)}{\sqrt{1+2A_m}},\quad
L_m=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{1+2A_m}},\quad
\Phi_i=\frac2{1+2A_m},
\]
总通量 \(\sim m^{1-\alpha}\to0\)，而 corner 低阶匹配、signed Gauss–Bonnet、Bishop 上界等均未矛盾 [Steps 19,21]。Step 25 重新推导 individual warping 方程，发现 Step 14 以来曾使用错误符号；正确为
\[
-\Delta_Bp=(1-K_B)p,\qquad -\Delta_Bq=(1-K_B)q,
\]
并由 \(S^2\times S^2\)、\(S^4\) 校准 [Step 25]。这撤销了 Step 20 的虚假 \(\int K_Bw=\int w\) 约束；正确 Green 配对只给 \(p\)-rod 与 \(q\)-rod flux equi-partition，并不产生内部加权曲率下界 [Step 25]。截至 Step 26，rod 恒等式、低阶角点、混合谱、flux equi-partition、水平方程局部校准与 Gauss–Bonnet 之间没有发现迫使 \(\int w\) 有拓扑一致下界的积分恒等式；结论是 BREAK-compatible，但还没有实际光滑度量 [Steps 25–26]。

## 高维正 Einstein collapse 与 Heisenberg 相对尺度机制 [Steps 24–27]

Step 24 按用户建议检查能否把四维自由圆塌缩 Bochner 障碍推广到所有奇维底空间。直接 Kaluza–Klein 计算否定了该猜想。对恒定长度主圆丛，取圆周期 \(2\pi\)、\(d\alpha=\pi^*F\)、单位竖直向量 \(U=t^{-1}\xi\)、\(\phi=tF\)，O’Neill 方程为
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_M^H=\operatorname{Ric}_B-\frac12(\phi\circ\phi),\quad
\operatorname{Ric}_M(U,U)=\frac12|\phi|^2,\quad
\operatorname{Ric}_M^{mix}=\pm\frac12d_B^*\phi
\]
[Step 24]。取
\[
B=S^2_{\operatorname{Ric}=2}\times N^d_{\operatorname{Ric}=1},\qquad
\phi=\sqrt2\,\omega_{S^2},
\]
得到每个 \(n\ge5\) 的精确正 Einstein collapse
\[
L(q,1)\times N^d\cong (S^3(\sqrt2)/\mathbb Z_q)\times N^d,
\]
纤维长度 \(2\pi\sqrt2/q\)、体积 \(\sim q^{-1}\)、截面曲率有界 [Step 24]。因此正 collapse 不能整体禁止，必须分类为 Einstein-compatible 或不兼容；四维圆障碍是低维特殊现象 [Step 24]。

Step 25–26 转向非阿贝尔 nilpotent fiber。初步 Milnor Ricci 观察显示 \(H_3\) intrinsic fiber Ricci 在两个生成方向为 \(-b^2/2\)、中心为 \(+b^2/2\)，似乎 positive pinching 可能迫使 bracket 消失 [Step 25]。用户指出二基本形式 \(T\) 可提供竖直 Ricci，不能仅靠点态 Milnor sign。Step 26 因此建立 \(T\)-active 对角 cohomogeneity-one \(H_3\) 模型
\[
g=dt^2+a(t)^2(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)+c(t)^2\theta_3^2,\quad [E_1,E_2]=E_3,
\]
定义
\[
b=c/a^2,\quad k_1=a'/a,\quad k_3=c'/c,\quad H=2k_1+k_3.
\]
Koszul/anholonomic moving frame 推导并由 `workspace/scripts/step26_heisenberg_moving_frame_ricci.py` 验证：
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=-2(k_1'+k_1^2)-(k_3'+k_3^2),
\]
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{11}=\operatorname{Ric}_{22}=-\frac{b^2}{2}-k_1'-Hk_1,\quad
\operatorname{Ric}_{33}=\frac{b^2}{2}-k_3'-Hk_3
\]
[Step 26]。

令竖直 Ricci 分量为 1 时，剩余 \(00\) 方程化为 Hamiltonian constraint
\[
C=4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+b^2+4=0,\qquad C'=-2HC.
\]
样本 \(b_0=20,k_1=10,k_3=-10.05\) 局部积分为精确正 Einstein ODE 解，误差 \(<10^{-12}\)，否定“正 Ricci 点态直接迫使非阿贝尔 bracket 小”的过强版本 [Step 26]。在约束面上得到
\[
|T|^2\ge\frac{b^2+4}{2},\qquad
|\partial_t\log b|^2\ge\frac54(b^2+4),
\]
说明大 bracket 必须伴随 \(|T|\sim b\) 与快速相对尺度变化，是分级/多尺度机制而非点态不可能 [Step 26]。

Step 27 将 Einstein 常数恢复为任意 \(\Lambda\)，得到约束
\[
C_\Lambda=b^2+4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+4\Lambda=0
\]
及恒等式
\[
|T|^2\ge\frac{b^2+4\Lambda}{2},\qquad
|(\log b)'|^2\ge\frac54(b^2+4\Lambda)
\]
在精确约束面上成立；pinched 版本损失 \(8\delta\) [Step 27]。当 \(\Lambda>0\) 且 \(\delta<\Lambda/2\) 时，\(b\) 在 regular 区间无临界点；闭圆轨道或普通光滑 tubular endpoints 的区间都无法闭合 [Step 27]。复双曲 \(\mathbb{CH}^2\) horosphere 数据
\[
\Lambda=-3/2,\quad b=1,\quad k_1=-1/2,\quad k_3=-1
\]
满足 \(C_\Lambda=0\)、\((\log b)'=0\)、\(k_1'=k_3'=0\)，解释负 Einstein 常数允许稳定非阿贝尔 nilpotent horosphere geometry，而正常数禁止 plateau [Step 27]。该模型定理只覆盖四维对角、无 twist、一维 base、普通端点的 \(H_3\) ansatz，不覆盖一般 infranil、twist-active、高维 base、edge/orbifold 端点或 toric fixed strata [Step 27]。

Step 27 还启动有限 Lean：`workspace/proofs/Step27H3Algebra.lean` 形式化两个精确恒等式、pinched 下界和正 pinched regime 中 rate 非零；`lean_check` 与依赖审计通过，证书为 `workspace/proofs/step27_h3_algebra_both_check_v2.json` 和 `workspace/proofs/step27_h3_algebra_rate_ne_zero_pinched_check.json` [Step 27]。

## Bochner 中心界、四维 bracket 控制与 almost-Killing 桥 [Steps 28–30]

Step 28 在用户提示下将 H3 ODE 机制提升为 ansatz-free 的 Bochner 中心界。对闭流形上的 Killing 场 \(Z\)，Bochner 给
\[
\int|\nabla Z|^2=\int \operatorname{Ric}(Z,Z)
\le(\Lambda+\delta)\int |Z|^2
\]
在 \(\operatorname{Ric}\le(\Lambda+\delta)g\) 情形成立 [Step 28]。若 \(Z\) 是 nilpotent fiber 中心方向，在 \(H_3\) intrinsic geometry 中
\[
|\nabla^F Z|^2=\frac{b^2}{2}|Z|^2,
\]
且 total \(|\nabla Z|^2\) 分解包含非负附加项，得到加权平均中心 bracket 界
\[
\langle b^2\rangle_{|Z|^2}\le 2(\Lambda+\delta)
\]
[Step 28]。脚本 `workspace/scripts/step28_bochner_killing_center_bound.py` 验证 H3 模型中 \(|\nabla Z|^2=c^2(2k_3^2+b^2/2)\)、Bochner 分部积分和 \(\mathbb{CH}^2\) consistency；综合笔记为 `workspace/notes/step28_bochner_center_bound_and_abelian_forcing.md` [Step 28]。

TTCS 对 Step 28 给出关键修正。第一，闭流形上的 compact Lie algebra 中不存在非阿贝尔 nilpotent 等距子代数；可用的是中心圆 Killing 作用，不是完整 Heisenberg 群等距作用 [Step 28]。第二，初始 induction 架构有缺口：Theorem A 控制 fiber bracket，不直接给 horizontal connection curvature \(|\phi|\) 的点态上界，无法自动给 quotient Ricci upper bound [Step 28]。第三，almost-Killing 版本的误差阈值可放宽：\(\tau=O(\varepsilon)\) 已足够使 normalized bracket 消失 [Step 28]。Step 28 还推导 Weitzenböck almost-Killing correction
\[
\int|\nabla Z|^2
=\int\operatorname{Ric}(Z,Z)+\frac12\int|\sigma|^2-\frac14\int(\operatorname{tr}\sigma)^2
\]
并形式化相关代数核于 `workspace/proofs/Step28BochnerKilling.lean`，依赖审计通过 [Step 28]。随后观察到同一 Bochner 分解给 horizontal twist 的加权 \(L^2\) 平均控制 \(\langle|\phi|^2\rangle\le4(\Lambda+\delta)\)，但仍是平均到点态的缺口 [Step 28]。

Step 29 根据用户的 allocation correction 改写正 collapse 路线。在四维，nilpotent collapse fiber 维数至多 3，因此 Lie algebra 只能 abelian 或 \(H_3\)，后者 2-step 且所有 bracket 落在中心；一旦存在尺度正确的中心 exact/almost-Killing 场，Step 28 Bochner 界已控制全部 fiber bracket，不需要 quotient induction 或点态 \(|\phi|^2\) 作为四维 crux [Step 29]。Step 29 同时用局部 Kaluza–Klein jet 计算显示点态 twist bound 不应作为目标：在
\[
g=e^{2\psi}(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)+e^{2u}(d\theta+A)^2
\]
中可通过 dilaton Hessian 和 base Ricci 2-jet 在原点隐藏任意 twist square \(S=B^2\)，使 \(\operatorname{Ric}(0)=\Lambda g(0)\) [Step 29]。该点-jet 不是全局反例，但足以否定从 \(C^0\) Ricci pinching 追求 naive pointwise \(|\phi|^2\) Moser bound 的路线 [Step 29]。脚本 `workspace/scripts/step29_dim4_allocation_and_twist_spike.py`、数据 `workspace/data/step29_dim4_allocation_and_twist_spike.json` 和 Lean `workspace/proofs/Step29TwistSpikeAlgebra.lean` 记录这部分 [Step 29]。

Step 29 还验证非中心 H3 左不变场的 Lie derivative 误差与 bracket 同阶：单位非中心场有 \(|L_Xg|^2=2b^2\)，almost-Killing correction 会变得 vacuous；中心方向结构上特殊 [Step 29]。由此四维正 collapse 的真正缺口变成：如何仅从 \(C^0\) Ricci pinching 与 collapse geometry 产生尺度正确、长度可比的中心 almost-Killing 场。Cheeger–Fukaya–Gromov 需全曲率界，Step 11 已否定；Kapovitch–Wilking/Naber–Zhang 给短环群的几乎幂零性，但不给 invariant metric 或 Lie-derivative 控制 [Steps 29–30]。

Step 30 在用户提示下提出 variational almost-Killing 思路：不“寻找” Killing 场，而令 \(Z\) 最小化 \(\int|L_Zg|^2\) 或径向场的 conformal-Killing 能量 \(\int |(L_Zg)^\circ|^2\)，以 Euler–Lagrange 系统提供最小误差，并与 Cheeger–Colding almost-splitting 的 Hessian estimate 关联 [Step 30]。TTCS 修正：径向 Ozuch channel 必须使用 trace-free conformal-Killing operator \(K_gZ=(L_Zg)^\circ\)，因为 \(r\partial_r\) 在平锥上是 conformal Killing；这些 variational fields 不可未经 Weitzenböck/model analysis 直接等同于 Ozuch ALE harmonic vector fields [Step 30]。该思路成为 collapse 与 bubble 两条路线可复用的工具想法，但截至 Step 36 未闭合 [Steps 30,36]。

## 四维正非塌缩 Route A：regular alternative、EH obstruction 与分类旁路 [Steps 30–33]

Step 30 重新打开自 Steps 7–10 后沉寂的四维正非塌缩 bubble 路线。关键 reorientation 是：若 \(\operatorname{Vol}(M_i)\ge v_0>0\)，Myers+Bishop 给全局非塌缩；若 GH limit 无 codimension-4 奇异集，则 Cheeger–Naber \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) 收敛、弱 Ricci 方程和 elliptic regularity 给 smooth exact Einstein limit，Cheeger–Gromov diffeomorphism recovery 把 Einstein metric 放回原 \(M_i\) [Step 30]。因此非塌缩 \(P_4^+\) 真正剩下的是 bubbling；regular noncollapsed alternative 本身已经给出同一 smooth topology 上的 Einstein 度量，而不需要 deformation theory [Step 30]。

Step 30–31 读取 Ozuch 2021 `Integrability of Einstein deformations and desingularizations` 与已有 Ozuch noncollapsed degeneration source，确认 EH first obstruction 是 Taub/Pohozaev conserved quantity。Orbifold expansion \(g_o=e+H_2+O(r^3)\) 与 ALE expansion \(g_b=e+H^4+O(r^{-5})\) 的边界积分在 exact Einstein degeneration 中必须消失；Eguchi–Hanson 情形 \(H^4=-\theta_1^-\circ\omega_1^+/(2r^4)\) 专化为
\[
R_+v=0
\]
对某个 EH orientation \(v\)，若允许 orientation 变化通常写作 \(\det R_+=0\) [Steps 30–31]。Step 31 的脚本 `workspace/scripts/step31_noncollapsed_dichotomy_spectral_audit.py` 验证标准正 Einstein 四维例：圆 \(S^4\) 有 \(\det R_+=1/27\ne0\)，无 EH bubbling；\(\mathbb{CP}^2\)、\(S^2\times S^2\) 作为 Kähler–Einstein 例满足 \(\det R_+=0\) [Step 31]。所有 Kähler–Einstein 四流形都有 \(W_+\) eigenvalue \(-\Lambda/3\)，故 \(R_+=W_+ + \Lambda/3\,\mathrm{Id}\) 有零特征值；但这只是第一障碍消失，不是 Kähler 判据 [Steps 31–33]。

Step 31 形成条件性非塌缩 dichotomy：在 A1 bubble-tree finiteness 与 A2 “near-Einstein degeneration inherits exact-Einstein Ozuch obstruction” 下，非塌缩正 pinched 序列要么 regular，给 \(M\) 上 Einstein metric；要么每个 EH singular point 的 \(R_+\) 有零特征值 [Step 31]。Step 32 修正了 Step 31 handoff 中的 Page metric 实验：Page 是 \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2\) 上的单个刚性正 Einstein metric，普通 blow-up 插入 \((-1)\)-球；EH \(A_1\) resolution 插入 \((-2)\)-球，且 Page 没有 \(t\to0\) bubble scale。对 Page 做 annular flux 只会得到 exact Einstein 的零一致性，不测试 A2 [Step 32]。Page 与 Chen–LeBrun–Weber 的真正意义是说明“无 Kähler–Einstein”不等于“无 Riemannian Einstein” [Step 32]。

Step 32–33 将 A2 从“flux detection experiment”改写为 ansatz-independence/amplitude theorem：任意 \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched 非塌缩 degeneration 必须在合适 neck/bubble expansion 或等价 projection theory 中显出同一个 unsuppressed first-obstruction coefficient [Steps 32–33]。线性 cosmological Einstein tensor
\[
\mathcal E_g=\operatorname{Ric}_g-\frac12s_gg+g
\]
在四维 positive normalization 下 divergence-free，满足
\[
\int_{\partial\Omega}\mathcal E_g(Z,\nu)
=\frac12\int_\Omega\langle\mathcal E_g,L_Zg\rangle
\]
且对 \(C^0\) Ricci defect 安全；但它是 first-order identity，不能直接看到 Ozuch Taub/Wronskian 中 \(H_2\)-\(H^4\) 的 bilinear cross term [Step 30–32]。正确对象是线性化算子的双线性 Wronskian/ Taub quantity [Step 32]。

Step 33 直接读取 LeBrun–Ozuch 2026 source `Desingularizations-of-Conformally-Kaehler-Einstein-Orbifolds`，纠正分类 bypass 的范围：Theorem B 假设 exact positive Einstein sequence、Hermitian/conformally Kähler positive Einstein orbifold limit、genuine singularity、ASD/admissible ALE bubbles；这些不是由 \(\det R_+=0\) 推出的结论 [Step 33]。在这些额外假设下，Theorem 4.1 将 smooth topology 限制为 Del Pezzo diffeotype：\(S^2\times S^2\) 或 \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#l\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2\), \(0\le l\le8\)，且 \(b_+=1\) [Step 33]。因此，条件于 missing Hermitian/admissible input，principal spin stress family \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) 对 \(k\ge2\) 不可能出现在该 classified noncollapsed branch；但 det \(R_+=0\) alone 不给这种排除 [Step 33]。

## Route A 的平衡环、mode-diagonal Wronskian 与 resonance 修复 [Steps 32–36]

## 高维范围重新定位与一般 Einstein 存在问题纠缠 [Steps 22–25, 28–36]

Step 22–24 重新审视 \(n\ge5\)。Knowledge 搜索、Wang survey、Yau 历史预览、LeBrun 高维 sign-coexistence、Lohkamp/Gao–Yau、Gromov–Lawson/Stolz 等没有给出一个已知闭高维流形且已知不承载任何符号 Einstein 度量的普适 reservoir [Steps 22–23]。Wang survey 明确指出高维中“是否每个闭流形都承载某个 Einstein 度量”仍未知，且没有一般非存在障碍；齐性空间“不存在 invariant Einstein”不等于底层无任意 Einstein 度量 [Step 23]。

这使高维反驳路线高度不对称：若所有闭 \(n\)-流形都承载某个 Einstein 度量，则 \(P_n^\sigma\) 对任意 \(\sigma\) 无条件成立；若存在 no-Einstein 流形，反驳 Yau26 还需在这些流形上实现 tight \(\pm1\) pinching [Steps 23–24]。Lohkamp 型负 Ricci 灵活性只给一侧符号，不给 \(\operatorname{Ric}\approx-g\) 的两侧算子控制；正标量曲率 surgery 也远弱于正 Einstein 或 tight positive Ricci pinching [Steps 23–24]。

因此高维研究从“找现成无 Einstein 拓扑”转为研究 tight pinching 左类本身：
\[
\{\text{承载任意紧 }\sigma\text{-pinching 的流形}\}
\subseteq
\{\text{承载 Einstein 度量的流形}\}\ ?
\]
[Steps 23–25]。Step 24 的正 Einstein KK collapse 说明高维正 collapse 可完全 Einstein-compatible；Step 28–29 的 Bochner center bound 可能帮助控制 collapse algebra，但仍缺从 Ricci-only geometry 产生中心 almost-Killing/N-structure 的桥 [Steps 24,28–29]。Steps 30–36 的四维 Route A 与 toric rod-chain工作基本未触及 \(n\ge5\) [Steps 30–36]。

## 当前路线结构、未完成工作与交接判断 [Steps 28–36]

当前研究已形成但未完成的主结构如下。

1. **完整 Yau26 仍开放，四维正分支被拆成非塌缩与塌缩两大前线。** 非塌缩 regular alternative 已清楚：无奇异集时 Cheeger–Naber limit 给 smooth Einstein metric 于同一 \(M\) [Steps 30–31]。Bubbling branch 需要 harmonic-radius/neck-energy input 与二阶 bubble-frame 2-jet matching，才能把 Ozuch EH first obstruction \(R_+v=0\) 从 exact Einstein degeneration 传到 \(C^0\)-pinched degeneration [Steps 31–36]。塌缩 branch 则集中在 toric/infranil collapse、Bochner center almost-Killing桥，以及新识别的 periodic ALF/Weyl rod-chain问题 [Steps 28–36]。

2. **非塌缩 Route A 的错误已被多次修复。** Page metric flux experiment 被撤回，因为 Page 不是 EH degeneration family [Step 32]。线性 cosmological Einstein tensor flux 被保留为 \(C^0\)-safe divergence identity，但不是 bilinear Taub obstruction 的检测器 [Steps 30–32]。Step 34 的 \(\delta\log(1/t)\) rate condition 被 Step 35–36 移除；正确比较在 bubble frame 固定 annulus 做 iterated limit [Steps 34–36]。当前缺口不是 rate hypothesis，而是 second-order blow-up \(k=(\hat g_i-g_{EH})/t_i^2\) 的存在与其 quadratic coefficient 与 orbifold \(R_+\) 2-jet 的匹配 [Steps 35–36]。

3. **Mode-diagonal A1 cone picture 是可复用的局部线性结构，但尚非完整 PDE 定理。** Flat \(\mathbb R^4/\{\pm1\}\) 上偶 \(l\) modes、Wronskian diagonal、\(l=0\) mass/volume invisibility、\(l=2\)/\(-4\) EH pair 已通过脚本和 Ozuch eq. (59) sanity check 支持 [Steps 33–34]。仍需将其放入实际 Bianchi/volume gauge、pure-gauge quotient 与 non-Einstein prelimit convergence 中 [Steps 34–36]。

4. **分类 bypass 只在强额外假设下有用。** LeBrun–Ozuch Theorem B 将 Hermitian/conformally Kähler、exact Einstein sequence、ASD/admissible ALE 作为假设；det \(R_+=0\) 不推出这些 [Step 33]。在这些假设下 smooth topology 为 Del Pezzo diffeotype，排除 \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), \(k\ge2\)，但这不是一般 branch-(b) 排除 [Step 33]。Page/CLW 继续提醒“无 KE”不能等同“无 Riemannian Einstein” [Steps 32–33]。

5. **正塌缩的 toric \(\alpha\)-family 仍是高价值 adversary。** Rod/corner algebra、修正后的 warping 方程、flux identities、local formal matching、CGB 能量、NUT smoothing 都没有杀死它 [Steps 19–26,34–36]。Step 36 的 NUT-vs-strut 纠正特别重要：alternating Delzant rods 通过 codimension-4 NUT transition，而不是 codimension-2 strut；所以 edge-cone strut defect 的粗能量爆炸论证不适用 [Step 36]。下一步若继续塌缩线，应直接研究 periodic alternating toric Ricci-flat Weyl/rod-chain regularity，而非重复 CGB 粗预算 [Steps 35–36]。

6. **Bochner center bound 是正 collapse 的稳固低阶工具，但桥梁仍缺。** 在存在中心 Killing 或尺度正确 almost-Killing 场时，四维 nilpotent fiber 的所有 bracket 都可用中心 Bochner \(L^2\) 控制 [Steps 28–29]。但从 \(C^0\) Ricci pinching 产生这些场、保证长度/scale comparability、以及处理 fixed strata 或 NUT transitions 仍未完成 [Steps 29–30,36]。点态 horizontal twist bound 已被局部 jet 计算 demote，不应作为主目标 [Step 29]。

7. **负分支旁线保持受限与未闭合。** Min–Oo、stable integral obstruction、MV/Ozuch obstruction-amplitude 都排除了若干简单负反例，但真正负分支仍在尺度逃逸、塌缩、零余量或高阶障碍中 [Steps 1–4,22,32]。A01/A03 cutoff-flow/Ishida–LeBrun 进展有潜力给特殊四维负 gap，但当前受相对 Sobolev/塌缩敏感性和 selected-support PDE 控制限制，尚非维数统一 Yau26 结果 [Steps 16,21–24,33–36]。

8. **高维仍与一般 Einstein 存在问题纠缠。** 没有已知 all-sign no-Einstein reservoir；正 Einstein collapse 在所有 \(n\ge5\) 已有 KK 例，说明不能简单禁止 collapse [Steps 22–24]。四维 Route A/rod-chain 的成败不会自动解决高维 [Steps 30–36]。

9. **形式化状态局部但干净。** 已通过 Lean 审计的文件包括 Step 27 H3 algebra、Step 28 Bochner Killing algebra、Step 29 twist-spike algebra；它们是可靠的局部代数/模型核，不是主命题形式化 [Steps 27–29]。Route A、Cheeger–Naber/Ozuch、edge-cone、rod-chain、collapse N-structure 等完全未形式化 [Steps 30–36]。

直接交接给下一 Agent4/Preceptor 的任务应按 Step 36 handoff：审查 positive-branch corrections 是否自洽，特别是 NUT-vs-strut 区分是否对 \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) stress family 的全部相邻 rods 成立，NUT 能量 \(O(1)\) 是否稳健，bubble-frame iterated limit 是否隐藏其他 rate 条件，非塌缩 conditional theorem 的逻辑链是否准确；同时把 A01/A03 负分支消息只作为待独立核验的旁线，不把它们并入已证主结论 [Step 36]。

# Results, Observations, and Their Meaning

## Exact proposition, normalization, and scope

- The controlling target is the user’s exact formulation: for every \(n\ge2\), find dimension-only constants \(c_n<C_n\) such that every closed connected smooth \(n\)-manifold carrying a smooth metric \(g\) with
  \[
  c_ng\le \operatorname{Ric}_g\le C_ng
  \]
  carries some smooth Einstein metric \(h\), with no required relation between \(g\) and \(h\), no restriction on \(\lambda\), and no sign, collapse, symmetry, curvature-operator, or topology hypothesis beyond closed connected smoothness. The dossier `Skills/qiushi-yau26/references/research/20260910.tex` is a research map, not a proof. [Step 1]

- For fixed \(n\), a same-sign interval is normalized by rescaling to a positive or negative branch:
  \[
  P_n^\sigma:\quad \|\operatorname{Ric}_g-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_n,\qquad \sigma=\pm1,
  \]
  implies Einstein existence on the underlying smooth manifold. An interval containing \(0\) would imply Einstein existence on every smooth \(n\)-manifold, because any metric can be rescaled until its Ricci endomorphism lies in that interval. Thus proving one normalized branch in every dimension suffices; a refutation in one dimension must defeat both possible signs. [Steps 1, 3, 23–25]

- Dimensions \(2\) and \(3\) are covered at ordinary mathematical level by uniformization and Ricci flow/geometrization. The unresolved geometric content starts in dimension \(4\), but a four-dimensional theorem alone cannot settle the all-dimensional Yau-26 target. [Steps 1, 5, 23–25]

- In dimension \(4\), no useful interval can straddle \(0\), because rescaling any metric makes the Ricci endomorphism arbitrarily small without changing the smooth topology. Any successful four-dimensional interval must therefore be one-sign. [Step 3]

- In dimensions \(n\ge5\), the inspected literature did not produce a closed smooth manifold known to admit no Einstein metric of any sign. Wang’s survey supports the statement that no general obstruction to Einstein existence is known in high dimensions and warns that nonexistence of invariant Einstein metrics does not prove nonexistence on the underlying smooth manifold. Thus a high-dimensional refutation would first require a no-Einstein topology and then a tight pinching construction on it; if every closed \(n\)-manifold admitted some Einstein metric, Yau-26 would be automatic in that dimension. [Steps 22–24]

## Negative branch, stability, and gluing evidence

- Direct reading of Min–Oo corrected an OCR ambiguity: \(d\) in the theorem denotes diameter. After normalizing \(\max |K|=1\), the extra hypothesis is \(d<\Lambda\), invariantly
  \[
  d(g)^2\max |K_g|<\Lambda^2.
  \]
  For \(n>3\), sufficiently small negative Ricci defect then yields an Einstein metric only inside this full-curvature/diameter class. This is not a pure Ricci-pinching theorem. [Step 1]

- Consequently, a no-Einstein sequence with
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_j}+g_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0
  \]
  must escape every bounded \(d^2\max |K|\) class, through sectional/Weyl concentration, diameter growth, collapse, or related degeneration. Exact large-diameter hyperbolic manifolds also show that a uniform diameter-curvature bound cannot be the final theorem: they have defect \(0\) and are already Einstein. [Steps 1, 22]

- The Morteza–Viaclovsky Calabi-region estimate was converted into the input metric’s operator norm. With
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{g_t}-\Lambda g_t-t\lambda\chi_t o
  =O_{g_{\mathrm{cal}}}(t^2\rho^2),\qquad g_t\sim t\,g_{\mathrm{cal}},
  \]
  raising one index makes the ordinary remainder \(O(t\rho^2)\), hence small on the core and at worst \(O(t^{1/2})\) near \(\rho\sim t^{-1/4}\), but turns the obstruction term \(t\lambda o\) into an order-\(|\lambda|\) non-scalar endomorphism defect. Weighted, \(L^p\), or GH-small residuals therefore do not imply the unweighted operator pinching required by Yau-26; multiple singularities cannot cancel a pointwise supremum defect. [Steps 1, 32]

- This Calabi scaling is the obstruction-amplitude principle later reused in the positive noncollapsed route: nonzero first obstruction produces a scale-critical operator-norm Ricci defect, so \(\delta_i\to0\) should force the first obstruction coefficient to vanish, provided arbitrary pinched degenerations admit an ansatz-independent neck/projection theory. The missing piece is not an exact-family experiment but a theorem that the same unsuppressed coefficient is present in all relevant degenerations. [Steps 1, 7, 30–32]

- Exact-Einstein degeneration results remain narrower than Yau-26. Ozuch weighted normal forms/gluing, LeBrun–Ozuch positive exact-Einstein rigidity, and Yao negative exact-Einstein resolution theory do not directly apply to arbitrary \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched metrics. The proposed one-neck projection/flux identity
  \[
  \int\langle \operatorname{Ric}(g_i)-g_i,\phi_i\rangle=t_i\mathcal O+o(t_i)
  \]
  was not proved; later work replaced this with a balanced-annulus Taub/Wronskian target. [Steps 7–9, 30–35]

- Under bubble rescaling \(\widehat g=r^{-2}g\), the Ricci endomorphism scales as
  \[
  |\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}|_{\widehat g}\lesssim r^2(1+\delta),
  \]
  so blow-ups of pinched sequences become Ricci-flat to order \(r^2\). This supports projection and ALE/ALF limit ideas but does not provide a weighted normal form. [Step 9]

## Corrected Seiberg–Witten and LeBrun evidence

- A factor-four error from Step 2 was retracted. For a four-dimensional Einstein metric \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\), \(s=4\lambda\) and
  \[
  \frac1{24}\int s^2\,d\mu=\frac23\lambda^2\operatorname{Vol},
  \]
  hence
  \[
  8\pi^2(2\chi+3\tau)
  =4\int |W^+|^2\,d\mu+\frac43\lambda^2\operatorname{Vol}.
  \]
  The older coefficient \(16/3\) and the resulting broad exclusion of \(X\#k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\), \(0<k<A\), were false. [Steps 2–3]

- The \(A\) versus \(A-k\) issue was resolved. Individual blow-up monopole classes have square \(A-k\), but LeBrun’s sharp estimate uses a sign family/convex hull and the averaged class \(a=\pi^*K_X\), with \(a^2=A\) and \((a^+)^2\ge A\). Computing only individual class squares misses the class used in the estimate. [Step 3]

- Source-checked LeBrun thresholds are:
  - scalar-only estimates exclude negative Einstein metrics for \(k\ge2A/3\), including the endpoint by strictness;
  - the refined scalar–\(W^+\) estimate improves this to \(k\ge A/3\), subject to orientation, monopole/polarization, chamber, and \(b_+\) hypotheses. [Steps 3–4]

- A stable integral obstruction survives the coefficient correction. If
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}+g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta,
  \]
  then \(\int |E|^2=O(\delta^2)\operatorname{Vol}\). In the refined LeBrun regime,
  \[
  \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\ge
  \sqrt{\frac{p-\frac13}{2}},\qquad p=k/A.
  \]
  At \(p=2/3\),
  \[
  \delta\ge\frac1{1+\sqrt6}\approx0.289897949.
  \]
  This is a scale-independent repulsion from negative pinching for fixed \(p>1/3\), but the margin vanishes as \(p\downarrow1/3\). [Steps 3–4]

- At the exact Ishida–LeBrun boundary, peer work recorded
  \[
  \frac{\operatorname{Vol}}{\pi^2A}\to\frac{32}{9},\qquad
  \frac{\int|W^+|^2}{\pi^2A}\to\frac4{27},\qquad
  \frac{\int|\operatorname{Ric}^0|^2}{\pi^2A}\to0,
  \]
  and
  \[
  \int(s+8\sqrt6\,|W^+|)^2=O(A\delta^2).
  \]
  Equality descriptions suggest almost-Kähler behavior and alignment with the lowest \(W^+\) eigenspace, but no retrieved quantitative theorem converts this total deficit into global near-Kähler rigidity; thin topology-bearing regions remain possible. [Step 4]

- Tight positive pinching implies positive scalar curvature. Therefore standard metric-independent Seiberg–Witten/monopole obstruction families used in the negative branch are poorly aligned with positive-branch counterexamples: the pinched metric itself has positive scalar curvature, although this does not prove Einstein existence on its topology. [Steps 3–4, 18, 25]

## Four-dimensional Chern–Weil accounting

- For either sign,
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta,\qquad \sigma=\pm1,
  \]
  pointwise minimization in
  \[
  8\pi^2\chi
  =\int\left(|W|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|E|^2}{2}\right)d\mu
  \]
  gives
  \[
  \beta(\delta)\operatorname{Vol}
  \le8\pi^2\chi-\int|W|^2
  \le a(\delta)\operatorname{Vol},
  \]
  where
  \[
  \beta(\delta)=
  \begin{cases}
  \frac23(1-\delta)^2,&0\le\delta\le\frac13,\\[1mm]
  \frac23(1+\delta)(1-2\delta),&\frac13\le\delta<\frac12,
  \end{cases}
  \qquad
  a(\delta)=\frac23(1+\delta)^2.
  \]
  The older lower coefficient \(\frac23(1-\delta)^2-2\delta^2\) is valid but weaker and superseded. [Step 4]

- Hence for \(\delta<1/2\),
  \[
  \chi(M)>0,\qquad
  \operatorname{Vol}(M)\le\frac{8\pi^2\chi(M)}{\beta(\delta)}.
  \]
  These are global volume/energy bounds and do not prevent local collapse or curvature concentration. [Step 4]

- Tight pinching also forces strict Hitchin–Thorpe. For
  \[
  \delta<\frac1{1+\sqrt3},
  \]
  one obtains
  \[
  2\chi>3|\tau|.
  \]
  This corrected the Step-17 claim that Hitchin–Thorpe could serve as an external obstruction to a finiteness-to-Einstein bridge: sufficiently tight pinching itself excludes Hitchin–Thorpe violators and equality cases. In particular \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\) and \(\#_4\mathbb{CP}^2\) are not candidate tightly positive-pinched counterexamples. [Steps 4, 18]

- With the session’s curvature-operator Hilbert–Schmidt convention,
  \[
  \int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2=8\pi^2\chi+\int|E|^2.
  \]
  Coefficients differ for the usual \((0,4)\)-tensor norm, so future Chern–Gauss–Bonnet computations must name the convention. Pinching plus the volume bound gives a global \(L^2\)-curvature bound for fixed topology but permits \(O(\chi)\) bubbles. [Steps 4, 10, 14]

- Chern transgression on a region \(U\),
  \[
  \int_U\left(|W|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|E|^2}{2}\right)
  =8\pi^2\chi(U)-\int_{\partial U}\Pi,
  \]
  remains a possible localization mechanism. No complete thick–thin theorem controls boundary transgression on singular or collapsed cuts. [Steps 5, 7]

## Positive comparison, collapse, and compactness

- Positive pinching with \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge(1-\delta)g\) gives Myers diameter control
  \[
  \operatorname{diam}(M,g)\le\pi\sqrt{\frac{n-1}{1-\delta}},
  \]
  Bishop volume upper bounds, \(b_1=0\), and finite \(\pi_1\). The order of \(\pi_1\) is not dimensionally bounded: normalized round lens spaces have \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) while \(|\pi_1|\to\infty\). [Steps 5–6]

- Exact positive Einstein collapse disproves any general “tight positive pinching implies noncollapse” claim. Round lens spaces, higher Hopf quotients, products such as \((S^3/\mathbb Z_q)\times S^{n-3}\) after matching Einstein constants, and later Kaluza–Klein families collapse with defect \(0\). These examples are Einstein-compatible; collapse itself is not evidence against \(P_n^+\). [Steps 6–7, 10, 24]

- Step 5’s assertion that bounded Ricci plus noncollapse gives a global harmonic-radius lower bound and smooth convergence was false and retracted. Exact Einstein sequences can develop Weyl concentration in dimension at least four. [Steps 5, 9]

- Direct reading of Cheeger–Naber established the correct replacement:
  - bounded Ricci and local noncollapse yield a noncollapsed limit that is \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) away from a closed singular set of Hausdorff/Minkowski codimension at least four;
  - in dimension four there are \(L^2\)-curvature and tubular-volume estimates such as
    \[
    \operatorname{Vol}(T_r\{r_h\le r\})\le Cr^4;
    \]
  - harmonic-radius \(\varepsilon\)-regularity uses GH closeness to \(\mathbb R^{n-3}\times C(Z)\), not merely small \(L^2\) curvature. [Steps 6, 9, 35]

- If a positive near-Einstein four-dimensional sequence with a uniform volume lower bound has no singular set in the Cheeger–Naber limit, then the limit solves \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) weakly on the whole smooth limit, elliptic regularity makes it smooth Einstein, and Cheeger–Gromov diffeomorphism recovery places an Einstein metric on the original smooth \(M_i\) for large \(i\). Thus the noncollapsed positive branch reduces to the bubbling alternative; regular noncollapse is an unconditional Einstein-existence case, not merely a regular-part theorem. [Steps 9, 30–33]

- In dimension four, cone annuli in rescaled bounded-Ricci, noncollapsed sequences converge to
  \[
  dr^2+r^2g_{S^3/\Gamma}
  \]
  under Cheeger–Naber volume-ratio hypotheses. This supplies neck geometry but not the weighted two-scale orbifold/ALE normal form needed to evaluate Biquard/Ozuch obstruction coefficients for merely pinched metrics. [Steps 9, 35]

- Cheeger–Naber’s four-dimensional finiteness theorem gives:
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<1/2,\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(M)\ge v>0
  \]
  implies finitely many diffeomorphism types, with the number depending on \((\delta,v)\). It does not assert that these types carry Einstein metrics. [Step 9]

- A conditional finite-cover amplifier was proved. If some \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(v_0>0\) give
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_0
  \Longrightarrow \operatorname{Vol}(N)\ge v_0
  \]
  for every closed simply connected four-manifold \(N\), then Myers makes \(\pi_1(M)\) finite; the universal cover has volume at least \(v_0\); Cheeger–Naber finiteness bounds \(\chi(\widetilde M)\); and
  \[
  \chi(\widetilde M)=|\pi_1(M)|\chi(M),\qquad \chi(\widetilde M)=2+b_2(\widetilde M)\ge2
  \]
  bounds \(|\pi_1(M)|\) and hence gives a volume lower bound for \(M\). The required gap must be topology-uniform; a lower bound \(v_0(\chi)\to0\) is circular. [Steps 10–11, 14]

## Weyl-energy stress family

- For
  \[
  M_k=\#_k(S^2\times S^2),\qquad \chi(M_k)=2k+2,
  \]
  Chern–Gauss–Bonnet and Bishop yield, under tight positive pinching,
  \[
  \int |W|^2\,d\mu
  \ge8\pi^2\left[
  \chi(M)-2\left(\frac{1+\delta}{1-\delta}\right)^2
  \right],
  \]
  hence
  \[
  \int|W|^2\ge16\pi^2k-O_\delta(1),\qquad
  \operatorname{Vol}\le\frac{24\pi^2}{(1-\delta)^2}.
  \]
  These manifolds have positive-Ricci metrics from surgery/core-metric constructions, but no evidence establishes arbitrarily tight two-sided pinching on those constructions. Einstein existence for \(k\ge2\) is unresolved in this record. [Steps 7–9, 18, 25]

- Combining the energy bound with noncollapsed finite-type control gives:
  \[
  \liminf_{k\to\infty}\delta_+(M_k)>0,
  \]
  or every sequence with \(\delta_+(M_k)\to0\) must satisfy
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}(M_k)\to0,\qquad
  \int|W|^2\ge16\pi^2k-o(k).
  \]
  The energy lower bound does not obstruct collapse; \(O(k)\) bubbles can carry \(O(k)\) energy. [Steps 8–9, 14]

- The strategic role of this family is precise but limited. Constructing tight collapsing pinched metrics would place these topologies in the left-hand pinched class, but would not refute Yau-26 without independent proof that they carry no Einstein metric. Conversely, an invariant volume obstruction would cover only the invariant subclass unless a general-to-invariant bridge were proved. [Steps 18–21, 25]

## Failure of pointwise \(C^0\)-Ricci regularity

- An explicit Calderón–Zygmund Hessian-spike family on the Einstein manifold \(S^2\times S^2\) disproves pointwise full-curvature control from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching. In local product-polar coordinates,
  \[
  g=dx^2+dy^2
  +e^{2(F_1+u)}d\theta^2
  +e^{2(F_2-u)}d\phi^2,\qquad
  F_1=\log\sin x,\quad F_2=\log\sin y.
  \]
  Opposite warping cancels \(\nabla^2u\) from the base Ricci block; only \(\Delta u\) enters fiber Ricci components, while mixed Riemann components retain the full Hessian. [Step 11]

- The spike
  \[
  w_\sigma(X,Y)
  =-\frac12XY\log(X^2+Y^2+\sigma^2)
  \]
  satisfies
  \[
  |\Delta w_\sigma|\le\frac94,\qquad
  \sup|\nabla w_\sigma|\lesssim0.362,\qquad
  \partial_{XY}w_\sigma(0)=\log(1/\sigma)\to\infty.
  \]
  Taking \(\sigma=e^{-\Lambda}\), \(a_\Lambda=\Lambda^{-2/3}\) gives smooth closed metrics with
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_g-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}
  =O(\Lambda^{-2/3})\to0,\qquad
  |\mathrm{Rm}_g|(0)\gtrsim\Lambda^{1/3}\to\infty.
  \]
  At \(\Lambda=500\), the recorded defect was about \(0.032\), center curvature about \(24.4\), and added Hessian \(L^2\)-energy about \(0.005\). [Step 11]

- The vanishing-energy statement concerns the added spike contribution, not total global \(\int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2\), which retains background/topological energy. The determinant is unchanged:
  \[
  e^{F_1+u}e^{F_2-u}=e^{F_1+F_2},
  \]
  so this is a noncollapsed, volume-preserving example. It is not a Yau-26 counterexample because \(S^2\times S^2\) already carries an Einstein metric. [Steps 11, 14, 22]

- A principal-symbol check explains why naive high-frequency TT perturbations do not give the same effect: Ricci and Weyl have the same second-order frequency scaling, and the principal Ricci-symbol kernel is gauge. The construction exploits nonlinear opposite-warp cancellation and endpoint Calderón–Zygmund behavior. [Steps 10–11]

- The CZ spike does not defeat the later harmonic-radius/annular formulation of the noncollapsed route. It refutes pointwise curvature regularity from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching, but its high Hessian is exponentially localized and can have small \(C^{1,\alpha}\) harmonic-coordinate effect; a sequence may have unbounded curvature and still converge to a smooth Einstein limit. The load-bearing regularity question is instead whether noncollapse, \(C^0\) Ricci pinching, and small buffered annular \(L^2\) curvature/volume-cone control give harmonic-radius control at the annulus scale. [Steps 33, 35]

## Collapse, Sobolev constants, and the four-dimensional negative smoothing route

- A collapsed model shows why raw critical-energy smallness is not collapse-neutral. On \(S^1_\ell\times B^3\), fiber-independent test functions force any downstairs four-dimensional \(L^4\) Sobolev constant to grow at least like \(\ell^{-1/4}\). A normalized hyperbolic/cusp model has \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\), \(|\mathrm{Rm}|^2=8/3\), and raw \(\int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2\to0\) as volume collapses, while the relative critical product
  \[
  A_\ell^2\|\mathrm{Rm}\|_2
  \]
  remains \(O(1)\). Thus raw local energy plus a dimension-only downstairs Sobolev constant cannot imply pointwise curvature bounds. [Step 22]

- The Step-21 Gaussian heat calculation did not provide positive evidence for a weighted parabolic theorem. In dimension four, both critical \(L^2\) energy and schematic estimates \(|a\,\mathrm{Rm}|\lesssim\beta/t\) are scale invariant; an \(O(1)\) Gaussian ratio is expected. The CZ spike is noncollapsed and does not probe the difficult collapsed regime. [Steps 21–22]

- Any valid collapsed smoothing theorem must either retain a relative Sobolev constant \(A_\alpha\) and the critical product \(A_\alpha^2\|F\|_2\), or work on genuine buffered noncollapsed covers where cutoff, weight \(a=\chi^2\), spatial test functions, and normalized cutoff flow pull back equivariantly. Exponential-map charts available only after positive-time curvature control cannot supply the initial Sobolev input. [Steps 22–24]

- The A01/A03 four-dimensional cutoff-flow negative-branch route remains conditional. It evolved to support-energy variables
  \[
  S_\alpha=A_\alpha^4H_{2,\alpha},\qquad
  \Gamma=\sup_\alpha S_\alpha^{1/2},
  \]
  and requires bounded-degree cooperative propagation rather than a false Whitney-volume-normal energy estimate. A load-bearing requirement is comparability of neighboring relative Sobolev constants; otherwise factors \((A_\alpha/A_\beta)^4\) can destroy volume-independent graph absorption. The abstract Nash shortcut was refuted by the inverse-square Hardy potential, so an explicit critical \(H_2\to H_3\) Wang/Moser step remains necessary. [Steps 23–24]

- This route still lacks a fully checked localized weak tensor-energy inequality including evolving measure, nested time-space cutoffs, finite-neighbor leakage, Hessian-\(a\) integration by parts, current-time critical-product control, and adaptation from \(-2a\operatorname{Ric}\) to \(-2a(\operatorname{Ric}+g)\). Even if completed, its recorded endpoint is at most a special critical four-dimensional negative Ishida–LeBrun gap, not unrestricted \(P_4^-\), any \(n\ge5\) theorem, or Yau-26. Ordinary Hitchin–Thorpe cannot be its endpoint because tight pinching already implies strict Hitchin–Thorpe. [Steps 22–27]

- Peer-session updates in Steps 29–36 remained unresolved for Yau-26 purposes. A01/A03 reported progress on terminal recalibration, general-\(p\) tensor inequalities, unregularized \(J_6\) persistence, and cutoff-jet continuation, but these were not independently fully verified in S0910A02. A03’s temporary claim that the route gave only per-manifold gaps because \(\gamma=S^2H_2^{1/2}\) diverges under collapse was later retracted at status level; the safest current S0910A02 evidence is that the negative-flow route is unresolved and remains sensitive to collapse/Sobolev constants, so it is not yet a dimension-only Yau-26 gap. [Steps 29, 33–36]

## General torus-invariant determinant and twist identities

- For a local \(T^2\)-invariant metric
  \[
  g=g_B+h_{IJ}(d\phi^I+A^I)(d\phi^J+A^J),
  \qquad w=\sqrt{\det h},
  \]
  exact symbolic jet calculations give
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^{V}
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}+\frac12|F|_h^2.
  \]
  Therefore exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\) implies
  \[
  \left(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|_h^2\right)w=2\lambda w.
  \]
  [Step 12]

- If the torus action has a degeneration boundary, \(w>0\) in the orbit-space interior and \(w=0\) at the boundary. Thus \(w\) is the positive ground state of a Schrödinger operator. In the exact positive-Einstein case,
  \[
  \lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)\le2\lambda;
  \]
  under
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta,
  \]
  Rayleigh testing gives
  \[
  \lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)\le2(1+\delta).
  \]
  No derivatives of the Ricci defect are needed. [Step 13]

- A mixed-Ricci computation gave
  \[
  d(wh_{IJ}*_BF^J)=0.
  \]
  Exact orthogonal transitivity for closed simply connected Einstein \(T^2\)-manifolds with fixed strata is source-supported, but no approximate orthogonal-transitivity theorem is known for merely pinched metrics. [Steps 12–13]

- For exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\), integration of the twisted determinant equation gives
  \[
  \Phi_{\partial}
  +\frac12\int_\Omega |F|_h^2w
  =2\int_\Omega w,
  \]
  and, with the session’s toric period normalization,
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_4
  =2\pi^2\Phi_{\partial}
  +\pi^2\int_\Omega |F|_h^2w.
  \]
  Twist increases volume for fixed boundary flux but can reduce boundary flux at fixed volume. [Step 22]

- Sign and normalization checks used:
  - a compact Einstein metric with \(\lambda\le0\) cannot have a nonzero Killing field with zeros, consistent with the positive Dirichlet eigenvalue consequence;
  - normalized round \(S^4\), radius \(\sqrt3\), has orbit space a quarter of \(S^2(\sqrt3)\), \(w=r_1r_2\),
    \[
    \Delta w=-2w,\qquad \int_\Omega w=6,\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(S^4)=24\pi^2.
    \]
  [Step 13]

- For a twist-free diagonal \(T^k\)-invariant metric
  \[
  g=g_B+\sum_{I=1}^kp_I^2\,d\theta_I^2,\qquad w=\prod_{I=1}^kp_I,
  \]
  one has
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^{V}
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}.
  \]
  Under normalized positive pinching and a degeneration boundary,
  \[
  k(1-\delta)
  \le\lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)
  \le k(1+\delta).
  \]
  The proof is independent of base dimension; symbolic checks covered \(k=1,\ldots,5\). This is an all-dimensional invariant identity, not a theorem for arbitrary manifolds. [Steps 13, 17]

## Corrected diagonal toric reduced system and formal toric collapse seed

- In the diagonal twist-free case
  \[
  g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2,\qquad w=pq,\quad v=\log(p/q),
  \]
  the vertical equations are
  \[
  r_p+r_q=-\frac{\Delta w}{w},\qquad
  r_p-r_q=-\frac1w\operatorname{div}(w\nabla v),
  \]
  while
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}^H
  =K_Bg_B-\left[
    \nabla^2\log w+
    \frac12\bigl(d\log w\otimes d\log w+dv\otimes dv\bigr)
  \right].
  \]
  [Steps 14, 18]

- Step 25 corrected a sign in the individual exact positive-Einstein warping equations. The correct equations are
  \[
  -\Delta_Bp=(1-K_B)p,\qquad
  -\Delta_Bq=(1-K_B)q,
  \]
  not \(-\Delta_Bp=(K_B-1)p\). Checks include:
  - on \(S^2\times S^2\), \(-\Delta\sin x=\sin x=(1-0)\sin x\);
  - on normalized \(S^4\), \(-\Delta r_1=\frac23r_1=(1-\frac13)r_1\). [Steps 25–26]

- This sign correction invalidated Step 20’s claimed interior identity \(\int K_Bw=\int w\). The correct Green calculation yields flux equi-partition
  \[
  \Phi_p=\Phi_q=\int_\Omega w,
  \]
  with \(K_B\) terms cancelling. It does not remove all interior information: \(p\) solves
  \[
  (-\Delta_B+K_B)p=p
  \]
  with Dirichlet data on \(p\)-rods and Neumann-type behavior on \(q\)-rods, and similarly for \(q\). The mixed-boundary ground-state eigenvalue is exactly \(1\). [Steps 25–26]

- The formal large-negative-curvature collar evades this mixed spectral constraint by cancellation. On a short adjacent rod, endpoint vanishing pins a tangential mode
  \[
  \mu\sim\pi^2/L^2\sim2A,
  \]
  offsetting the well \(K_B=-A\) and leaving transverse \(\cosh(\sqrt A\,n)\)-type behavior instead of oscillatory instability. The remaining possible obstruction lies at corner-to-interior transition or next-order matching, not in the retracted coarse integral identity. [Step 26]

- The corrected orbit curvature relation is
  \[
  K_B
  =\frac14\left(|\nabla v|^2-|\nabla\log w|^2\right)
  =-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle.
  \]
  The earlier \(K_B\ge3\) claim was false. It was checked on the flat orbit rectangle of \(S^2\times S^2\) and the spherical orbit space of normalized \(S^4\). [Step 14]

- In the simply connected toric setting, the orbit space is a disk-like polygon with geodesic edges and right-angle vertices, and
  \[
  \int_\Omega K_B\,dA=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}m
  \]
  for \(m\) vertices. This matches \(S^4\), \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), and \(S^2\times S^2\). [Step 13]

- Near a rod where one circle collapses, the corrected edge equation is
  \[
  Q''+\bigl(1-2K_B|_{\mathrm{edge}}\bigr)Q=0,
  \]
  and the fixed two-sphere has intrinsic curvature
  \[
  K_\Sigma=1-2K_B|_{\mathrm{edge}}.
  \]
  [Steps 13–14]

- For periodic rod labels
  \[
  (1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),\ldots
  \]
  on even polygons, every adjacent pair is a standard basis up to sign. Integral cohomology/intersection-form computations for tested \(m=4,6,8,10,12\) gave rank \(m-2\), determinant \(\pm1\), even parity, and signature zero; explicit unimodular splittings through \(m\le14\) gave hyperbolic planes, strongly consistent with \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\). A full Orlik–Raymond diffeomorphism proof remains required if topology becomes theorem-critical. [Steps 18–19]

- In a fixed-point chart
  \[
  g=dr^2+\mu(r,t)^2dt^2+p(r,t)^2d\theta^2+q(r,t)^2d\phi^2
  \]
  with
  \[
  \mu=1+ur^2+\cdots,\quad
  p=r+ar^3+\cdots,\quad
  q=t(1+ur^2)+bt^3+\cdots,
  \]
  the base edge curvature is \(K_B=-2u\). Independent warped-product and Christoffel calculations give
  \[
  -6a-4u-1=0,\qquad -6b-4u-1=0.
  \]
  Writing \(A=-K_B=2u\),
  \[
  a=b=-\frac{2A+1}{6},
  \]
  matching the one-dimensional rod ODE. [Step 19]

- The next formal order remains solvable with \(A\) free. Choosing
  \[
  q_{05}=\frac{(1+2A)^2}{120}
  \]
  gives
  \[
  m_{40}=-\frac{A(2A+1)}{24},\quad m_{22}=0,\quad
  p_{50}=\frac{22A^2+10A+1}{120},\quad p_{32}=0,\quad
  q_{23}=-\frac{A(2A+1)}{12}.
  \]
  Thus local smoothness parity, right-angle corner conditions, and low-order exact Ricci equations impose no cap on \(A\). [Step 19]

- The exact rod identity follows from the edge ODE and unit endpoint slopes:
  \[
  \int_{\mathrm{rod}}(1-2K_{\mathrm{edge}})Q\,ds=2,
  \]
  hence
  \[
  \Phi_i=\int Q\,ds=2+2\int K_{\mathrm{edge}}Q\,ds.
  \]
  If \(K_{\mathrm{edge}}=-A\) is constant,
  \[
  Q(s)=\frac{\sin(\sqrt{1+2A}\,s)}{\sqrt{1+2A}},\qquad
  L=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{1+2A}},
  \]
  and
  \[
  \Phi_i=\frac{2}{1+2A}
  =\frac{2L^2}{\pi^2}.
  \]
  With the toric period convention,
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_4=2\pi^2\sum_i\Phi_i=4\sum_iL_i^2.
  \]
  This reproduces \(24\pi^2\) for normalized \(S^4\), \(18\pi^2\) for normalized \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), and \(16\pi^2\) for \(S^2\times S^2\). [Steps 20–21]

- Cauchy–Schwarz gives only
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_4\ge\frac{4L_{\mathrm{tot}}^2}{m}.
  \]
  Thus \(O(1)\) control of perimeter, coarse scale, or comparable modulus can at best yield a \(C/m\) lower bound, insufficient for the topology-uniform \(v_0\) needed by the finite-cover amplifier. [Step 21]

- The formal adversary takes
  \[
  A_m=m^\alpha,\qquad 1<\alpha\le2.
  \]
  Then
  \[
  L_m\sim\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2\,m^{\alpha/2}},\qquad
  \Phi_i\sim m^{-\alpha},\qquad
  \sum_i\Phi_i\sim m^{1-\alpha}\to0.
  \]
  A collar width carrying the signed Gauss–Bonnet burden has width-to-rod-length ratio tending to about \(1/\pi\) (recorded near \(0.312\) at \(m=200\)). The family passes the rod ODE, unit slopes, low-order corner equations, flux equi-partition, determinant equation at the formal level, signed Gauss–Bonnet scaling, and mixed spectral cancellation. [Steps 19, 21, 25–26]

- A regular right-angled polygon of constant curvature \(-A\) cannot realize the rod length: its side asymptotic is \(1.762747/\sqrt A\), whereas the rod ODE requires \(\pi/\sqrt{2A}=2.221441/\sqrt A\), ratio \(1.2602155895\). This excludes only the overly symmetric regular constant-curvature model, not strip-like boundary collars with nearly flat interiors. [Step 21]

- After the Step-25 sign correction, no verified coarse integral identity forces \(\int w\) bounded below independently of \(m\). The formal \(\alpha\)-family is therefore BREAK-compatible at the level of all tested scalar, rod, corner, spectral, and integral conditions. It remains not a global smooth metric: unresolved issues include nonlinear global filling, next-order corner-to-interior matching, horizontal traceless control in transition regions, matrix-fiber/twist effects, holonomy, and global smoothness. [Steps 19–21, 25–26]

## Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Kottler edge family and collapsed ALF interpretation

- Flexible edge expansions showed that arbitrarily negative edge curvature is locally compatible with exact Einstein equations:
  \[
  R_2=A/2,\qquad
  p_3=-(2A+1)/6,\qquad
  R_4=-A(2A+1)/24.
  \]
  The earlier failure after imposing \(a(r)=\cosh(\sqrt A\,r)\) was an artifact of overconstraining the ansatz. [Step 15]

- The exact separated germ
  \[
  g=dr^2+p(r)^2d\theta^2+a(r)^2g_{S^2(\kappa)},
  \qquad \kappa=1+2A,
  \]
  satisfies
  \[
  a'=Ap,\qquad
  2aa''+(a')^2=\kappa-a^2,
  \]
  with first integral
  \[
  a(a')^2=\kappa(a-1)-\frac{a^3-1}{3}.
  \]
  Its second zero of \(p\) occurs at
  \[
  a_+=\frac{-1+\sqrt{9+24A}}2,
  \]
  and the second-bolt slope is
  \[
  \mu=\frac{2a_++1}{a_+(a_++2)}.
  \]
  [Step 15]

- This family is Euclidean Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Birmingham–Kottler:
  \[
  f(\rho)=1-\frac{2M}{\rho}-\frac{\rho^2}{3},\qquad
  \rho_h=(1+2A)^{-1/2},\qquad
  M=\frac{A+\frac13}{(2A+1)^{3/2}}.
  \]
  The horizon ratio is \(a_+\), and the surface-gravity ratio is \(\mu\). [Step 16]

- The second degeneration is a codimension-two cone along an embedded \(S^2\), not an isolated \(\mathbb R^4/\Gamma\) point. Atiyah–LeBrun edge-cone Chern–Weil theory, with defects involving terms such as
  \[
  2(1-\beta)\chi(\Sigma),\qquad
  (1-\beta^2)[\Sigma]^2,
  \]
  is the relevant bookkeeping framework, not isolated-orbifold Eguchi–Hanson/Biquard theory. [Step 16]

- Smoothing the black-hole bolt gives cone angle \(2\pi\mu\) at the cosmological bolt and collapsing volume as \(A\to\infty\); smoothing the cosmological bolt gives volume tending to \(24\pi^2\) but a large cone angle at the small bolt. Both ends are smooth only for \(\mu=1\), hence \(A=0\), the Nariai product \(S^2(1)\times S^2(1)\). The matching is nondegenerate:
  \[
  \left.\frac{d\mu}{dA}\right|_{A=0}=-\frac43.
  \]
  No quantitative \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched stability analogue has been proved. [Steps 16–17]

- Step 34 identified the high-\(A\) bolt scaling as Euclidean Schwarzschild. Each formal rod/bolt region has curvature scale \((2A)^2\), area scale \(2\pi/A\), and transverse width scale \(\pi/A\), giving an \(8\pi^2\) curvature-energy quantum per rod in the model. Rescaling by \(\sqrt{2A}\) sends the cosmological constant to zero and the Kottler mass to
  \[
  \widehat M
  =\frac{\sqrt{2A}(A+1/3)}{(2A+1)^{3/2}}
  \to \frac12.
  \]
  The limiting local model is Euclidean Schwarzschild, which is ALF, not ALE, and not anti-self-dual. [Step 34]

- Step 35 corrected the isolated-bubble interpretation: since
  \[
  L=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{1+2A}},\qquad \sqrt{2A}\,L\to\pi,
  \]
  adjacent rods remain at finite distance after \(\sqrt A\)-rescaling if rod spacings are comparable. The collapsed limit of the formal \(\alpha\)-family should be viewed as an infinite or periodic toric Ricci-flat rod-chain problem with Schwarzschild-type \(S^2\) bolts and NUT transitions, not a single isolated ALF Schwarzschild bubble. [Step 35]

- Step 36 corrected the “no energy slack for struts” argument. In Atiyah–LeBrun edge-cone formulas, a codimension-two strut contributes a separate defect term; it is not simply bulk \(\int|W|^2\) energy. A smoothed conical deficit of angle \(2\pi(1-\beta)\) at transverse scale \(\varepsilon\) has heuristic energy cost
  \[
  \int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2\sim (1-\beta)^2|\Sigma|/\varepsilon^2,
  \]
  which can diverge or remain \(O(1)\) depending on smoothing scale. Thus bulk energy saturation alone does not prove struts impossible. [Step 36]

- The same Step 36 analysis found that the alternating Delzant rod model has NUTs rather than struts. Adjacent rod normals in a smooth toric 4-manifold must form a \(\mathbb Z^2\)-basis; same-label adjacent rods would violate the Delzant condition. In the alternating \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\)-type model, adjacent rods collapse different \(S^1\) factors and meet at codimension-four \(T^2\)-fixed points (NUTs), not codimension-two edge-cone struts. Heuristic NUT smoothing costs \(O(1)\) per corner because curvature concentration occurs in a four-dimensional ball: \(\varepsilon^{-4}\varepsilon^4=O(1)\). This removes the divergent strut-energy obstruction for the main formal \(\alpha\)-family. [Step 36]

- The collapsed positive branch is therefore a concrete but unresolved Weyl/gravitational-instanton decision problem. If a smooth periodic alternating toric Ricci-flat 4-manifold exists with Schwarzschild-type \(S^2\) bolts and smooth NUT transitions, it would be a serious BREAK mechanism for smooth toric collapse with \(\operatorname{Ric}\to g\). If impossible, the impossibility proof may reveal the needed topology-uniform positive-collapse obstruction. Current evidence has not decided existence or nonexistence. [Steps 35–36]

## Kaluza–Klein circle collapse in all dimensions

- For a constant-length principal circle metric, with circle period \(2\pi\),
  \[
  g=\pi^*g_B+t^2(d\theta+A)^2,\qquad
  U=t^{-1}\xi,\qquad \phi=tF,
  \]
  and two-form convention \(|F|^2=\sum_{i<j}F_{ij}^2\),
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_M^H
  =\operatorname{Ric}_B-\frac12(\phi\circ\phi),\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_M(U,U)=\frac12|\phi|^2,\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_M^{\mathrm{mix}}=\pm\frac12d_B^*\phi.
  \]
  Exact \(\operatorname{Ric}_M=g_M\) is equivalent to
  \[
  |\phi|^2=2,\qquad d_B^*\phi=0,\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_B=g_B+\frac12\phi\circ\phi,
  \]
  while \(d\phi=0\) follows from connection curvature/Bianchi. [Steps 6, 24]

- For a closed three-dimensional base, writing \(\phi=*b\) makes \(b\) closed and coclosed, and the equations force
  \[
  |b|^2=2,\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_B=2g_B-\frac12b\otimes b,
  \]
  contradicting Bochner. Quantitatively, the pinched constant-fiber model is impossible for
  \[
  \delta<\frac1{1+\sqrt2}.
  \]
  This applies only to constant fiber length and free circle action; variable dilaton, singular fibers, and general collapse are outside it. [Step 6]

- The suggested extension of this obstruction to every odd-dimensional base was false. For any normalized closed positive Einstein \(N^d\), \(d\ge2\), take
  \[
  B=S^2_{\operatorname{Ric}=2}\times N^d_{\operatorname{Ric}=1},
  \qquad \phi=\sqrt2\,\omega_{S^2}.
  \]
  These satisfy the Kaluza–Klein equations. Choosing Chern number \(q\) over the \(S^2\) factor and
  \[
  t=\frac{\sqrt2}{q}
  \]
  gives exact positive Einstein metrics on
  \[
  L(q,1)\times N^d
  \cong (S^3(\sqrt2)/\mathbb Z_q)\times N^d
  \]
  in every total dimension \(n=d+3\ge5\), with fiber length \(2\pi\sqrt2/q\), volume proportional to \(q^{-1}\), and bounded sectional curvature. [Step 24]

- Thus codimension-one positive Einstein collapse exists in \(n=3\) and every \(n\ge5\), while the three-base/four-total-dimensional Bochner obstruction is exceptional. The proper all-dimensional positive-collapse program is to characterize collapse as Einstein-compatible or incompatible, not to forbid it wholesale. [Step 24]

## Nilpotent collapse, Heisenberg models, and Bochner center bounds

- Lower Ricci bounds provide group-theoretic collapse structure but not automatically a controlled smooth submersion. Naber–Zhang/Kapovitch–Wilking give almost-nilpotent short-loop groups under \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-(n-1)\) and a fibered fundamental group of rank at most the codimension of the Ricci limit; maximal rank gives noncollapse on suitable local covers. Rong’s smooth infra-nil fiber bundles require local rewinding-volume and GH-to-regular-base hypotheses. None of these sources automatically controls the original metric’s O’Neill tensors \(A,T,N\). [Steps 26–27]

- In the totally geodesic \(T=0\) Heisenberg case, with
  \[
  [e_1,e_2]=b e_3,
  \]
  the intrinsic fiber Ricci tensor is
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}^F
  =\operatorname{diag}\left(-\frac{b^2}{2},
  -\frac{b^2}{2},\frac{b^2}{2}\right),
  \qquad \operatorname{scal}_F=-\frac{b^2}{2}.
  \]
  The twist contribution \(Q\ge0\) has rank at most \(\binom d2\) for base dimension \(d\). Exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) would require
  \[
  Q=\operatorname{diag}
  \left(1+\frac{b^2}{2},1+\frac{b^2}{2},1-\frac{b^2}{2}\right).
  \]
  Hence the upper pinching bounds the center term, and an \(H_3\) fiber over a two-dimensional base is impossible by rank in the \(T=0\) case. This is a special algebraic obstruction, not general abelian forcing. [Step 26]

- The second fundamental form can compensate Milnor anisotropy. For the diagonal cohomogeneity-one metric
  \[
  g=dt^2+a(t)^2(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)+c(t)^2\theta_3^2,
  \qquad [E_1,E_2]=E_3,
  \]
  set
  \[
  b=\frac{c}{a^2},\qquad k_1=\frac{a'}a,\qquad k_3=\frac{c'}c,\qquad H=2k_1+k_3.
  \]
  A moving-frame/Koszul calculation gives
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{00}
  =-2(k_1'+k_1^2)-(k_3'+k_3^2),
  \]
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{11}=\operatorname{Ric}_{22}
  =-\frac{b^2}{2}-k_1'-Hk_1,
  \]
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{33}
  =\frac{b^2}{2}-k_3'-Hk_3.
  \]
  [Step 26]

- For exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=\Lambda g\), the vertical equations become
  \[
  k_1'=-\Lambda-\frac{b^2}{2}-Hk_1,\qquad
  k_3'=-\Lambda+\frac{b^2}{2}-Hk_3,
  \qquad
  (\log b)'=k_3-2k_1,
  \]
  and the \(00\)-equation is the constraint
  \[
  C_\Lambda=b^2+4k_1^2+8k_1k_3+4\Lambda=0,
  \]
  preserved by
  \[
  C_\Lambda'=-2HC_\Lambda.
  \]
  [Steps 26–27]

- Exact algebraic identities are
  \[
  2|T|^2-(b^2+4\Lambda)
  =2(2k_1+k_3)^2-C_\Lambda,
  \]
  \[
  4((\log b)')^2-5(b^2+4\Lambda)
  =4(3k_1+k_3)^2-5C_\Lambda,
  \]
  where \(|T|^2=2k_1^2+k_3^2\). On the exact constraint surface,
  \[
  |T|^2\ge\frac{b^2+4\Lambda}{2},\qquad
  |(\log b)'|^2\ge\frac54(b^2+4\Lambda).
  \]
  [Steps 26–27]

- If the four diagonal Ricci components satisfy
  \[
  |\rho_i-\Lambda|\le\delta,
  \]
  elimination gives
  \[
  S=b^2+4k_1^2+8k_1k_3=2\rho_0-4\rho_1-2\rho_3,
  \]
  and robust bounds
  \[
  |T|^2\ge
  \frac{b^2+4\Lambda-8\delta}{2},
  \qquad
  |(\log b)'|^2\ge
  \frac54(b^2+4\Lambda-8\delta).
  \]
  For \(\Lambda>0\) and \(\delta<\Lambda/2\), the normalized bracket \(b\) has no critical point on the regular region. [Step 27]

- This is stronger than a pointwise Milnor obstruction. Large \(b\) is locally compatible with exact positive Einstein equations, but forces large shape operator and rapid relative scaling. In the exact nonnegative regime,
  \[
  \left|\frac d{dt}\frac1b\right|\ge\frac{\sqrt5}{2},
  \]
  while
  \[
  K_{12}=-\frac34b^2-k_1^2.
  \]
  Thus regions with \(b\ge B\) have thickness \(O(B^{-1})\) and carry \(O(B^2)\) curvature; persistent ungraded nonabelian bracket plateaux are impossible, although thin high-curvature shells are allowed. [Steps 26–27]

- A local numerical integration with \(b_0=20\), \(k_1=10\), \(k_3=-10.05\) satisfied the exact positive-Einstein ODE and constraint to sampled errors below \(10^{-12}\), demonstrating explicitly that large bracket can be compensated only by \(|T|\sim b\) and rapid bracket variation. This supports the formulas but is not needed for the exact inequalities. [Step 26]

- The sign dependence is real. Complex hyperbolic \(CH^2\) horosphere data
  \[
  \Lambda=-\frac32,\qquad b=1,\qquad k_1=-\frac12,\qquad k_3=-1
  \]
  satisfy
  \[
  C_\Lambda=0,\qquad (\log b)'=0,\qquad k_1'=k_3'=0,
  \]
  with expected sectional-curvature pattern \(-1\) and \(-1/4\). For \(\Lambda<0\), \(b^2+4\Lambda\) can be negative and the positive lower bounds become vacuous, permitting stable nonabelian horosphere geometry. [Step 27]

- For a periodic one-dimensional regular orbit space, positive \(b\) must have a critical point, contradicting the positive-pinched rate inequality. Under ordinary smooth tubular-end hypotheses on a compact interval, the boundary Heisenberg nilmanifold can only be the central-circle boundary of a disk bundle over a torus; then \(c\to0\), \(a\to a_0>0\), and \(b=c/a^2\to0\) at both endpoints, forcing an interior maximum and contradicting rate nonvanishing. Consequently no compact closed model exists for
  \[
  \delta<\Lambda/2
  \]
  within the diagonal \(H_3\), one-dimensional-base, no-twist ansatz with ordinary smooth tubular ends. This does not cover orbifold/edge/nonordinary singular ends, finite-quotient infranil variants outside the assumptions, higher-dimensional bases with twist, non-diagonal metrics, or arbitrary collapsed manifolds. [Step 27]

- Step 28 generalized part of the positive-sign Heisenberg mechanism using Bochner. For a central Killing field \(Z\) in a nilpotent fiber structure,
  \[
  \int |\nabla Z|^2=\int\operatorname{Ric}(Z,Z)
  \le(\Lambda+\delta)\int |Z|^2.
  \]
  In an \(H_3\) fiber with unit central direction and bracket \(b\),
  \[
  |\nabla^F Z|^2=\frac{b^2}{2}|Z|^2,
  \]
  and \(\nabla_UZ=\nabla^F_UZ+T_UZ\) has orthogonal nonnegative pieces, giving the weighted estimate
  \[
  \langle b^2\rangle_{|Z|^2}\le2(\Lambda+\delta).
  \]
  This is ansatz-free and dimension-free once such a central Killing field exists. [Step 28]

- TTCS corrected the scope of Step 28: a compact Lie algebra has no nonabelian nilpotent subalgebra because \(\operatorname{ad}_X\) is both skew and nilpotent only when zero. Thus the full Heisenberg group cannot act isometrically on a closed manifold in the required way; only the central circle can. The Bochner bound controls brackets landing in the center, not an entire nonabelian isometric nilpotent action. [Step 28]

- Step 28 also derived the almost-Killing correction
  \[
  \int|\nabla Z|^2
  =\int\operatorname{Ric}(Z,Z)
  +\frac12\int|\sigma|^2-\frac14\int(\operatorname{tr}\sigma)^2,
  \qquad \sigma=L_Zg,
  \]
  giving a route if one can produce vector fields with \(\|L_Zg\|\) controlled at the collapse scale. TTCS sharpened that the scale requirement \(\tau=O(\varepsilon)\) already suffices for normalized bracket vanishing. [Step 28]

- The same Bochner decomposition bounds horizontal twist only in weighted \(L^2\), not pointwise:
  \[
  \langle |\phi|^2\rangle_{|Z|^2}\le4(\Lambda+\delta)
  \]
  in the recorded normalization. The remaining induction gap is average-to-pointwise or, after Step 29’s reallocation, scale comparability/field production rather than a missing Bochner identity. [Step 28]

- In dimension four, every nilpotent collapse fiber has dimension at most three, hence is abelian or \(H_3\), so \([\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n]\subseteq\mathfrak z\). Therefore, once a central exact or scale-correct almost-Killing field exists, the Bochner center estimate controls every fiber bracket in weighted \(L^2\). The horizontal-twist quotient-induction problem first bites for 3-step fibers in \(n\ge5\), not in the four-dimensional bracket-control crux. [Step 29]

- Step 29 showed pointwise horizontal twist bounds should not be pursued from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching alone. For a local circle-bundle metric
  \[
  g=e^{2\psi}(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)+e^{2u}(d\theta+A)^2
  \]
  with
  \[
  A=-(By/2)\,dx+(Bx/2)\,dy,\quad
  u=H(x^2+y^2+z^2)/2,\quad
  \psi=p_a(x^2+y^2)/2+p_cz^2/2,
  \]
  one has \(\operatorname{Ric}(0)=\Lambda g(0)\) for arbitrary twist square \(S=B^2\) after choosing
  \[
  H=(S-2\Lambda)/6,\qquad
  p_a=-(4\Lambda+7S)/24,\qquad
  p_c=(5S-4\Lambda)/24.
  \]
  A dilaton Hessian and base Ricci 2-jet can therefore hide an arbitrary pointwise twist spike at a point. [Step 29]

- Noncentral nilpotent fields cannot replace the center in the Bochner strategy. In \(H_3\), a unit noncentral left-invariant field has \(|L_Xg|^2=2b^2\), the same scale as the bracket being controlled, making the almost-Killing correction vacuous. [Step 29]

- The key unresolved positive-collapse bridge is producing central almost-Killing fields with scale-comparable length and \(\int |L_Zg|^2/\int |Z|^2=O(1)\) from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching alone. Cheeger–Fukaya–Gromov would supply this under bounded full curvature, but the CZ spike forbids assuming such curvature; Kapovitch–Wilking/Naber–Zhang provide nilpotent short-loop groups, not invariant metrics or Lie-derivative control. [Steps 28–30]

## Four-dimensional positive noncollapsed Route A: exact ends, balanced annulus, and obstruction transfer

- Step 30 reopened the dormant positive noncollapsed bubble route. If a positive near-Einstein four-dimensional sequence with volume bounded below does not bubble, it yields an Einstein metric on the same smooth topology. Hence the noncollapsed no-Einstein counterexample locus is exactly the bubbling locus; this is where Ozuch/Biquard obstruction theory is relevant. [Step 30]

- A divergence-free cosmological Einstein tensor was identified as a \(C^0\)-Ricci-safe first-order pairing:
  \[
  \mathcal E_g=\operatorname{Ric}_g-\frac12s_gg+g
  \]
  in dimension four for positive normalization. If \(A=\operatorname{Ric}_g-g\), then
  \[
  \mathcal E_g=A-\frac12(\operatorname{tr}A)g,
  \]
  so \(\mathcal E_g=O(\delta)\) pointwise and is divergence-free by contracted Bianchi. Ozuch’s identity gives
  \[
  \int_{\partial\Omega}\mathcal E_g(Z,\nu)
  =\frac12\int_\Omega\langle\mathcal E_g,L_Zg\rangle.
  \]
  TTCS confirmed the four-dimensional estimate
  \[
  \left|\int_{\partial\Omega}\mathcal E_g(Z,\nu)\right|
  \le 2\delta\,\operatorname{Vol}(\Omega)^{1/2}J(Z)^{1/2},
  \qquad J(Z)=\int |L_Zg|^2.
  \]
  This is useful for \(C^0\)-safe bulk control but is linear and not itself the Ozuch \(H_2\)-\(H^4\) Taub obstruction. [Step 30]

- TTCS corrected the radial variational-field proposal: rotations may use \(L_Zg\), but the radial/dilation channel should use the conformal-Killing operator
  \[
  K_gZ=(L_Zg)^\circ
  \]
  and energy \(\int |K_gZ|^2\), because \(r\partial_r\) is conformal Killing and raw \(\int|L_Zg|^2\) has an irrelevant flat-cone \(R^4\) volume term. The minimizer satisfies \(\delta KZ=0\); Ozuch’s ALE fields are harmonic vector fields satisfying vector Laplace equations, and the two are not automatically identical without a model/Weitzenböck analysis. [Step 30]

- Ozuch 2021 was source-read for Taub/Pohozaev preserved quantities. For an orbifold expansion \(g_o=e+H_2+O(r^3)\) and ALE expansion \(g_b=e+H^4+O(r^{-5})\), Theorem 4.6 gives vanishing boundary integrals of \(\operatorname{Ric}_e^{(2)}(H_2,H^4)\) against cone rotations and \(r\partial_r\). Corollary 4.10 specializes Eguchi–Hanson with
  \[
  H^4=-\theta_1^-\circ\omega_1^+/(2r^4)
  \]
  to the vector condition \(R_+v=0\) for the EH orientation \(v\); allowing EH orientation to vary gives \(\det R_+=0\). [Steps 30–31]

- The spectral layer computed the self-dual curvature operator
  \[
  R_+=W_++\frac13\mathrm{Id}
  \]
  for standard positive Einstein four-manifolds. Round \(S^4\) has \(\det R_+=1/27\neq0\), excluding EH bubbling by the first obstruction. \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) and \(S^2\times S^2\) have \(R_+\) eigenvalues \((1,0,0)\). Every Kähler–Einstein four-manifold has \(W_+\) eigenvalues \((2\Lambda/3,-\Lambda/3,-\Lambda/3)\), so \(\det R_+=0\) identically after positive normalization. Thus the first-obstruction condition partitions non-Kähler generic limits from the Kähler-Einstein-compatible locus. [Step 31]

- The conditional noncollapsed dichotomy from Step 31 is: assuming bubble-tree finiteness for near-Einstein sequences and transfer of the exact-Einstein Ozuch obstruction to \(C^0\)-pinched degenerations, either the original smooth \(M\) carries an Einstein metric, or every singular point of the positive Einstein orbifold limit has \(W_+\) eigenvalue \(-1/3\), equivalently \(R_+v=0\) for the relevant EH orientation and \(\det R_+=0\) after orientation variation. The open bridge is the obstruction transfer, not gluing sufficiency. [Step 31]

- Step 32 rejected the proposed Page-metric flux experiment. Page is a single rigid Einstein metric on \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\), obtained by smooth blow-up with a \((-1)\)-sphere; an EH resolution of an \(A_1=\mathbb C^2/\{\pm1\}\) point inserts a \((-2)\)-sphere and needs a degeneration parameter \(t\to0\). Any flux on an exact rigid Einstein metric would vanish as a consistency check and would not test A2. Page and Chen–LeBrun–Weber instead show that “no Kähler–Einstein metric” is not “no Riemannian Einstein metric.” [Step 32]

- Step 32 also corrected flux order accounting. The relevant Taub/Wronskian obstruction is bilinear in the linearized cone modes, not linear in \(\mathcal E_g\). With
  \[
  H_2\sim r^2,\qquad t^4H^4\sim t^4r^{-4},
  \]
  the boundary pairing
  \[
  r^3\bigl(H_2\partial(t^4H^4)-t^4H^4\partial H_2\bigr)
  \]
  has scale \(t^4\), independent of radius, because \(2+(-4)=-2\). The balanced radius is
  \[
  r=t^{2/3},
  \]
  where both pieces have size \(t^{4/3}\). A localized residual from \(C^0\) Ricci defect has scale \(O(\delta r^6)=O(\delta t^4)\), so the error/signal ratio is \(O(\delta)\) on that dyadic shell. At macroscopic \(r\sim1\), the same nonconservation is \(O(\delta)\) against signal \(t^4\), so global neck summation is invalid. [Steps 32–33]

- Step 33 reframed A2 as a single balanced-annulus comparison: at \(r\approx t^{2/3}\), after Bianchi/volume gauge, the flux-visible \(l=2\) component should be exactly the Wronskian-dual \(H_2/t^4H^4\) pair up to \(o(t^4)\) in pairing. This is narrower than proving a global weighted normal form. [Step 33]

- The flat \(A_1\)-cone sanity computation found that in Bianchi/TT gauge on \(\mathbb R^4/\{\pm1\}\), homogeneous symmetric tensor modes have roots
  \[
  \alpha=l,\qquad \alpha=-l-2,
  \]
  and antipodal parity keeps even \(l\). The \(l=0\) pair corresponds to pure gauge/removable volume-mass modes; \(l=1\) is odd and absent; \(l=2\) is the first even non-gauge regular mode, dual to \(r^{-4}\). This supports the \(H_2/H^4\) pairing but is not yet a full Lichnerowicz indicial theorem with all gauge and representation details. [Step 33]

- Step 34 converted the sanity check into a mode-diagonal statement for the flat \(A_1\) cone. The Wronskian pairs only within a single angular harmonic mode. The \(l=0\) mass/volume mode can be larger at \(r=t^{2/3}\), with size \(O(t^{2/3})\), but is invisible to the \(l=2\) Wronskian by angular orthogonality. The \(l=2\) pair \((2,-4)\) carries the \(t^4\) signal and is Ozuch’s first obstruction \(R_+v=0\); higher \(l\) and cross-mode pairs are zero or subleading. [Step 34]

- Step 34 initially found a logarithmic resonance in the radial equation
  \[
  f''+\frac3r f'-\frac8{r^2}f=S.
  \]
  A constant source \(S=\delta\) produces \(\delta r^2\log r/6\), causing a relative \(O(\delta\log(1/t))\) error if one transports the growing \(H_2\) coefficient inward through the whole neck. Step 35 corrected this as an artifact of reading the wrong coefficient through the long neck. In the rescaled bubble frame \(\hat g=t^{-2}g\), the Ricci defect and the ambient curvature 2-jet signal both scale as \(t^2\); over a fixed annulus \(\rho\in[1,R]\), the relative error is
  \[
  O(\delta\log R)+O(1/R).
  \]
  The correct limiting procedure is fixed \(R\), let \(\delta_i\to0\), then \(R\to\infty\). No hypothesis \(\delta\log(1/t)\to0\) should be part of the candidate theorem. [Steps 34–36]

- The real noncollapsed A2 input after Step 35 is ansatz-independent second-order bubble-frame convergence: after rescaling around an EH bubble, produce
  \[
  k=\lim \frac{\hat g_i-g_{\mathrm{EH}}}{t_i^2}
  \]
  with quadratic growth, satisfying
  \[
  D\operatorname{Ric}_{\mathrm{EH}}(k)=\Lambda g_{\mathrm{EH}}+O(\delta_i)
  \]
  on fixed bubble-frame annuli, and match the quadratic asymptotic part of \(k\) to the orbifold \(R_+\) 2-jet. Cheeger–Naber \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) convergence and harmonic-radius control make this meaningful but do not by themselves transmit a second jet for non-Einstein prelimit metrics. [Step 35]

- The harmonic-radius/small-energy input was clarified. Existing exact-Einstein sources use Gao/Anderson-style \(\varepsilon\)-regularity: noncollapse plus small local \(L^2\) curvature gives curvature and harmonic-radius control in the Einstein setting. Cheeger–Naber supplies bounded-Ricci, noncollapsed harmonic-radius weak type estimates and cone-annulus \(C^1\) control under almost constant volume ratio. For merely \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched metrics, a safe theorem is not yet available in this record: one must combine noncollapse, volume-cone/annulus control, and no intermediate curvature-energy drops. [Steps 33, 35]

## LeBrun–Ozuch classification bypass and higher obstructions

- Step 33 source-checked LeBrun–Ozuch 2026. Its Theorem B assumes an exact sequence of smooth compact oriented positive Einstein four-manifolds, a Hermitian/conformally Kähler positive Einstein orbifold limit with a genuine singularity, and admissibility, meaning all ALE bubbles are anti-self-dual in the induced orientation. It does not derive Hermitian or Kähler structure from \(\det R_+=0\). Under its hypotheses, Theorem 4.1 forces the smooth topology to be Del Pezzo type, with \(\pi_1=0\), \(b_+=1\), \(b_-\le8\): \(S^2\times S^2\) or \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\), \(0\le\ell\le8\). [Step 33]

- Conditional on the missing Hermitian/admissible input, the principal spin stress family \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\), \(k\ge2\), cannot occur in that classified noncollapsed branch because it has even form \(kH\) and \(b_+=k\ge2\), while the only even/spin Del Pezzo member is \(S^2\times S^2\) itself. This is a topological filter, not a volume gap and not a conclusion from \(\det R_+=0\) alone. [Step 33]

- Odaka–Spotti–Sun arXiv:1210.0858 was confirmed as the Kähler–Einstein del Pezzo compactification/classification source direction, but full source access remained limited through runtime; its results should not be used beyond the source-grounded statements already checked or separately read. [Steps 32–33]

- Chen–LeBrun–Weber and LeBrun Hermitian sources support the existence/status of positive Einstein metrics on \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#2\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\) and Page on \(\mathbb{CP}^2\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\). These examples reinforce that KE nonexistence on a given complex structure does not provide a Riemannian Einstein nonexistence result. [Steps 32–33]

A 14-dimensional chessboard \((8+8)\) family of EH configurations satisfies all 84 identified stable Ricci-flat constraints. Thus known higher obstructions do not exclude all bubble configurations. This evidence is \(\Lambda=0\)/K3/Ricci-flat-compatible and should not be imported into the positive \(\Lambda>0\) branch without sign-specific evidence. [Steps 31–33]

## Characteristic classes and normalization checks

- For a Ricci-flat ALE four-manifold with asymptotic group \(\Gamma\),
  \[
  \frac1{8\pi^2}\int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2
  =\chi(X)-\frac1{|\Gamma|}.
  \]
  Eguchi–Hanson therefore carries \(12\pi^2\) in the session’s convention, not \(8\pi^2\). This quantum applies to isolated ALE bubbles, not codimension-two rods or ALF/ALG/ALH collapse. [Steps 6, 9–10]

- For \(M=X\#k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\), with
  \[
  A=2\chi(X)+3\tau(X),
  \]
  one has
  \[
  \int p_1(TM)=3\tau(M)=A-2\chi(X)-3k,
  \]
  while
  \[
  2\chi(M)+3\tau(M)=A-k.
  \]
  Negative-branch arguments must distinguish the tangent-bundle Pontryagin number from the calibrated \(\Lambda^2_+\) Chern–Weil quantity. [Steps 12–13]

- Standard Taub–NUT–AdS did not furnish a finite calibrated-defect residue model. Core-containing balls have problematic mean energy; smaller covers unwrap toward hyperbolic geometry with macroscopic calibrated defect. No theorem of “one NUT, one fixed obstruction cost” was established. [Steps 12–16]

- The toric rod-count convention was made explicit in Step 36: for smooth toric 4-manifold polygons in the alternating family, number of rods/corners equals \(\chi=b_2+2\). Earlier “no slack” arguments are sensitive to whether rods or \(b_2\) are being counted; this must remain explicit in any energy-budget proof. [Steps 35–36]

# Session Knowledge Used or Established

- Constant metric rescaling leaves the Ricci \((0,2)\)-tensor unchanged while changing its endomorphism relative to the metric. Bubble rescaling suppresses the Ricci endomorphism quadratically in length scale. These facts underlie branch normalization, zero-straddling exclusion, and Ricci-flat blow-up limits. [Steps 1, 3, 9]

- Weighted smallness, \(L^p\) smallness, GH closeness, and unweighted operator Ricci pinching are distinct. Raising an index with a small glued metric can convert tensor-small residuals into order-one endomorphism defects. [Steps 1, 32]

- \(C^0\) Ricci pinching alone cannot provide pointwise curvature control, even with defect tending to zero and small added \(L^2\) Hessian energy. Approximate-to-exact arguments must use weak/test-field projections, finite-\(p\) harmonic-coordinate control, extra PDE structure, symmetry identities, or scale-adapted cover methods rather than universal pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-regularity. [Steps 8, 10–11, 22, 33–35]

- In dimension four, tight pinching gives comparison bounds, positive Euler characteristic, strict Hitchin–Thorpe, and global curvature-energy budgets. Under noncollapse and no singular set it gives Einstein existence on the same topology; with bubbling, the problem reduces to ALE/annular obstruction transfer. Over families with unbounded Euler characteristic, defect-to-zero sequences must collapse while carrying unbounded Weyl energy. [Steps 8–9, 18, 30–36]

- Exact Einstein collapse means positive-branch noncollapse cannot be the theorem. The relevant question is whether every sufficiently tightly pinched collapsing topology is Einstein-compatible. Known examples—lens/Hopf quotients, products, and KK circle families—are compatible. The formal toric \(\alpha\)-family remains a collapsed stress model but not a global metric or counterexample. [Steps 6–7, 19–26, 34–36]
