  under \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\). This is first-obstruction degeneracy, not a Kähler–Einstein characterization. The obstruction-amplitude argument remains conditional on deriving an appropriate gluing or annular normal form [Steps 7–8].

- A weak projection/flux identity was selected as the desired bridge from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching to gluing obstructions:
  \[
  \int\langle\operatorname{Ric}(g_i)-g_i,\Phi_i\rangle
  =t_i\mathcal O+o(t_i),
  \qquad \|\Phi_i\|_{L^1}=O(t_i).

  The reason was to avoid differentiating the Ricci defect. Ordinary ADM-type tests do not detect the Eguchi–Hanson \(\rho^{-4}\) term, so a quadratic cone field or boundary-flux formulation is needed. This bridge was not proved [Steps 8–9].

Positive-Ricci constructions do not imply \(\delta_+\to0\), and \(k=1\) is already Einstein. Cheeger–Naber finiteness implies that a hypothetical infinite family with \(\delta_+\to0\) must collapse in total volume, while Chern–Gauss–Bonnet forces Weyl energy to grow linearly with \(k\) [Steps 7–9].

- After the nine-step opening, the work moved to Execute, but not initially on the one-neck projection bridge alone. A conditional finite-cover amplifier became the organizing four-dimensional reduction: if every simply connected closed four-manifold with fixed positive pinching has a topology-independent volume lower bound \(v_0\), then the universal cover has volume at least \(v_0\); Cheeger–Naber finite-type control bounds \(\chi(\widetilde M)\); Euler multiplicativity bounds \(|\pi_1(M)|\); and hence all closed manifolds in the class have a volume lower bound. The corrected argument uses the universal cover directly, including for nonorientable \(M\), and applies Cheeger–Naber directly to \(M\) after obtaining the gap. It does not assert a classification of quotient actions and does not produce Einstein metrics [Step 10].

- The all-dimensional positive-collapse split was sharpened using universal covers: along a collapsed sequence, either \(\operatorname{Vol}(\widetilde M_i)\) remains bounded below and \(|\pi_1(M_i)|\to\infty\), or the universal covers themselves collapse. Exact Einstein lens spaces and products such as \((S^3/\mathbb Z_q)\times S^{n-3}\) realize the first alternative in dimensions \(3\) and \(n\ge5\). Therefore a general theorem cannot be “collapse is impossible”; dimension four is special only after reduction to simply connected covers [Step 10].

- The regularity bottleneck was relocated from a single neck obstruction to average-to-pointwise curvature control. Source auditing distinguished Cheeger–Tian’s Einstein \(\varepsilon\)-regularity from the weaker bounded-Ricci conclusions of Cheeger–Tian/Li, Li smoothing, and Naber–Zhang accessible-cover harmonic-radius theory. Under \(\operatorname{Ric}=g+E\) with only \(\|E\|_{L^\infty}\ll1\), harmonic coordinates yield finite \(W^{2,p}\)/\(C^{1,\alpha}\) control but not pointwise curvature bounds; derivatives of the Schouten tensor obstruct the usual curvature Moser iteration [Step 10].

- The proposed high-frequency TT/WKB counterexample mechanism was rejected at symbol level. Ricci and Weyl have the same principal second-derivative scaling on a fixed noncollapsed Einstein background, and the Ricci-symbol kernel is gauge. A genuine Ricci-small/Weyl-large mechanism would need nonlinear cancellation, collapse, or endpoint Calderón–Zygmund behavior [Step 10].

- The Calderón–Zygmund probe was then promoted to the first Execute target. It succeeded in producing an explicit counterexample to pointwise \(C^0\)-Ricci \(\varepsilon\)-regularity on the closed Einstein manifold \(S^2\times S^2\). Opposite warping cancels the full Hessian from the Ricci base block, leaves only \(\Delta u\) in fiber Ricci, and retains the trace-free Hessian in Riemann curvature. Appropriate mollified logarithmic spikes give \(\|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\), small \(L^2\) Hessian energy, and unbounded pointwise curvature [Step 11].

- This CZ construction changed the regularity architecture. Pointwise Cheeger–Tian-type regularity under \(C^0\) Ricci pinching is false; direct reliance on bounded-curvature Cheeger–Fukaya–Gromov collapse is therefore unavailable. Harmonic radius, \(C^{1,\alpha}/W^{2,p}\), finite-\(p\) Calderón–Zygmund control, BMO control, Li smoothing, and weak test-field pairings remain possible. The spike is not a Yau–26 counterexample: it is constructed on an Einstein topology and preserves the determinant/fiber-area density, so it concentrates curvature without causing volume collapse [Steps 11, 14].

  \[
  g=g_B+h_{IJ}(d\phi^I+A^I)(d\phi^J+A^J),\qquad
  w=\sqrt{\det h},
  \]
  symbolic calculations established
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^V
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}+\frac12|F|_h^2,

  and the mixed equations gave the twist conservation law
  \[
  d(w h_{IJ}*_BF^J)=0.
  \]
  This redirected the collapse problem toward orbit-space determinant and rod geometry [Step 12].

  \[
  \left(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|_h^2\right)w=2\lambda w.
  \]
  With a degeneration boundary, \(w\) is a positive Dirichlet ground state. Twist is a nonnegative potential and therefore does not defeat scale pinning. For positive \(C^0\) pinching, Rayleigh testing with \(w\) gives

  \lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)\le2(1+\delta)

  without approximate orthogonal transitivity or derivatives of the Ricci defect. This was recognized as a symmetry-generated realization of the weak projection-bridge idea [Step 13].

This source applies to the exact Einstein setting, not to arbitrary pinched metrics [Step 13].

For normalized round \(S^4\), the orbit space is a quarter of \(S^2(\sqrt3)\), \(w\) satisfies \(\Delta w=-2w\), \(\int_\Omega w=6\), and \(\operatorname{Vol}=24\pi^2\) [Steps 13–14].

The classical \(\pi j_{0,1}^2\) constant applies to flat planar domains; the orbit-space metric can have highly negative curvature, as the CZ and edge-spike work permit. Thus the spectral bound alone does not give an unconditional lower bound for \(\operatorname{Area}(\Omega,g_B)\) [Steps 14, 17–18].

- The reduced diagonal formulas were corrected rather than discarded. With \(w=pq\) and \(v=\log(p/q)\),
  \[
  K_B=\frac14\left(|\nabla v|^2-|\nabla\log w|^2\right)
      =-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle,
  \]
  not the earlier false \(K_B\ge3\) formula. The corrected edge equation is
  \[
  Q''+(1-2K_B|_{\rm edge})Q=0.
  \]
  These corrections preserve the determinant and rod program but remove the optimistic curvature-sign shortcut [Step 14].

A bound \(v_0(\chi)\to0\) yields a circular Cheeger–Naber estimate and cannot control \(\chi(\widetilde M)\). This merged the toric polygon problem with the large-\(k\) \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) tail [Step 14].

- The Chern–Gauss–Bonnet energy budget was explicitly demoted as a possible contradiction to boundary collapse. Shrinking fixed spheres can carry fixed bubble-scale \(L^2\) energy independent of their area, and \(O(\chi)\) such bubbles are compatible with the topological energy budget. The relevant leverage must come from smooth rod/holonomy matching or the full Ricci equations, not from merely bounding total \(L^2\) curvature [Steps 14–15].

- An exact high-corner Einstein FEM search was rejected as the wrong experiment. The pinching problem allows inequalities and need not solve the full exact reduced Einstein system; exact nonexistence at \(m=8,10\) would not decide whether \(\delta\)-pinched metrics exist. Source checks also corrected an overstatement: available toric and Hermitian results do not classify all \(T^2\)-invariant positive Einstein four-manifolds [Step 15].

- Coarse two-dimensional spectral, signed Gauss–Bonnet, and unit-closure constraints were found insufficient. A formal edge model with \(K_B=-A\) has flux \(2/(1+2A)\); choosing \(A=m^2\) gives total flux \(O(1/m)\). Conformal-base computations showed that highly negative curvature can localize at geodesic edges while \(\lambda_1\le2\). These are relaxed two-dimensional models, not four-dimensional Ricci-pinched metrics, but they decisively reject the idea that the spectral bound alone yields a \(\chi\)-uniform gap [Step 15].

- Flexible local edge analysis also rejected a purely local obstruction. After repairing an overconstrained series ansatz, the exact local Einstein equations admit arbitrary negative edge-curvature parameter \(A\). The separated germ satisfies
  \[
  a'=Ap,\qquad
  2aa''+(a')^2=\kappa-a^2,
  \]
  and closes at a second bolt with slope
  \[
  \mu=\frac{2a_++1}{a_+(a_++2)}<1
  \quad(A>0).
  \]
  Thus the obstruction, if present, lies in global smooth closure rather than the local rod equations [Step 15].

- This separated germ was identified and verified as Euclidean Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Birmingham–Kottler. The second-bolt defect is a codimension-two edge cone along an embedded \(S^2\), not an isolated \(\mathbb R^4/\Gamma\) singularity. Therefore Biquard–Ozuch/Eguchi–Hanson first-obstruction theory is not the appropriate tool for this rod; Atiyah–LeBrun edge-cone characteristic formulas and cone-angle/holonomy matching are the relevant language. The ALE obstruction route remains valid for isolated noncollapsed orbifold bubbles elsewhere [Step 16].

- A normalization subtlety was recorded. If the period smooths the small black-hole bolt, the cosmological bolt has cone angle \(2\pi\mu\) and the volume tends to zero as \(A\to\infty\). If the period smooths the cosmological bolt, the volume tends to the round \(S^4\) value \(24\pi^2\), but the small bolt has cone angle \(2\pi/\mu\). The Nariai limit \(A\to0\) gives \(S^2\times S^2\) with volume \(16\pi^2\). The collapsed first-bolt normalization therefore does not simply converge smoothly to round \(S^4\) [Step 16].

- The exact separated Einstein closure theorem was completed: in the cohomogeneity-one \(S^1\times SO(3)\)-symmetric class with two smooth \(S^2\) bolts, smoothness requires \(\mu=1\), which forces \(A=0\); the metric is the Nariai product \(S^2(1)\times S^2(1)\). The matching is nondegenerate, with \(d\mu/dA|_{A=0}=-4/3\) [Step 17].

- A proposed pinched separated stability theorem was not accepted as proved. Although Step 17 recorded a conditional ODE-stability version, the user immediately emphasized that a \(C^0\)-Ricci-pinched separated metric need not remain globally close to one exact Schwarzschild–de Sitter solution; the equations degenerate at bolts and interval length is not controlled. A collapsing smooth pinched separated family remains a live BREAK possibility until a genuine differential-inequality argument rules it out [Steps 17–18].

- The diagonal twist-free determinant identity was extended to \(T^k\)-invariant metrics:
  \[
  g=g_B+\sum_{I=1}^k p_I^2\,d\theta_I^2,\qquad
  w=\prod_{I=1}^kp_I,
  \qquad
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^V=-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}.
  \]
  Under normalized positive pinching and a degeneration boundary, Barta/Rayleigh arguments give
  \[
  k(1-\delta)\le\lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)
  \le k(1+\delta).
  \]
  This is the only current A02 mechanism with an all-dimensional form, but it requires a large torus action and does not address arbitrary metrics [Step 17].

- The Step 17 route assessment initially declared a “Bridge 3” obstruction using Hitchin–Thorpe examples such as \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\). This was corrected in Step 18. Tight normalized pinching itself implies strict Hitchin–Thorpe:
  \[
  2\chi\pm3\tau>0
  \quad\text{when}\quad
  \delta<\frac1{1+\sqrt3},
  \]
  in either sign. Hence Hitchin–Thorpe violators and equality cases—including \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\) and \(\#_4\mathbb{CP}^2\)—cannot enter an arbitrarily tightly pinched family. Hitchin–Thorpe is a consequence of the hypothesis, not an external obstruction to converting finiteness into Einstein existence [Step 18].

- The positive-branch obstruction census was correspondingly revised. Positive pinching gives positive scalar curvature, so the Seiberg–Witten/monopole mechanisms used in the negative LeBrun setting are unavailable for such an input. The current recorded assessment is that known four-dimensional Einstein nonexistence mechanisms are automatically avoided by sufficiently tight positive pinching. Thus the positive branch is presently a BUILD/pinching-rigidity program; refutation would require a new Einstein-nonexistence mechanism. The relevant stress topologies include \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) for \(k\ge2\) and \(\#_3\mathbb{CP}^2\), not Hitchin–Thorpe violators [Step 18].

- The Step 17 demotion of the toric work to a mere “laboratory” was also corrected. A general-to-invariant reduction is necessary to prove a theorem for every simply connected pinched collapse, but it is unnecessary for directly constructing or obstructing pinched metrics on the actual toric stress family \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\). The current A02 primary target is therefore a direct toric BUILD/BREAK test on the \((2k+2)\)-rod models of this family [Step 18].

- Periodic primitive labels
  \[
  (1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),\ldots
  \]
  were adopted as the concrete even-polygon models. Computational intersection-form checks for \(m=4,\dots,14\) produced even unimodular signature-zero forms and explicit splittings into \(kH\), consistent with \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\). A full Orlik–Raymond source or elementary diffeomorphism argument remains required before using this as a theorem rather than a topology certificate [Step 18].

- The immediate Execute fork is now explicit. On these toric models, either construct smooth \(T^2\)-invariant metrics with defect \(\delta_m\to0\) and collapsing flux/volume, which would break the simply connected volume-gap route but would not itself refute Yau–26 because Einstein nonexistence is unknown; or show that rod, corner, horizontal Ricci, twist, or holonomy matching enforces a uniform defect/volume gap. Diagonal failure must be distinguished from a genuine invariant obstruction because non-diagonal fiber metrics or twist may add flexibility [Step 18].

- The orbifold/ALE bubble-tree route remains assigned to the noncollapsed approximate-to-exact problem from Steps 8–9, but it was not chosen as the immediate A02 primary investment. Before Lichnerowicz-spectrum correction can be decisive, one needs a weighted annular normal form under only \(C^0\) Ricci pinching; Step 11 rules out obtaining that from generic pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-regularity [Steps 17–18].

- Parallel A01/A03 negative-branch smoothing claims were explicitly not accepted as complete. Their localized Li/Ricci-flow bootstrap has a transition-region/domain mismatch, Ricci flow has no finite propagation speed, and comparable-ball smallness does not automatically control all cutoff regions. The remaining load-bearing gap is a degenerate weighted \(\varepsilon\)-regularity estimate converting coupled \(L^2\) control into a bound such as \(\|\chi^2\operatorname{Rm}\|\le C/t\). Critical Sobolev cancellation, conditional topological recalibration, cover-mean transport, and bounded-curvature averaging remain useful, but neither peer branch is closed [Steps 16–18].

- Higher dimensions remain essentially open. Exact Einstein quotient collapse shows that noncollapse cannot be the goal. The \(T^k\) determinant identity offers a symmetry-restricted all-dimensional scale constraint, and products with Einstein spheres can transport positive-pinched inputs from dimension four to dimensions \(n\ge6\), but neither operation preserves a useful no-Einstein conclusion without additional theorems. Dimension five and general nonsymmetric \(n\ge5\) metrics have no current mechanism comparable to the four-dimensional Euler/Weyl theory [Steps 10, 17–18].

### Research Line

- The research began by fixing the exact logical burden of Yau–26 and testing whether known almost-Einstein and obstruction results already settled a normalized branch. Min-Oo identified how a negative sequence could escape restricted stability; ALE gluing identified the distinction between weighted residual control and the required pointwise Ricci-operator control. These results changed the opening question from “is an existing stability theorem enough?” to “what degeneration lets a tightly Ricci-isotropic metric evade Einstein existence?” [Step 1].

- Four-dimensional gauge theory was the first sustained attempt to answer that question. The Step 2 arithmetic error and the user’s correction forced a reconstruction of the LeBrun inequalities. The failed broad obstruction claim yielded a more reusable conclusion: a strict metric-independent integral obstruction is stable under small trace-free Ricci error and therefore tends to exclude the pinched input metric itself. Because the surviving near-equality regime addressed only the negative sign, A02 moved away from treating it as the central route [Steps 2–4].

- Chern–Gauss–Bonnet then unified the positive-collapse and negative-bubbling discussions. Tight pinching gives a sign-blind Euler/Weyl budget and excludes bounded-curvature total collapse, but not local thin regions, Weyl concentration, or negative-branch diameter escape. Later bubble analysis clarified that the budget can be saturated by one fixed quantum per shrinking topological feature, so it is an accounting identity rather than a uniform-collapse obstruction [Steps 4, 8, 14–15].

- The positive branch gained comparative priority because Myers and Bishop give dimension-only diameter and volume ceilings, whereas the negative branch retains uncontrolled diameter. Initial hopes for noncollapsed smooth convergence were repaired using Cheeger–Naber: regular Einstein convergence occurs away from a codimension-four singular set, but singular removal and same-topology Einstein existence remain open. In four dimensions, an infinite tightly pinched topological family must collapse in total volume, making collapse—not ordinary compactness—the decisive remaining positive-branch regime [Steps 5, 9].

- Collapse models then corrected the program’s taste. Berger anisotropy showed that a fixed-connection shrinking ansatz is not the right universal model, while lens spaces showed that exact Einstein collapse exists. The four-dimensional Euler argument removed globally free circle collapse but left fixed strata and curvature concentration. This made singular orbit geometry, rather than generic noncollapse, the natural positive-branch focus [Steps 5–7].

- The first-obstruction and Cheeger–Naber lines were combined into the proposed weak projection bridge. The intended principle was to extract gluing obstructions by pairing the \(C^0\) Ricci defect against smooth approximate cokernel data rather than differentiating it. This remained conditional because arbitrary pinched sequences were not known to enter weighted ALE normal form [Steps 7–9].

- Step 10 converted the noncollapsed theorem into the conditional finite-cover amplifier and audited the regularity literature. The audit showed that the desired collapse theorem could not simply quote no-volume Einstein \(\varepsilon\)-regularity: the Einstein equation supplies the differential curvature inequality, whereas \(C^0\) Ricci pinching supplies only bounded inhomogeneity. This made the average-to-pointwise question the next decisive test [Step 10].

- Step 11 settled that test negatively. The opposite-warping CZ spike demonstrated that arbitrarily small \(C^0\) Ricci defect and small \(L^2\) Hessian energy can coexist with arbitrarily large pointwise curvature. This invalidated a generic “small energy implies curvature supremum” bridge and any collapse plan that required Ricci-only pointwise regularity. It simultaneously preserved weaker \(L^p\), BMO, harmonic-radius, smoothing, and test-field routes [Step 11].

- The same construction revealed why toric determinant variables are natural. Opposite warping changes the ratio of circle lengths while leaving their product \(w\) fixed. This explains both the Ricci/Weyl decoupling and why the CZ family cannot collapse volume. The research therefore shifted from generic regularity to the orbit-area determinant and rod closure needed to make both circle lengths small [Steps 11–12, 14].

- The toric determinant calculation produced the cleanest derivative-free bridge so far. The vertical Ricci trace directly controls a Schrödinger equation for \(w\), and the Killing fields provide the smooth test data. Exact twist contributes a nonnegative potential rather than destroying scale pinning. Exact source results supplied orthogonal transitivity when needed for Einstein metrics, but the pinched spectral inequality itself did not require proving approximate transitivity [Steps 12–13].

- The first optimistic toric picture combined spectral pinning, flat-domain Faber–Krahn, corner closure, and a uniform-edge-curvature model. In that idealized setting the shrinking flux per rod is compensated by the number of rods. Subsequent corrections removed each unjustified shortcut: \(K_B\) has no fixed positive sign; signed Gauss–Bonnet allows negative edge curvature to localize; the Euclidean Faber–Krahn area constant does not apply to arbitrary curved orbit spaces; and the energy budget permits \(O(\chi)\) boundary bubbles [Steps 14–17].

- Step 15 sharpened the enemy rather than ending the route. Relaxed two-dimensional models can collapse their total rod flux, and local exact Einstein edge germs allow arbitrarily negative edge curvature. The missing condition is global smooth closure. Recognition of the germ as Schwarzschild–de Sitter made this precise: one exact separated small bolt creates a scale-invariant cone-angle mismatch at the other horizon. Edge-cone, rod-holonomy, and multi-bolt matching—not isolated ALE obstruction—are the correct local language [Steps 15–16].

- The separated exact theorem then closed one narrow subproblem: exact smooth two-bolt closure forces Nariai \(S^2\times S^2\). It did not settle pinched closure because the bolt equations are singular and \(C^0\) Ricci inequalities do not place the metric in a soft tube around an exact SdS solution. The research therefore stopped short of converting exact rigidity into an unsupported pinched theorem [Steps 16–18].

- Step 17 briefly prompted a global pivot toward orbifold/ALE Lichnerowicz computations and characterized the invariant work as blocked by general-to-invariant and finiteness-to-existence bridges. Step 18 repaired both judgments. Hitchin–Thorpe violators are already excluded by tight pinching, so they do not obstruct the positive program. More importantly, direct construction or obstruction on the toric \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) stress family requires no reduction from arbitrary metrics. The invariant work is therefore load-bearing for deciding whether the conditional simply connected volume-gap strategy is plausible, even though it cannot by itself prove the general theorem [Steps 17–18].

- The current positive four-dimensional research line is consequently a direct BUILD/BREAK experiment on smooth toric \((2k+2)\)-rod models. The diagonal residual system is
  \[
  r_p+r_q=-\frac{\Delta w}{w},\qquad
  r_p-r_q=-\frac1w\operatorname{div}(w\nabla v),
  \]
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}^H
  =K_Bg_B-\left[
    \nabla^2\log w+
    \frac12\left(d\log w\otimes d\log w+dv\otimes dv\right)
  \right].
  \]
  The candidate BREAK seed uses edge curvature \(K_B\sim-m^2\) and rod flux \(2/(1+2m^2)\), but it must be completed into a smooth global four-metric whose full vertical and horizontal Ricci eigenvalues all lie in \(1\pm\delta_m\). A persistent horizontal, corner, primitive-label, cone-angle, or twist obstruction would instead identify the theorem needed for a \(\chi\)-uniform invariant gap [Steps 15, 18].

- This direct toric fork has limited but clear relation to the original goal. A successful collapsing construction would invalidate the simply connected volume-gap amplifier as currently formulated, but would not refute Yau–26 because \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) may still admit Einstein metrics and no current obstruction decides that. A uniform toric gap would strengthen the BUILD case and justify investing in the still-open general-to-invariant collapse bridge. Neither outcome settles noncollapsed orbifold desingularization, the negative branch, dimensions \(n\ge5\), or final formalization [Step 18].

- The noncollapsed and negative lines remain available rather than erased. The weak ALE projection bridge is still the intended mechanism for isolated orbifold degeneration once an annular normal form is obtained. A01/A03’s smoothing and accessible-cover work remains a possible common infrastructure, but the cutoff transition estimate is unresolved. The negative LeBrun zero-margin problem, diffuse \(\Lambda^2_+\) curvature/characteristic-class transport, and calibrated defect propagation remain dormant or parallel possibilities rather than completed arguments [Steps 8–18].

- The active handoff after Step 18 is to implement the toric crux probe on \(m=6\), then \(m=8,10\), with boundary errors controlled and full Ricci endomorphism defect measured. The computation must report flux/volume and the dominant residual component, and must treat failure of the diagonal twist-free ansatz cautiously. If diagonal flexibility is insufficient, the recorded next extension is the full invariant matrix-fiber system
  \[
  g=g_B+h_{IJ}(d\phi^I+A^I)(d\phi^J+A^J),
  \]
  using the determinant and mixed-Ricci formulas already established [Step 18].

## Min-Oo 负分支稳定性：反例必须发生尺度逃逸 [Steps 1-2]

研究逐段核对 Min-Oo 论文 OCR 和正文记号，纠正了把额外条件误解为局部 \(r^{-2}\) 曲率控制的倾向。论文中的 \(d\) 是直径；先归一化 \(\max|K|=1\)，再要求 \(d<\Lambda\)，故真正的尺度不变量条件是
\[
d(g)^2\max|K_g|<\Lambda^2.
\]
在 \(n>3\)、负标量归一化、小 Ricci 各向异性且满足该尺度控制时，Min-Oo 得到 Einstein 存在，阈值依赖 \(n,\Lambda\) [Step 1]。

由此得到持续可用的“Min-Oo 逃逸”结论：若存在底层流形均无 Einstein 度量而
\(\delta_-(g_j)\to0\) 的序列，则必有
\[
d(g_j)^2\max|K_{g_j}|\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
否则可取统一 \(\Lambda\)，最终落入 Min-Oo 定理 [Steps 1-2]。这没有消除负分支，但把反例机制收窄为直径逃逸、Weyl/全曲率集中、塌缩或线性化近核退化。

## Orbifold 解消：加权近 Einstein 与题目所需 \(C^0\) pinching 的分离 [Steps 1-3]

会话组最早提出使用 Morteza–Viaclovsky、Ozuch 型 orbifold 解消，在无 Einstein 流形上制造近 Einstein 度量。研究直接读取 MV Calabi 胶合区 Lemma 4.1–4.2、Ozuch 文献，并运行 `workspace/scripts/orbifold_scaling_exponents.py`，将加权估计换算为题目要求的无权 Ricci 端omorphism 范数 [Step 1]。在 Calabi 核和过渡区，
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_t}-\Lambda g_t-t\lambda\chi_t o
=O_{g_{\rm cal}}(t^2\rho^2),\qquad g_t\sim t\,g_{\rm cal}.
\]
经 \(g_t^{-1}\) 提升指标后，普通余项在核心区为 \(O(t)\)，在 \(\rho\sim t^{-1/4}\) 的过渡区至多为 \(O(t^{1/2})\)；但第一障碍项 \(t\lambda o\) 变成阶一的非标量端omorphism [Steps 1-2]。TTCS 又通过 Calabi 核上障碍张量的特征值差确认，即使优化标量 Einstein 常数，仍留下正的非标量谱间隙 [Step 1]。

因此，已知第一障碍非零的 MV 非存在例以及 Ozuch 的 \(L^p\)/GH 近 Einstein 例不能直接给出 \(\delta_\sigma\to0\)。多个奇点的障碍在积分意义相消也不够，因为题目误差是逐核心、逐点上确界；每个局部第一障碍必须消失，或在变动族中至少满足相对幅度 \(|\lambda_j|/|\Lambda_j|\to0\)，之后还需由高阶或全局障碍阻止底层流形承载任何 Einstein 度量 [Steps 1-3]。这条否定结果没有终止解消路线，而是把目标收窄为：寻找第一局部障碍消失但高阶/全局障碍仍非零的解消，或从 \(C^0\) pinching 直接抽取障碍投影。Steps 7-9 的投影桥和 Steps 17-18 的 bubble-tree 正规形讨论均由此发展。

\left(2|W^\pm|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|E|^2}{2}\right)
\]
得到两式严格为正 [Step 18]。因此 \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\) 这类违反 HT 的流形以及 \(\#_4\mathbb{CP}^2\) 这类等号流形根本不可能进入任意紧 pinching 序列，不能作为正分支敌人。正 pinching 还给正标量曲率，通常的 SW/monopole 非存在机制也不能直接用于候选反例。由此，四维正分支的“有限型到 Einstein”问题被重新理解为 pinching-rigidity：紧 pinching 是否自动把拓扑压入已知或预期正 Einstein 区域，而不是让已知 HT/LeBrun 障碍流形进入有限列表 [Step 18]。

CGB 记账也纠正了对塌缩的理解。若另有统一 \(|\mathrm{Rm}|\le K\)，则 Weyl 上界与正的 \(\beta V\) 给出总体积下界；所以紧 Ricci pinching 下不可能发生“全曲率有界且总体积趋零”的四维塌缩 [Step 4]。这不排除固定总体积下的局部注入半径退化、细颈、曲率集中 cap、orbifold/ALE 泡，也不处理负分支直径逃逸。用户提出有边界 CGB/Chern transgression 的厚–薄局部化，但仅 \(C^0\) Ricci 控制下边界项能否统一估计仍未解决 [Step 5]。

## 正分支紧致性计划的纠偏：非塌缩不等于全局光滑 [Steps 4-9]

任意维数中，正 pinching 给
\(\operatorname{Ric}\ge(1-\delta)g\)，从而 Myers 直径上界、Bishop 体积上界、Bochner 的 \(b_1=0\) 和有限基本群 [Steps 4-5]。但透镜空间说明 \(|\pi_1|\) 没有仅依维数的一致上界；\(b_1=0\) 也不能排除扭结环导致的塌缩 [Steps 3,5]。

Step 5 最初试图证明两侧 Ricci 界、直径界、总体积非塌缩加 \(\delta_i\to0\) 自动给统一 harmonic radius、光滑 Einstein 极限和同一微分拓扑。两个 TTCS 分支均指出该结论在 \(n\ge4\) 错误：即使精确 Einstein 序列也可发生 Weyl 集中、orbifold 极限和 ALE 泡，非塌缩并不提供全局 harmonic-radius 下界 [Step 5]。原定理被添加 erratum；直接可靠版本需额外 \(|\mathrm{Rm}|\le K\)。修正见 `workspace/notes/step5_erratum_theorem2_correction.md` 和 `workspace/plans/step5_corrected_positive_branch_plan.md`。

随后重新读取 Cheeger–Naber、Naber–Zhang 和 Ozuch，得到介于“自动光滑”和“毫无结构”之间的正确图景。有界 Ricci 加局部非塌缩给 codimension-4 奇异集、四维 \(L^2\) 曲率及 harmonic-radius 分布控制；塌缩情形在最大纤维化幂零秩等条件下，可在局部覆盖上获得 harmonic/conjugate radius 与拓扑控制 [Step 6]。但仅有
\[
\operatorname{Ric}=g+E,\qquad \|E\|_{C^0}\le\delta
\]
不是控制 Weyl 导数的闭合椭圆系统；点态曲率通常还需 Einstein 方程或 \(\nabla\operatorname{Ric}\) 控制 [Steps 5-6]。这推动研究改用积分配对，把导数移到光滑测试张量上，而不假设不存在的 \(\nabla E\) 界 [Steps 8-10]。

Step 9 从 Cheeger–Naber 得到本会话首个直接的四维拓扑有限性结果：若
\[
\|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<1/2,
\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(M)\ge v>0,
\]
则 Myers 给统一直径，Bishop–Gromov 从总体积和直径给每点单位球非塌缩，Cheeger–Naber Theorem 1.12 推出仅出现有限多个微分同胚型，常数依赖 \((\delta,v)\) [Step 9]。全维非塌缩序列则可在 codimension-4 奇异集外收敛到 Einstein regular part；四维奇异点为孤立 orbifold 点，而 \(n\ge5\) 的横截面自身可能有奇异集，不能照搬四维 ALE 图景 [Step 9]。

## 塌缩模型的连续修正：Berger、透镜空间、Kaluza–Klein 与自由作用 [Steps 2-7]

Berger sphere 计算显示固定 Hopf 连接而缩短纤维会使竖直 Ricci 趋零、水平 Ricci 保持阶一，故 \(\delta_+\to1\) [Step 2]。研究一度把它理解为“非商塌缩普遍产生阶一各向异性”，但 Step 3 用圆透镜空间修正：\(S^3/\mathbb Z_m\) 的局部圆度量可满足 \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) 而体积和注入半径趋零；更高奇维球面商也给 exact Einstein quotient collapse [Steps 3,7]。所以不能证明塌缩普遍不存在，而应区分 Einstein-compatible collapse 与坏塌缩。

Step 6 对恒定纤维长度主圆丛
\[
g=\pi^*g_B+t^2\alpha^2,\qquad \phi=tF
\]
推导 Kaluza–Klein Ricci 方程。在三维底空间写 \(\phi=*b\) 后，精确 \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) 会要求 \(|b|^2=2\)、\(db=d^*b=0\) 及
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_B=2g_B-\frac12b\otimes b.
\]
沿 \(b\) 的正 Ricci 与闭底空间非零 harmonic 一形式的 Bochner 恒等式冲突；相同估计在该模型中给出
\[
\delta<\frac1{1+\sqrt2}
\]
时的定量阻碍 [Step 6]。该结果严格限于恒定纤维长度的自由主圆丛；变纤维、dilaton、平均曲率与奇异轨道不在范围内。相关计算见 `workspace/scripts/step6_positive_collapse_probes.py` 和 `workspace/notes/step6_positive_collapse_regularity_probes.md` [Step 6]。

四维全局自由 \(S^1\) 作用满足 \(\chi(M)=\chi(M^{S^1})=0\)，而紧正 pinching 给 \(\chi>0\)，因此自由圆塌缩可由拓扑排除 [Step 7]。这不排除固定点/奇异轨道、orbifold 商或无曲率界的广义 F-structure。会话组后续的 nil\(^3\)、orbit-volume、accessible-cover 探索多次修正符号和适用范围，没有形成一般 cusp-collapse 排除定理 [Steps 6-10]。

## 四维正分支的能量预算、障碍正规形与高拓扑压力测试 [Steps 7-9]

Step 7 将四维正分支组织为四项相互关联的工作：自由作用的 Euler 排除；无需非塌缩假设的 \(L^2\) 曲率预算；Biquard/Ozuch 型第一障碍；以及
\[
M_k=\#_k(S^2\times S^2)
\]
这一 uniformity 测试族 [Step 7]。

通过 `workspace/scripts/step7_det_R_obstruction.py` 计算 \(\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2\)–Eguchi–Hanson 解消的相关曲率块，得到圆 \(S^4\) 的 \(\det R_+=1/27\neq0\)，而合适归一化/方向下的 \(S^2\times S^2\)、\(\mathbb{CP}^2\) 有 \(\det R_+=0\) [Step 7]。结合早期尺度分析，TTCS 确认：在已经处于 Biquard–Ozuch 胶合正规形时，非零第一障碍在 EH 核产生阶一非标量 Ricci 缺陷，多奇点不能在 \(C^0\) 上相消，高阶 \(O(t)\) 项也不能消除该谱差 [Step 7]。但任意 \(C^0\)-pinched 集中序列是否可置入这种正规形仍是开放缺口。

Step 7 曾把 \(\det R_+=0\) 等同于 Kähler–Einstein 选择；Step 8 修正为它仅表示某个 \(W^+\) 特征值为 \(-s/12\)，是相关方向下 Kähler–Einstein 度量满足的必要型代数条件，并不推出 Hermitian/Kähler [Step 8]。LeBrun–Ozuch、Yao 等刚性结果均有精确 Einstein、符号、临界能量或光滑 ALE blow-up 等额外假设，不能直接用于任意 \(C^0\)-pinched 序列 [Steps 7-8]。

对正分支还补出 Weyl 能量下界：
\[
\int|W|^2\ge
8\pi^2\left[
\chi-2\left(\frac{1+\delta}{1-\delta}\right)^2
\right].
\]
对 \(M_k\)，\(\chi=2k+2\)，故
\[
\int|W|^2\ge16\pi^2k-O_\delta(1),
\]
而总体积仍有维数一致上界 [Step 8]。这说明若高 \(k\) 流形达到紧 pinching，必须在 neck、ALE 尺度、固定轨道或塌缩奇异层中承载线性于 \(k\) 的 Weyl 能量。结合 Step 9 非塌缩有限型，得到尾部二分：若 \(M_k\) 上可有 \(\delta_k\to0\)，则总体积必须趋零，同时 Weyl 能量趋无穷；不能说全族都有统一正 gap，因为 \(S^2\times S^2\) 本身是 Einstein [Steps 8-9]。这一族当时只是压力测试，并非已知反例；Step 18 后它变成直接 toric BUILD/BREAK 对象。

## 投影桥构想与 Cheeger–Tian/Li/Naber–Zhang 审计 [Steps 8-10]

Step 8 提出在单个 EH neck 上构造近 cokernel 测试张量 \(\phi_i\)，希望获得
\[
\int\langle\operatorname{Ric}(g_i)-g_i,\phi_i\rangle
=t_i\,\mathcal O(R_+(p),\text{orientation})+o(t_i),
\qquad \|\phi_i\|_{L^1}=O(t_i).
\]
这样 \(C^0\) pinching 直接使左侧为 \(O(\delta_it_i)\)，无需 \(\nabla E\) [Step 8]。由于 EH 衰减阶四且 ADM mass 为零，普通平移/旋转质量通量可能看不到障碍；测试场应匹配锥坐标二次增长和 \(\rho^{-4}\) 系数 [Step 9]。尺度审计发现二次增长场的外环 \(L^1\) 可能发散或主导，需边界通量、截断补偿或严格正规形误差；该桥始终未被误记为完成 [Steps 8-9]。计划见 `workspace/plans/step8_projection_bridge_target.md`。

Step 10 决定从九步 Explore 转入 Execute，但没有把单 neck 桥作为唯一主线，而是审计 Cheeger–Tian、Li、Naber–Zhang 的真实输入。Cheeger–Tian 的无体积假设点态 \(\varepsilon\)-正则性是 Einstein 四流形定理；主 JAMS 原文未取得，现有依据主要来自 Ge–Jiang 的准确转述。Ge–Jiang Theorem 3.4/Cheeger–Tian–Li 已给有界 Ricci、小绝对 \(L^2\) 曲率下的可比尺度选择；Li II 可在无局部能量集中的区域平滑；Naber–Zhang Proposition 6.4 在固定尺度模型、最大幂零秩与局部覆盖条件下给 harmonic radius，而 Proposition 6.5 的点态曲率还需 Einstein 或 \(\nabla\operatorname{Ric}\) 控制 [Step 10]。因此真正缺口不是“没有任何尺度选择”，而是仅 \(C^0\) Ricci 数据下从平均能量到点态曲率的升级。

Step 10 还提出普适覆盖体积放大器。若闭、单连通四流形在
\[
\|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_0
\]
下有拓扑无关体积下界 \(v_0\)，则任意闭四流形也有统一体积下界：正 Ricci 使 \(\pi_1\) 有限；普适覆盖保持 pinching 且体积至少 \(v_0\)；Cheeger–Naber 非塌缩有限型给
\(\chi(\widetilde M)\le X(\delta_0,v_0)\)；又
\[
\chi(\widetilde M)=|\pi_1(M)|\chi(M),\qquad
\chi(\widetilde M)=2+b_2\ge2,
\]
且 \(\chi(M)\) 为正整数，所以覆盖次数有界，进而
\(\operatorname{Vol}(M)\ge v_0/X\) [Steps 10-11]。TTCS 修正了原笔记的非可定向和有限商表述：直接使用单连通、因而可定向的普适覆盖；得到总体积 gap 后，应直接对 \(M\) 应用 Cheeger–Naber，而非假定有限多个 cover 类型只有有限个群作用 [Step 10]。这只是条件性 Proposition A；有限微分型并不产生 Einstein 度量。

## Calderón–Zygmund Hessian spike：点态 \(C^0\)-Ricci 正则性被否定 [Step 11]

Step 11 首先检验 Step 10 的核心正则性猜想，而不是继续抽象路线讨论。研究在闭 Einstein 流形 \(S^2(1)\times S^2(1)\) 上取相反 warping：
\[
g=dx^2+dy^2
+e^{2(F_1+u)}d\theta^2
+e^{2(F_2-u)}d\phi^2,
\quad
F_1=\log\sin x,\quad F_2=\log\sin y.
\]
相反号使 \(\operatorname{Hess}u\) 在 Ricci 基块精确抵消；纤维 Ricci 只通过 \(\Delta u\) 感知扰动，而混合 base–fiber Riemann 分量保留完整 Hessian [Step 11]。

选取
\[
w_\sigma(X,Y)
=-\frac12XY\log(X^2+Y^2+\sigma^2),
\]
可使 \(|\Delta w_\sigma|\) 一致有界、\(\sup|\nabla w_\sigma|\) 一致有界，而
\[
(w_\sigma)_{XY}(0)=\log(1/\sigma)\to\infty.
\]
令振幅 \(a_j=\Lambda^{-2/3}\)、\(\sigma_j=e^{-\Lambda}\)，构造得到
\[
\|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_j}-g_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=O(\Lambda^{-2/3})\to0,
\qquad
|\operatorname{Rm}_{g_j}|(0)\gtrsim\Lambda^{1/3}\to\infty,
\]
同时局部 Hessian/\(\mathrm{Rm}\) 的 \(L^2\) 贡献可趋零；数值审计如 \(\Lambda=500\) 时记录 \(\delta\approx0.032\)、中心曲率约 \(24.4\) [Step 11]。完整推导、符号检查和数据见 `workspace/notes/step11_cz_spike_and_proposition_A.md`、`workspace/scripts/step11_cz_spike_analytical.py`、`workspace/data/step11_cz_hessian_spike.json`。

该构造证明：仅凭 \(C^0\) Ricci pinching 与小局部 \(L^2\) 曲率，不能推出 Cheeger–Tian 型点态曲率上界。其机制是二维 endpoint Calderón–Zygmund 现象；TTCS 的线性化符号检查同时说明，固定非塌缩 Einstein 背景上的单频 TT/WKB 扰动中 Ricci 和 Weyl 主符号同阶，不能提供这种分离，真正机制依赖非线性相反 warping [Steps 10-11]。仍可能保留的是有限 \(p\) 的 \(L^p\)、BMO、harmonic-radius 控制、Li smoothing，以及对 Ricci 缺陷的弱测试场配对。

这一结果是正则性反例，不是 Yau26 反例：底层 \(S^2\times S^2\) 本身 Einstein；且
\[
e^{F_1+u}e^{F_2-u}=e^{F_1+F_2}
\]
使轨道面积密度和总体积保持不变，不能产生体积塌缩 [Steps 11,14]。

## 从 CZ 结构转向 \(T^2\)-不变约化：行列式方程与谱钉扎 [Steps 12-13]

CZ 例使研究认识到同一 ansatz 正是二维轨道空间上的 \(T^2\)-不变约化，因此转向一般局部形式
\[
g=g_B+h_{IJ}(d\phi^I+A^I)(d\phi^J+A^J),
\qquad
w=\sqrt{\det h}.
\]
Step 12 用精确符号 jet 计算得到
\[
\operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^V
=-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}+\frac12|F|_h^2.
\]
所以若 \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\)，则
\[
\left(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|_h^2\right)w
=2\lambda w.
\]
混合 Ricci 在适当 gauge 中给守恒 twist 方程
\[
d\!\left(w h_{IJ} *_BF^J\right)=0
\]
[Step 12]。计算见 `workspace/scripts/step12_toric_determinant_symbolic.py`、`step12_toric_mixed_ricci_gauge_compare.py` 及对应 JSON。

Step 13 纠正了 Step 12 把近似正交可积性视为谱结论前提的悲观判断。若轨道空间有退化边界，\(w>0\) 于内部、\(w=0\) 于边界，上式表明 \(2\lambda\) 是
\(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|^2\) 的 Dirichlet ground-state 特征值；非负 twist 势不会破坏尺度钉扎。正 \(C^0\) pinching 时，直接以 \(w\) 作 Rayleigh 测试得到
\[
\lambda_1^D(\Omega,g_B)\le2(1+\delta),
\]
无需 \(\nabla E\)、点态曲率正则性或近似正交可积 [Step 13]。这成为投影桥思想在对称情形中的具体实现：Killing 场本身提供光滑测试数据。

符号与因子经两个锚点校验。若 \(\lambda\le0\) 且有退化边界，正 Dirichlet 特征值给矛盾，与 Bochner 对非正 Einstein Killing 场的结论一致。对归一化圆 \(S^4(\sqrt3)\)，轨道空间是 \(S^2(\sqrt3)\) 的四分之一，\(w=r_1r_2\) 满足 \(\Delta w=-2w\)，
\(\int_\Omega w=6\)，从而总体积 \(24\pi^2\)，边界通量也与固定球面积匹配 [Step 13]。数据见 `workspace/data/step13_toric_spectral_anchors.json`。

来源 `Knowledge/.../Toric-Einstein-4-manifolds-with-non-negative-sectional-curvature.../object.md` 的相关行支持：单连通闭 toric 四流形的多边形商、测地边和直角顶点；精确 Einstein 情形下 twist 常数由混合方程恒定并在奇异轨道消失；极性情形的轨道体积本征函数定理 [Step 13]。这只是精确 Einstein 情形的来源支持，不能自动推广到 \(C^0\)-pinched 一般度量。

## Toric 商空间、错误的曲率公式与粗体积机制 [Steps 12-14]

在 twist-free 对角约化
\[
g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2
\]
中，精确 \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) 给
\[
\Delta_B(pq)=-2pq.
\]
矩形分离模型
\[
p=\frac{L_x}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi x}{L_x},\qquad
q=\frac{L_y}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi y}{L_y}
\]
满足
\[
\frac{\pi^2}{L_x^2}+\frac{\pi^2}{L_y^2}=2,
\]
AM–GM 给 \(\operatorname{Vol}_4\ge16\pi^2\)，等号是 \(S^2\times S^2\) [Step 12]。这只是 sanity check，不是一般 invariant volume gap。

轨道空间为带测地边和直角角点的圆盘时，Gauss–Bonnet 给
\[
\int_\Omega K_B\,dA
=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}m,
\]
其中 \(m\) 为角点/固定点数，标准 toric 情形通常等于 \(\chi(M)\) [Step 13]。Step 14 曾因把 \(\operatorname{Hess}\log(pq)\) 与 \(\operatorname{Hess}p/p+\operatorname{Hess}q/q\) 混淆而错误推出 \(K_B\ge3\)；该结论当步撤回，正确公式为
\[
K_B
=\frac14\left(|\nabla v|^2-|\nabla\log w|^2\right)
=-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle,
\qquad
w=pq,\quad v=\log(p/q).
\]
相应边缘方程也修正为
\[
Q''+(1-2K_B|_{\rm edge})Q=0
\]
[Step 14]。修正后在 \(S^2\times S^2\) 的平底和 \(S^4\) 的 \(K_B=1/3\) 商空间上均校准正确。

Step 14 曾将谱上界与欧氏 Faber–Krahn 常数结合，声称
\[
\operatorname{Area}(\Omega)\ge
\frac{\pi j_{0,1}^2}{2(1+\delta)}.
\]
Step 17 TTCS 指出这不是无条件结论：经典 \(\pi j_{0,1}^2\) 常数适用于平面欧氏域，而实际 \(g_B\) 可有任意负高斯曲率；没有底曲率或适当等周控制时不能用这一公式 [Step 17]。因此 Steps 14-16 基于“基底面积无条件有统一下界”的措辞均被降为条件性模型直觉，不能作为 volume-gap 证明。

若假设边缘 \(K_B\) 均匀，单位闭合和边缘 ODE 给每边通量约
\[
\Phi=\frac{2}{1-2K_B},
\]
结合角点 Gauss–Bonnet可使 \(m\Phi\) 在 \(m\to\infty\) 时稳定。这一计算曾把研究倾向推向 BUILD，但其关键均匀性假设随后被 Step 15 的非均匀边界集中模型否定为不具代表性 [Steps 14-15]。

## 非均匀边缘集中：粗谱和 Gauss–Bonnet 约束不足 [Step 15]

Step 15 接受用户纠正，不再在 \(m=8,10\) 多边形上求解完整精确 Einstein 系统，因为这主要检验精确分类而非 \(\delta\)-pinched relaxation。来源核对也表明 arXiv:2311.04840 只在非负截面曲率附加条件下分类；LeBrun 的 Hermitian Einstein 定理同样不是任意 \(T^2\)-不变 Einstein 分类 [Step 15]。

研究改为测试边缘 ODE、谱和 Gauss–Bonnet 的放松系统。若每条边局部取
\[
K_B=-A,
\]
则
\[
Q''+(1+2A)Q=0,\qquad
\Phi=\frac{2}{1+2A}.
\]
取 \(A=m^2\) 时，总通量
\[
m\Phi\sim \frac1m\to0,
\]
说明这些粗约束形式上允许体积塌缩 [Step 15]。`workspace/scripts/step15_boundary_bubble_relaxation.py` 保存了该计算。共形矩形有限差分实验还构造出测地边附近 \(K_B\ll0\) 的局部尖峰，同时保持计算出的 \(\lambda_1\le2\)；这仅证明纯二维谱几何不能排除边界负曲率集中，不是四维 Ricci 度量构造 [Step 15]。

Page 度量的显式 U(2) 公式被用于校准商空间边缘曲率，得到约 \([-0.095,0.075]\) 的温和变号。由于坐标尚未转换到 primitive toric rod 归一化，通量输出不是严格 per-sphere Gauss–Bonnet 检验；CLW 没有取得足够显式数据 [Step 15]。

局部边缘 Einstein 方程也没有给出 BUILD 障碍。最初固定
\(a(r)=\cosh(\sqrt A r)\) 的级数在高阶失败，但这只是过度约束；允许 \(a(r)\) 自由后，可对任意 \(A\) 递归满足检查到的 Einstein 方程。进一步得到分离 germ
\[
g=dr^2+p(r)^2d\theta^2+a(r)^2g_{S^2(\kappa)},
\qquad \kappa=1+2A,
\]
满足
\[
a'=Ap,\qquad
2aa''+(a')^2=\kappa-a^2,
\]
及第一积分
\[
a(a')^2
=\kappa(a-1)-\frac{a^3-1}{3}.
\]
第二个 \(p\)-零点处的归一化斜率为
\[
\mu=\frac{2a_++1}{a_+(a_++2)}<1
\qquad(A>0).
\]
因此任意大的负边缘曲率在局部与精确 Einstein 方程兼容，但最简单的分离闭合产生锥角不匹配 [Step 15]。主记录为 `workspace/notes/step15_boundary_bubble_relaxation_and_edge_germ.md`。

## Schwarzschild–de Sitter 识别、edge-cone 修正与分离精确刚性 [Steps 16-17]

Step 16 识别出 Step 15 germ 是归一化 \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) 下的 Euclidean Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Birmingham–Kottler 家族。取
\[
f(\rho)=1-\frac{2M}{\rho}-\frac{\rho^2}{3},
\]
并令
\[
\rho_h=(1+2A)^{-1/2},\qquad
M=\frac{A+1/3}{(2A+1)^{3/2}},\qquad
a=\rho/\rho_h,
\]
符号计算确认
\[
a_+=\frac{-1+\sqrt{9+24A}}2
\]
正是两视界半径比，且 \(\mu\) 是两端 surface gravity 比 [Step 16]。脚本为 `workspace/scripts/step16_sds_dictionary_check.py`，数据为 `workspace/data/step16_sds_dictionary_check.json`。

这同时纠正了 Step 15 把第二端理解为孤立 \(\mathbb R^4/\Gamma\)/EH 型点的错误。第二端是同一 \(S^1\) 沿整个嵌入 \(S^2\) 退化形成的余维二 edge-cone，角度为 \(2\pi\mu\)，不是孤立 orbifold 点；所以 Biquard–Ozuch/Eguchi–Hanson 第一障碍不是该 rod singularity 的匹配工具。相应工具是 Atiyah–LeBrun 的 edge-cone Chern–Weil 公式，其 Euler/signature 缺陷为
\[
2(1-\beta)\chi(\Sigma)
\pm(1-\beta^2)[\Sigma]^2
\]
[Step 16]。这不撤销 EH 障碍在线性化孤立 orbifold 泡问题中的价值，只是分离 rod 闭合应使用锥角/holonomy 和记账。

两种周期归一化也被区分：若先平滑小黑洞 bolt，第二端角度为 \(2\pi\mu\)，且 \(A\to\infty\) 时总体积趋零；若先平滑 cosmological bolt，则总体积趋 \(24\pi^2\) 的圆 \(S^4\) 值，但小 bolt 有角度 \(2\pi/\mu\)。两者只在 \(A=0\) 的 Nariai 极限一致，得到 \(S^2\times S^2\)、体积 \(16\pi^2\) [Step 16]。

Step 17 由此证明精确分离刚性：在该 cohomogeneity-one、主轨道 \(S^1\times S^2\)、两端均为光滑 \(S^2\) bolt 的精确 Einstein 类中，固定 primitive 周期要求两端斜率相同，即 \(\mu=1\)；上述公式给 \(\mu=1\iff A=0\)，所以唯一解是 Nariai \(S^2(1)\times S^2(1)\) [Step 17]。并计算
\[
\left.\frac{d\mu}{dA}\right|_{A=0}=-\frac43.
\]
这是一项严格而窄的精确结果。Step 17 曾写出基于 ODE 稳定性的条件性 pinched separated gap，但 bolt 处方程退化、区间长度和高阶控制均未从 Ricci 不等式推出；因此没有建立无条件的“\(\delta\)-pinched 即 \(A=O(\delta)\)”定理 [Steps 16-17]。用户明确要求把平滑双 bolt 的 pinched collapse 继续视为可能的 BREAK 候选，而不能由精确 SdS 刚性直接排除 [Step 17]。

## 一般 \(T^k\) 行列式恒等式与高维触角 [Step 17]

为避免 invariant 工作完全局限于四维，Step 17 对 twist-free 对角
\[
g=g_B+\sum_{I=1}^k p_I^2\,d\theta_I^2,
\qquad w=\prod_{I=1}^kp_I
\]
证明
\[
\operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^V
=-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}.
\]
证明只用乘积法则，独立于底维数；符号脚本对 \(k=1,\dots,5\) 作了校验 [Step 17]。若竖直方向各 Ricci 本征值位于 \(1\pm\delta\)，则
\[
k(1-\delta)\le
\frac{-\Delta_Bw}{w}
\le k(1+\delta).
\]
在有 Dirichlet 退化边界时，Barta/ground-state 论证给
\[
k(1-\delta)\le\lambda_1^D(\Omega,g_B)
\le k(1+\delta).
\]
TTCS 确认 Barta 下界有效；这与被撤回的 Faber–Krahn 面积结论不同 [Step 17]。该恒等式是目前少数明确延伸到高维的结构，但需要高秩 torus 对称及退化边界，不能代替任意 \(n\ge5\) 机制。

## 路线评估的两次修正：bubble-tree、Hitchin–Thorpe 与 toric 工作的地位 [Steps 17-18]

Step 17 在六步 invariant 研究后进行全局路线评估，指出三个桥：一般度量到 invariant collapse、invariant polygon volume gap、有限微分型到 Einstein 存在。TTCS 生成器提出非塌缩 orbifold/ALE bubble-tree 路线，可通过具体解消上的 Lichnerowicz 谱与 DeTurck 残差比较来区分可修正、有限维障碍或反例。该路线绕过“先获得全局 torus 对称”，但它真正的前置条件不是已被 Step 11 否定的点态 \(C^0\)-Ricci \(\varepsilon\)-正则性，而是适用于 \(C^0\)-pinched 序列的加权 annular normal form、harmonic-radius 或弱正规形 [Steps 17-18]。因此该方向被保留为 Steps 8-9 非塌缩投影桥的正确归宿，但没有立即启动未经前提支持的 Lichnerowicz 数值工程。

Step 17 同时错误地把 \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\) 的 Hitchin–Thorpe 非存在说成“Bridge 3 的根本障碍”，并误提其是否可能 tight pinched 为开放。Step 18 用早期 sign-blind CGB 结论纠正：tight pinching 自身已严格排除所有 HT 违反和等号流形；\(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\)、\(\#_4\mathbb{CP}^2\) 不能进入候选 [Step 18]。Sha–Yang 的范围也被纠正为 \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) 的正 Ricci 构造，而非 \(\#_k\mathbb{CP}^2\) [Steps 17-18]。

Step 17 还一度因“一般到 invariant 桥未建”而把 Steps 12-17 降为实验室。Step 18 纠正这种过度降级：若目标是直接判定
\[

\]
是否承载 \(\delta_k\to0\) 的正 pinched 度量，构造方向可直接采用这些流形已有的 toric/quasitoric 多边形模型，无需先证明任意一般塌缩都会 toric [Step 18]。一般到 invariant 桥仍是证明所有一般度量不塌缩所必需，但不是在该实际压力族上做 BUILD/BREAK 构造或 obstruction 的前提。

因此正分支当前被重新定位为两层问题：

对角 polar probe 使用
\[
g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2,\qquad
w=pq,\quad v=\log(p/q).

\[
r_p+r_q=-\frac{\Delta w}{w},\qquad
r_p-r_q=-\frac1w\operatorname{div}(w\nabla v),

水平块为
\[
\operatorname{Ric}^H
=K_Bg_B-
\left[
\nabla^2\log w+
\frac12\bigl(d\log w\otimes d\log w+dv\otimes dv\bigr)
\right].
\]
因此数值目标是直接最小化
\[
\sup\max\left(
|r_p-1|,\ |r_q-1|,\
\|\operatorname{Ric}^H-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\right)
\]
并同步监测
\[
\operatorname{Vol}=4\pi^2\int_\Omega w
=2\pi^2\times(\text{总边界通量})
\]
[Step 18]。`workspace/scripts/step18_diagonal_toric_residual_evaluator.py` 已在 \(S^2\times S^2\) 上做解析零残差校准；有限差分仍有明显边界误差，\(N=257\) 时约 \(0.052\)，所以只是 scaffold，不能把当前数值残差当作几何 obstruction [Step 18]。

下一主计算应从 Step 15 的高负边缘种子
\[

Q''+(1+2A)Q=0,\qquad
m\Phi\sim1/m

出发，在 \(m=6\) 后扩展到 \(m=8,10\)，检查完整水平、竖直 Ricci 误差及 primitive rod/corner smoothness。若对角 ansatz 失败，必须区分是实质性的 rod/holonomy/horizontal traceless 障碍，还是缺少一般矩阵纤维 \(h_{IJ}\)、twist \(A^I\) 的 ansatz 人为限制 [Step 18]。执行计划见 `workspace/plans/step18_toric_crux_execute_plan.md`。

# Results, Observations, and Their Meaning

## Exact proposition, normalization, and quantifiers

- The controlling target is the user’s unchanged formulation: for every \(n\ge2\), find dimension-only constants \(c_n<C_n\) such that every closed connected smooth \(n\)-manifold carrying a metric \(g\) with
  \[
  c_ng\le \operatorname{Ric}_g\le C_ng
  \]
  carries some Einstein metric, with no required relation between the input and output metrics and no restriction on the signs of the interval or Einstein constant. The dossier `Skills/qiushi-yau26/references/research/20260910.tex` is a research map, not a proof. [Step 1]

- For fixed \(n\), let \(P_n^\sigma\), \(\sigma=\pm1\), denote the assertion that some \(\delta_n>0\) makes
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_g-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_n
  \]
  sufficient for Einstein existence on the underlying manifold. Rescaling reduces any same-sign interval to one normalized branch. An interval containing \(0\) would imply Einstein existence on every smooth \(n\)-manifold, because any metric can be rescaled until its Ricci endomorphism lies in that interval. Thus proving one normalized branch in every dimension suffices, while a refutation in one dimension must defeat both signs, potentially on different no-Einstein manifolds. [Steps 1, 3]

- Dimensions \(2\) and \(3\) are covered at the ordinary mathematical level by uniformization and Ricci-flow/geometrization respectively. The unresolved geometric content begins in dimension \(4\), but a four-dimensional result alone cannot settle the all-dimensional target. [Steps 1, 5]

- In dimension four, known no-Einstein smooth manifolds rule out any viable interval with \(c_4<0<C_4\): after multiplying an arbitrary metric by a sufficiently large constant, its Ricci endomorphism approaches zero while the smooth topology remains unchanged. Hence any successful four-dimensional interval must have one sign. [Step 3]

## Negative branch and known stability results

- Direct reading of Min–Oo corrected an OCR ambiguity: \(d\) in the theorem denotes diameter. After normalizing \(\max|K|=1\), the extra condition is \(d<\Lambda\); invariantly it is
  \[
  d(g)^2\max|K_g|<\Lambda^2.
  \]
  For \(n>3\), sufficiently small negative Ricci defect then yields an Einstein metric, but the threshold depends on the full-curvature/diameter class. This is not a pure Ricci-pinching theorem. [Step 1]

- A source-supported contrapositive follows. If no-Einstein manifolds \((M_j,g_j)\) satisfy
  \[
  \delta_-(g_j)=\|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_j}+g_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0,
  \]
  then
  \[
  d(g_j)^2\max|K_{g_j}|\to\infty.
  \]
  Otherwise a bounded subsequence would eventually enter a fixed Min–Oo class. Any negative-branch counterexample must therefore escape through sectional/Weyl concentration, diameter growth, collapse, or comparable degeneration. [Step 1]

- The Morteza–Viaclovsky Calabi-region estimate was converted carefully into the input metric’s operator norm:
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{g_t}-\Lambda g_t-t\lambda\chi_to
  =O_{g_{\mathrm{cal}}}(t^2\rho^2),
  \qquad g_t\sim t\,g_{\mathrm{cal}}.
  \]
  Raising one index makes the remainder \(O(t\rho^2)\), hence \(O(t)\) in the core and at worst \(O(t^{1/2})\) on \(\rho\sim t^{-1/4}\). The first-obstruction term behaves differently: \(t\lambda o\) becomes
  \[
  \lambda g_{\mathrm{cal}}^{-1}o+o(1),
  \]
  whose non-scalar eigenvalue spread is order one. Thus weighted, \(L^p\), or GH-small gluing residuals do not imply the unweighted operator pinching required by Yau-26. Multiple singularities cannot cancel a pointwise supremum defect. [Step 1]

- A viable desingularization counterexample would therefore require all local first obstructions to vanish, or a varying family with relative obstruction tending to zero while some higher/global obstruction still prevents every Einstein metric. The Calabi calculation concerns real dimension at least six; four-dimensional Eguchi–Hanson models have additional orientation and rotation parameters. [Step 1]

- Exact-Einstein degeneration sources remain narrower than the Yau-26 hypothesis. Ozuch’s weighted gluing/normal-form results, LeBrun–Ozuch’s positive exact-Einstein rigidity, and Yao’s negative exact-Einstein resolution results do not directly apply to arbitrary metrics with only \(C^0\) Ricci pinching. The proposed one-neck projection/flux identity
  \[
  \int\langle \operatorname{Ric}(g_i)-g_i,\phi_i\rangle
  =t_i\,\mathcal O+o(t_i)
  \]
  remains unproved; long-annulus \(L^1\) growth suggests that a boundary or Pohozaev formulation may be needed. [Steps 7–9]

- Under bubble rescaling \(\widehat g=r^{-2}g\), the Ricci endomorphism scales as
  \[
  |\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}|_{\widehat g}
  \lesssim r^2(1+\delta),
  \]
  so blow-ups of pinched sequences become Ricci-flat to order \(r^2\). This scale separation supports projection methods but does not supply the necessary weighted normal form. [Step 9]

## Corrected Seiberg–Witten and LeBrun evidence

- A factor-four error from Step 2 was fully retracted. If \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\) in dimension four, then \(s=4\lambda\) and
  \[
  \frac1{24}\int s^2\,d\mu
  =\frac23\lambda^2\operatorname{Vol}(g),
  \]
  giving
  \[
  8\pi^2(2\chi+3\tau)
  =4\int|W^+|^2\,d\mu
   +\frac43\lambda^2\operatorname{Vol}(g).
  \]
  The former coefficient \(16/3\) and the conclusion that every \(X\#k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\), \(0<k<A=c_1^2(X)\), is excluded from negative Einstein geometry were false. [Steps 2–3]

- The \(A\) versus \(A-k\) issue was resolved. Individual blow-up monopole classes have square \(A-k\), but LeBrun’s sharp estimate uses the sign family/convex hull and the averaged class \(a=\pi^*K_X\), with \(a^2=A\) and a metric-dependent self-dual projection satisfying \((a^+)^2\ge A\). Computing only individual class squares misses the class used in the estimate. [Step 3]

- Source-checked thresholds are:
  - the scalar-only LeBrun estimate excludes negative Einstein metrics for \(k\ge2A/3\), including the endpoint by strictness;
  - the refined scalar–\(W^+\) estimate improves this to \(k\ge A/3\), under its orientation, monopole/polarization, and \(b_+\) hypotheses. [Steps 3–4]

- A stable integral obstruction survives the correction. If
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}+g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta,
  \]
  then \(\int|E|^2=O(\delta^2)\operatorname{Vol}\). An all-metric curvature inequality with a fixed strict Einstein-obstruction margin also excludes sufficiently tight pinching. In the recorded refined LeBrun regime,
  \[
  \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}
  \ge \sqrt{\frac{p-\frac13}{2}},
  \qquad p=\frac{k}{A},
  \]
  subject to the theorem’s hypotheses. At \(p=2/3\),
  \[
  \delta\ge\frac1{1+\sqrt6}\approx0.289897949.
  \]
  At fixed \(p>1/3\) this is a scale-independent repulsion from negative pinching; the margin vanishes only as \(p\downarrow1/3\). [Steps 3–4]

- At the exact Ishida–LeBrun boundary, peer work recorded the near-saturation profile
  \[
  \frac{\operatorname{Vol}}{\pi^2A}\to\frac{32}{9},\qquad
  \frac{\int|W^+|^2}{\pi^2A}\to\frac4{27},\qquad
  \frac{\int|\operatorname{Ric}^0|^2}{\pi^2A}\to0,
  \]
  and
  \[
  \int\bigl(s+8\sqrt6\,|W^+|\bigr)^2=O(A\delta^2).
  \]
  Available sources give qualitative equality mechanisms involving almost-Kähler geometry and the lowest \(W^+\) eigenspace, but no retrieved quantitative theorem turns this total deficit into global near-Kähler rigidity; thin topology-bearing regions remain possible. [Step 4]

- Tight positive pinching implies positive scalar curvature. Consequently the usual metric-independent Seiberg–Witten/monopole nonexistence mechanisms cannot directly provide a positive-branch counterexample under their standard hypotheses: the pinched input metric itself has positive scalar curvature. This does not prove that every tightly positive-pinched topology is Einstein; it means the currently used monopole obstruction families are poorly aligned with that branch. [Steps 3–4, 18]

## Four-dimensional Chern–Weil accounting and strict Hitchin–Thorpe

- For
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-\sigma g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta,
  \qquad \sigma=\pm1,
  \]
  pointwise minimization in
  \[
  8\pi^2\chi
  =\int\left(|W|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|E|^2}{2}\right)d\mu
  \]
  gives
  \[
  \beta(\delta)\operatorname{Vol}
  \le8\pi^2\chi-\int|W|^2
  \le a(\delta)\operatorname{Vol},
  \]
  where
  \[
  \beta(\delta)=
  \begin{cases}
  \frac23(1-\delta)^2,&0\le\delta\le\frac13,\\[1mm]
  \frac23(1+\delta)(1-2\delta),&\frac13\le\delta<\frac12,
  \end{cases}
  \qquad
  a(\delta)=\frac23(1+\delta)^2.
  \]
  The earlier coefficient \(\frac23(1-\delta)^2-2\delta^2\) is valid but weaker and superseded. [Step 4]

- Therefore, for either sign and \(\delta<1/2\),
  \[
  \chi(M)>0,\qquad
  \operatorname{Vol}(M)\le\frac{8\pi^2\chi(M)}{\beta(\delta)}.
  \]
  These are global volume/energy statements and do not prevent local injectivity-radius collapse or curvature concentration. [Step 4]

- Tight pinching also forces strict Hitchin–Thorpe in both signs. For
  \[
  \delta<\frac1{1+\sqrt3},
  \]
  the oriented Chern–Weil formulas yield
  \[
  2\chi>3|\tau|.
  \]
  This corrects Step 17’s temporary claim that Hitchin–Thorpe fundamentally obstructed the “finiteness-to-Einstein” bridge. Hitchin–Thorpe violators and equality cases cannot enter a sufficiently tightly pinched class in the first place. In particular, \(\#_5\mathbb{CP}^2\) and \(\#_4\mathbb{CP}^2\) are not candidate tightly pinched positive-branch counterexamples. [Steps 1–4, 18]

- With the session’s curvature-operator Hilbert–Schmidt convention,
  \[
  \int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2
  =8\pi^2\chi+\int|E|^2.
  \]
  Coefficients change under the usual \((0,4)\)-tensor norm, so later CGB computations must name the convention. Pinching plus the volume bound gives a global \(L^2\)-curvature bound for fixed topology, but allows \(O(\chi)\) curvature bubbles. [Steps 4, 10, 14]

- Chern transgression on a region \(U\),
  \[
  \int_U\left(|W|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|E|^2}{2}\right)
  =8\pi^2\chi(U)-\int_{\partial U}\Pi,
  \]
  remains the prospective localization mechanism. No complete thick–thin theorem controlling the boundary transgression on singular/collapsed cuts has been proved. [Steps 5, 7]

## Positive branch: comparison, collapse, and model restrictions

- If \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge(1-\delta)g\), Myers and Bishop give
  \[
  \operatorname{diam}(M,g)
  \le\pi\sqrt{\frac{n-1}{1-\delta}}
  \]
  and a dimension-only volume upper bound. Bochner gives \(b_1=0\), and \(\pi_1\) is finite. Its order is not dimensionally bounded: normalized round lens spaces satisfy \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) while \(|\pi_1|\to\infty\). [Steps 5–6]

- Exact positive Einstein collapse disproves any general “tight pinching implies noncollapse” principle. Round lens spaces and higher odd-dimensional Hopf quotients collapse in volume and injectivity radius with defect \(0\). Products such as \((S^3/\mathbb Z_q)\times S^{n-3}\), after matching Einstein constants, give corresponding exact collapsed examples in \(n\ge5\). Thus the all-dimensional problem must distinguish Einstein-compatible collapse from topology that cannot support Einstein metrics. [Steps 6–7, 10]

- For a constant-fiber-length principal circle connection metric over a closed three-manifold,
  \[
  g=\pi^*g_B+t^2(d\theta+A)^2,\qquad \phi=tF,
  \]
  the recorded formulas are
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}(U,U)=\frac{|\phi|^2}{2},\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_{\mathrm{hor}}
  =\operatorname{Ric}_B-\frac12\phi\circ\phi,\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\pm\frac12d^*\phi.
  \]
  Writing \(\phi=*b\), exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=g\) forces
  \[
  |b|^2=2,\quad db=d^*b=0,\quad
  \operatorname{Ric}_B=2g_B-\frac12b\otimes b,
  \]
  contradicting Bochner. The pinched model is impossible for
  \[
  \delta<\frac1{1+\sqrt2}.
  \]
  This applies only to constant fiber length; variable dilaton, singular fibers, fixed points, and general collapse remain outside it. [Step 6]

- In oriented dimension four, a global free \(S^1\) or torus action is incompatible with tight positive pinching because such an action has \(\chi=0\), while \(b_1=0\) gives \(\chi=2+b_2\ge2\). This does not exclude actions with fixed sets, orbifold fibrations, or general local F-structures. [Step 7]

## Cheeger–Naber regularity and noncollapsed finiteness

- Step 5’s claim that bounded Ricci plus noncollapse gives a global harmonic-radius lower bound and smooth convergence was false and was retracted. Exact Einstein sequences can develop Weyl concentration in dimensions at least four. [Steps 5, 9]

- Direct reading of Cheeger–Naber established the correct replacement:
  - bounded Ricci and local noncollapse give a noncollapsed limit that is \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) away from a closed singular set of Hausdorff and Minkowski codimension at least four;
  - in dimension four there are \(L^2\)-curvature and tubular-volume estimates such as
    \[
    \operatorname{Vol}(T_r\{r_h\le r\})\le Cr^4;
    \]
  - the harmonic-radius \(\varepsilon\)-regularity theorem uses GH closeness to \(\mathbb R^{n-3}\times C(Z)\), not merely small \(L^2\) curvature. [Steps 6, 9]

- Consequently, a noncollapsed sequence with
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_i}-g_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0
  \]
  has a subsequential regular part converging in \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\); the almost-Einstein equation passes weakly and elliptic regularity makes the regular limit smooth Einstein. This is an all-dimensional regular-part theorem, not same-topology Einstein existence. [Step 9]

- In dimension four, cone annuli in rescaled bounded-Ricci, noncollapsed sequences converge to
  \[
  dr^2+r^2g_{S^3/\Gamma}
  \]
  under the Cheeger–Naber volume-ratio hypotheses. This gives source-backed neck geometry but not the weighted glued normal form required to evaluate Biquard/Ozuch obstruction coefficients for merely pinched metrics. [Step 9]

- Cheeger–Naber Theorem 1.12 gives the strongest established four-dimensional positive-branch finiteness result:
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta<\frac12,\qquad
  \operatorname{Vol}(M)\ge v>0
  \]
  implies only finitely many diffeomorphism types, with the number depending on \((\delta,v)\). Myers supplies diameter control and Bishop–Gromov converts total noncollapse into local noncollapse. This theorem does not assert Einstein existence on any of those types. [Step 9]

## Weyl-energy stress family and the finite-cover amplifier

- CGB and Bishop give the sharp lower Weyl budget
  \[
  \int|W|^2\,d\mu
  \ge8\pi^2\left[
  \chi(M)-2\left(\frac{1+\delta}{1-\delta}\right)^2
  \right].
  \]
  For
  \[
  M_k=\#_k(S^2\times S^2),\qquad \chi(M_k)=2k+2,
  \]
  any tightly positive-pinched metric satisfies
  \[
  \int|W|^2\ge16\pi^2k-O_\delta(1),\qquad
  \operatorname{Vol}\le\frac{24\pi^2}{(1-\delta)^2}.
  \]
  These manifolds have positive-Ricci metrics from surgery/core-metric constructions, but no evidence establishes tight two-sided pinching on those constructions. Einstein existence for \(k\ge2\) remains unresolved in this record. [Steps 7–9, 18]

- Combining this with noncollapsed finite-type control yields a tail dichotomy:
  \[
  \liminf_{k\to\infty}\delta_+(M_k)>0,
  \]
  or any sequence with \(\delta_+(M_k)\to0\) must satisfy
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}(M_k)\to0,\qquad
  \int|W|^2\ge16\pi^2k-o(k).
  \]
  The energy lower bound is not an obstruction to collapse: \(O(k)\) bubbles can carry \(O(k)\) fixed energy quanta. [Steps 8–9, 14]

- A conditional finite-cover amplifier was proved. Suppose some \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(v_0>0\) satisfy
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_0
  \Longrightarrow \operatorname{Vol}(N)\ge v_0
  \]
  for every closed simply connected four-manifold \(N\). For any closed \(M\) in the same pinched class, Myers makes \(\pi_1(M)\) finite. Its universal cover \(\widetilde M\) satisfies the same pinching and \(\operatorname{Vol}(\widetilde M)\ge v_0\). Cheeger–Naber finiteness bounds \(\chi(\widetilde M)\) by a constant \(X(\delta_0,v_0)\), while
  \[
  \chi(\widetilde M)=|\pi_1(M)|\chi(M),\qquad
  \chi(\widetilde M)=2+b_2(\widetilde M)\ge2,
  \]
  and \(\chi(M)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). Hence
  \[
  |\pi_1(M)|\le X,\qquad
  \operatorname{Vol}(M)\ge\frac{v_0}{X}.
  \]
  The universal gap then lets Cheeger–Naber be applied directly to \(M\). No finite-group-action classification on the covers is needed. [Steps 10–11]

- The gap in this amplifier must be topology-uniform. A bound \(v_0(\chi)\to0\) makes the attempted Cheeger–Naber bound on \(\chi(\widetilde M)\) circular. [Step 14]

## Failure of pointwise \(C^0\)-Ricci \(\varepsilon\)-regularity

- An explicit Calderón–Zygmund Hessian-spike family on the already Einstein manifold \(S^2\times S^2\) disproved a pointwise Cheeger–Tian analogue under only \(C^0\) Ricci pinching. In local product-polar coordinates use
  \[
  g=dx^2+dy^2
  +e^{2(F_1+u)}d\theta^2
  +e^{2(F_2-u)}d\phi^2,
  \qquad
  F_1=\log\sin x,\quad F_2=\log\sin y.
  \]
  Opposite warping cancels \(\nabla^2u\) from the base Ricci block; only \(\Delta u\) enters the fiber Ricci components, while mixed Riemann components retain the full Hessian. [Step 11]

- The spike function
  \[
  w_\sigma(X,Y)
  =-\frac12XY\log(X^2+Y^2+\sigma^2)
  \]
  satisfies
  \[
  |\Delta w_\sigma|\le\frac94,\qquad
  \sup|\nabla w_\sigma|\lesssim0.362,
  \qquad
  \partial_{XY}w_\sigma(0)=\log(1/\sigma)\to\infty.
  \]
  Taking \(\sigma=e^{-\Lambda}\) and amplitude \(a_\Lambda=\Lambda^{-2/3}\) gives smooth closed metrics with
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}_g-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(\Lambda^{-2/3})\to0,
  \qquad
  |\mathrm{Rm}_g|(0)\gtrsim\Lambda^{1/3}\to\infty.
  \]
  The numerical check at \(\Lambda=500\) recorded defect about \(0.032\), center curvature about \(24.4\), and spike Hessian \(L^2\)-energy about \(0.005\). [Step 11]

- The vanishing-energy statement concerns the added Hessian/spike contribution, not the total global \(\int_{S^2\times S^2}|\mathrm{Rm}|^2\), which retains the nonzero topological/background energy. Locally, the construction can make the extra \(L^2\) energy small while pointwise curvature diverges. [Step 11]

- This construction is not a Yau-26 counterexample because \(S^2\times S^2\) already carries an Einstein product metric. It establishes that bounded Ricci, even with defect tending to zero, does not yield pointwise curvature control. Harmonic-radius, \(C^{1,\alpha}\), finite-\(p\) Calderón–Zygmund, or BMO control may survive. [Step 11]

- A principal-symbol check explains why naive high-frequency TT perturbations do not produce the same phenomenon on a fixed Einstein background: Ricci and Weyl have the same second-order frequency scaling, and the principal Ricci-symbol kernel is gauge. The spike exploits nonlinear opposite-warp cancellation and endpoint Calderón–Zygmund behavior. [Steps 10–11]

- Peer-session attempts to repair the negative branch through localized Li smoothing remain incomplete. The claimed closure was withdrawn because the cutoff/transition domains did not match, Ricci flow has no finite propagation speed, and comparable-ball smallness only covers centers near selected good points. Valid pieces include Sobolev volume cancellation and some cutoff-defect estimates, but the missing weighted \(\varepsilon\)-regularity/plateau-accessibility step has not been proved. [Steps 16–18]

## General \(T^2\)-invariant determinant identity

- For a local \(T^2\)-invariant metric
  \[
  g=g_B+h_{IJ}(d\phi^I+A^I)(d\phi^J+A^J),
  \qquad w=\sqrt{\det h},
  \]
  exact symbolic jet calculations give
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^{V}
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}+\frac12|F|_h^2.
  \]
  Therefore exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\) implies
  \[
  \left(-\Delta_B+\frac12|F|_h^2\right)w
  =2\lambda w.
  \]
  [Step 12]

- If the torus action has a degeneration boundary, \(w>0\) in the orbit-space interior and \(w=0\) at the boundary. Thus \(w\) is the positive ground state of the Schrödinger operator. The nonnegative twist potential does not destroy scale pinning. In particular,
  \[
  \lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)\le2\lambda
  \]
  in the exact positive-Einstein case. Under
  \[
  \|\operatorname{Ric}-g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta,
  \]
  Rayleigh testing with \(w\) gives
  \[
  \lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)\le2(1+\delta).
  \]
  No derivatives of the Ricci defect or approximate orthogonal transitivity are required. [Step 13]

- A mixed-Ricci computation in the gauge \(A_x=0,\ A_y=fx\) yielded
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_{xI}
  =\frac12\partial_y(wh_{IJ}f_J),\qquad
  \operatorname{Ric}_{yI}
  =-\frac12\partial_x(wh_{IJ}f_J),
  \]
  corresponding to
  \[
  d(wh_{IJ}*_BF^J)=0.
  \]
  Exact orthogonal transitivity for closed simply connected Einstein \(T^2\)-manifolds with fixed strata is also source-supported: the twist quantities are constant and vanish on the singular strata. This exact result does not give approximate transitivity for merely pinched metrics. [Steps 12–13]

- Sign and factor checks were made against two independent anchors:
  - a compact Einstein metric with \(\lambda\le0\) cannot have a nonzero Killing field with zeros, matching the positive Dirichlet-eigenvalue consequence;
  - for normalized round \(S^4\), radius \(\sqrt3\), the orbit space is a quarter of \(S^2(\sqrt3)\), \(w=r_1r_2\), and
    \[
    \Delta w=-2w,\qquad
    \int_\Omega w=6,\qquad
    \operatorname{Vol}(S^4)=4\pi^2\int_\Omega w=24\pi^2.
    \]
  [Step 13]

## Twist-free toric reduction and corrected orbit geometry

- In the diagonal polar case
  \[
  g=g_B+p^2d\theta^2+q^2d\phi^2,\qquad
  w=pq,\quad v=\log(p/q),
  \]
  the vertical Ricci eigenvalues satisfy
  \[
  r_p+r_q=-\frac{\Delta w}{w},\qquad
  r_p-r_q=-\frac1w\operatorname{div}(w\nabla v),
  \]
  while the horizontal block is
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}^H
  =K_Bg_B-\left[
    \nabla^2\log w
    +\frac12\bigl(d\log w\otimes d\log w+dv\otimes dv\bigr)
  \right].
  \]
  These formulas define the full normalized positive Ricci residual used in the later computational scaffold. [Steps 14, 18]

- For exact \(\operatorname{Ric}=\lambda g\),
  \[
  \Delta_Bw=-2\lambda w.
  \]
  In the rectangular separated model,
  \[
  p=\frac{L_x}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi x}{L_x},\qquad
  q=\frac{L_y}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi y}{L_y},
  \]
  the condition
  \[
  \frac{\pi^2}{L_x^2}+\frac{\pi^2}{L_y^2}=2
  \]
  yields
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_4\ge16\pi^2
  \]
  by AM–GM, with equality at \(S^2\times S^2\). This is an ansatz result, not a general invariant volume gap. [Step 12]

- The Step 11 opposite-warp spike preserves the determinant:
  \[
  w=e^{F_1+u}e^{F_2-u}=e^{F_1+F_2}.
  \]
  It can concentrate curvature but cannot change the fiber-area density or collapse the total volume. A volume-breaking ansatz must shrink both \(p\) and \(q\), rather than use opposite determinant-preserving warps. [Step 14]

- The earlier formula \(K_B\ge3\) was erroneous and retracted. The corrected relation is
  \[
  K_B
  =\frac14\left(|\nabla v|^2-|\nabla\log w|^2\right)
  =-\langle\nabla\log p,\nabla\log q\rangle.
  \]
  It was checked on the flat orbit rectangle of \(S^2\times S^2\) and the spherical orbit space of normalized \(S^4\). [Step 14]

- In the simply connected toric setting, the orbit space is a disk-like polygon with geodesic edges and right-angle vertices. Gauss–Bonnet gives
  \[
  \int_\Omega K_B\,dA
  =2\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}m,
  \]
  where \(m\) is the number of fixed points/vertices. This matches \(S^4\), \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), and \(S^2\times S^2\). [Step 13]

- Near an edge where one circle collapses, the corrected edge equation is
  \[
  Q''+\bigl(1-2K_B|_{\mathrm{edge}}\bigr)Q=0,
  \]
  and the intrinsic curvature of the fixed two-sphere is
  \[
  K_\Sigma=1-2K_B|_{\mathrm{edge}}.
  \]
  The earlier sign variant was corrected using the \(S^4\) anchor. [Steps 13–14]

- Step 14 temporarily applied the flat Euclidean Faber–Krahn constant to conclude
  \[
  \operatorname{Area}(\Omega)
  \ge\frac{\pi j_{0,1}^2}{2(1+\delta)}.
  \]
  This is not valid for an arbitrary orbit-space metric \(g_B\) with uncontrolled negative Gauss curvature. Step 17/18 retracted the unconditional area bound. The spectral eigenvalue estimate remains valid, but no universal base-area lower bound follows from the classical flat-domain Faber–Krahn inequality in this setting. [Steps 14, 17–18]

## Nonuniform boundary curvature and the toric collapse enemy

- A uniform-edge-curvature toy model gave a stabilizing total rod flux as \(m\to\infty\), but it was not robust. If
  \[
  K_B|_{\mathrm{rod}}=-A,
  \]
  then the edge equation becomes
  \[
  Q''+(1+2A)Q=0,
  \]
  and unit endpoint closure gives
  \[
  \Phi_{\mathrm{rod}}=\frac{2}{1+2A}.
  \]
  Taking \(A=m^2\) on an \(m\)-rod relaxation yields total flux
  \[
  m\Phi_{\mathrm{rod}}
  =\frac{2m}{1+2m^2}\sim\frac1m,
  \]
  formally driving
  \[
  \operatorname{Vol}_4=2\pi^2\sum\Phi_{\mathrm{rod}}
  \]
  to zero. [Steps 14–15]

- Finite-difference experiments on conformal rectangles, normalized to fixed area and with geodesic straight edges, found examples with strongly negative localized edge curvature while \(\lambda_1\le2\). Recorded examples included:
  \[
  \lambda_1\approx1.906,\quad K_{\mathrm{edge}}\approx-916
  \]
  for amplitude \(0.25\), width \(0.03\), and
  \[
  \lambda_1\approx1.792,\quad K_{\mathrm{edge}}\approx-9.68\times10^5
  \]
  for amplitude \(3\), width \(0.05\). These are two-dimensional relaxations, not four-dimensional pinched metrics. They establish only that spectral pinning, signed Gauss–Bonnet, and unit edge closure do not by themselves prohibit localized negative boundary curvature. [Step 15]

- A Page-metric quotient calculation found a mild sign-changing base-curvature profile, approximately
  \[
  K_B\in[-0.095,0.075].
  \]
  The curvature profile is a useful calibration, but the accompanying flux diagnostics were not source-grade because the \(U(2)\)/Euler-angle coordinates were not converted to primitive toric rod coordinates. A comparable Chen–LeBrun–Weber profile was not obtained. [Step 15]

## Boundary Einstein germs and Schwarzschild–de Sitter recognition

- Flexible formal edge expansions showed that arbitrarily negative edge curvature is locally compatible with exact Einstein equations. For the checked expansion,
  \[
  R_2=A/2,\qquad
  p_3=-(2A+1)/6,\qquad
  R_4=-A(2A+1)/24,
  \]
  and higher coefficients solve the residual recursively. The earlier failure obtained after imposing \(a(r)=\cosh(\sqrt A\,r)\) was an artifact of overconstraining the ansatz, not a local obstruction. [Step 15]

- The exact separated germ
  \[
  g=dr^2+p(r)^2d\theta^2+a(r)^2g_{S^2(\kappa)},
  \qquad \kappa=1+2A,
  \]
  satisfies
  \[
  a'=Ap,\qquad
  2aa''+(a')^2=\kappa-a^2,
  \]
  with first integral
  \[
  a(a')^2=\kappa(a-1)-\frac{a^3-1}{3}.
  \]
  Its second zero of \(p\) occurs at
  \[
  a_+=\frac{-1+\sqrt{9+24A}}2,
  \]
  and the second-bolt slope is
  \[
  \mu=\frac{2a_++1}{a_+(a_++2)}.
  \]
  [Step 15]

- Step 16 recognized and algebraically verified this germ as Euclidean Schwarzschild–de Sitter/Birmingham–Kottler with
  \[
  f(\rho)=1-\frac{2M}{\rho}-\frac{\rho^2}{3},
  \qquad
  \rho_h=(1+2A)^{-1/2},
  \qquad
  M=\frac{A+\frac13}{(2A+1)^{3/2}},
  \]
  and \(a=\rho/\rho_h\). The horizon ratio \(\rho_c/\rho_h\) equals \(a_+\), and the surface-gravity ratio equals \(\mu\). [Step 16]

- This corrected the singularity type. The second degeneration is a codimension-two cone along an embedded \(S^2\), with cone angle \(2\pi\mu\) when the first bolt is smoothed; it is not an isolated \(\mathbb R^4/\Gamma\) point. Therefore Eguchi–Hanson/Biquard/Ozuch isolated-orbifold obstruction theory is not the matching tool for this rod. Atiyah–LeBrun edge-cone Chern–Weil theory, with defects involving
  \[
  2(1-\beta)\chi(\Sigma)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  (1-\beta^2)[\Sigma]^2,
  \]
  is the relevant bookkeeping framework. [Step 16]

- Period normalization matters:
  - smoothing the black-hole bolt gives cone angle \(2\pi\mu\) at the cosmological bolt and volume tending to zero as \(A\to\infty\);
  - smoothing the cosmological bolt gives volume tending to \(24\pi^2\) but a large cone angle at the small bolt;
  - the two normalizations agree only in the Nariai limit \(A=0\), which is \(S^2\times S^2\) with volume \(16\pi^2\).
  Thus the first-bolt-smooth collapsed family does not simply converge smoothly to round \(S^4\). [Step 16]

- An exact separated rigidity theorem follows: in the cohomogeneity-one Einstein class with principal orbit \(S^1\times S^2\) and two smooth \(S^2\) bolts, smooth closure at both ends requires
  \[
  \mu=1,
  \]
  hence \(A=0\), so the metric is the Nariai product \(S^2(1)\times S^2(1)\). The matching is nondegenerate:
  \[
  \left.\frac{d\mu}{dA}\right|_{A=0}=-\frac43.
  \]
  [Step 17]

- A pinched analogue was not proved. The bolt equations degenerate as \(p\to0\), interval length is not a priori controlled, and a \(\delta\)-pinched separated metric need not remain globally near one exact Schwarzschild–de Sitter member. Any statement that smooth pinched closure forces \(A=O(\delta)\) remains conditional on an unproved uniform ODE stability lemma. [Steps 16–17]

## General diagonal \(T^k\) spectral identity

- For a twist-free diagonal \(T^k\)-invariant metric over an \(m\)-dimensional base,
  \[
  g=g_B+\sum_{I=1}^k p_I^2\,d\theta_I^2,
  \qquad
  w=\prod_{I=1}^kp_I,
  \]
  a product-rule calculation gives
  \[
  \operatorname{tr}_h\operatorname{Ric}^{V}
  =-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}.
  \]
  The identity was symbolically checked for \(k=1,\ldots,5\) on a two-dimensional base, while the proof itself is independent of the base dimension. [Steps 13, 17]

- Under normalized positive pinching,
  \[
  k(1-\delta)\le-\frac{\Delta_Bw}{w}\le k(1+\delta).
  \]
  If \(w>0\) inside and vanishes on a degeneration boundary, the ground-state/Barta argument gives
  \[
  k(1-\delta)
  \le\lambda_1^{\mathrm{Dir}}(\Omega,g_B)
  \le k(1+\delta).
  \]
  This is the principal all-dimensional invariant result obtained in the session. It requires a sufficiently large torus action and degeneration boundary and does not address arbitrary manifolds. [Step 17]

## The direct toric \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) crux

  \]

Explicit unimodular congruences for \(m\le14\) split the forms into \(k\) hyperbolic planes. ## Characteristic-class and bubble normalization checks

- For a Ricci-flat ALE four-manifold with asymptotic group \(\Gamma\),
  \[
  \frac1{8\pi^2}\int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2
  =\chi(X)-\frac1{|\Gamma|}.
  \]
  Eguchi–Hanson therefore carries \(12\pi^2\), not \(8\pi^2\), in the stated convention. This quantum applies to isolated ALE bubbles, not codimension-two rods or general ALF/ALG/ALH collapsed bubbles. [Steps 6, 9–10]

  \]
  the tangent-bundle Pontryagin number is
  \[
  \int p_1(TM)=3\tau(M)=A-2\chi(X)-3k,
  \]
  while the calibrated self-dual-bundle quantity is
  \[
  2\chi(M)+3\tau(M)=A-k.
  \]
  Negative-branch arguments must distinguish \(p_1(TM)\) from the \(\Lambda^2_+\) Chern–Weil density. [Steps 12–13]

- Standard Taub–NUT–AdS did not yield the hoped-for finite calibrated-defect residue model. Core-containing balls have problematic mean energy, smaller annular covers unwrap toward hyperbolic geometry with macroscopic calibrated defect, and the surviving issue appears to involve diffuse mixed \(\Lambda^2_+\) curvature rather than an established “one NUT, one fixed obstruction cost” theorem. [Steps 12–16]

# Session Knowledge Used or Established

- Constant rescaling leaves the Ricci \((0,2)\)-tensor unchanged while changing the metric, and bubble rescaling suppresses the Ricci endomorphism quadratically in length scale. These facts underlie branch normalization, the zero-straddling interval argument, and Ricci-flat blow-up limits. [Steps 1, 3, 9]

- Weighted smallness, \(L^p\) smallness, GH closeness, and unweighted operator pinching are distinct. In gluing or collapse, raising an index with the small input metric can convert a tensor-small residual into an order-one endomorphism defect. [Step 1]

- Pointwise curvature control cannot be recovered from \(C^0\) Ricci pinching alone, even with defect tending to zero and small added \(L^2\) Hessian energy. Future approximate-to-exact arguments must use weak/test-field projections, harmonic-coordinate finite-\(p\) control, additional PDE structure, or symmetry identities rather than a general pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-regularity theorem. [Steps 8, 10–11]

- In dimension four, tight pinching simultaneously gives comparison-geometry bounds and topological curvature-energy budgets. Under noncollapse this yields finite diffeomorphism type; over families with unbounded Euler characteristic, any defect-to-zero sequence must collapse while carrying unbounded Weyl energy. [Steps 8–9]

- Strict Hitchin–Thorpe is automatically enforced for sufficiently tight pinching in both signs. Known positive-branch obstruction families based on Hitchin–Thorpe violation or standard metric-independent monopoles therefore do not furnish tightly positive-pinched counterexamples. The positive branch is presently a topology-rigidity/existence problem inside an already strongly restricted class. [Steps 3–4, 18]

- Invariant determinant identities provide a rare derivative-free bridge: Killing fields themselves supply smooth test data, and the trace of vertical Ricci controls an orbit-volume eigenfunction. This works with \(C^0\) Ricci bounds and survives twist through a nonnegative potential. [Steps 12–13]

- Spectral pinning alone does not control orbit-space area or localized negative boundary curvature without an independent base-curvature hypothesis. The former Step 14 flat Faber–Krahn lower bound is not available on arbitrary curved orbit spaces. [Steps 15, 17–18]

- The toric \(\#_k(S^2\times S^2)\) problem is a direct construction/obstruction test and does not require reducing arbitrary metrics to invariant ones. No smooth pinched collapsing family has yet been constructed, and no uniform rod/holonomy obstruction has yet been proved. [Step 18]

- The separated two-bolt problem is exactly governed by Schwarzschild–de Sitter cone-angle matching. Exact smooth closure is rigid, but no quantitative \(C^0\)-Ricci pinched stability theorem has been established. [Steps 15–17]

- The all-dimensional mechanism remains weak. The diagonal \(T^k\) determinant identity is valid in arbitrary base dimension but only applies when a large torus action and degeneration boundary are present. Exact Einstein quotient collapse in odd and higher dimensions prevents any universal noncollapse strategy. [Steps 10, 17–18]

- Neither normalized branch has been proved in dimension four, and no argument covers all \(n\ge5\). The negative smoothing route, noncollapsed orbifold projection bridge, positive toric collapse test, topology-to-Einstein existence step, and Lean formalization all remain unfinished. [Steps 1–18]
